doc.summary: Models come from one generated catalog (curated JSON compiled into a registry for TypeScript and Rust). Family slots say which generation is live. Auto picks a model per message from plan, task, capability, privacy rules, health and expected cost. Manual choice is plan-gated. Each app warns or falls back when a model lacks an ability. Two resolvers (TypeScript, Rust) share one policy and a conformance fixture. Review update: 8 of 28 live family defaults were promoted without the eval gate, and 27 of 28 family fallback chains are empty.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how AGI Workforce lists models and chooses one for each message. It supports two requirements: the product is **model agnostic** (one experience over many models) and **provider agnostic** (many inference hosts, none required). [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4, §7; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:7-10)

**Plain terms**
- *Catalog*: the list of models with their facts (price, limits, abilities). Hand-edited input is `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json`; the compiler writes the generated files. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:35-58; AGENTS.md:§4)
- *Registry*: the compiled catalog plus routes, harnesses, runtime profiles and Auto policy. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/generated/registry.ts)
- *Family slot*: a named seat such as "the balanced model of one vendor". The slot, not the code, says which generation sits in it. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json)
- *Route*: one way to serve a model (a provider host plus a harness, which is the adapter that talks to that host). The same model can have several routes at different prices. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:143-162; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:36-58)
- *Trust mode*: where a request may run. The code names `local`, `on_device`, `byok` (own key) and `managed_cloud`. The product modes are mode:local, mode:own-key and mode:cloud. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:36)
- *Auto*: the default choice. The router picks a model for every message. *Manual*: the user names a model. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1722-1760)
- *Slot* in Auto policy: a named preference such as a cheap general slot or a coding slot, listed in `routing-policies.json`. There are 47 of them. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json, auto.slots)

The rule is that no consumer keeps its own copy of model data, and a model ID may be a literal only inside the catalog. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§3, §4)

Sources of truth, highest rank first: generated registry and policy JSON, then the resolver code, then tests, then prose. Where this page and a doc disagree, the code wins. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§2)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Build the catalog
1. A person edits `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` (and the other catalog files: routes, harnesses, gateways, developers, governance, retired models, routing policies, family slots). [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:40-58)
2. `pnpm sync:models` runs the compiler. It checks the output against `schema/registry.schema.json` with Ajv, resolves `family:<provider>/<family>` references to the live model, and writes: `packages/ai/model-registry/generated/registry.json` and `registry.ts`, `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json`, and Rust mirrors in `crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/generated/` and `crates/agiworkforce-model-registry/src/generated/`. [code] (compile.mjs:26-31,40-79,135-146; package.json:386-388)
3. `pnpm sync:models:check` fails when generated files drift. Never hand-edit `models.json`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4) [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/package.json scripts)
4. Guards fail an inline model-ID literal: `check:model-id-literals` (TS/JS) and a Rust script. [code] (package.json:219; AGENTS.md:§4)

The generated registry today has 394 models, 463 routes, 38 harnesses and 15 runtime profiles (counted by reading `generated/registry.json` for this page; this is a snapshot, not a stable fact). [executed-by-reading, not a test run] 389 models are `live`.

### 2. Capability data per model
Every model carries one fixed vocabulary of 22 capability names (text/image/audio/video in and out, streaming, structured output, function calling, reasoning, image editing, realtime, reranking, tool schema support, computer use, agentic, web search, deep research, code execution, prompt caching). `null` means "not verified" and consumers treat it as not offered. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/schema/registry.schema.json:729-800)

The registry splits these into **intrinsic** (about the model) and **route-dependent** (needs a provider route or an AGI harness, so never sufficient alone). [code] (registry.schema.json:1027-1050; model-catalog.ts:190-194) The docs say the same: web search, memory, MCP, code execution and computer use are not intrinsic model abilities. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4)

Apps read a simpler 13-flag view (`streaming`, `tools`, `vision`, `json`, `thinking`, `computerUse`, `agentic`, `imageGen`, `videoGen`, `search`, `research`, `codeExecution`, `caching`) mapped from the registry names. [code] (model-catalog.ts:172-188) Surfaces must read this metadata, never guess from a model name. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:34)

### 3. Which generation is live (family slots)
`model-families.json` has 28 family slots. Each has an `active` model, a `previous` one, a bounded `fallbackChain` (policy limit 3), a history, and a snapshot of price, capabilities and limits taken at promotion. [code] (model-families.json policy.fallbackChainLimit; families.*) Promotion gates are: provider availability, family identity, lifecycle eligibility, capability coverage, regression thresholds (cost rise limit 25%), registry validation. Preview models never take a stable slot. [code] (model-families.json policy)

Commands: `pnpm models:families` (inspect), `models:families:promote`, `models:families:rollback`, each with `--slot <id> --apply`. [code] (package.json:394-396; AGENTS.md:§4)

Routes and defaults point at `family:<provider>/<family>`, so swapping a model edits only the family file. [code] (routing-policies.json auto.slots, e.g. `modelKey` values of the form `family:...`)

Current state (read 2026-11-24): of the 28 slots, 13 are marked `seeded` (taken from the authored roster, no gate run) and 15 carry a real promotion record. [code] (model-families.json) **Eight active records say the eval gate was not run**: openai/gpt-frontier, gpt-balanced, gpt-fast, gpt-image; (model name), (model name); google/(model name) (different wording, same meaning) and google/gemini-flash-image. At least one says it was made on the owner's instruction. [code] (model-families.json, families.*.active.promotionReason; re-counted by script on 2026-11-24) So several live defaults skipped the promotion gate that AGENTS.md:§4 describes. [inferred]

**Fallback chains are almost always empty.** 27 of 28 slots have a `fallbackChain` of length 0 and one has length 1, though the policy limit is 3. For most families the only recovery from a bad promotion is rollback to the `previous` model, not a fallback chain. [code] (model-families.json, counted by script; packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/families.mjs:374)

To see the live model for a slot, read that file or run `pnpm models:families`; this page does not name models.

### 4. Choosing a model: Auto
The resolver is `resolveAutoRoute` in `packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts`. A request carries: the selection (`auto`, a profile alias, or a model), task type, plan tier, trust mode, current model, and optional rules (US-only, zero data retention, no-training, residency region, workspace model policy, excluded providers and hosts, budget left, health data). [code] (auto.ts:165-376)

Steps for an Auto request:
1. **Refuse early** if the trust mode is not permitted, a mandatory session capability is missing (`mandatory_capability_unavailable`), or the runtime profile does not fit. [code] (auto.ts:1722-1740, 568-612)
2. **Pick a cost band.** Aliases are `auto` (default, computed per task), `auto-economy`, `auto-balanced`, `auto-premium`. For `auto`, the task chooses the band (for example simple chat and general use economy, coding and reasoning premium, long context balanced). Then `resolveRoutingLane` clamps the band by the plan's entry in `tierMaximumProfiles`: free and basic economy, pro balanced, max, enterprise and byok premium. The plan id is first passed through `normalizeTier`, because `tierMaximumProfiles` has no keys for `max_15x`, `team` or `team_premium`; an unknown result defaults to economy. [code] (routing-policies.json auto.aliases, autoProfileByTask, tierMaximumProfiles; auto.ts:1198-1206)
3. **Take the ordered slots** for that task and band, restricted to the plan's allow-list `tierAllowedSlots` (six entries: free, basic, pro, max, enterprise, byok). Free gets three slots. A separate `fallbackSlot` is also chosen per tier from that list. This allow-list, not only the band clamp, decides which models a plan can reach. [code] (auto.ts:1205-1207; routing-policies.json auto.tierAllowedSlots)
4. **Optional reorder stages**: task-family stage (quality floor then cost order; kill switch `AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE`), caller `preferSlots` (reorder only), canary and shadow. [code] (auto.ts:1198-1225; task-family-routing.ts; packages/ai/routing/README.md)
5. **Prefer the conversation's current model** (continuity, protects prompt cache) while it is still eligible, affordable and, under the task-family stage, not more than 2 times the cost of the cheapest candidate that meets the floor. [code] (auto.ts:755, 1840-1900; routing-policies.json auto.continuity)
6. **Walk the slots**: each candidate must pass eligibility; the first dispatchable, affordable one wins. A slot whose model would bill a long prompt at a dearer input tier hands over to a cheaper backup. [code] (auto.ts:1960-2030)
7. **Fallbacks**: if only unhealthy candidates remain, try health fallbacks, then the fallback slot, then a jurisdiction fallback slot, else `no_eligible_route`. The decision lists up to 4 fallback routes, with at most 2 same-model routes before another model. [code] (auto.ts:757-764, 2030-2125)

**Eligibility of one model** (`evaluateEligibility`): the model must be in the account's admitted set, live, not deprecated or past its retirement date, allowed for the plan, allowed by US-only / excluded-provider / no-training / developer-country rules, have a route in the request's trust mode, hold every intrinsic capability the task needs, and meet the task's minimum context. [code] (auto.ts:1340-1430)

**Eligibility of one route** (`routeAdmissionRejections`): not on an excluded host, inside the required region, allowed by the workspace policy, commercial status not blocked (experimental routes cannot serve managed traffic), selectable and live, harness runs on the calling app, zero-retention satisfied if asked, no-training satisfied if asked, harness features the task needs are `implemented`. [code] (auto.ts:1042-1140)

### 5. How routing weighs cost, quality, latency, privacy
| Factor | Where it acts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy and policy | Admission, a hard filter before any ranking. Trust mode, zero data retention, no-training, region, US-only, developer country, workspace policy | auto.ts:1042-1140, 1340-1430 |
| Quality | Slot order per task and band; per-family `qualityFloor` in the task-family stage | routing-policies.json auto.tasks, auto.taskFamilies; task-family-routing.ts |
| Cost | Inside the floor-meeting set, order by expected cost of the route actually dispatched; routes then rank by expected cents; budget left can skip a model; long-prompt price tiers trigger a backup | docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:78-98; auto.ts:1144-1170, 1623-1690 |
| Latency and health | Routes rank healthy first, then credentialed, then lower observed penalty (failure rate and time to first token in bands), then cost, then the model default route, then route id. Switch `AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH` | auto.ts:859-980, 1144-1160 |
| Cache | A route holding a warm cache is kept unless it costs more than 1.25 times the cheapest | auto.ts:735, 1160-1178 |

The named profiles (Instant, High, Code, Research) carry quality, cost and latency weights, but `weightedScore` is exported and not called by `resolveAutoRoute`; only the profile id is attached to the decision. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/profiles/index.ts:137-169; auto.ts:1466) So latency has no direct weight in slot ordering today. [inferred]

### 6. Manual choice
If the selection is not an alias, the resolver checks that model alone with the same eligibility rules and returns it as `explicit`. A pinned route (`requiredRouteId`) must be healthy and credentialed or the call fails with `explicit_route_ineligible`. A named model ignores the Auto-only `excludedProviders` list but still obeys excluded hosts, region and developer-country rules. [code] (auto.ts:1750-1850, 150-235 comments) Same-model routes rotate before any substitution. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:55-57)

### 7. Preview
`previewAutoRoute` explains a decision (candidates, admission, reasons) with no upstream call, and shares helpers with the real resolver so it cannot name a different winner. [code] (packages/ai/routing/README.md; auto.ts:2204) It is exposed as api:POST /api/llm/v1/route/preview. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/route/preview/route.ts:200)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Plans.** Display names come from `BILLING_PLAN_PRICING`: Local Mode, Local Mode + BYOK, Free, Basic, Premium (id `pro`), Max, Ultra (id `max_15x`), Team, Team Premium, Enterprise. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:166-230) Plan ids in routing are `free`, `basic`, `pro`, `max`, `enterprise`, `byok`; `team` maps to `pro`, `max_15x` and `team_premium` map to `max`; unknown strings fall to `free`. [code] (auto.ts:650-680) Relationship names: plan:free, plan:basic, plan:pro (Premium), plan:max, plan:max_15x (Ultra), plan:enterprise.

**Local Mode is a plan tier.** It has id `local-only`, label "Local Mode", price 0 USD monthly and yearly, and is visible on web, desktop and mobile. Its limits set `maxSandboxes` 0, `maxScheduledTasks` 0 and `codeHarnessDailyCeilingCents` 0, so cloud sandboxes, scheduled tasks and the cloud code harness are off in Local Mode. Projects, knowledge storage, custom MCP servers, concurrent turns and connector tools are `unlimited`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:166-172, 236, 583-597) The desktop app builds a local device account with plan `local-only`, display name "Local Mode" and `subscriptionStatus` `none`, which is consistent with local use needing no subscription. [code] (apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:1945-1953)

**Plan limits on Auto.** Two tables in the policy: the highest cost band (`tierMaximumProfiles`) and the allowed slots (`tierAllowedSlots`), each keyed free, basic, pro, max, enterprise, byok. Free gets three slots (`free_workhorse`, `free_workhorse_fast`, `fast_anthropic`) and the economy band; basic five slots and economy; pro, max and enterprise progressively more. The selectable `auto` alias carries `tierPolicy.minTier: basic`. [code] (routing-policies.json auto.tierAllowedSlots, tierMaximumProfiles, aliases.auto.tierPolicy; auto.ts:1198-1207; model-catalog.ts:956-975) These are two mechanisms that both name Free: the alias gate says Basic, while the lane clamp and slot list serve Free an economy band. How the picker and server reconcile them was not traced. [unknown] See Gaps.

**Plan limits on manual choice.** Three tables decide a named model: `tierAllowedModels` (economy, pro additions, flagship additions) in the catalog, `minTier` on the model, and `canAccessModelForSubscriptionTier`. Free may name only economy models marked `minTier: free`. Pro adds the pro tier; Max and Enterprise add flagships. [code] (model-catalog.ts:2196-2262) A locked model shows a plan label in the picker. [code] (model-picker.ts:247-270)

**Provider switching inside one conversation** is allowed only for max, max_15x, team_premium and enterprise. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/design-system/user-identity.ts:50-52; apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/tierGuard.ts)

**Modes.**
| Mode | Trust mode in code | What the router does |
|---|---|---|
| mode:cloud | `managed_cloud` | Routes over AGI-held provider credentials; plan tier tables apply; managed ledger bills credits |
| mode:own-key | `byok` | Routes to direct provider routes with the user's own key; tier band is `premium`; CLI says BYOK and local models are not gated by subscription tier |
| mode:local | `local` (desktop, CLI) and `on_device` (mobile) | Routes only to harnesses that list that trust mode: for `local` the registry lists `ollama/chat` and `lmstudio/chat-completions`; for `on_device` it lists none |
[code] (auto.ts:1691-1708; registry.json runtimeProfiles read 2026-11-24; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:920-935)

Nothing may move a Local chat to BYOK or cloud without an explicit, consented fork. Registry membership never authorizes crossing. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§6) Enforced by `check:trust-boundaries` and per-surface trust-boundary tests. [requirement] The resolver refuses a trust mode the workspace does not permit (`allowedTrustModes`). [code] (auto.ts:333-338)

**Local inference is free of any paid plan.** The registry prices the `local-only` plan at 0 USD. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-172) [requirement] (task statement). Whether local use needs an account or sign-in on each app is not fully established. Mobile locks Cloud models behind sign-in, which implies Cloud needs an account; whether on-device chat does is [unknown]. [inferred] (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts, lock reason text not located at the line a reviewer cited)

**Execution boundary for on-device models.** On mobile, the first use of an on-device model needs an outside service: the on-device catalog points at huggingface.co download URLs with pinned SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes. After the download, running the model is on the device. [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts:3-16) Whether any app lets a user side-load the files offline was not checked. [unknown]

**Privacy rules that admit or refuse routes** (all passed in by the caller, all fail closed): zero data retention, no-training (vendor and host must both keep inputs out of training; a provider with no recorded policy is refused), US-only (plans max and enterprise only), data residency region, workspace allow/deny policy, developer-country rule. [code] (auto.ts:165-376,1042-1140; routing-policies.json auto.providerPolicies) Managed Auto also avoids Chinese-headquartered providers entirely by a caller-supplied exclusion; a model the user names is still served. [code] (auto.ts:200-225 comment)

**Subscription link.** Plan, access rules and quotas come from the one AGI Subscription system; the router only reads the plan id and an account-admitted model set. [requirement] (task statement) [inferred] from `admittedModelKeys` and `subscriptionTier` fields. The entitlement service itself is covered by another page.

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
**Resolver outcomes.** The resolver never throws for a policy refusal. It returns `unavailable` with a code: `unknown_selection`, `unknown_task`, `unknown_runtime_profile`, `runtime_profile_unavailable`, `runtime_profile_mismatch`, `explicit_model_ineligible`, `explicit_route_ineligible`, `mandatory_capability_unavailable`, `trust_mode_not_permitted`, `model_not_available_in_region`, `no_eligible_route`, plus a list of reasons. [code] (auto.ts:471-492)

**Capability mismatch.** With a named model: refuse (`explicit_model_ineligible`) unless the caller sets `fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch`, in which case Auto answers and the reason is `capability_fallback`. Mobile and Chrome set it true; the web admission sets it false for an exact selection. [code] (auto.ts:1822-1836; cloudDispatchRouting.ts:94; managedChatRouting.ts:55; admission.ts:253) A *mandatory* session capability (from the capability handshake) is never replaced by a weaker substitute, and a missing capability document with mandatory needs fails closed. [code] (evaluator.ts header; auto.ts:568-612)

**Provider failure.** Candidates carry health; an unhealthy first choice is parked and healthy ones are tried first. The decision lists fallback routes, and a failure on one route rotates to same-model routes before another model. A reply that came from a fallback carries a reason code (for example `managed_failover`, `openrouter_route_failover`, `insufficient_credits`, `free_limit_reached`, `free_capacity_unavailable`, `research_unsupported_model`) through a response header and the client shows plain text for it. [code] (auto.ts:1980-2060; packages/contracts/types/src/chat-fallback-reason.ts:43-150)

**Bad family promotion.** Because 27 of 28 family fallback chains are empty, the recovery path is `models:families:rollback` to the `previous` model, not an automatic chain. [code] (model-families.json; families.mjs:374)

**Capability the route stopped honouring.** The capability-health store records misses; for a request that carries tools or a structured format, a second resolution demotes a route with recorded losses. A turn with no tools costs nothing. [requirement] (provider-routing.md:127-134) [code] (auto.ts:869-980)

**Budget.** A model that exceeds the remaining budget is skipped except for the fallback slot. [code] (auto.ts:1985-1992)

**Free Auto.** Never returns a route not verified as zero cost; every doubt means ineligible, so it can answer "no free capacity right now". [code] (free-auto.ts:1-45)

**Policy cannot be read.** Admission refuses with `policy_unreadable`, `no_training_route` or `no_route`. A workspace policy read that fails deliberately fails open for ungoverned scopes. [code] (admission.ts:70-110; auto.ts:312-320 comments) Whether failing open on a read error matches the trust rules was not checked. [unknown]

**Retired models.** A model past its deprecation date is refused as an explicit choice; retired IDs keep a record so old history still shows a name. [code] (auto.ts:1710-1721; model-catalog.ts:1469-1500)

**Verification status.** Everything above is implementation status read from code, plus counts made by reading the JSON catalog files on 2026-11-24. No test, app run or production check was made for this page. Recorded runs in the project: none cited here. [unknown]

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Requirements that bind this subject [requirement]:
- One experience over many models: surfaces read capability metadata, never model-name substrings. (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:34; AGENTS.md:§4)
- Provider agnostic: add or swap a model by editing catalog or family files only, then `pnpm sync:models`. (AGENTS.md:§4)
- Cost is a first-class constraint; a stronger model is not the default because it is stronger. (AGENTS.md:§7)
- Local, own-key and cloud are separate trust boundaries; no silent crossing. (AGENTS.md:§6)
- Execution boundaries are explicit: what runs on the device, what needs AGI servers, what needs outside services. The `trust-mode-surface-matrix` and `docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md` own that. (task statement; docs/generated/trust-mode-surface-matrix.md)
- Local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid plan.
- Documentation availability is separate from account, region and route availability. (AGENTS.md:§4)

Proposals [proposed]:
1. Make one module the owner of plan access. Today `tierAllowedSlots` (policy), `tierAllowedModels` plus `minTier` (catalog) and the hardcoded `TIER_POLICIES` (model-catalog.ts) all state it.
2. Decide which resolver is canonical (TS or Rust) and generate the other, or keep the conformance fixture and record the decision.
3. Use the profile weights in ordering, or delete the unused weights, so latency has an explicit place.
4. Give on-device models a registry record with the same capability vocabulary so the picker and warnings treat them like cloud models.
5. Show one shared wording for each capability loss on every app, from one catalog of messages, not per-app strings.
6. Fill family fallback chains, or record that rollback is the only recovery, and run the eval gate for the eight slots promoted without it.

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Implementation gaps (the code is missing or not connected):
1. **On-device models are outside the registry.** The on-device catalog lives in `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts` with its own five capability flags (`text`, `visionIn`, `audioIn`, `toolCalls`, `structuredOutput`) and model ID literals; it does not use the 22-name vocabulary or the `family:` slots. Mobile's `on_device` runtime profile lists zero harnesses. This sits outside AGENTS.md:§4's statement that the generated catalog is the only place for model IDs. Its files are fetched from huggingface.co. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/on-device-models.ts:1-45; local-llm/src/catalog.ts:1-80; registry.json runtimeProfiles['mobile/local-chat'])
2. **Plan tables are stated three times.** Policy `tierAllowedSlots`, catalog `tierAllowedModels` with `minTier`, and hardcoded `TIER_POLICIES` (which has no `basic` and lists `free` slots as a short list). They can drift. [code] (routing-policies.json; model-catalog.ts:1121-1413,2196-2262)
3. **Auto alias floor vs Free.** `aliases.auto.tierPolicy.minTier` is `basic`, yet `tierAllowedSlots.free` and `tierMaximumProfiles.free` serve Free an economy Auto lane, and free-lane code adds the TypeScript-only Free Auto stage. How the picker reconciles this was not traced. [code] (routing-policies.json; auto.ts:1198-1207) [unknown] for the reconciliation
4. **Two resolvers.** The TS and Rust resolvers share one fixture, but the file header says which is canonical is an open question. Free Auto, the task-family stage, canary, shadow, health, `preferSlots` and caller exclusions exist only in TypeScript; the CLI's Rust path gets plain static policy. [code] (crates/agiworkforce-model-registry/tests/auto_route_conformance.rs:1-12; free-auto.ts:1-45; auto.ts:200-260 comments)
5. **Named profile weights are unused** by the resolver (`weightedScore` has no caller outside tests). [code] (profiles/index.ts:169; auto.ts:1466)
6. **Family promotions skipped the gate.** 13 of 28 slots were seeded without a gate run, and 8 active records say the eval gate was not run (see How it works today, section 3). 27 of 28 fallback chains are empty. [code] (model-families.json)
7. **VS Code BYOK and local** profiles are `unwired`; mobile, desktop and CLI local profiles are `partial`. [code] (registry.json runtimeProfiles)
8. **Capability warnings are per app.** Web, VS Code, Chrome, CLI and mobile each have separate copy and checks; no shared module emits them. [code] (files listed under Differences between apps)
9. **Desktop Electron local inference path** was not found in `apps/desktop/electron`. [unknown]
10. **Stray generated files** `generated/registry.json.orig` and `src/generated/model_registry.json.orig` exist beside tracked outputs (untracked). [code] (directory listing; git ls-files)
11. **Local Mode loses cloud features.** Sandboxes, scheduled tasks and the cloud code harness are set to 0 for `local-only`; which app screens explain this to the user was not checked. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:583-597) [unknown] for the UI.

Verification gaps: no run of any test, guard or app was made for this page; no evidence was found of a live check that each app shows the warnings above.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Run these (not run for this page; the project forbids builds and tests during knowledge-base writing). Prefer `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh` or `light-job.sh` on a 16 GB machine. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md Delegation)

| Question | Command or file |
|---|---|
| Is the generated catalog current? | `pnpm sync:models:check` |
| Catalog integrity and literals | `pnpm check:model-catalog`, `pnpm check:model-id-literals` |
| Which model is live in each family | `pnpm models:families` |
| Which family promotions skipped the gate | read `active.promotionReason` and `evaluation.seeded` per slot in `model-families.json` |
| Registry and family tests | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/model-registry test` |
| Resolver behaviour | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/routing test` |
| TS and Rust agree | run the routing test with `AGI_UPDATE_ROUTING_CONFORMANCE` unset, then `cargo test -p agiworkforce-model-registry` |
| What would Auto pick for this account | call api:POST /api/llm/v1/route/preview with `selection`, `taskType`, optional `capabilitiesInUse` |
| Full guard chain | `pnpm check:llm-operability` |
| What a model can do | find its row in `generated/registry.json` (`capabilities`, `limits`, `routes`) |

Check by hand in the app: pick a text-only model with an image attached on Web (expect the Switch panel); pick a no-tools model in VS Code (expect the modal); send an image on mobile with a model at its image limit (expect the limit message). [proposed]

Note: for `apps/web`, run tests through its own package script, and `tsc` needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§12)

key_facts.fact: The model catalog is generated: people edit catalog JSON under packages/ai/model-registry/catalog, and pnpm sync:models compiles registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and two Rust mirrors.
Never hand-edit packages/contracts/types/src/models.json; a model ID may be a literal only in the catalog, enforced by check:model-id-literals and a Rust guard.
The generated registry read on 2026-11-24 holds 394 models, 463 routes, 38 harnesses and 15 runtime profiles; 389 models are live.
Every model has one 22-name capability vocabulary; null means unverified and is treated as not offered.
Capabilities are split into intrinsic (model) and route-dependent (needs route or AGI harness); route-dependent ones are never sufficient alone.
model-families.json has 28 family slots; each has active, previous, fallbackChain (limit 3), history and snapshots; defaults point at family:<provider>/<family>.

13 of 28 family slots are seeded (no gate run); 8 active promotion records say the eval gate was not run (openai gpt-frontier, gpt-balanced, gpt-fast, gpt-image; anthropic (model name), (model name); google (model name), gemini-flash-image).
Family fallback chains are empty for 27 of 28 slots and hold one entry in the other, though the policy limit is 3; recovery from a bad promotion is mostly rollback to the previous model.
Promote or roll back a family with pnpm models:families:promote or :rollback --slot <id> --apply; inspect with pnpm models:families.

Auto aliases are auto (default), auto-economy, auto-balanced, auto-premium; auto computes the band per task, and resolveRoutingLane clamps it by tierMaximumProfiles (free/basic economy, pro balanced, max/enterprise/byok premium) after normalizeTier; unknown tiers default to economy.

tierMaximumProfiles and tierAllowedSlots each have six keys (free, basic, pro, max, enterprise, byok); max_15x, team and team_premium rely on normalizeTier. Free's allowed slots are free_workhorse, free_workhorse_fast, fast_anthropic.
The auto alias has tierPolicy minTier basic while Free has an economy band and three allowed slots; the reconciliation is not traced.
Auto policy has 47 slots, 11 task types and 12 task families.
Privacy and policy rules are hard admission filters applied before ranking: trust mode, zero data retention, no-training, region, US-only, developer country, workspace policy.
Route ranking order: healthy, credentialed, lower observed penalty, lower expected cost, model default route, route id; a warm-cache route is kept unless it costs over 1.25 times the cheapest.
The task-family stage orders only the already-admitted set by expected cost among candidates meeting a quality floor; it is a permutation, with kill switch AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE.
Auto keeps the conversation's current model for cache continuity while it stays eligible and costs at most 2 times the cheapest floor-meeting candidate.

A named model is served as 'explicit'; if it is ineligible the resolver returns explicit_model_ineligible, unless fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch is set (mobile and Chrome set it, web exact selection clears it).
Billing follows the model's official price while cost follows the served route, so a cheaper host does not change what the user pays.
Plan display names: Local Mode, Local Mode + BYOK, Free, Basic, Premium (id pro), Max, Ultra (id max_15x), Team, Team Premium, Enterprise.

Local Mode (plan id local-only) is priced at 0 USD, is visible on web, desktop and mobile, and has maxSandboxes 0, maxScheduledTasks 0 and codeHarnessDailyCeilingCents 0; so sandboxes, scheduled tasks and the cloud code harness are off.
Desktop builds a local device account with plan local-only, name Local Mode and subscriptionStatus none.
Mobile on-device model files are downloaded from huggingface.co with pinned SHA-256 hashes and sizes, so first use needs an outside service.
Free may name only economy models marked minTier free; pro adds pro models; max and enterprise add flagships.
Switching provider inside one conversation is allowed only for max, max_15x, team_premium and enterprise.
Web warns before a model switch: 'Switch to <model>?' with findings for no images, no tools or context overflow, and a Switch anyway button.
VS Code shows a modal listing losses (no tools, no images, smaller context) before switching, with a Switch anyway choice.
Chrome browser actions fail with '<model> does not support browser tools, screenshots, and streaming.' when the chosen model lacks tools, vision or streaming; Auto picks a capable model instead.
The CLI drops tools for a local model that does not advertise tool support and prints a notice that the turn runs without tools.
Mobile maps unavailable routing codes to fixed messages, for example 'No available AGI Cloud model supports this request. Try a different model or remove the attachment.'
The Rust crate agiworkforce-model-registry holds a second resolver (resolve_auto_route) over the same generated policy; both replay one conformance fixture, and which is canonical is undecided.
Free Auto, task-family stage, canary, shadow, health ranking and preferSlots are TypeScript-only; the Rust resolver has no counterpart.
Runtime profiles: local profiles for desktop, mobile and CLI are partial; mobile on_device lists zero harnesses; desktop local lists ollama and lmstudio harnesses; VS Code BYOK and local are unwired.
Mobile on-device models come from a separate catalog (packages/platform/local-llm) with five capability flags, not the registry vocabulary.
Named routing profiles (Instant, High, Code, Research) define quality, cost and latency weights, but weightedScore is not called by resolveAutoRoute.
Every routing decision is traced in table routing_decision_traces (migration 0212) and compared hourly by /api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout.

missing.fact: Family fallback chains are empty for 27 of 28 slots and hold one entry in the 28th, although the policy limit allows more. So for most families the only recovery from a bad promotion is rollback to the 'previous' model, not a fallback chain.
missing.evidence: packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json (script count: chain lengths 0 x27, 1 x1); packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/families.mjs:374 (slice to policy.fallbackChainLimit).

doc.summary: The product reaches models through one adapter contract (ProviderAdapter in @agiworkforce/types). Shared helper packages (provider-protocol, provider-runtime) and 17 provider packages plus a factory implement it. Web owns retry, failover and deadlines for managed cloud. The Rust CLI and desktop use their own engine (agiworkforce-llm). Gateways are declared as data in the model registry. Images, speech and search mostly bypass the provider packages. Local mobile inference uses a separate package. Mobile cloud models are gated by a cloud-unlocked flag and plan tier, and mobile also lists provider-funded Free quota chat models that run in the cloud.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
AGI Workforce must work with many model vendors without product code depending on any one of them. Three layers do this.

1. **Contract.** `ProviderAdapter` is the one interface every provider implements: `id`, `label`, `auth`, `config`, `catalog()` and `stream(req, signal)`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/provider-adapter.ts:595-613)
2. **Shared helpers.** `@agiworkforce/provider-protocol` holds pure payload-shaping functions (no IO, no SDK). `@agiworkforce/provider-runtime` holds error classification, retry maths, a stream idle watchdog, base-URL checks and credential-failover memory. [code] (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/index.ts:1-17; packages/ai/provider-runtime/src/index.ts:1-22)
3. **Adapters.** One package per vendor under `packages/ai/providers/*`, built through one registry, `@agiworkforce/providers-factory`. Apps must not import a leaf package's internals. [code] (packages/ai/providers/README.md, 'Public API / Exports'; packages/ai/providers/factory/src/index.ts:96-160)

Which model runs on which route is data, not code. The catalogs in `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/` (`harnesses.json`, `gateways.json`, `model-routes.json`, `provider-hosts.json`) decide it. Model ids live only in the generated catalog; this page names none. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)

Two separate engines exist because the languages differ. TypeScript (web, extensions, mobile helpers) uses the packages above. Rust (CLI, desktop Tauri) uses `crates/agiworkforce-llm`, which holds only provider mechanics (wire types, request building per dialect, stream decoding, tool-call assembly, idle watchdog, error classification). Policy such as provider choice, keys, routing and fallback stays in the apps. [code] (crates/agiworkforce-llm/src/lib.rs:1-20)

Product rules that shape this subject: model agnostic and provider agnostic; Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently move a Local chat to BYOK or cloud. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md, 'Enforcement Rules')

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Provider packages (what each is used for)

Adapter registry ids come from `PROVIDER_ADAPTER_IDS`. [code] (packages/ai/providers/factory/src/index.ts:98-117)

| Package folder | Registry id | Use | Notes (basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic | anthropic | chat | Uses the official Anthropic SDK; also serves Anthropic-dialect routes via a base URL [code] (anthropic/src/index.ts:73-81; web provider-adapter-service.ts:257-283) |
| openai | openai, openai_compat | chat, plus the shared OpenAI-compatible translation | Responses API for catalog-known models on the native route, Chat Completions for proxies [code] (providers/README.md 'Known Caveats'); compat adapter reused by other vendors and gateways [code] (factory/src/index.ts:127-139) |
| google | google | chat | Gemini; REST, not the Google SDK [code] (google/src/index.ts:206) |
| xai | xai | chat | OpenAI-compatible [code] (xai/src/index.ts:22) |
| deepseek | deepseek | chat | OpenAI-compatible with cache-usage parsing [code] (deepseek/src/cache-usage.ts exists) |
| groq | groq | chat (speed) | OpenAI-compatible [code] (groq/src/index.ts:112) |
| moonshot | moonshot | chat | [code] (moonshot/src/index.ts:130) |
| minimax | minimax | chat | [code] (minimax/src/index.ts:113) |
| qwen | qwen | chat; quota probe | Fallback endpoints and a quota probe helper [code] (qwen/src/quota-probe.ts; factory/src/index.ts:38-44) |
| zhipu | zhipu | chat | [code] (zhipu/src/index.ts:147) |
| perplexity | perplexity | search-grounded chat | Returns a citations list on the last chunk [code] (perplexity/src/index.ts:6-13) |
| nvidia | nvidia_nim | chat (hosted open models) | Default host integrate.api.nvidia.com [code] (nvidia/src/index.ts:25) |
| openrouter | open_router | chat via aggregator; media routes use direct fetch elsewhere | Provider routing prefs, cache control [code] (openrouter/src/provider-routing.ts, cache-control.ts) |
| vercel-gateway | vercel_gateway | chat via aggregator; embeddings; evaluation (decision transport) | [code] (vercel-gateway/src/embeddings.ts, evaluation.ts; harnesses.json keys 'vercel_gateway/embeddings','vercel_gateway/evaluation') |
| workers-ai | workers_ai | chat via Cloudflare AI Gateway compat endpoint | [code] (workers-ai/src/index.ts:1-12) |
| ollama | ollama | local chat (default http://localhost:11434) | Dynamic catalog [code] (ollama/src/index.ts:8-9) |
| lmstudio | lmstudio | local chat (default http://localhost:1234/v1) | Catalog read live from /v1/models [code] (lmstudio/src/index.ts:3-9,39) |
| factory | (registry) | builds any adapter; `createGatewayAdapter` for declarative gateways | Holds no keys [code] (factory/package.json description; factory/src/gateway.ts) |

No leaf package exists for images, speech or search. [code] (packages/ai/providers directory listing)

### Request path on web (managed cloud)

1. `ADAPTER_PROVIDERS` maps a provider id to `buildAdapter`, `buildChatRequest`, `mapError` and a `wireMode`. It is built from three sources: protocol routes from the registry, gateway routes (only if the flag is on), and a hand-written table for 14 named providers. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-providers.ts:54-60,126-258)
2. `resolveProviderFromModel` picks the provider from the catalog; if the vendor key is missing and an OpenRouter slug exists, it falls to OpenRouter. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/provider-adapter-service.ts:185-225)
3. `buildServerProviderAdapter` reads the key from env, validates any `*_BASE_URL` override against the allowlist, and calls `createProviderAdapter`. Keys and endpoints live in the web deployment, never in the factory. [code] (provider-adapter-service.ts:313-399)
4. The adapter streams `StreamChunk` values. Each adapter wraps its stream in `withStreamIdleWatchdog` and maps errors through `classifyError`. [code] (e.g. anthropic/src/index.ts:130; provider-runtime/src/index.ts header)

### Gateways and protocol routes

A gateway is any OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages compatible endpoint. It needs no package: add an entry to `gateways.json`, point a harness at it with `gatewayId`, set env var names. [requirement] (docs/development/add-a-gateway.md) The registry lists nine gateway definitions: openrouter_via_gateway (not wired), cheaperinference, cheaperinference_anthropic, deepinfra, together, novita, experientiallabs, experientiallabs_anthropic, workers_ai. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/gateways.json keys)

The whole gateway path is off unless `AGI_ROUTING_GATEWAY_ROUTES=1`. The flag is enforced at admission (`admittedHarnessIds` drops gateway harnesses) and at dispatch (`ADAPTER_PROVIDERS` gets no gateway entry). [code] (apps/web/lib/services/gateway-routing.ts:13,52-54; adapter-providers.ts:109-124) The base URL taken from env must match the host the registry declares, or the adapter is refused. [code] (gateway-routing.ts:56-84)

'Protocol routes' are harnesses with a literal `baseUrl`, such as the DeepSeek, Moonshot and Zhipu Anthropic-dialect endpoints; they reuse the generic Anthropic or OpenAI adapters. [code] (harnesses.json 'deepseek-anthropic/messages' etc.; provider-adapter-service.ts:257-283)

### Retry and failover (web)

Retry and failover are owned by web, not by adapters. [code] (provider-runtime/src/index.ts:7-19; no adapter imports `withRetry`)

- **Same-route retry** happens only before any chunk reaches the client: the first chunk is peeked, and a failure there is retried on the same route. Max attempts are 2 for most retryable classes, `MAX_OVERLOAD_RETRIES` (3) for `server_overload`. Never retried on the same route: `auth`, `context_overflow`. [code] (provider-deadlines.ts:27,184-228,241-250; provider-runtime/src/retry.ts:10-14)
- **Rotation** to another route happens above that, in `managed-failover.ts`. Eligible classes: connection, server_error, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, api_timeout, rate_limit, quota_exhausted, empty_response, unsupported_input; plus credential rejection (`auth`), which blocks that provider's remaining routes. Never rotated: billing_exhausted, safety, content_blocked. [code] (managed-failover.ts:102-150,234-248)
- **Auto vs named model.** Across models only for Auto. A named model may rotate to other routes of the same model; it is never answered by a different model. An unfunded account may rotate once, for Auto only. [code] (managed-failover.ts:1-60,171-180)
- **Tool state pins the provider.** Once a provider has minted tool-call ids in the turn (step 2 or later), the turn stays on it. [code] (managed-failover.ts:321-329)
- **Grounded requests** get at most 1 same-provider candidate before a different provider is required. [code] (provider-runtime/src/retry.ts:21, MAX_SAME_PROVIDER_RETRIES_FOR_GROUNDED_REQUEST)
- Rotation does not create a second charge: one reservation spans all attempts and settlement prices the model that served. [code] (managed-failover.ts header comment)

### Timeouts

| Name | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Function limit for chat completions | 300 000 ms | apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:1 |
| Turn first-token budget | 40 000 ms | deadline-policy.ts:12 |
| Per-provider first-token deadline | 25 000 ms (clamped to the turn's remaining budget, floor 1 000 ms) | deadline-policy.ts:14; nestedDeadlineMs |
| Provider stream deadline | equals the tool-loop budget (300 000 - 60 000 ms reserve) | deadline-policy.ts:3-10 |
| Adapter stream idle watchdog (TS) | 90 000 ms default | provider-runtime/src/watchdog.ts:1 |
| Backoff | base 500 ms, max 32 000 ms | provider-runtime/src/retry.ts:13-14 |
| CLI stream idle timeout (Rust) | 300 s | apps/cli/src/models/mod.rs:31 |
| Image generation provider deadline | 55 000 ms | deadline-policy.ts:63 |

### Rust surfaces

CLI and desktop Tauri map their own provider enums onto `ProviderSpec { dialect, base_url, auth, extra_headers }`. Dialects are Anthropic, Gemini, OllamaNative, OpenAiResponses and OpenAiCompat. [code] (crates/agiworkforce-llm/src/spec.rs:48-75; apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:412-465) The CLI keeps its own fallback rule that refuses a cloud fallback from a local session. [code] (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:75-86; tests at 4525-4572)

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
- **Credentials.** Web reads managed keys from environment variables named in `SERVER_PROVIDER_CONFIG` and `PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV_KEYS` (for example a `<PREFIX>_API_KEY` per provider, with alternates for Google, Qwen, NVIDIA, Workers AI and the Vercel gateway). Values are never recorded here. [code] (provider-adapter-service.ts:35-68)
- **Base URL overrides** come from `<PREFIX>_BASE_URL` and are accepted only for allowlisted hosts over https (http only for localhost and 127.0.0.1). [code] (provider-adapter-service.ts:128-146; provider-runtime/src/base-url.ts:1-30,60-90)
- **Gateway env names** (`baseUrlEnv`, `apiKeyEnv`, optional extra header envs) are named in `gateways.json`; values come from the process environment. [requirement] (docs/development/add-a-gateway.md) [code] (gateway-routing.ts:56-84)
- **Registry data** is generated into `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` and a generated registry; do not hand-edit. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)
- **Per-request state.** `CredentialFailoverState` remembers which provider accounts were refused in one request, and can be seeded with credentials a shared breaker already holds open. [code] (provider-runtime/src/failover.ts:15-57)
- **Persisted routing evidence.** Routing decisions are stored in `table:routing_decision_traces` (migration 0212) and rollout benchmarks in `table:model_rollout_benchmarks`. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md, 'Rollout' section). Not opened in the schema; [unknown] whether names match the migrations.
- **Device stores.** Mobile tracks installed on-device models in `storage/installedModels` (store name not verified). [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/localModelRuntime.ts:6-10)
- **Model catalog hosts.** `provider-hosts.json` feeds the egress allowlist (`REGISTRY_DECLARED_PROVIDER_HOSTS`). [code] (provider-runtime/src/base-url.ts:1,31-34)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
Modes are declared as runtime profiles in `harnesses.json`. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json, runtimeProfiles)

| Profile | Mode | Harness groups | Status in registry |
|---|---|---|---|
| web/cloud-chat | mode:cloud | managed-text, managed-media | implemented |
| desktop/cloud-chat | mode:cloud | managed-text, managed-media | implemented |
| desktop/byok-chat | mode:own-key | byok-text | implemented |
| desktop/local-chat | mode:local | local-text (ollama, lmstudio) | partial |
| mobile/cloud-chat | mode:cloud | managed-text, managed-media | implemented |
| mobile/local-chat | mode:local (on_device) | none | partial |
| cli/byok-chat | mode:own-key | byok-text | implemented |
| cli/managed-chat | mode:cloud | managed-text | implemented |
| cli/local-chat | mode:local | none | partial |
| vscode/byok-chat | mode:own-key | byok-text | unwired |
| vscode/managed-chat | mode:cloud | managed-text | implemented |
| vscode/local-chat | mode:local | none | unwired |
| chrome/managed-chat, chrome/managed-browser-task | mode:cloud | managed-text | implemented |
| chrome/browser-task | mode:local | none | implemented |

- **Trust boundaries.** A Local-to-BYOK move must be an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label. Managed gateway defaults must never apply to Local or strict BYOK. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md; packages/ai/providers/README.md 'What Does Not Belong Here')
- **Local is free of payment.** Local inference needs no paid subscription. [requirement] (task product context). On mobile, the cloud gating described below does not apply to local models. Whether sign-in is required on each app is a separate question: [unknown] from this research.
- **Routing order for managed.** Workspace policy, commercial status, trust mode, harness reachability, lifecycle stage, zero data retention and capabilities admit a route; only then do health, credentials and cost rank them. [requirement] (provider-routing.md, 'Model identity and serving routes')
- **Billing follows the model, cost follows the route.** The user is debited the model's official price; a cheaper host is the company's saving. [requirement] (provider-routing.md)
- **Gateway admission.** Gateway routes ship as `experimental_only` until a reseller agreement is confirmed; that value is refused for managed traffic. [requirement] (add-a-gateway.md) The training opt-out setting refuses gateways whose `trainsOnInputs` is unknown, opt_out or varies_by_route. [requirement] (add-a-gateway.md); enforced in managed failover for every hop. [code] (managed-failover.ts header, 'noTrainingOnly')
- **Plans on web.** Plan-based access to models is checked by `canAccessModel` (`apps/web/lib/model-tiers`) during rotation; a tier-restricted refusal rotates. [code] (managed-failover.ts:60-75, 'model_tier_restricted'). The plan names and quotas live in the subscription system (see SYS-subscription-entitlements, id not verified).
- **Plans on mobile.** The mobile model list takes a `cloudUnlocked` flag and a `subscriptionTier`. A cloud model is `locked` when cloud is not unlocked or when `canAccessCloudModelForTier` refuses the tier for that model. Local models are not gated by these checks. This is mobile-side list logic; it is a separate code path from web's server-side `canAccessModel`. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:180-190,275-306). Whether both paths read one shared entitlement source is [unknown]; the cited code does not show it.

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
- **Classification.** `classifyError` maps any error to a category with `retryable`, `fallbackable`, optional `retryAfterSeconds`. Categories include aborted, api_timeout, rate_limit, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, context_overflow, max_output, tool_validation, invalid_model, invalid_input, unsupported_input, media_too_large, auth, billing_exhausted, quota_exhausted and more. [code] (provider-runtime/src/errors.ts:33-80,817)
- **Money is not auth.** `billing_exhausted` is separate from `auth` so an unfunded account does not look like a bad key and silently push spend onto another paid provider. [code] (errors.ts:58-67; managed-failover.ts:117-140)
- **Retry-After.** A provider-requested wait longer than the ceiling, or longer than the turn's remaining first-token room, ends the retry. [code] (provider-deadlines.ts:198-228)
- **Nothing leaks across attempts.** Rotation happens before the first byte reaches the client, so failed-attempt text cannot appear. After the first chunk the attempt is committed and errors flow out. [code] (provider-deadlines.ts:230-240; managed-failover.ts header)
- **Stream idle.** TS adapters raise `StreamIdleTimeoutError` after the idle window; Rust has `IdleWatchdog` and the CLI sets 300 s. [code] (watchdog.ts; crates/agiworkforce-llm/src/watchdog.rs; apps/cli/src/models/mod.rs:31)
- **Config errors.** A missing key throws `ProviderConfigurationError` naming the env var. A gateway with a missing or off-host base URL throws before any request. [code] (provider-adapter-service.ts:328-345; gateway-routing.ts:56-84)
- **SSRF.** A non-allowlisted base-URL override is ignored with a warning (web) or refused (gateway). [code] (provider-adapter-service.ts:128-146)
- **Rust conformance.** Replay fixtures freeze decode behaviour per dialect and HTTP error classification. [code] (crates/agiworkforce-llm/tests/conformance.rs:1-20)
- **Adapter retries by SDK.** Adapters pass no retry setting to the OpenAI or Anthropic SDK constructors, so any default SDK retry applies underneath web's own retry. Not verified in the SDK source. [inferred]
- **Worked example.** A managed Auto turn gets a 529 on the first route: it retries the same route up to the overload limit within the 40 s first-token budget, then rotates to the next admitted route, even to another model. A pinned model rotates only to another route of the same model. If the error was billing_exhausted it does not rotate (except one Auto exception). [code] (provider-deadlines.ts; managed-failover.ts)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
[proposed] These are my suggestions, not statements of current behaviour.

- One place should own provider endpoints and key variable names for web. Today `SERVER_PROVIDER_CONFIG`, `provider-endpoints.ts`, harness `baseUrl`s and `STATIC_ALLOWED_MANAGED_PROVIDER_HOSTS` repeat the same facts.
- Speech, image and media calls should go through the same adapter contract (or a sibling media contract) so a provider swap needs no edit in route files.
- The Rust CLI should read endpoints and dialect from the generated registry mirror (`crates/agiworkforce-model-registry`) rather than literals, to match the 'no hardcoding' rule. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)
- The `harnesses.json` entry for the mistral harness should either point to a real package or be removed.
- Stale docs should be fixed: the code comment pointing at `services/api-gateway` and the provider-runtime header claim about mobile and the Chrome extension (see outdated_documents).
- Local and BYOK should each have a single documented rule on whether sign-in is needed, tied to the subscription system.
- Mobile's tier gating and web's `canAccessModel` should read one shared entitlement source, so every app follows the one AGI Subscription system. [proposed]

key_facts.fact: Every vendor adapter implements one interface, ProviderAdapter, with catalog() and stream(req, signal); apps depend on it, not on vendor SDKs.

There are 17 leaf provider packages plus a factory: anthropic, deepseek, google, groq, lmstudio, minimax, moonshot, nvidia, ollama, openai, openrouter, perplexity, qwen, vercel-gateway, workers-ai, xai, zhipu.
The factory has 18 adapter ids, including a generic openai_compat id used for protocol routes and gateways. It holds no keys.
Adapters do not retry. Retry runs at the stream-start seam in web, and rotation runs above it in managed-failover.ts.
Same-route retry allows 2 attempts for most retryable classes and 3 for server_overload; auth and context_overflow are never retried on the same route.
Timeouts: turn first-token budget 40 s, per-provider first-token deadline 25 s, function limit 300 s, TS stream idle default 90 s, CLI stream idle 300 s.

Rotation categories: connection, server_error, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, api_timeout, rate_limit, quota_exhausted, empty_response, unsupported_input. Never rotated: billing_exhausted, safety, content_blocked.
Only Auto may switch models during failover; a named model rotates only across routes of the same model.
Once a provider has minted tool-call ids in a turn (step 2 onward) the turn stays on that provider.
Billing exhaustion is classified separately from auth so unfunded accounts do not rotate onto another paid provider; one Auto-only exception exists.
Gateway routes are declarative (gateways.json plus a harness gatewayId) and off unless AGI_ROUTING_GATEWAY_ROUTES=1; the flag is enforced at admission and at dispatch.
Nine gateway definitions exist in the catalog; openrouter_via_gateway is deliberately not wired.
Base URL overrides are accepted only for allowlisted hosts, https only (http for localhost and 127.0.0.1); the allowlist is a static list plus registry-declared hosts.
Web keeps keys in environment variables and builds adapters server-side; unconfigured providers throw ProviderConfigurationError naming the variable.
Perplexity is the search-grounded chat provider (citations on the last chunk), and the only web-search provider entry is Perplexity Search.
Image generation uses OpenAI and Google by direct fetch, defaulting to Google if its key exists, else OpenAI; a Stability branch exists but throws unsupported.
Speech to text and text to speech are OpenAI by direct fetch; the transcription route requires the voice_transcription slot to resolve to an OpenAI model.
Rust engine agiworkforce-llm speaks five dialects (Anthropic, Gemini, OllamaNative, OpenAiResponses, OpenAiCompat), never reads keys itself, and redacts auth in Debug output.
The CLI hard-codes endpoint URLs for Anthropic, Gemini and pre-registered OpenAI-compatible providers in Rust.
Mobile on-device inference uses @agiworkforce/local-llm with llama.rn, ExecuTorch and system models, not the TS provider packages.

Mobile cloud models are gated by a cloudUnlocked flag and the subscription tier (canAccessCloudModelForTier); a cloud model is 'locked' otherwise. Local models are not gated by these checks. This is mobile-side list logic, separate from web's server-side canAccessModel.

Mobile also lists provider-funded Free quota chat models: surface cloud_managed, runtimeLabel 'Provider-funded Free', described as promotional quota, shown only when cloud is unlocked. They are cloud calls, not on-device.
Runtime profiles mark vscode/byok-chat and vscode/local-chat unwired, and the desktop, mobile and CLI local profiles partial.
A mistral harness is declared in the registry but names a nonexistent package, and web ADAPTER_PROVIDERS has no mistral entry.
Apps may not import provider leaf internals; multi-provider code uses the factory. Routing decisions belong to packages/ai/routing.

doc.summary: Local inference runs a model on the user's device. It works on Mobile (Apple and Google system models, plus downloaded ExecuTorch and llama.rn models), and in the CLI and VS Code through Ollama and LM Studio. Public Desktop and Web refuse it, and the Chrome extension has none (it reports localModels false). No account or plan is needed on Mobile or the CLI. Mobile Local chats are plain text. They have no tools or web search and are not synced. Chat content never goes to AGI servers, but Mobile Local mode still lets a few signed-in account controls (terms, age check, account deletion, data export) reach AGI servers, and it allows direct BYOK provider hosts.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
Local inference means the model answers on the user's own machine. The prompt, the files and the answer are not sent to AGI servers or to an outside model provider. It is the "Local" trust boundary, one of three. The others are BYOK (bring your own key) and Managed Cloud. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:111, docs/product/requirements.md:478-492)

Why it exists:
- Local mode must need no AGI account and no hidden cloud call. It must fail closed: if a feature needs remote compute, the app says so and offers a fork. It must not route silently. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492)
- Local and BYOK must stay useful without paying AGI. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:84)
- The brief for this page adds that local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription. Account or sign-in is a separate question from payment.

**Execution boundary in one line.** Local chat on Mobile runs entirely on the device. Chat content, files and telemetry are not sent to AGI servers. The network is used for the one-time model download from a third-party host, and the egress guard also lets through a short list of signed-in account controls (see Rules) and direct BYOK provider hosts. In the CLI and VS Code, a model server on the same computer does the work. Public Desktop (Electron) has no Local chat at all. The Chrome extension has no local inference. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:24-35, :317-327; see Rules and Differences below)

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline (the Cloud turn path), and any page on AGI Subscription entitlements.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Mobile (surface:mobile, mode:local)

**Four runtimes in three tiers.** The shared package `@agiworkforce/local-llm` picks the tier at send time. [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts:105-146, packages/platform/local-llm/src/types.ts:1-3)

| Tier | Runtime | What it is | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `foundation_models` (iOS) | The Apple system model, already in the OS. No download. | Native module reports it available. The Swift code checks iOS 26 or newer. [code] (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIFoundationModels.swift:22-23) |
| 1 | `aicore` (Android) | The Google system model, reached through the ML Kit GenAI Prompt API. No download. | Native module reports available. [code] (apps/mobile/native/android/AGICoreModule.kt:10-22) |
| 2 | `executorch` | Model files (`.pte`) run by react-native-executorch. | Device RAM at least 3500 MB, or RAM unknown and the module is present. [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/capabilities.ts:4, :75-76) |
| 3 | `llama_rn` | A GGUF file run by llama.rn. | Always marked available. Needs a model path. [code] (capabilities.ts:77, selector.ts:127-129) |

Selection order in `localGenerate`: it refuses if the device is thermally throttled. Then it uses Tier 1 when the chosen model is the system model. Then Tier 2 when the model has an ExecuTorch preset. If Tier 2 throws, it falls back to Tier 3 when a file path exists. Otherwise it fails with "No local model is ready. Download a local model first, or join AGI Cloud when it is available." [code] (selector.ts:105-146)

**Which models can be picked.** The picker lists catalog entries marked `shipsInV1`, and filters again by what the platform can run. The catalog is a hand-written list in `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts`, not the generated model catalog. Today four entries ship: a default text model ("AGI Standard"), a small lite model ("AGI Lite"), the Apple system model and the Google system model. The vision and other entries have `shipsInV1: false`, so they are not selectable on Mobile. [code] (catalog.ts:34-35, :152-153, :178-179, :197-198, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:102-111, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/catalogSelectability.ts:20-28). For exact model names and sizes read `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts`. Do not copy them from this page.

**What a person must do first.**
1. Pass the age gate. It runs before everything, including Local Mode. The answer is held on the device, from an OS age range or a typed age. [code] (apps/mobile/app/index.tsx:12-14, apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/ageGate.ts:98-106, apps/mobile/__tests__/age-gate-guards-cloud-not-local.test.ts:8-24)
2. Finish onboarding. It shows a short first-run disclosure to accept, with managed cloud off. Then it asks for a name and work description (optional), detects the device tier, and offers a model. The person can skip the download and go to chat. [code] (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:299-312, :395-398)
3. Download a model, unless they use a system model. The default is a multi-GB download. The Apple and Google system models need no download, but only work where the OS offers them. [code] (service.ts:168, installStore.ts:152-176)
4. Without a ready model the chat tab shows "Download a model to chat" or "No compatible local models", and the send is stopped. [code] (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:721-745, :1494)

**How a download works.** [code] (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts)
- ExecuTorch models: `tier2LoadModel` fetches the model, tokenizer and tokenizer config through `react-native-executorch-expo-resource-fetcher`. The source URLs are Hugging Face addresses in the catalog. Files land in `<documents>/react-native-executorch/`. (installStore.ts:497-524, catalog.ts:5-6, modelStoragePaths.ts:4)
- GGUF models: `downloadModel` requires HTTPS, a 64-hex SHA-256, and a safe file size. It resumes from a `.partial` file, then checks the SHA-256 in chunks. Files land in `<documents>/models/<id>/model.gguf`. (modelDownload.ts:97-143, :293-330)
- Before the first byte: the device must be online, and on Wi-Fi unless the person turned on "Download over cellular". Free disk must cover the size plus 256 MB. (modelDownload.ts:190-230, installStore.ts:379, :521)
- After: model folders are excluded from iCloud and device backup, and kept in Documents so the OS does not purge them. (modelDownload.ts:80-91)
- Each install is recorded in the `installed_models` table of the on-device encrypted database. (storage/migrations.ts:49-60, storage/db.ts:25)
- On startup, records whose files are gone are dropped so the app offers Download again. (services/executorchModels.ts:81-100)

**A Local turn.** In `sendMessage`, the mode comes from the conversation, or from the model id (cloud-managed ids mean cloud, everything else is local). A Local chat refuses cloud models, and a cloud chat refuses local models. It never switches silently. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2255-2282, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/conversationMode.ts:7-9)
The Local branch then:
- builds the history, adds the local system prompt, resolves the model reference, and calls `localGenerate` with an abort signal; (chatExecutionStore.ts:3036-3098)
- streams tokens, splits out any thinking tags, records speed and memory, and commits the answer into the local on-device store; (chatExecutionStore.ts:3135-3230)
- returns before any cloud code (consent, entitlements, web search, tools, sync) runs. (chatExecutionStore.ts:3232-3236 vs :2374-2390)

### CLI (surface:cli, mode:local)
The CLI does not download models. It probes servers the person already runs: Ollama at `http://localhost:11434` and LM Studio at `http://localhost:1234/v1`, or a configured base URL. It lists installed models with `agi models scan` and checks a model is installed before a turn. [code] (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:6-8, :54-73, :244-330, apps/web/app/local/page.tsx:25-31) Run it with `agi --provider ollama --model <model>`. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:195-196)
First-run onboarding has "Local model, no account needed". It never shows the cloud login in that path. [code] (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:264, :387, :839-851)
The session privacy mode is `Local`, and its description says no prompt, chat or file context should leave the device. [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:255-290)

### VS Code (surface:vscode, mode:local)
The extension has no model runtime of its own. It starts the local `agi app-server` from the AGI CLI and asks it for local models, then shows them in an "On this device" group. The CLI must be installed, and the workspace must be trusted. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:714-745, src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2034-2060, README.md:23-38)

### Desktop (surface:desktop)
Public Desktop is the Electron shell and is Cloud-only for chat. The dispatcher returns `unsupported-platform` for every command in `LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS` before permission handling, and the device profile reports `localModels: false`. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3237-3244, :3365-3367, :2298, packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:3-10) A Desktop coding session runs the bundled CLI, which can use a local model. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3239-3241, docs/architecture/desktop.md:113-115)

### Chrome extension (surface:chrome)
No local inference. Its device heartbeat to the cloud bridge sends `capabilities.localModels: false`. The words "ollama" and "lmstudio" in its side panel are only provider icon ids. [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39, apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10938, :10943)
