sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
**Mobile.**
- Local conversations and messages live in the on-device SQLite database `agi_mobile.db`. It uses a SQLCipher key kept under the storage id `agi_sqlcipher_db_key_v1`. [code] (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:22-25)
- A Local chat session is labelled `executionAuthority: local_device`, `storageScope: local_device`, `syncPolicy.syncEligible: false`. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/sessionLabeling.ts:66-80)
- Cloud sync is only queued when the mode is cloud. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2950-2957)
- Table `installed_models` columns: id, display_name, runtime (`local` or `cloud`), format (`gguf`, `safetensors`, `mlx`, `onnx`, `pte`), size_bytes, sha256, local_path, installed_at, last_used_at, capabilities. [code] (storage/migrations.ts:49-60, storage/installedModels.ts:5-12)
- The store `useModelInstallStore` persists `allowCellularDownloads`, which defaults to false. The "Download over cellular" choice is shown in onboarding and in Settings, Storage. [code] (installStore.ts:379, :383, modelDownload.ts:192)
- Model files: `<documents>/models/<safe-id>/model.gguf` and `<documents>/react-native-executorch/`. Both are excluded from backup. [code] (modelStoragePaths.ts:3-5, modelDownload.ts:79-91, :102-105)
- Memory, personalization and past-chat context for Local chats come from the local settings store and on-device memory. They are not the account memory. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2789-2820, apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/pastChatContext.ts:117-124)
- "Delete all local chats" appears in Data controls when the app mode is Local. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:449-470)

**Chat turn metadata** saved on the answer: `localMode`, `localModelId`, `localRuntime`, `localModelName`, tokens per second. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:3178-3194)

**CLI.** Local-boundary memory goes to a separate file, so Local content never mixes with BYOK or Managed memory. [code] (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:35-42) Local base URLs are read from the CLI config (`config.base_url`). [code] (local_models.rs:55-67)

**Desktop and Web.** No local model state is stored. The unused web types `LocalModelSettings.baseUrls` are only normalised, with loopback required. [code] (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:150-165)

**Server-side.** A Local Mobile chat writes nothing to AGI tables. The CLI device heartbeat records `localModels` in table:device_registrations column `local_models_available`, but the CLI only sends it in Managed mode. The Chrome extension also sends a heartbeat, always with `localModels: false`. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0207_device_registrations.sql:40, apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:64-80, apps/cli/src/device_registry.rs:172-177, apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-373, apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Account / sign-in, by surface.** This is separate from payment.

| Surface | Account needed for Local chat? | Where the code says so |
|---|---|---|
| surface:mobile | No. A signed-out user reaches the app. Routing only forces onboarding and the age gate. A signed-out user is not sent to sign-in unless a session just ended. | rootRouting.ts:44-60 [code] |
| surface:cli | No. Local first run skips cloud login. The README says Local mode and BYOK need no plan. | onboarding.rs:839-851; README.md:335-337 [code] |
| surface:vscode | No. An AGI Cloud account is only for Managed Cloud and cloud extras. The CLI does the local work. | README.md:35-38 [code] |
| surface:desktop | Not applicable. Local chat is not offered. Sign-in (Clerk) is needed for the Cloud chat that Desktop does offer. | docs/architecture/desktop-local-runtime.md:11-17 [requirement], dispatcher.ts:3365-3367 [code] |
| surface:web | No local inference. | no code found [inferred] |
| surface:chrome | No local inference. Heartbeat reports `localModels: false`. | deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39 [code] |

**Payment / plan.** No plan, entitlement or quota check sits on the Mobile Local branch. The entitlement call `ensureCloudEntitlementsReadyForRequest` and the consent call `ensureCloudSendConsent` are in the cloud branch only. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2374-2390, :3036-3232) The mobile model list contains no plan lock for local models. A model is `locked` only for an environment or cloud tier reason, and local entries never get one. [code] (service.ts:85-95, :168) The CLI states that Local needs no plan. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:335-337) The "Free plan" has no bearing on Mobile Local. Subscription accounting is therefore not applied to Local turns. No local usage is reported to an AGI Subscription system. [inferred] from the absence of any usage call in the Local branch.

One payment-linked rule exists in Web code: the composer hides the "Local models" row when the user's plan is Free (`!freePlan && localModels.available`). It is only reachable on a host whose shell is `tauri` (see Differences). [code] (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:1043, :1766, packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:690-692) This conflicts with the requirement that local inference is free of any paid subscription. See Gaps.

**Trust-boundary rules.**
- A Local chat never takes cloud models, and a cloud chat never takes local models. Mobile gives an error and asks for a separate chat. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2263-2282)
- **Mobile egress guard in Local mode.** The guard says Local Mode is "on-device + BYOK only" and blocks calls to our managed-cloud hosts before any network I/O. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:24-35, :300-327) It lets four kinds of request through:
  - A content report the user chose to send (POST to the report path only), except while a withdrawal is in progress.
  - Signed-in account controls (`authControl`): terms acceptance, the age check that opens Cloud, account deletion status, scheduling and cancellation, the identity check for deletion only, and the data export. The code comment says none carries chat content and these rights must not depend on sharing with AI providers. The age check must pass before Cloud opens, so blocking it would keep Cloud shut. Paths and methods are listed in `SIGNED_IN_ACCOUNT_CONTROLS`, and some requests must match a body rule (for example the age check carries only age evidence). A bearer token is required (per the finding checked at egressGuard.ts:210-244; the bearer test itself was not re-read).
  - Withdrawal controls (`withdrawalControl`): list schedules, set one inactive, list unfinished runs, pause a run, revoke the Ask from Siri token. Each only stops work.
  - Direct-to-provider BYOK hosts and other non-AGI hosts, passed on to `secureFetch`.
  So a Local-mode phone can still contact AGI servers for these account controls when the person is signed in and uses them. It does not send chat content, files or telemetry. [code] (egressGuard.ts:210-244, :300-327)
- CLI: Local, BYOK and Managed are session privacy modes. A Local session refuses cloud calls (`CloudError::NotManaged`), and sub-agents get no off-device route. [code] (cloud/client.rs:368-373, apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:39-45)
- CLI and Rust base URLs for local servers must be loopback. Non-loopback is shown as `blocked`. [code] (local_models.rs:104-110, :152-155, apps/web/app/local/page.tsx:34 says the same in marketing)
- TypeScript contract: a local server URL must be on this machine, or the request is refused. [code] (inference.ts:171-205)
- Local to BYOK or Cloud is a fork, not a mode flip. The original Local thread stays Local. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:115, docs/product/suite.md:62)
- VS Code: a Local default model is never replaced by a cloud model. Cloud-only commands send nothing and say so. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/cloudModelBoundary.ts:12-47)

**Features in Mobile Local mode.**

| Feature | Works? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Streaming text chat, with thinking text split out | Yes | chatExecutionStore.ts:3052-3115 [code] |
| Local system prompt | Yes | stores/chat/localSystemPrompt.ts:3-12 [code] |
| Chat mode and style prompts | Yes (added to history) | chatExecutionStore.ts:2774-2780 [code] |
| Projects: instructions and sources | Yes, local projects | chatExecutionStore.ts:2758-2772 [code] |
| Memory, personalization, past-chat context | Yes, from device stores | chatExecutionStore.ts:2789-2822 [code] |
| Image attachments | Text only: on-device OCR text goes in. The model cannot see pixels. | chatExecutionStore.ts:1241-1262 [code] |
| Document attachments | Added as context; kept on the device | chatExecutionStore.ts:2471-2473, :2685-2705 [code]; whether parsing is fully on-device is [unknown] |
| Vision models | Not selectable in v1 | catalog.ts shipsInV1 false [code] |
| Tools, connectors, web search, code execution | No. The Local branch returns before they run. Settings show "Cloud only" for the account switches. | chatExecutionStore.ts:3232-3236; capabilities/index.tsx:318 [code] |
| Image and video generation | No, `requires_cloud` | resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:252, resolveMobileVideoGenerationRequest.ts:107 [code] |
| Live voice | No, turn based only | liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25 [code] |
| Cloud sync and account history | No | sessionLabeling.ts:66-80 [code] |
| Share preview | Local chats can be previewed from the local store | share-preview/index.tsx:107-117 [code] |

Auto model modes also work in Local: they pick between installed models and the system model by tier. [code] (localModelRuntime.ts:44-85)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
**Mobile.**

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No model downloaded | Send is stopped. The tab shows "Download a model to chat" and offers Models. (chat.tsx:721-745, :1494) |
| Selected model gone from disk | Record is dropped, so the model shows Download again. If the chat still points at it: "This Local Mode chat uses a model that is no longer available on this device." (executorchModels.ts:81-100, chatExecutionStore.ts:1293-1294) |
| Offline at download | `offline` error; "Reconnect and try again." (modelDownload.ts:190-197) |
| Cellular without consent | `wifi_required` error naming "Settings, Storage, Download over cellular". (modelDownload.ts:198-208) |
| Not enough disk | `storage_full`, with the needed and free sizes. Needs the file size plus 256 MB. (modelDownload.ts:216-229) |
| Bad checksum | `ChecksumMismatchError` / `checksum_mismatch`. (modelDownload.ts:19-25, imports) |
| Device under 3.5 GB RAM | ExecuTorch and vision models are `unavailable` or `locked`: "This device cannot run this on-device model." (installStore.ts:111-132) |
| Device too hot | `Device is thermally throttled, inference paused.` (selector.ts:43, :113) |
| Out of memory | "This device ran out of memory for the on-device model. Close other apps, or choose a smaller model." (chatExecutionStore.ts:1413-1414) |
| System model off or still preparing | Marked unavailable for this session and the chat moves to a ready model. (localModelRuntime.ts:170-188, installStore.ts:262-290) |
| ExecuTorch fails | Falls back to llama.rn if a GGUF path exists; otherwise the error is thrown. (selector.ts:118-142) |
| Empty reply | "The local model returned an empty response. Try again with a shorter prompt." (chatExecutionStore.ts:3124-3126) |
| Stop pressed | Abort signal reaches the runtime; the turn ends without a committed answer. (chatExecutionStore.ts:3089-3118, :3125) |
| Our cloud host called in Local mode (not on the allow list) | `EgressBlockedError` code `EGRESS_BLOCKED_LOCAL_MODE`, thrown before any network I/O. (egressGuard.ts:24-35, :300-327) |

Removal of a model while it is answering is refused with "This model is replying now. Try again when it finishes." [code] (modelDownload.ts:69-76)

**CLI.** An unreachable server reports `not reachable ... Start Ollama` or `Start the local server and load a model`. A model not installed gives the list of what is installed, and tells the user to run `agi models scan`. Several providers holding the same model name give an error asking the user to pick a provider. [code] (local_models.rs:171-206, :294-330, :114-139)

**Desktop.** Any local-inference command gets `unsupported-platform` with the text that Desktop answers every conversation in the cloud. [code] (dispatcher.ts:3242, :3365-3367)

**VS Code.** With no local model: the picker says "No local models found. Start Ollama or LM Studio and load a model". A cloud-only utility with a Local default sends nothing and says so. [code] (ChatStateManager.ts:2047-2055, cloudModelBoundary.ts:34-47)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are established requirements, not statements about the code. Where code differs, the Gaps section says so.

- Local needs no AGI account, keeps storage on the device, makes no hidden cloud call, and fails closed when a feature needs remote compute. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492)
- Local and BYOK stay useful without paying AGI. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:84)
- A Local thread stays Local. Crossing to BYOK or Cloud is a visible fork with consent. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:115, docs/product/suite.md:55-62)
- A local model that cannot call tools should have tool use hidden or disabled for that route. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:299)
- Brief for this page: local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription. Sign-in is a separate question. [requirement] (task brief; no repository document located that states "desktop" in this sentence)
- Competitor behaviour was not examined for this page. [unknown]

[proposed] If Desktop is meant to offer Local chat, it needs a decision record that replaces D-2026-09-15-04. Then a real handler for the six commands is needed, with no `!freePlan` gate on the web row. Until then, product copy must say Desktop reaches local models only through coding sessions.

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Implementation status (is the code there and connected) is kept apart from verification status (has anyone run it). Nothing here was run by me. I did not run the repository's tests, apps or builds.

| # | Gap | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Desktop vs requirement.** The brief says local inference on desktop is free of a paid subscription. Public Desktop (Electron) has no Local chat. It is refused by design in the dispatcher, per founder decision D-2026-09-15-04. Local models on Desktop exist only through a coding session that runs the bundled CLI. | [code] (dispatcher.ts:3237-3244, :3365-3367), [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-86) |
| 2 | **Web local-chat code with no backend.** The composer, the `useLocalModels` hook, `runLocalTurn` and the six command names exist, but no handler for them was found in the Tauri Rust code or Electron. The `hostHasLocalMode` gate lets only a `tauri` shell through. | [code] and [inferred] (see Differences) |
| 3 | **Free-plan gate in that Web code.** `!freePlan && localModels.available` hides the Local row for Free-plan users. If a host ever supports it, this ties Local to a paid plan. | [code] (ComposerFooter.tsx:1043, :1766) |
| 4 | **No checksum for ExecuTorch downloads in app code.** The installed record stores `sha256: null` and delegates the fetch to the library. Only GGUF downloads are verified by the app. | [code] (installStore.ts:187-205, modelDownload.ts:97-107) |
| 5 | **Catalog is not generated.** AGENTS.md says model IDs live only in the generated catalog. The local on-device catalog is a hand-written TypeScript list with URLs and hashes. Whether the model-id guards exempt it was not checked. | [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts), [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4) |
| 6 | **Local text chats only.** Tool use, web search, vision and live voice are not available in Mobile Local. Local image text is OCR only. | [code] (see Rules) |
| 7 | **No usage or entitlement accounting for Local turns.** Correct for the free requirement, but nothing shows Local usage to the AGI Subscription system. | [inferred] |
| 8 | **`ollama-manifest.json` does not match the CLI.** See outdated documents. | [code] |
| 9 | **Mobile v1 vision models are not shippable.** `qwen`-family vision entries have `shipsInV1: false`, so the premium Auto profile falls back to the default text model. | [code] (catalog.ts:59-60, localModelRuntime.ts:57-62) |
| 10 | **Mobile Local mode is not fully offline from AGI.** The requirement says Local makes no hidden cloud call. The guard lets signed-in account controls (terms, age check, account deletion, scheduling, step-up, data export) reach AGI servers, and allows direct BYOK provider hosts. These are user-driven and carry no chat content by the code's own comment, so this is a narrow, visible exception rather than a hidden chat route. Whether product copy and the first-run disclosure state it was not checked. | [code] (egressGuard.ts:24-35, :210-244, :300-327), [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492) |
| 11 | **Verification.** I found test files for these paths (listed in How to verify) but I did not run them, and found no document recording a real device run of local chat. | [unknown] |

key_facts.fact: Public Desktop (Electron) refuses every local-inference command with unsupported-platform and reports localModels false; its chat is Cloud-only.
The six refused commands are local_model_servers, local_model_list, local_chat_start, local_chat_cancel, local_model_settings_read and local_model_settings_write.
Desktop coding sessions run the bundled CLI, which can use a local model; this is the only way local models reach public Desktop.
Mobile has four local runtime names: foundation_models (Apple), aicore (Google), executorch, and llama_rn, grouped into tiers 1, 2 and 3.
ExecuTorch (tier 2) needs at least 3500 MB RAM, or unknown RAM with the module present; llama.rn (tier 3) is always marked available.
Four catalog entries ship on Mobile v1 (default text, lite text, Apple system model, Google system model); vision entries are not shippable.
The on-device model catalog is a hand-written TypeScript list, not the generated model catalog.
Mobile model downloads come from Hugging Face over HTTPS; GGUF files are SHA-256 verified, resumable, Wi-Fi only by default, and need free disk of file size plus 256 MB.
ExecuTorch downloads are fetched by the react-native-executorch resource fetcher; the app records sha256 null for them, so it does not verify a checksum itself.

Model files are stored under documents/models/<id>/model.gguf and documents/react-native-executorch/, excluded from backup; installs are recorded in the installed_models table of the on-device encrypted SQLite database.
Mobile Local chat does not require sign-in: routing sends a signed-out user to the app after the age gate and onboarding, and the Local send branch has no auth check.
The age gate runs before everything on Mobile including Local Mode, and the answer is held on the device.
Mobile Local turns carry no plan, entitlement or consent check; those calls are in the cloud branch only.
A Mobile Local chat refuses cloud models and a cloud chat refuses local models, with an error asking for a separate chat.
Mobile Local branch returns before tools, web search, connectors and sync; account switches show 'Cloud only'; image/video generation and live voice need cloud.
On Mobile Local, image attachments become on-device OCR text only; the model cannot see pixels.

The mobile egress guard describes Local Mode as 'on-device + BYOK only' and throws EgressBlockedError (EGRESS_BLOCKED_LOCAL_MODE) for our managed-cloud hosts before any network I/O, except for an allow list.

In Mobile Local mode the guard still allows signed-in account controls to AGI servers: terms acceptance, the age check that opens Cloud, account deletion status, scheduling and cancellation, the deletion identity check, and data export. The guard comment says none carries chat content. It also allows a user-sent content report, withdrawal controls, and direct BYOK provider hosts.
Local Mobile sessions are labelled local_device storage with syncEligible false; cloud sync is queued only in cloud mode.
The CLI supports exactly two local runtimes, Ollama (default http://localhost:11434) and LM Studio (default http://localhost:1234/v1); it discovers models but does not download them.
The CLI Local first run needs no account and never shows cloud login; README states Local mode and BYOK need no plan.
CLI Local sessions refuse cloud calls (CloudClient::admit allows Managed only), and the device heartbeat only runs for Managed, so Local does not report to AGI servers.
VS Code has no model runtime of its own; it asks the CLI app-server for local models and shows an 'On this device' group; an AGI Cloud account is not required for Local.
VS Code never swaps a Local default model for a cloud model; Code Review, Suggest Terminal Command and inline completions run only on AGI Cloud and send nothing when a Local model is selected.

The Chrome extension has no local inference. Its device heartbeat to the cloud bridge always sends capabilities.localModels false, and the only 'ollama' and 'lmstudio' strings in its side panel are provider icon ids.
Web has local-chat UI and client code gated to a host whose shell is tauri; no handler for the six local-inference commands was found in Rust or Electron, so the path appears to have no backend.
The Web composer hides the Local models row for Free-plan users (!freePlan && localModels.available), a plan-linked rule in a path that is not reachable on Electron.
The shared local-inference contract requires loopback base URLs, refuses attachments, and hides models under 1B parameters.
Public marketing says Local runs in the CLI with Ollama and LM Studio, costs $0 and needs no account.
Requirement: Local mode needs no AGI account, keeps storage local, makes no hidden cloud call and fails closed.

pages.title: Execution boundaries: Local, own key, Cloud

doc.summary: The product has three execution modes. Local runs on the device. Own key sends requests straight to the user's provider. Cloud goes through AGI servers, which call providers, and is the only metered, synced path. One shared host list, per-app egress guards, a mobile consent record and CI proofs enforce the boundary. Subscription rules attach to Cloud capabilities only, and they are not one uniform check: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome need the Free-and-up chat capability, while CLI and VS Code need a Pro-tier capability. The Electron Desktop refuses on-device inference by a recorded decision. The desktop renderer guard fails open for a host it cannot parse. Two shared contract functions are not called directly by product code (one has no caller; the other has one wrapper caller).

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
AGI Workforce can answer a request in three separate ways. Each one has its own promise about where the data goes. This page maps those ways, says which capability works in which one, and says what stops data crossing from one to the next.

| Mode | Short meaning | Where inference runs | Who pays for inference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:local | On-device or loopback model. Nothing leaves the device. | The phone (mobile), or a model server on the same machine such as Ollama or LM Studio (CLI, retained Tauri build) | Nobody. No plan check was found on the mobile Local path. |
| mode:own-key | Bring your own key (BYOK). The device calls the user's own provider directly. | An outside provider, with the user's key | The user, at the provider |
| mode:cloud | AGI-managed access. The device calls AGI servers, which call providers. | AGI servers, then outside providers | AGI, metered against the account's plan |

Why it exists:

- AGENTS.md section 6 says Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries (a line data must not cross without permission). Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or Cloud. A Local-to-BYOK move must be an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)
- The product requirement says Local is free of any paid subscription, and that account or sign-in requirements are a separate question from payment. [requirement] (task brief; docs/product/requirements.md:478-486 says Local needs no AGI account)
- A guard fails closed. If the app cannot tell which mode it is in, it must treat the request as Local and block our-cloud egress. [code] (packages/contracts/trust-boundaries/src/egress-policy.ts:5-10). One exception is recorded under Gaps: the desktop renderer guard does not block a target whose host it cannot parse.

Vocabulary:

- **Egress** means data leaving the device.
- **Our-cloud host** means a host name owned by AGI infrastructure: the web app, Vercel, Neon database, Clerk sign-in.
- **Provider label** means the visible name of the outside provider that will receive data.
- **Entitlement** means what the account's plan allows.

Plan names. The code tier names are free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise, plus the zero-price tiers local-only and byok. The labels shown to people are Basic for basic, Premium for pro, Max for max and Ultra for max_15x. This page writes the label and, where a rule is stated, the code tier set. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-16, 166-232, 332-341)

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline, SYS-subscription-entitlements (names assumed from the brief; not opened).

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. The three modes are not the same on every app

The policy table is `docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:36-45`. It says what each app is allowed to offer. The harness catalog says what is implemented. They differ in places.

| App | mode:local | mode:own-key | mode:cloud | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| surface:mobile | Yes, on-device model (partial in the harness catalog) | No. The remote-chat gate accepts a `byokKeys` flag but never reads it | Yes, after sign-in and provider consent. A `v1LocalOnly` build flag exists that blocks Cloud without an explicit unlock; no released build sets it | [code] (apps/mobile/services/remoteChatGate.ts:3-14; packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json, profile mobile/local-chat) |
| surface:web | Code paths exist for `local:` model ids and a Local-to-BYOK fork. Policy says Web has neither. Reachable in a plain browser: [unknown] | Same as left | Yes | [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:55-65; apps/web/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts:181-239); [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:38) |
| surface:desktop (public Electron shell) | Refused. The shell rejects every local-inference command. The code names decision D-2026-09-15-04 (chat is Cloud-only) as the reason; local coding reaches local models only through the bundled CLI | Not offered for chat | Yes. It loads the hosted web app | [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3235-3244, 3366-3367) |
| surface:desktop (retained internal Tauri build) | Partial | Implemented, with a Local-to-BYOK fork | Yes | [code] (harnesses.json profiles desktop/local-chat, desktop/byok-chat; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/llm.rs:1211-1215). AGENTS.md section 5 says Tauri is internal code, not the public Desktop. |
| surface:cli | Partial. Models served on loopback | Implemented | Implemented; Cloud models need Premium (pro tier set) or higher | [code] (harnesses.json cli profiles; apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:5-6; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:925-960) |
| surface:vscode | Unwired | Unwired | Implemented | [code] (harnesses.json vscode profiles) |
| surface:chrome | Policy says no. A local `chrome/browser-task` profile exists | No | Yes | [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:45); [code] (harnesses.json chrome profiles) |

### 2. Which mode a request is in

- **Mobile.** One persisted value, `appMode`, is `local` or `cloud`. Default is `local`. Every write passes one admission function, so the value cannot become `cloud` unless the signed-in account's provider-sharing permission is current. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts:17-51, 60-66; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/cloudModeDoor.ts:94-102)
- **Desktop (Tauri renderer).** `useAppModeStore` holds `local` or `cloud`. `selectPrivacyMode` maps `local` to the `local` privacy mode and everything else to `managed`. The guard treats anything not `managed` as private, and an exception while reading it also counts as private. A browser build with no Tauri forces `cloud`. [code] (apps/desktop/src/stores/appModeStore.ts:28-33, 45, 104-106; apps/desktop/src/stores/privacyBoundary.ts:3-8)
- **Server.** Each provider call is classified by `trustModeContract(mode)`: where content rests, whose key pays, what may serve as fallback. An unreadable mode is treated as the strictest mode. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/trust-mode-contract.ts:50-80; apps/web/lib/server/trust-boundary-crossing.ts:90-100)
- **A conversation keeps its mode.** On mobile, a Local conversation refuses Cloud models and a Cloud conversation refuses local models, with a message telling the person to start a separate chat. [code] (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2285)

The shared contract names the toggle as two values, `local` and `cloud`. BYOK is a sub-mode of the local position, not a third toggle value. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/sessions/execution-profile.ts:1-20)

### 3. The egress guard

The guard is a replacement for `fetch`. It reads the mode, looks at the host, and throws before any network call when the rule says no.

1. One shared, platform-free list of our-cloud hosts and one matcher live in `@agiworkforce/trust-boundaries`. The list holds the web domain, the Vercel domain, the Neon domain and four Clerk domains. Matching is by suffix, ignores case and ignores a trailing dot. [code] (packages/contracts/trust-boundaries/src/egress-policy.ts:32-64)
2. BYOK provider hosts are deliberately absent from the list, so a direct call to the user's own provider is never blocked. [code] (egress-policy.ts:25-29)
3. **Desktop guard.** In private mode it extracts the host; if the host is on the list it throws `EgressBlockedError`; otherwise it calls `fetch`. It fails open when the host cannot be parsed: `extractHost` returns null on a parse error (for example a relative URL), and the guard throws only for a non-null host on the list. A relative-path request in private mode is therefore not blocked by this guard. [code] (apps/desktop/src/lib/egressGuard.ts:23-45, 56-67)
4. **Mobile guard.** It treats Cloud as open only when `appMode` is `cloud` and the account's provider consent is current. Otherwise it blocks any our-cloud host (the shared list plus the hosts from the configured API and signalling URLs) before network I/O, except exact carve-outs. Reading either mode fails closed to Local. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:72-126, 336-357)

   | Carve-out in Local mode | What it allows | Conditions |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Signed-in account controls | Terms acceptance, age-eligibility check, account deletion status and deletion, cancel-deletion schedule, identity step-up for deletion only, data export | Exact API origin, a Bearer token, an allowed method and path, no query string; some fix the body (egressGuard.ts:215-253) |
   | Withdrawal controls | List schedules, set one inactive, list unfinished runs, pause one run, revoke the Ask from Siri token | Bearer token, fixed body and limited query keys (egressGuard.ts:280-303) |
   | Content report | One POST the person chose to send | Its own Send tap, no query, not while a withdrawal is in progress (egressGuard.ts:136, 193-201, 343-347) |

   Sign-in and session refresh do not pass through this guard. They run through the auth SDK, so they reach the sign-in hosts in either mode. [code] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:28 states this; egressGuard.ts has no sign-in path)
5. All mobile API calls go through `apiFetch`, which calls `guardedFetch`. Product analytics goes through it too, and is switched on only in Cloud. [code] (apps/mobile/services/api.ts:329-342; apps/mobile/services/productAnalytics.ts:30-35)

### 4. The consent step into Cloud on mobile

- Entering Cloud triggers a native alert titled "Share with AI providers?". It names every provider the app can route to and offers Allow, Not now and Details. Details opens the provider list page and then asks again. [code] (apps/mobile/services/providerConsent.ts:81-90, 270-287)
- Allow writes a record under `agi:cloud-provider-consent:v1` holding the account owner id, the provider ids covered, the time and the surface. [code] (providerConsent.ts:58-62, 224-244)
- The consent counts as current only if it belongs to the signed-in account, covers every provider now in the list (a new provider means the question is asked again), and no withdrawal is in progress. [code] (providerConsent.ts:208-217)
- Declining leaves the app in Local. [code] (cloudModeDoor.ts:57-73)
- Withdrawing writes a marker first, so a crash mid-way still closes Cloud on next launch. It returns the app to Local, then pauses schedules and running tasks, and turns off Ask from Siri. If pausing could not finish, a toast says tasks may still run. [code] (providerConsent.ts:159-175, 247-257; cloudModeDoor.ts:151-176)

### 5. Moving a Local chat to a provider

There is no single mechanism. Each app does it differently.

| App | Mechanism | What the person sees | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| surface:mobile | None. A Local chat cannot continue in Cloud. The only crossing is a manual copy of selected chats' text, from the Data controls screen, while in Cloud mode | One alert showing counts and limits, buttons Cancel and Sync to Cloud. No secret scan or payload preview was found in the code read | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:145-235) |
| surface:web | If the active chat is Local and the chosen model is a direct own-key provider, sending opens a consent dialog instead of sending. Regenerate is refused with an explanation | Choose context items (last 10 messages plus the outgoing prompt), see the redacted preview, confirm. The dialog shows `Local to Direct BYOK` and the provider name, says the original Local thread is unchanged, and creates a separate conversation | [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:55-118; apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:4456, 7971-7975; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/LocalByokHandoffDialog.tsx:75-110) |
| surface:desktop (Tauri) | A fork dialog builds the same preview and creates a new own-key conversation with only the approved, redacted messages. The Rust command stores it and leaves the Local conversation untouched | Preview expires after 15 minutes. The dialog does not pass a provider name | [code] (apps/desktop/src/features/byok/ByokConversationDialog.tsx:12, 113-130; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/llm.rs:1211-1277) |
| surface:desktop (Tauri), folder to Cloud | A sheet reads selected local files, previews them and attaches them to a managed chat. Findings block confirmation | Label "AGI Managed Cloud" | [code] (apps/desktop/src/features/context-handoff/CloudFolderAttachSheet.tsx:173-182, 258-273) |
| surface:cli | Local-to-cloud continuation creates a session that inherits no source messages, so unselected context is never written to the destination | The consent screen was not opened in this pass | [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:1088-1107); consent UI [unknown] |

The shared preview builder redacts secrets with a scanner, hashes the exact payload, sets `consentRequired: true`, and marks the preview `blocked` when it finds secrets and `blockOnFindings` is on (default on). [code] (packages/platform/utils/src/privacyHandoff.ts:111-167)

The written requirement lists eight steps for a crossing: user action, context selection, secret scan, payload preview, provider label, retention and cost disclosure, consent, new branch preserving the original. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:7.4, lines 135-146)

### 6. What crosses and what does not

- Local chats do not reach AGI servers through the guarded network path. Sign-in traffic and on-device model downloads are outside that path (see Gaps).
- Own-key traffic goes to the provider and never to our hosts. Our servers do not see it. [code] (egress-policy.ts:25-29)
- Cloud is the only path that writes to the shared chat store and the only metered path. [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:73-75)
- Server-side semantic decisions refuse Local and own-key sessions before any transport exists. [code] (apps/web/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts:241-302)

### 7. Capability tables

Columns: where it runs; whether the mode offers it; the subscription rule. Plan tiers and labels are in `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-16, 166-232`. In the tables, "Premium and above" means the code set PRO_TIERS (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise). "Basic and above" means PAID_TIERS (basic and every higher tier). [code] (billing-catalog.ts:332-341)

[code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2290, 2373; apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts:30-60) |

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Plan catalog.** Tiers and capability sets: [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-364). Labels: basic is Basic, pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra.

| Capability | Plans that include it |
| --- | --- |
| managed_chat, chat_tools, projects, memory_personalization, skills, cloud_sync | plan:free, plan:basic, plan:pro, plan:max, plan:max_15x, plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise |
| connectors, remote_control | PAID_TIERS: plan:basic and every higher plan (not free) |
| agi_work, deep_research, image_generation, managed_api, developer_surfaces, slack_app, artifact_connectors | PRO_TIERS: plan:pro and every higher plan (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise) |
| video_generation | plan:max_15x and plan:enterprise only |
| team_admin | plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise |
| enterprise_controls | plan:enterprise |

plan:local-only and plan:byok are in the catalog as free tiers with unlimited projects and custom MCP servers and zero sandboxes and scheduled tasks. They hold none of the capabilities above. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-178, 583-616)

**Rules that bind the modes**

1. Local needs no plan. Mobile Local chat has no account, plan or entitlement check on its path. Only an on-device age confirmation, a downloaded model and the app's own gates apply. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2290, 2373; rootRouting.ts:30-60)
2. Cloud requires sign-in. On mobile it also requires the current provider consent and the cloud feature flag; a build with `v1LocalOnly` set blocks Cloud without an explicit unlock. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2349-2385; remoteChatGate.ts:3-8)
3. An app is mapped to a plan capability before a Cloud chat is served: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome use `managed_chat`; CLI and VS Code use `developer_surfaces`; the open API uses `managed_api`. A token bound to no app gets no capability and fails closed. This means the same Free or Basic account gets Cloud chat on four apps and none on CLI and VS Code. It is not one uniform subscription check, which departs from the requirement that every app connects to one subscription system with one set of access rules; whether this is intended is [unknown]. [code] (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:42-52, 96-113)
4. The CLI hides every managed model from Free, Basic and own-key accounts. Local and own-key models are never gated by tier. [code] (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:925-960)
5. The capability handshake grants a capability only if all four layers grant it: model, tier, surface, settings. A missing grant fails closed. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/capability-handshake/registry.ts:45-70; capability-handshake-service.ts:112-125)
6. A credential found in a payload refuses the provider call in every mode, including Cloud. Own-key mode refuses a route that would use the platform key. Local refuses every fallback unless a person approved it. [code] (trust-boundary-crossing.ts:86-134)
7. Operator kill switch `AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA` can refuse Cloud compute for everyone. It is on unless set to `0`, `false` or `off`. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:39-53, 61-70)
8. Transitions: tightening a mode needs no approval; loosening always does. This rule is written as `refuseTrustTransition`. No product code calls it (see Gaps). [code] (trust-mode-contract.ts:123-137)
9. Own-key and Local conversations never fall into managed routing silently on the server: `fallback-leaves-trust-boundary` and `platform-key-not-permitted` refusals exist. [code] (trust-boundary-crossing.ts:24-29, 120-134)
10. The declared tier policy lists which provider surfaces a tier may use, and Free lists only managed cloud. No code reads that field. So the rule "own key is a paid feature" is not enforced from it. [code] (model-catalog.ts:1088, 1245, 1401; grep found no reader)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Statements marked [requirement] come from project documents. Statements marked [proposed] are suggestions of this page, not decisions.

1. **Local is free and needs no account.** [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:478-486). The mobile code matches this. The Electron code does not match the stated requirement that desktop local inference is free of a subscription: it removes local inference from the public Desktop by a recorded decision (D-2026-09-15-04, cited at dispatcher.ts:3235-3241). Whether the founder wants that decision reversed is not settled in the code. [unknown]
2. **A crossing needs eight things.** User action, context selection, secret scan, payload preview, provider label, retention and cost disclosure, consent, a new branch that preserves the original. [requirement] (requirements.md:7.4). The web fork dialog covers most of these; retention and cost disclosure were not found in the dialog. The Tauri fork lacks a provider label and does not block on secrets. The mobile manual copy shows counts and limits only.
3. **Every crossing should be one code path.** [proposed] `refuseTrustTransition` already states the rule (loosening needs an approval), and `evaluateProviderEgress` already enforces key attribution on the server. A single client-side helper that every app's fork dialog must call, and a guard that fails when a dialog is built without a provider label, would turn the written rule into an enforced one.
4. **Plan rules should be read from one table.** [proposed] Own-key use is declared as paid in a tier policy field that nothing reads. Either enforce it or delete it. The product statement says own key and local models are not subscription features, which is the behavior the CLI code has.
5. **One subscription rule across apps.** [requirement] (task brief: every app connects to one subscription system). [proposed] Decide whether CLI and VS Code Cloud chat should keep a Premium-and-above rule while the other four apps allow Free; if yes, record it as a decision, if not, align `free-chat-surface-policy.ts`.
6. **Fail closed on an unparseable host.** [proposed] The desktop renderer guard could block a private-mode request whose host it cannot determine, or resolve relative URLs against the page origin first.
7. **Docs follow code.** [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 2: prose is rank 6). The trust-boundaries table should be edited where it disagrees with the harness catalog.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Nothing below was run by this pass. These are the commands and files to use.

1. **Shared host list.** `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/trust-boundaries test` runs `egress-policy.test.ts`. Check that a BYOK provider host is not on the list.
2. **All surface proofs together.** `pnpm check:trust-boundaries` (script `scripts/check-trust-boundaries.mjs`). It runs the web, extension, mobile, VS Code, types, Rust routing and Rust send-message proofs, then fails if a Tauri crate pulls in a remote crash reporter.
3. **Mobile only.** Run `trust-boundary.test` in `apps/mobile` in small chunks (the project notes the test runner can hang and exhaust memory). Look at the cases named Local content-report consent, Cloud Mode permission, withdrawal and age check.
4. **Desktop renderer.** `pnpm check:desktop-local-egress` fails a bare `fetch` in the renderer. `pnpm check:rust-egress-boundary` checks the Tauri crate. Add a case for a relative URL in private mode to see the fail-open behaviour.
5. **Plan rules.** Read `BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS`, `PAID_TIERS`, `PRO_TIERS` and `BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS` in `billing-catalog.ts`. For a live account, call `GET /api/me` and read the capability handshake document (`granted`, `deniedBy`, `denialReasons`).
6. **By hand (human check, as the project prefers).** In the mobile app: (a) stay in Local, send a message, confirm no request to the web hosts appears in a proxy; (b) switch to Cloud, confirm the alert names the providers; (c) decline, confirm the app stays Local; (d) withdraw, confirm Cloud closes and schedules pause. In the web app: start a Local chat if reachable, pick an own-key model, confirm the dialog appears with the provider name.
7. **Open questions to settle by running:** whether the web build can reach the Local path at all; whether the main chat route calls the server crossing check; whether an own-key plan is needed on any app.

A green result of any of these says nothing about a build a person installed. The guards read the working tree, not a commit (AGENTS.md section 12).

key_facts.fact: One shared, platform-free list of our-cloud hosts (web domain, Vercel, Neon, four Clerk domains) is the single source for every device guard. Matching is suffix-based, case-insensitive and trailing-dot tolerant.
BYOK provider hosts are deliberately not on the our-cloud list, so direct own-key calls are never blocked.

The mobile guard treats Cloud as open only when appMode is cloud and the signed-in account's provider consent is current. Otherwise any our-cloud host throws EgressBlockedError before network I/O. It fails closed when mode, consent or withdrawal state cannot be read.
In mobile Local mode only three classes of request reach our servers: signed-in account controls, withdrawal controls, and one content report the person sends with its own Send tap.

The desktop renderer egress guard fails open for a target whose host cannot be parsed: extractHost returns null on a parse error and the guard throws only for a non-null host on the our-cloud list. A relative-path request in private mode is not blocked by this guard.

The mobile consent alert is titled 'Share with AI providers?' and names every provider the app can route to. Consent is stored per account with the provider ids covered, and is not current if a new provider has been added or a withdrawal is in progress.

Every write to the mobile app mode passes one admission function, so the mode cannot be Cloud without current consent. Declining keeps Local. Withdrawal returns to Local, pauses schedules and runs, and turns off Ask from Siri.

A mobile conversation keeps its mode. A Local chat refuses Cloud models and a Cloud chat refuses local models; there is no in-app continuation from Local to Cloud. The only crossing is a manual, confirmed copy of selected chats' text, done in Cloud mode.
Mobile has no own-key mode. The remote-chat gate accepts a byokKeys flag and never consults it.
The mobile remote-chat gate has a v1LocalOnly build flag; when set, Cloud is blocked without an explicit unlock. No released build sets it.
Mobile Local chat needs no AGI account or plan on its path; the router lets a signed-out user into the app after onboarding and an on-device age confirmation.

The public Electron Desktop shell refuses every local-inference command with 'unsupported-platform'. The code names decision D-2026-09-15-04 (desktop chat is Cloud-only) as the reason, and says local coding sessions reach local models through the bundled CLI. This conflicts with the stated product requirement that desktop local inference is free.
The desktop renderer guard reads the privacy mode; anything not 'managed', or an exception while reading it, counts as private. A script fails any renderer file that calls fetch directly.

The shared preview builder redacts secrets, hashes the payload, sets consentRequired true and marks the preview blocked when findings exist and blockOnFindings is on (default on). The Tauri own-key fork passes blockOnFindings false and no provider label; the folder-to-Cloud sheet passes true and the label 'AGI Managed Cloud'.

On web, sending from a Local chat to a direct own-key model opens a consent dialog instead of sending, and regenerate is refused. The dialog shows 'Local to Direct BYOK' with the provider name and says the Local thread is unchanged.

The Tauri Rust command llm_create_byok_fork stores only the already-approved messages as a new own-key conversation and leaves the Local conversation untouched; it does not itself check that consent was given.

The server mode contract defines Local as device storage, no key, fallback refuse; own key as user-provider storage, user key, same-boundary fallback; managed as managed-cloud storage, platform key, sync across devices.
refuseTrustTransition (loosening a mode needs approval) is exported but no product file calls it; only a support-claims file names it.

evaluateProviderEgress refuses a provider call that carries a secret, uses a platform key under an own-key conversation, or uses an unapproved or boundary-leaving fallback; every decision produces an audit event. Its only direct product caller is buildProviderEgressGateResponse in managed-compute-gate.ts, which three product files use (artifact completion, experiential-free completions route, free-quota turn).

Code plan tiers are free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise (plus local-only and byok at zero price). Labels shown to people: basic is Basic, pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra. PAID_TIERS means basic and above; PRO_TIERS means pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise.

Plan capabilities: chat, tools, projects, memory, skills and sync are in every tier from free; connectors and remote control are PAID_TIERS; AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API and developer surfaces are PRO_TIERS; video only max_15x and enterprise.

Which plan capability a Cloud chat needs depends on the calling app: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome need managed_chat (all tiers from free); CLI and VS Code need developer_surfaces (PRO_TIERS); the open API needs managed_api. A token bound to no app gets none. So a Free or Basic account gets Cloud chat on four apps and not on CLI or VS Code: not one uniform subscription check.

Plan limits by tier: Free has 5 projects, 5 uploads per day, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 2 sandboxes, 0 scheduled tasks and no coding-agent budget; Basic has 3 scheduled tasks and 5 sandboxes; Premium (pro) has 5 scheduled tasks and 10 sandboxes. local-only and byok tiers have 0 sandboxes and 0 scheduled tasks.

AGI Code (cloud coding) is included when a plan has both a sandbox allowance and a daily coding-agent budget above zero, which starts at Basic. This differs from the PRO_TIERS rule for CLI and VS Code Cloud models.
Every product tier allows web search and voice. Free has no manual model selection, no image or video generation, and 10 voice minutes per month.
The tier policy declares which provider surfaces each tier may use (Free: managed cloud only), but no code reads that field, so own-key use is not blocked by it.

Mobile live voice, web search, deep research, cloud code execution and Cloud-side memory are reached only in the Cloud branch of the send path. Turn-based speech capture on mobile requires an on-device recognizer and refuses otherwise.
Mobile Cloud sync, product analytics and Cloud memory run only in Cloud mode; the mobile sync engine also needs an account epoch.

The CLI discovers local models on loopback addresses (Ollama and LM Studio defaults) and never gates local or own-key models by plan; it hides every managed model from Free, Basic and own-key accounts.
CI runs check:trust-boundaries (seven surface proofs plus a no-remote-crash-reporting check on the Tauri crate) and check:rust-egress-boundary. This pass ran none of them.

The harness catalog marks mobile Local, desktop Local and CLI Local as partial, VS Code Local and own key as unwired, and records Cloud as implemented on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

pages.title: AGI Subscription: plans, entitlements, usage and limits

doc.summary: One AGI Subscription system serves all six apps. The account row resolves to a plan tier (own paid row, then team seat, then Free). Tier tables give capabilities and credit allowances (5-hour and weekly rolling windows, plus a billing-period total). A database reservation gates each managed turn. Stripe sells plans on web; mobile sells nothing in v1. Paid sales sit behind an access-code gate. Apps read /api/me, but CLI, VS Code, mobile, Tauri desktop and Chrome add local plan logic. Local and own-key plans carry no managed usage and no payment; which apps actually offer Local or own-key is set by the trust-boundary document, not by the plan catalog.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
**AGI Subscription** is the single system that decides what a signed-in account may do in the cloud and how much managed AI it may spend. It exists so Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome never keep separate plan rules. [requirement] (docs/product/commercial.md:74-81: one user has one `subscriptions` row and one billing owner; the same entitlement applies to every surface).

Plain terms used below:
- **Plan tier**: the stored plan name (`free`, `basic`, `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`, plus `local-only` and `byok`). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-15)
- **Credit**: the only usage unit customers see. 1 credit = $0.005 of provider cost (5,000 microUSD). [requirement] (docs/architecture/credits.md:7-16)
- **Entitlement**: the answer to "what plan does this account hold right now, and is it paid up". [code] (apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts:217-228)
- **Window**: a time slice with its own cap: rolling 5-hour, rolling weekly, and the billing period (monthly). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts:31-85)

What it does not govern: local inference and BYOK (the user's own provider key). Plans `local-only` and `byok` carry zero managed credits in every window, product limits of zero sandboxes and zero scheduled tasks, and they are absent from the cloud chat capability tiers, so managed chat, cloud sync and projects are denied to them. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:20-24, 33-34; billing-catalog.ts:322-336, 583-616). That is the code basis for "local inference needs no payment". Mobile Local mode never asks the server for a plan. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts, function `refreshTier` returns early unless app mode is `cloud`). Whether an account or sign-in is needed for Local is a separate question; the trust-boundary document says sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mobile mode, and the requirements document says a fresh install with no account reaches Local chat. [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:45-60; docs/product/requirements.md:943, 1067). Not verified in code by this page. [unknown]

A plan tier existing is not the same as a mode being available on an app. See "Rules: access, plans, modes".

Public names differ from stored ids: `pro` is shown as Premium and `max_15x` as Ultra. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:191-208). Old ids `hobby` and `pro_plus` fold to `basic` and `max`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:1029-1041)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Who is the account, and what plan does it hold
`resolveEntitlementBundle` is the one entry point. Order: (1) the user's own paid, entitled `subscriptions` row; (2) a team seat in an organization whose owner subscription is entitled, whose plan is seat-bearing and whose seat rank is within `licensed_seats`; (3) the user's own lapsed or free row; (4) none. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts:376-413)

A status counts as entitled only if it is `active` or `trialing`. Any other status collapses the effective plan to `free`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/subscription-entitlement.ts:3-17). Enterprise also tolerates `past_due` and `unpaid` unless the contract is in read-only collection. [code] (subscription-entitlement.ts:19-43)

Access ladder: rank 2 `active`/`trialing` gets managed execution, plan features, purchased-credit spend and plan change; rank 1 `incomplete`/`past_due` gets none (billing portal only); rank 0 everything else. Unknown status ranks 0. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/subscription-access-policy.ts:16-28, 55-79)

### 2. Asking "may this account use X"
- **Capabilities** are static tables keyed by tier: `BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS` and `canUseBillingPlanCapability`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:302-372)
- **Product limits** (projects, storage, concurrent turns, sandboxes, scheduled tasks, attachments) come from `BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:580-731)
- Apps get both through `GET /api/me`, which returns `plan` (tier, display name, status, period end, `effective_tier`, `subscription_source`, `billing_owner`), `feature_flags`, a `capability_handshake` document, and attachment and message limits. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:250-345)
- The handshake is built from four layers: model, tier, surface, settings (operator kill switches, account and workspace switches). A capability is granted only if every layer grants it. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/capability-handshake-service.ts:114-132, 353-383)

### 3. Spending: reserve, run, settle
Every managed turn calls `reserveManagedUsageRequest`. It checks the organization spend cap, resolves the plan allowance (catalog version and revenue context from the open credit period), applies promotion caps, then calls a database function that takes a per-user lock and decides in one place. Variants: normal plan windows, `extra_usage` funding, and per-app artifact runtime. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:738-878)
The turn then settles through `finalizeManagedUsageRequest`, which also writes `provider_cost_events`. [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:1140-1190; docs/product/commercial.md:298-306)

Order of funding: plan windows, then bonus credits (soonest expiry first), then purchased credits only when a plan limit is hit and usage credits (extra usage) are on. A turn that crosses a cap finishes on the plan; the next one goes to credits. [requirement] (docs/architecture/credits.md:44-50; docs/product/commercial.md:239-258)

### 4. Free accounts use a separate ledger
Free turns are admitted by `free-trial-service` against `free_daily_usage_reservations` and `website_auto_economy_trial_usage`, using the same Free numbers from the limits table. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/free-trial-service.ts:40-46, 394-409; apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:91-92, 119-138). The paid ledger helpers return a zero budget for Free (`isFreeSubject`), so Free admission depends on the Free ledger only. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/managed-usage-policy.ts:98-115)

### 5. Buying
- **Web**: `POST /api/checkout` creates a Stripe Checkout subscription session; the Stripe webhook writes the subscription and credit period. [code] (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:494-529; apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts:1-100)
- **Top-ups** (extra credits) via `/api/billing/top-up`, only on an active paid plan billed by Stripe, Apple or Google. [code] (apps/web/app/api/billing/top-up/route.ts:150-168)
- **Mobile stores**: compiled out in v1. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2)
- **Sales gate**: before checkout, an account with no live paid subscription needs waitlist access. [code] (checkout/route.ts:297-310)
