sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
### Plans, prices and allowances (code is the source)
Prices (monthly, USD): Free 0; Basic 7; Premium (`pro`) 20; Max 100; Ultra (`max_15x`) 200; Team 25 per seat (240 a year); Team Premium 125 per seat (1,200 a year); Enterprise by contract. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-231). India prices exist for Basic through Ultra and Team. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:189-217)

| Plan (id) | 5-hour credits | Weekly | Monthly | Flagship weekly cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free (`free`) | 200 | 1,500 | 2,000 | none |
| Basic (`basic`) | 10 | 100 | 400 | none (the flagship cap exists only for Premium, Max, Ultra and per-seat team plans) |
| Premium (`pro`) | 50 | 500 | 2,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Max (`max`) | 250 | 2,500 | 10,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Ultra (`max_15x`) | no cap (null) | 5,000 | 20,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Team (`team`, per seat) | 50 | 500 | 2,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Team Premium (`team_premium`, per seat) | 250 | 2,500 | 10,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Enterprise | unlimited flag; all window numbers are zero but the plan is treated as uncapped | | | |
| Local-only, BYOK | 0 | 0 | 0 | none (no managed usage) |

Source: [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:20-85, 250-292; ratio 0.3 at line 27). Matches docs/architecture/credits.md:29-42. Enterprise: `unlimited: true` makes the plan credit allowance Infinity, and the ledger allocation uses an uncapped constant. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:82-84, 284-290; apps/web/lib/server/managed-usage-policy.ts:95-102). Catalog versions 1 to 4 all point at the same table today, so grandfathering is a mechanism, not yet a difference. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:89-96)

Allowances are scaled by the revenue the subscriber's channel and currency produce versus a US web subscriber (store commission, card fees, included tax). [code] (billing-revenue.ts:96-148). A zero cap means zero allowed usage; a null cap means no cap. [requirement] (commercial.md:108-123)

### Capabilities by plan
[code] (billing-catalog.ts:322-364)
- Free and up: managed chat, chat tools, projects, memory, skills, cloud sync.
- Basic and up: connectors, Remote Control.
- Premium and up (incl. team plans, Enterprise): AGI Work, Deep Research, image generation, managed API, developer surfaces (CLI and VS Code cloud), Slack app, artifact connectors.
- Ultra and Enterprise only: video generation.
- Team, Team Premium, Enterprise: team admin. Enterprise only: SSO, SCIM and admin controls.
- Local-only and BYOK: none of the above (not in the cloud chat tiers).

### Product limits (examples)
Free: 5 projects, 1 concurrent turn, 2 sandboxes, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 0 scheduled tasks, 5 attachment uploads a day. Max: 5 concurrent turns, 15 scheduled tasks. Ultra: 10 concurrent turns, 25 scheduled tasks. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:617-690). Free daily caps: 1,000 message writes, 100 conversation creates, 25 MiB egress, 10 emails, 200 vector queries. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:484-490)

### Tables (names seen in code)
| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| table:subscriptions | one row per user: plan_tier, status, period dates, stripe_subscription_id, stripe_price_id, apple_original_transaction_id, google_purchase_token, plan_catalog_version [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:39-55; checkout/route.ts:280-285) |
| table:token_credits | credit period balance (allocated, used, top-up portion, catalog version) [requirement] (commercial.md:225-232) |
| table:credit_transactions | the usage ledger: `deduction`, `purchase`, `refund` rows with `amount_microusd`, `metadata.is_overage`, `metadata.is_flagship` [code] (rolling-usage.ts query; top-up/route.ts:190-196) |
| table:managed_usage_requests | one row per reservation with idempotency key and `is_overage` [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:919-939) |
| table:provider_cost_events, table:cogs_adjustments | cost of goods ledger [requirement] (commercial.md:298-322) |
| table:billing_disputes, table:billing_refund_requests | disputes and refunds [requirement] (commercial.md:189-223) |
| table:free_daily_usage_reservations, table:website_auto_economy_trial_usage | Free ledger [code] (free-trial-service.ts:647-660) |
| table:organizations, table:organization_members | seats: licensed_seats, licensed_premium_seats, seat_type, premium_paid_through [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:62-93; team-seat-entitlement.ts:18-36) |
| table:beta_invites, table:beta_redemptions | access codes [code] (waitlist/access/route.ts:34-48; billing-waitlist-access.ts:47-53) |
| table:waitlist | per-plan waitlist joins [code] (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/route.ts GET) |
| table:mobile_iap_transactions, table:mobile_app_transactions | store purchase records [code] (mobile-iap-ledger-service.ts:158-203) |

### Periods and windows
- 5-hour and weekly windows are **rolling**: spend in the last 5 hours or 168 hours. They refill as old spend leaves, not at a fixed clock time. [code] (rolling-usage.ts; quota text in billing-catalog.ts:922-941)
- The monthly total follows the subscription billing period, not a calendar month. [code] (managed-usage-period.ts:46-75)
- Allowance does not roll over; purchased credits carry across renewals; bonus credits expire after 90 days; Japan purchases expire after six months. [requirement] (credits.md:44-50; commercial.md:231-236)

### Top-ups and extra usage
Two different rates, not to be confused. A top-up buys 50 credits per $1 paid (before discount). A credit is defined as $0.005 of provider cost, so $1 of provider cost is 200 credits. The two numbers are different things: the first is the sale price, the second is the cost unit. [code] (billing-topups.ts:5) [requirement] (credits.md:12-16, 71-78). Packs $20, $50, $100, $250, $1,000; discounts 0, 5, 10, 20, 30 percent; auto-reload an extra 5 percent; purchase min $20, max $1,000, $2,000 a day; auto-reload threshold 100 to 100,000 credits (default 500). [code] (billing-topups.ts:5-14). Extra usage (usage credits) must be switched on in Settings > Billing for purchased credits to be spent. [requirement] (commercial.md:247-251)

### Configuration names (purposes only)
- STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Stripe API and webhook signature. [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:12-13)
- STRIPE_PRICE_* (for example the Basic monthly USD price): Stripe price ids per plan, interval and currency. [code] (apps/web/lib/pricing.ts:54-57)
- AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1: forces paid upgrades open. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-30)
- AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA: incident kill switch for managed compute. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40)
- Flag `billing.upgrades_open`: runtime operator switch for the sales gate. [code] (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/billing-upgrades.ts:3)
- Flag `billing.usage_promotions`. [requirement] (credits.md:54-55)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Which apps offer which mode
The plan catalog lists `local-only`, `byok` and every other plan as selectable on web, desktop and mobile. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:235-247). That is only plan visibility. It does not mean a mode runs on that app. The trust-boundary document sets the real mode support: [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:45-60)

| App | Local | Own key | Cloud (subscription) |
|---|---|---|---|
| surface:mobile | yes, on device | not offered | yes; needs the account's current consent to share with AI providers |
| surface:web | no | no | cloud only |
| surface:desktop (public Electron) | chat: no (rejects local-inference commands); local coding sessions run the bundled CLI and may use a local model or a provider key | chat: no key accepted; coding sessions via CLI yes | chat is cloud only |
| surface:cli | yes | yes (`Byok` tier; enforcement left to the user) | managed models need a subscription |
| surface:vscode | yes | yes | subscription required for managed models |
| surface:chrome | no | no | cloud only |

The CLI tier enum has its own `Byok` variant whose enforcement is the user's responsibility, so local and BYOK CLI use is not gated by the account tier. [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:184-200)

In mobile Local mode, the egress guard blocks every managed-cloud host except account controls, withdrawal controls and a content report the user chooses to send; sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mode. [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:47-49)

### Rules by mode
| Mode | Subscription rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| mode:local | No plan or payment needed. Mobile Local does not call `/api/me`. Plan id `local-only` has zero managed credits and no sandboxes. Usable on mobile, CLI, VS Code and desktop coding sessions only. | [code] (store.ts `refreshTier` guard; billing-catalog.ts:583-599) [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:45-60) |
| mode:own-key | `byok` plan: zero managed credits; user pays the provider. Not offered on mobile or web. | [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:34) [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:46, 56-57) |
| mode:cloud | Needs sign-in. Free uses the Free ledger; paid plans use the reservation system. Managed Free is public alpha for signed-in users. | [requirement] (commercial.md:8-14, 20-29) |

A Local-to-cloud move is a separate trust-boundary decision. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)

### Plan resolution rules
1. Own entitled paid row wins over a seat. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:395-398)
2. A seat applies only if the org plan is seat-bearing (per-seat or contract), the member's join-order rank is within `licensed_seats`, and the owner subscription is entitled. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:104-120, 139-143)
3. Premium seat type depends on `premium_paid_through` and `licensed_premium_seats`. [code] (team-seat-entitlement.ts:18-75)
4. Plans below rank 2 resolve to Free. [code] (subscription-entitlement.ts:12-17)
5. If the seat lookup fails for a workspace member and the caller asked for strictness (`/api/me`), the call throws instead of reporting Free. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:258-264, 401-409) [requirement] (CLI comment tier_cache.rs:696-700)

### One billing owner
The source is read in this order. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:47-67)
1. No row reads as `none`.
2. A malformed Stripe subscription id, or ids from more than one of Stripe, Apple, Google, reads as `unverified`; every billing action fails closed.
3. A valid Stripe subscription id reads as `stripe`; an Apple id as `apple`; a Google token as `google`.
4. No such ids and a `free` tier reads as `none`.
5. No such ids but a valid Stripe customer id reads as `stripe`.
6. Otherwise (a non-free tier with no store id, no Stripe subscription id and no Stripe customer id) it reads as `manual`: organization-managed or granted by hand.

`/api/me` reports `manual` for any seat holder. [code] (me/route.ts:304-307)
Handoff: a second channel loses while the owner is still entitled; once the owner is terminal the new purchase takes over and clears the other ids. [requirement] (commercial.md:86-99). Store rows expire three days after the paid-through date. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:31, 83-107)

### Sales gate and waitlist
- Applies to an account with no live paid subscription. It needs `billing.upgrades_open` on (or env override), or any row in `beta_redemptions`. Otherwise checkout returns HTTP 403 with the waitlist code. [code] (checkout/route.ts:297-310; billing-waitlist-access.ts:38-66)
- The flag reads closed on any failure. [code] (billing-upgrade-gate.ts:10-34)
- Existing paid accounts keep entitlements; Free users need no code for Free managed usage. [requirement] (commercial.md:57-72)
- Access codes open acquisition only; they grant no plan or trial. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/admin-surfaces.md:145). Redeemed through `validate_and_redeem_invite_code`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/access/route.ts:44-48)
- Observation: the gate query counts any `beta_redemptions` row for the user, not only rows from billing-upgrade invites. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts:47-53) [inferred] that a beta-program redemption also opens checkout.
- Mobile v1 sells nothing. When store purchase turns on, it opens with no waitlist or code. [requirement] (commercial.md:66-70)

### What happens at a limit
The database refuses a reservation with a decision; the server maps it to HTTP and a code. [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts, `reservationError` and `PLAN_LIMIT_WINDOWS`)
| Decision | HTTP | Code | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| declined (period used up) | 402 | `insufficient_credits` | add credits or upgrade or wait |
| extra_usage_required | 402 | `extra_usage_required` | turn on usage credits |
| session_limit | 429 | `rolling_five_hour_limit_reached` | wait for refill, credits, or upgrade |
| weekly_limit | 429 | `rolling_weekly_limit_reached` | same |
| flagship_weekly_limit | 429 | `flagship_weekly_limit_reached` | choose a standard model |
| artifact_limit | 429 | `artifact_runtime_limit_reached` | per-app cap, other chats unaffected |
| organization spend cap | 402 | `organization_spend_cap_reached` | admin |
| anything else | 503 | `billing_unavailable` | retry |
Free codes: `free_trial_token_budget_reached`, `free_trial_model_only`, `free_trial_feature_unavailable`; plan lacks capability: `plan_upgrade_required`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:884-921)
Recovery action: Free gets Upgrade; paid self-serve plans whose block is cleared by credits get Add credits; accounts not billed by Stripe, Apple or Google are told to wait or ask whoever manages the plan. [code] (work-usage.ts:22-39, 78-94; managed-usage-request-service.ts:86-104)
The next upgrade ladder is Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra; Team and Enterprise have none. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:32-37, 847-860)

### Plan changes
Upgrade goes through `/api/upgrade` with immediate proration; a tier upgrade starts a new billing period and carries usage and purchased balance. Downgrade is the Stripe portal only; the smaller allowance applies at the next renewal while tier gates drop at once. [requirement] (commercial.md:144-170). Disputes set `past_due`, revoke the period's remaining credits and restore them on a win; refunds revoke the refunded share. [requirement] (commercial.md:187-206)

### Trials
No plan in the catalog sets `trialDays`, so catalog trials do not exist today; a trial can still arrive through a referral. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-231 has no `trialDays`; checkout/route.ts:431-438, 454)

### Plans granted by hand
A `subscriptions` row with a paid tier and no store id, no Stripe subscription id and no Stripe customer id is the `manual` source. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:56-66). The mobile review account is meant to get its plan this way. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md:92, 179, 431). The tool or admin route that writes such a row was not found. [unknown]

sections.heading: Differences between apps
sections.markdown:
### How each app reads the same entitlement
All five client apps call `GET /api/me` (the surface is passed as a query value) and use `plan.effective_tier`, `plan.tier`, `plan.status` and `capability_handshake`. Usage meters come from `/api/usage`.

| App | How it reads the entitlement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| surface:web | Server code resolves the bundle directly and enforces on every managed route; billing screens in `features/billing`. | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:384; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:399-460) |
| surface:desktop | The public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it uses web's resolution. The Tauri code is retained internal code, not the shipped Desktop; it calls `/api/me?surface=desktop`, then uses `canUseBillingPlanCapability` and shared model lists. | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5) [code] (apps/desktop/src/services/cloudAccountAuth.ts:693; apps/desktop/src/services/desktopCloudEntitlements.ts:1-71) |
| surface:mobile | Zustand tier store, persisted; refresh only in cloud mode; reads tier, status, source, period end, handshake, attachment and message limits. Defaults to Free until the first refresh; `planCheckOf` reports `confirmed`, `checking` or `unconfirmed`. | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts `refreshTier`; planCheck.ts) |
| surface:cli | Caches the tier and handshake in `~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml` for 300 s; fetch timeout 3 s; reads usage from `/api/usage`. | [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:31-35, 734-826; usage_summary.rs:11-32) |
| surface:vscode | Same 300 s cache in extension global state; plan comparison table built from shared catalog functions. | [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/tierResolver.ts TIER_CACHE_TTL_MS; features/account-auth/planComparison.ts:1-90) |
| surface:chrome | Fetches `/api/me?surface=web` and answers capability questions with the shared `resolveCapabilityDocumentDecision`. Cloud only. | [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts:20-92) [requirement] (commercial.md:29; trust-boundaries.md:60) |

### Where an app checks plans in its own way
Rows 8 and 9 describe the retained Tauri build, which is internal code and not the public Desktop (the public Desktop shows the hosted web app). They are listed because they are still in the repository.

| # | App | Place | What it does differently |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | surface:cli | apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:184-252 | Own `UserTier` enum including `Byok`; own `tier_rank` and `managed_auto_routing_tier` (Team grouped with Pro; Max, Ultra and Team Premium with Max; Free, Basic and BYOK with free). |
| 2 | surface:cli | tier_cache.rs:677-710, 734-826 | A fresh cache is returned without a network call; a lower fetched tier never replaces a higher cached one, so a downgrade can lag. |
| 3 | surface:cli | apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:22-31 | Own copies of entitled and payment-failed status lists and of the workload labels. |
| 4 | surface:vscode | integrations/tierResolver.ts `coerceTier` | Own tier whitelist and legacy alias map (`hobby`, `pro+`, `pro_plus`), plus a `local` tier. |
| 5 | surface:mobile | apps/mobile/src/features/billing/subscriptionSource.ts | Own terminal-status set (copy of the server's) and own source labels. |
| 6 | surface:mobile | settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:155; model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:293 | Direct comparison `=== 'free'`. |
| 7 | surface:mobile | store.ts | Falls back to `effectivePlanTier(plan.tier, plan.status)` when the server omits `effective_tier`. |
| 8 | surface:desktop (retained Tauri code only) | apps/desktop/src/stores/auth.ts:796 | Sets `subscriptionStatus` locally to `none` for Free and `active` for everything else, without reading the server status. This is a client-side display value. |
| 9 | surface:desktop (retained Tauri code only) | src-tauri/src/core/llm/llm_router.rs:757, 842 | A routing hint, not an entitlement check: `free`, `basic` or `hobby` count as a budget plan when choosing a route. |
| 10 | surface:chrome | features/side-panel/freePlanNotices.ts; cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts | Free-plan notices and a free-trial gateway client of its own (contents not read). [unknown] |
| 11 | surface:web | many files (about 300 reference plan tiers under apps/web) | Direct `isFreeBillingPlanTier` checks for example in top-up route, LLM route, pricing page, voice allowance. |
| 12 | all | Free vs paid | Free is admitted through a separate ledger (free-trial-service) from paid reservations. |

### Mobile purchase state
`nativePurchases: false` means no purchase, upgrade, top-up or restore control, no store connection and no Play Billing permission. It is fixed per build, never switched by OTA update or server. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:1-14). Server-side store verification, catalog and notification routes exist for when it is turned on. [code] (apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap/*). Mobile shows web billing links for Stripe or manual sources and store links for Apple or Google. [code] (subscriptionSource.ts:44-58)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
| Situation | Behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Usage database cannot answer a reservation | HTTP 503 `billing_unavailable`; no model call (fails closed) | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:283-300) |
| Organization policy or spend lookup fails | 503 `billing_unavailable` | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:331-365) |
| Plan catalog lookup fails | falls back to the current catalog, logs a warning | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:598-612) |
| Rolling usage read fails (display and limit-context paths) | logs a warning and treats usage as 0 (fails open for those reads) | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/rolling-usage.ts, `getRollingUsage` catch) |
| Operator sales switch unreadable | gate stays closed | [code] (billing-upgrade-gate.ts:10-34) |
| Waitlist access check errors | checkout refused with 503 | [code] (checkout/route.ts:299-306) |
| Billing owner unverifiable | all Stripe billing actions refused with a conflict | [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:58, 129-136) |
| Subscription lookup fails at checkout | 503, no session created | [code] (checkout/route.ts:286-293) |
| Stripe already bills this customer | 409 conflict | [code] (checkout/route.ts:415-428) |
| Webhook: rate limit or bad signature | rejected before processing | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:34-52) |
| Webhook: event already done | 200 `Event already processed` | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:56-69) |
| Webhook: same event still processing | 503 with `Retry-After: 10` | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:60-66) |
| Webhook: handler throws | whole event rolled back (one transaction), marked failed, HTTP 500 so Stripe retries | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:71-93) |
| Out-of-order Stripe event resurrecting a canceled row | refused | [requirement] (commercial.md:184-186) |
| Seat lookup fails for a workspace member | `/api/me` errors rather than report Free; other paths log and fall back to the user's own row | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:401-409) |
| Owner seat type lookup fails | entitled at the Standard seat | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:360-374) |
| Seat member ledger cannot be provisioned | logged; entitlement still returned | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:198-208) |
| CLI tier fetch fails or times out (3 s) | no tier returned; caller uses its configured default; HTTP 401 clears cache and asks for re-login | [code] (tier_cache.rs:790-826) |
| Mobile refresh fails | keeps cached tier, returns false | [code] (store.ts `refreshTier` catch) |
| Idempotency key reused | 409 `idempotency_in_progress`, `idempotency_replay` or `idempotency_conflict` | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts `reservationError`) |
| Enterprise invoice overdue | read-only stage denies managed compute but keeps reads | [requirement] (docs/runbooks/enterprise-billing.md:218) |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Established requirements, then proposals.

**Requirements the code already follows**
- One account, one subscription row, one billing owner, one entitlement for all surfaces. [requirement] (commercial.md:74-81)
- Credits are the only customer unit; plan numbers live only in `managed-usage-limits.ts`. [requirement] (credits.md:85-87)
- Model and provider names are never hard-coded in consumers; usage cost comes from the registry and rate card. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4; credits.md:20-25)
- Local and own-key use stays usable without managed usage. [requirement] (commercial.md:79-81)
- Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters (owner decision recorded in project memory; the UsageSection test holds it). [unknown] whether this is enforced on every app; only the web test is named.

**Proposals (not decisions)**
- [proposed] Move CLI, VS Code and Tauri status lists, tier ranks and alias maps to one shared function in `@agiworkforce/types` and generate the Rust copy through the existing protocol-type export, so there is one place to change a plan.
- [proposed] Have `/api/me` (or the handshake) carry a ready-made `is_free` and `is_paid` field so apps stop comparing to the string `free`.
- [proposed] Limit the sales-gate redemption query to invites of the billing-upgrade kind, so a beta redemption does not silently open checkout, if that is not intended.
- [proposed] Record a documented, audited operator path for plans granted by hand, so the `manual` source has a known writer.
- [proposed] Make the CLI cache honour a lower fresh tier from the server after a cancellation, or document the up-to-5-minute lag as accepted.
- [proposed] Make the plan catalog surface visibility match real mode support, or document that it is plan visibility only, so a reader does not take `local-only` as available on web.

**How a human or agent would check, without changing production**
1. Compare `MANAGED_USAGE_LIMITS` with the credits.md table (they agree as read).
2. In a local build with seeded accounts, call `GET /api/me` for each tier and check `plan.effective_tier`, `capability_handshake.granted` and `/api/usage` windows against the tables above.
3. Drive a Free account to a window limit and confirm the code and recovery action per the limit table.
4. With the gate closed, `POST /api/checkout` for a Free account should return 403 with the waitlist code; after redeeming a code, it should create a session.
5. Replay a Stripe test event twice and confirm the second is skipped.
6. On mobile, confirm no purchase control appears while `nativePurchases` is false.
7. Run `pnpm check:llm-operability` (guard chain) per AGENTS.md section 12 for the model-literal and catalog guards.

key_facts.fact: Plan tiers are local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; pro is shown as Premium and max_15x as Ultra.
The plan catalog marks every plan, including local-only and byok, selectable on web, desktop and mobile. This is plan visibility, not mode support.

Mode support by app: mobile has Local and Cloud (no BYOK); web is Cloud only; public Desktop chat is Cloud only and rejects local-inference commands; Chrome is Cloud only; CLI and VS Code support subscription, BYOK and local models.
local-only and byok get zero managed usage in every window, are absent from the cloud chat capability tiers (managed chat, cloud sync, projects denied), and have zero sandboxes and scheduled tasks.
Enterprise has unlimited managed usage: unlimited true with zero window numbers, plan credit allowance Infinity, and an uncapped ledger allocation constant.
The CLI has its own Byok tier whose enforcement is left to the user, so local and BYOK CLI use is not gated by the account tier.

A mobile fresh install with no account reaches Local chat; in Local mode the egress guard blocks managed-cloud hosts except account controls, withdrawal controls and a user-sent content report; sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mode. Not verified in code by this page.
Monthly USD prices: Basic 7, Premium 20, Max 100, Ultra 200, Team 25 per seat, Team Premium 125 per seat; Enterprise is contract priced.
1 credit equals $0.005 of provider cost (5,000 microUSD); credits are the only usage unit shown to customers.

A top-up buys 50 credits per $1 paid; this is the sale rate and differs from the cost unit (1 credit = $0.005 of provider cost, 200 credits per $1 of cost). Minimum $20, maximum $1,000, $2,000 a day; auto-reload threshold 100 to 100,000 credits.

Per-plan credit windows (5-hour / weekly / monthly): Free 200/1,500/2,000; Basic 10/100/400; Premium 50/500/2,000; Max 250/2,500/10,000; Ultra none/5,000/20,000; Team 50/500/2,000 per seat; Team Premium 250/2,500/10,000 per seat.
Ultra (max_15x) has no 5-hour cap (null); a zero cap means zero allowed usage.
Flagship-model usage is capped at 30% of the weekly allowance on Premium, Max, Ultra and per-seat team plans; Basic and Free have no flagship cap.
The 5-hour and weekly windows are rolling sums over the last 5 and 168 hours of credit_transactions deductions; rows tagged is_overage are excluded.
The monthly window follows the subscription billing period; periods over 45 days (yearly) are cut into monthly slices anchored to the start date.
Entitlement resolves in one function: own entitled paid row, then team seat, then own lapsed or free row, then none.
Only active and trialing statuses are entitled; any other status collapses the effective plan to free. Enterprise also tolerates past_due and unpaid unless collection is read-only.

Apps ask for entitlement through GET /api/me, which returns plan, effective_tier, subscription_source, billing_owner, feature flags and a four-layer capability handshake (model, tier, surface, settings).

Capabilities by tier: connectors and Remote Control from Basic; AGI Work, Deep Research, images, managed API, developer surfaces from Premium; video only Ultra and Enterprise; team admin on team plans and Enterprise.
Every managed turn reserves usage through a per-user database function and is refused with a typed decision (402 or 429 codes) or 503 billing_unavailable when billing cannot answer.
Funding order is plan windows, then bonus credits, then purchased credits only when usage credits are on; a turn that crosses a cap finishes on the plan.

Free accounts are admitted through a separate Free ledger (free_daily_usage_reservations and website_auto_economy_trial_usage); the paid ledger helpers give Free a zero budget. Free product limits include 5 projects, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 0 scheduled tasks, 5 daily attachment uploads and 2 sandboxes.

Checkout is gated: an account without a live paid subscription needs billing.upgrades_open on (or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1) or any beta_redemptions row; otherwise POST /api/checkout returns 403 with the waitlist code. The flag reads closed on any error.

A subscription has one billing owner. A malformed Stripe subscription id or ids from more than one channel read as unverified and fail closed. With no store id and no Stripe subscription id: free tier reads none; a valid Stripe customer id reads stripe; otherwise a non-free tier reads manual. Store rows expire 3 days after paid-through.

The Stripe webhook rate-limits and verifies the signature, dedupes by event id (200 if done, 503 with Retry-After 10 if still processing), runs the handler and idempotency mark in one transaction, and returns 500 on failure so Stripe retries.
Mobile v1 sells nothing: storePurchases.json has nativePurchases false, compiled per build; mobile only refreshes the tier in cloud mode.
CLI and VS Code cache the account tier for 300 seconds; the CLI keeps a higher cached tier over a lower fetched one and times out the fetch at 3 seconds.
Team seat entitlement comes from the organization owner's subscription, limited by join-order rank within licensed_seats; /api/me reports subscription_source manual for seat holders.
The offline licensing verifier (TypeScript package and Rust crate) is not wired into any app runtime.
Catalog versions 1 to 4 all map to the same allowance table; a subscription records the version it was sold under.
No plan in the catalog sets trialDays, so trials come only from referrals.
Access codes open acquisition only and grant no plan or trial.

Apps with their own plan logic include the CLI tier enum, the VS Code alias map and mobile direct free comparisons. The retained Tauri code (not the public Desktop) derives subscription status locally and uses a free/basic/hobby budget-plan routing hint, which is not an entitlement check.

doc.summary: One AGI account, held by an identity provider (Clerk today, behind a swappable port), signs in on every app. Web signs in with email, code, password, passkey or provider buttons. Desktop hands off to the browser with a one-time code. Mobile signs in natively. CLI, VS Code and Chrome link through device codes or the web session. Every sign-in meets terms and 18-and-over checks. Local use needs no account.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** Authentication proves who a person is. Identity ties that person to one account that all six apps share. The product keeps the identity provider behind a small interface (a "port") so the provider can change without touching routes or pages. [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11) names `clerk` as the default provider; `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` selects it. Web code asks `getIdentityProvider()` and never builds a client itself [code] (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts).

**Why it exists.** One account lets chat history, plan and devices follow the person across Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. It also gives the server one place to enforce account status, terms, the 18-and-over rule and revocation.

**What it is not.** Sign-in is not payment and not entitlement. Plans, quotas and usage are a separate subsystem (the AGI Subscription system); sign-in only supplies the account id those rules attach to. [inferred] from the sign-in routes carrying no plan check (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/approve/route.ts, token/route.ts). Local inference on mobile and desktop is not gated by payment; whether it is gated by an account differs by app (see Differences between apps).

**Credential families, in one table.**

| Family | Used by | Issuer | Lifetime found in code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity-provider session cookie and session token | Web (and Desktop window, which shows hosted web) | Clerk | Provider-side lifetime [unknown]; product cap 30 days from creation by default |
| Identity-provider native session token plus a signed "surface proof" token | Mobile | Clerk (mobile token template) | Provider-side [unknown] |
| Identity-provider token bound to the extension origin | Chrome | Clerk via `syncHost` | Provider-side [unknown] |
| Developer token (JWT signed by the web app) plus rotating refresh token | CLI, VS Code (and the retained Tauri desktop build) | Web app, after browser approval | Access 7 days, refresh 30 days |
| `sk_live_` / `sk_test_` API keys | Programmatic callers | Web app | Out of scope here |

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Sign-in service
The provider is Clerk [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11; apps/web/proxy.ts:17-18 imports the port). Web middleware `proxy` wraps every session route with `identityMiddleware.withSession`, passing an **authorized-party allowlist**. If the allowlist cannot be resolved, the proxy answers 503 instead of running unverified, because a provider skips the origin check when the list is empty [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:192-224, 340). The proxy also sends a signed-out visitor from a protected product route to `/login?redirectTo=...` when no session cookie exists, but `/chat` itself stays open (guest chat) [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:324-330).

Enabled sign-in providers come from `AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS` (`google`, `github`, `microsoft`, `apple`; default Google and GitHub; `passkey` is a flag in the same list) [code] (packages/client/client-runtime/src/authProviders.ts; apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts).

### 2. Web sign-in steps
1. `/login` or `/signup` render the same entry screen (apps/web/app/signup/page.tsx calls `AuthEntryScreen`) [code].
2. `AuthFlow` runs a step machine: `email` -> `password` | `code` -> `second_factor` -> `new_password` | `notice` [code] (apps/web/features/auth/authContract.ts, AuthFlow.tsx). Methods are `password`, `email_code`, `passkey`; provider buttons and enterprise SSO redirect through `/auth/sso-callback` [code] (authContract.ts; IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:296-301, 649-655). Code length is 6, resend cooldown 30 s, minimum password 8 [code] (authRoutes.ts constants in authContract.ts).
3. On sign-up the person types an age first; under 18 is refused before any provider call [code] (apps/web/features/auth/useSignupAgeGate.ts; packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:1).
4. Both flows end at `/login/complete` or `/signup/complete`, a server page that checks in order: a live session exists (else a stale-session recovery screen, not a redirect, to avoid a loop); account is allowed (locked, recovery, suspended, deleted are refused with a notice); primary email confirmed; adult-eligibility decision (`ineligible` shows a refusal, `unconfirmed` asks for age); Terms acceptance; then redirect to a safe destination [code] (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:41-120).
5. `postAuthDestination` sends the person to the requested path, or a new chat; sign-in loop paths and `/` map to new chat [code] (apps/web/features/auth/postAuthDestination.ts).

### 3. Desktop hand-off to the browser (public Electron app)
The desktop window never shows a password field. A signed-out window shows a data page with Start and Cancel buttons [code] (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts). Steps:
1. Shell makes a random 32-byte **verifier**, keeps it in memory only, and computes its SHA-256 **challenge** [code] (apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:39-41).
2. Shell opens the system browser at `https://<cloud origin>/auth/desktop?challenge=...`. The pending attempt lives 10 minutes [code] (browserSignIn.ts:13, 47-53).
3. The page `/auth/desktop` needs a web session; if none, it sends the person to `/login` and back. It then POSTs the challenge to `api:POST /api/auth/desktop/grant` (CSRF required, rate limit `device-link`, refused for developer-token callers) and gets a one-time code stored hashed with a 60-second life [code] (apps/web/app/auth/desktop/DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx; apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop/grant/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/desktop-sign-in.ts:7, 33-47). If a passkey is required for the account, the page detours to the account-security verify page first [code] (DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx).
4. The browser navigates to the deep link `agiworkforce-cloud://sign-in?code=...&challenge=...` [code] (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-sign-in.ts; host-bridge.ts:4).
5. The shell checks the link's challenge against its pending one. Any mismatch, reuse, relaunch or cancel yields `expired`. On match it loads `/auth/desktop/complete#code=...&verifier=...` in the window [code] (browserSignIn.ts `readBrowserSignInLink`).
6. That page (only runs if the host bridge reports browser sign-in support) POSTs code and verifier to `api:POST /api/auth/desktop/redeem`. The server marks the grant consumed only if the code hash and `sha256(verifier)` match and it has not expired, then asks the identity provider for a **sign-in ticket** valid 60 s, which the page exchanges for a session in the window [code] (DesktopSignInComplete.tsx:73-84; desktop-sign-in.ts:50-67; redeem/route.ts).
7. The window's persistent partition is `persist:agi-cloud` [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:24).

The retained Tauri desktop code instead uses the CLI-style device-code flow (`apps/desktop/src/services/desktopNativeSignIn.ts` imports `requestDeviceAuthorization`, `pollDeviceAuthorization`) [code]. It is internal, not the public desktop [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5).

### 4. Mobile native sign-in
The app wraps everything in `ClerkProvider` with Clerk's secure token cache [code] (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:58-59, 994). Sign-in screen steps are `email`, `password`, `code`, with email-code, password, passkey-adjacent second factors, Apple and other providers via `useSSO` and `useSignInWithApple` [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:5-7, 46). On iOS the app shows either both Apple and other providers or none (App Store rule 4.8) [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/loginProviders.ts). A native token has no web origin, so each API call carries the session token as Bearer plus a second "surface proof" token from a Clerk template, sent in `SURFACE_TOKEN_HEADER` [code] (apps/mobile/services/authSession.ts; apps/mobile/src/integrations/clerk.ts:79-146). The server admits such a pair only if both tokens lack an origin claim, name the same subject and the proof binds a known surface [code] (apps/web/lib/server/native-session-token.ts).

### 5. CLI and VS Code device linking (RFC 8628 device grant)
1. Client calls `api:POST /api/auth/device/code` with `surface` of `cli`, `vscode`, `chrome` or `desktop`. Server stores a pending row and returns `device_code` (UUID), a short `user_code` (XXXX-XXXX), verification URL, interval 5 s, lifetime 900 s [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/code/route.ts:24-31, 80-120; grant-policy.ts).
2. Client opens `/auth/device?user_code=...&surface=...`. The signed-in person sees the client name and scopes (`account:read`, `managed-cloud:use`) and approves or denies with `api:POST /api/auth/device/approve` [code] (apps/web/app/auth/device/page.tsx; approve/route.ts).
3. Approval is refused when: caller is itself a developer-token session; the account's device sign-in setting is off (403 `DEVICE_SIGNIN_DISABLED`, 503 if unreadable); Terms need re-acceptance; the 18-and-over decision is not confirmed [code] (approve/route.ts:45-190).
4. Client polls `api:POST /api/auth/device/token`. Answers: `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied`, `expired_token`, `account_unavailable`, `terms_acceptance_required`, age refusal, or tokens. On success the server consumes the code and inserts a hashed refresh token in a new family, in one transaction [code] (token/route.ts:70-250).
5. Access token is a JWT (issuer `agiworkforce-api-gateway`) valid 604800 s; refresh token is 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, valid 30 days [code] (developer-token.ts:9-11; device-refresh-token.ts:5-22).
6. `api:POST /api/auth/device/refresh` rotates the pair; a replayed old refresh token marks the whole family compromised and revokes it [code] (refresh/route.ts, refresh-token-family.ts `finishFamilyAsCompromised`).
7. CLI stores the grant in the OS keyring (service `com.agiworkforce.cli.auth`), or an owner-only file when `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92, 175, 778). VS Code stores it in `SecretStorage` under `agiWorkforce.accountToken` [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:220-229).
8. Sign-out calls `api:POST /api/auth/logout` with the access token and/or refresh token; it revokes the token id and the whole session family [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts; apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:451-485).

### 6. Chrome extension link to the web session
The extension does not run its own sign-in form. `openClerkSignIn` opens `<web origin>/sign-in?redirectTo=/auth/chrome-extension` in a tab; `/sign-in` is a permanent redirect to `/login` [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/clerkAuth.ts:216-223; apps/web/next.config.ts:155). The page `/auth/chrome-extension` only reports signed-in or signed-out and tells the person to return to the side panel [code] (apps/web/app/auth/chrome-extension/page.tsx). The extension's Clerk client uses `syncHost` (the web origin from `CLERK_SYNC_HOST`) so it mirrors the web session, and requires a token whose `azp` claim equals the extension's own origin [code] (clerkAuth.ts:84-92, 129-135). Cookie changes on the sync host (`__client_uat*`) trigger a re-read, so signing out on the web signs the extension out [code] (clerkAuth.ts `watchSyncHostSession`). Extension sign-out also DELETEs the synced web session by id [code] (clerkAuth.ts:247-280). A dev-only bearer in `chrome.storage.local` exists in development builds [code] (freeTrialClient.ts:371, 409).

### 7. Session length
- Product cap: any session older than `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME_HOURS` (default 720 h = 30 days, measured from creation) is refused and ended; the provider's own idle expiry also applies [code] (apps/web/lib/auth/session-policy.ts:1-60; api-auth.ts `assertSessionWithinAbsoluteLifetime`).
- Provider-side idle length is a Clerk dashboard setting, not in the repo [unknown].
- Device grants: access 7 days, refresh 30 days (above).

### 8. 18-and-over step
`ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE` is 18 [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:1). The server stores only an outcome (`eligible` or `ineligible`), the minimum it was judged against and how it was reached; never the age [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0425_adult_eligibility.sql; adult-eligibility.ts). A decision counts only while its minimum is at least the current one. `api:GET /api/eligibility` reads state; `api:POST /api/eligibility` submits evidence (`declared_age`, `age_checked_on_device`, `platform_age_signal`) [code] (apps/web/app/api/eligibility/route.ts). An `ineligible` outcome is final until support reviews it [code] (adult-eligibility.ts comment). Confirmed state is cached 5 minutes per server instance [code] (adult-eligibility.ts:55).

### 9. Linked devices and sign-out everywhere
- Every non-web surface registers with `api:POST /api/devices/heartbeat` (rate limit `device-heartbeat`, CSRF), which upserts `table:device_registrations` keyed by user, surface and install id and links the credential family and identity session id [code] (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts). CLI calls it after login [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1052; device_registry.rs:6).
- `api:GET /api/settings/devices` lists them; `api:DELETE /api/settings/devices/{deviceId}` unlinks one (options `lost` and `logoutAll`), `PATCH` renames, `POST` stops remote work [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts:431-433).
- `api:GET /api/settings/sessions` lists provider sessions and ends any past lifetime; `api:DELETE /api/settings/sessions/{sessionId}` ends one; `api:DELETE /api/settings/sessions` is **sign out everywhere**: CSRF, step-up proof (`session.revoke_all`), revokes every other provider session, then the current one, and revokes every device refresh credential; sends a security notice; on partial failure answers 502 with counts so the caller can retry [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:189-274).

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Every authenticated API request** passes, in order: token verification (developer token, then identity-provider token with authorized-party check, then native token plus surface proof), absolute session lifetime, account status (`active` only; `locked`, `recovery_pending`, `suspended`, `banned`, `deletion_scheduled`, `deleted` are refused; fail-closed after one retry), account security (passkey or step-up where required), MFA policy for workspaces, and IP allow-list [code] (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:452-480; account-status.ts:1-10; docs/security/security.md:345 [requirement]).

**Token-class restrictions.**
- A surface token used as a Bearer is refused (`surface_token_as_bearer`) [code] (api-auth.ts:365-368).
- A developer-token session may not approve a device or grant a desktop sign-in; it needs an interactive session [code] (approve/route.ts:45; desktop/grant/route.ts).
- API keys work only on endpoints that declare an API-key scope [code] (api-auth.ts:437-447).

**Terms.** Device approval, device token and refresh each re-check Terms acceptance; a poller keeps its approved code and waits while the person accepts on the web [code] (token/route.ts:155-170).

**18-and-over enforcement points (server).** Enforced: `/login/complete`, device approve, device token and refresh, product page layouts (chat, tasks, code, workspace, quick-ask, admin, welcome), the LLM chat-completions gate, embeddings, audio transcription, speech, live voice sessions, image and video generation, and mobile intents [code] (grep of `adult-eligibility` and `requireAdultEligibility` across apps/web/app and apps/web/lib). Not enforced on every API route: settings, billing, export and deletion deliberately stay reachable [code] (require-adult-eligibility.ts comment). An unreadable decision refuses, never admits (503) [code] (adult-eligibility-gate.ts).

**Modes and plans.**

| Mode | Account needed to sign in? | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| mode:local (mobile) | No account. The device asks for age first (18 threshold, or higher by region rule) before any screen; sign-in appears only when the person chooses Cloud | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts:38-60; ageGate.ts:56-70) |
| mode:local (CLI, VS Code) | No account; local models and BYOK work without `agi login` | [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1013, "Run `agi login` for your AGI account, or `agi login <provider>` to use your own API key") |
| mode:own-key (CLI, VS Code) | Provider API key saved in keyring or SecretStorage; no AGI sign-in required | [code] (auth.rs API_KEY_PROVIDERS; extension-vscode utils/api.ts:228-237) |
| mode:cloud (all) | AGI account, adult-eligibility confirmed, Terms accepted; plan rules then apply elsewhere | [code] (device/approve, token routes; llm auth-gate.ts:282) |

Entitlement and quota decisions are not made by the sign-in code. Device scope `managed-cloud:use` says only "subject to plan and workspace permissions" [code] (device/code/route.ts:41-46). See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for how a turn is gated after identity.

**Trust boundary.** Signing in must not silently move a Local chat to Cloud or BYOK [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6). On mobile, sign-in and session refresh run through the provider SDK and reach the provider hosts in either mode; only the listed account controls pass the egress guard in Local [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:47).

| surface:web | `/login`, `/signup`: email, code, password, passkey, provider buttons, enterprise SSO | Provider session cookie | Provider sign-out; settings page can end other sessions or all | Guest chat on `/chat` without session (proxy leaves `/chat` open); signed-in needed for the rest of product routes [code] (proxy.ts:324-330) |
| surface:desktop (Electron, public) | System browser, challenge and code hand-off, then ticket in the window | `persist:agi-cloud` partition | Page reports signed-out account; shell switches window to sign-in screen | The window shows the hosted app; signed-out window shows the sign-in screen [code] (main.ts followSignedInState ~766-780). Local-folder features need no AGI account [inferred; not opened] |
| surface:desktop (Tauri, retained internal) | Device-code flow (`desktopNativeSignIn.ts`) | Native store | [unknown] | [unknown] |
| surface:mobile | Native screens with Clerk hooks; Apple, Google and others; age check on account | Secure token cache; surface proof per request | `signOut` ends this session or hands over to another saved account; `signOutAllAccounts` ends every session on this device only | None for Local; age gate first [code] |
| surface:cli | Device code in terminal (`agi login`) | OS keyring or owner-only file | `agi logout`: revokes the device session on the server and forgets caches | None for local models or BYOK |

**Notable asymmetries.** Mobile "sign out of all accounts" ends sessions on this phone, not on every device; the account-wide action is in Settings, Account security (`DELETE /api/settings/sessions`) [code] (store.ts:277-281; mobile account-security/service.ts:171-186). CLI and VS Code never hold a provider session cookie; they hold a signed developer token the server can revoke by family. Chrome and Mobile tokens are provider tokens, so revocation is by provider session id.

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
| Situation | Behaviour | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Authorized-party allowlist unresolvable | Proxy answers 503 for session routes | [code] proxy.ts:217-224, 340 |
| Desktop link used twice, after relaunch, after cancel, or from a different attempt | Shell reports `expired`; window shows expired notice; person restarts | [code] browserSignIn.ts `readBrowserSignInLink` |
| Desktop redeem fails (code expired or used) | 404 "expired or already used"; complete page offers "Continue in your browser" and "Sign in here instead" | [code] redeem/route.ts; DesktopSignInComplete.tsx |
| Browser cannot open from desktop shell | Screen state `unopened` | [code] signInScreen.ts |
| Device code unknown, expired, already processed | 404 or 409 with a message to restart | [code] device/code route GET, approve |
| Device poll too fast | `slow_down` with new interval; CLI adds 5 s | [code] token/route.ts:51-70; oauth.rs |
| Device approval while Terms outdated | 403 with `acceptanceUrl`; poll returns `terms_acceptance_required` and keeps the code approved | [code] approve, token routes |
| Account suspended between approval and poll | `account_unavailable` with recovery URL; no token issued | [code] token/route.ts:110-130 |
| Refresh token replayed | Family marked compromised and revoked; owner notified | [code] refresh/route.ts, refresh-token-family.ts |
| Revocation lookup fails | Developer-token requests are denied with 503, not allowed | [code] api-auth.ts:330-340 |
| Sign-out everywhere partly fails | 502 with counts; current session kept; retry finishes | [code] settings/sessions/route.ts:216-236 |
| Stale client session reaches `/login/complete` | Recovery screen; one automatic retry marker `authRetry=1`; no redirect loop | [code] login/complete/page.tsx:52-62 |
| Age decision unreadable | 503 `age_eligibility_unavailable`; no admission | [code] adult-eligibility-gate.ts |
| Secure storage unavailable (mobile) | Dedicated screen | [code] apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/SecureStorageUnavailable.tsx (file exists) |
| OS keyring locked (CLI) | Message explains unlock or `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` | [code] auth.rs:175 |
| Region blocked | 451 JSON for API, rewritten page for browsers, before identity runs | [code] proxy.ts:240-262 |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Everything here is [proposed] unless a requirement is cited.

- [requirement] Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud stay separate trust boundaries; sign-in never reroutes Local work (AGENTS.md section 6).
- [requirement] Local inference on mobile and desktop must not need a paid plan. Whether it needs an account is open; today mobile Local needs none (see Rules).
- [proposed] State the provider-side session idle length in code or a doc owned by `docs/security/security.md`, so engineers need not open the provider dashboard.
- [proposed] Give the Chrome extension a stated signed-out behaviour in one place.
- [proposed] Make Mobile "sign out all accounts" wording say it affects this device only, and link to account-wide sign-out.
- [proposed] Apply the 18-and-over gate through one shared function at the API layer rather than per route, so a new route cannot forget it.

key_facts.fact: The identity provider is Clerk by default, selected through a port; `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` can name another provider but only `clerk` is implemented.
Web proxy returns 503 for session routes if the authorized-party allowlist cannot be resolved, instead of authenticating without the origin check.
A signed-out visitor to a protected product route is redirected to /login with redirectTo, but /chat is exempt from the cookie check.
Desktop sign-in uses a PKCE-like hand-off: the shell keeps a random verifier in memory, sends its SHA-256 challenge to the browser, and redeems a one-time code with the verifier.
The desktop pending attempt lives 10 minutes; the server grant and the sign-in ticket live 60 seconds; the grant is stored only as a hash.
The desktop deep link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud and the host is sign-in.
Redeem is accepted only in a desktop host that reports browser sign-in support, so a grant opened in an ordinary browser fails.
CLI, VS Code and (in the Tauri build) desktop link through an RFC 8628 device grant: code issued with 900 s life and 5 s poll interval, approved on /auth/device, exchanged at /api/auth/device/token.
Device access tokens are web-signed JWTs valid 7 days; refresh tokens are 32 random bytes stored as SHA-256 hashes and valid 30 days, rotated on use.
A replayed refresh token marks its whole family compromised and revokes it.
Device approval is refused for developer-token callers, when the account has device sign-in switched off, when Terms need acceptance, or when no current 18-and-over decision exists.
Mobile Cloud calls send the Clerk session token as Bearer plus a Clerk-template surface proof in a separate header; the server admits a native token only with a matching proof.
Mobile root routing requires a device-level age gate before any screen, then lets signed-out users stay in the app; sign-in screens open only on request or when a ended session is owed.
The Chrome extension reuses the web session through Clerk syncHost, requires a token whose azp equals the extension origin, and opens /sign-in which redirects to /login.
The minimum account age is 18 on every surface; the server stores only outcome, minimum age, method and time, never the age.
An age decision made under a lower minimum no longer counts and the person is asked again; an ineligible outcome stands.

Server-side 18-and-over enforcement covers login-complete, device grant, product page layouts, LLM chat, embeddings, transcription, speech, live voice, image and video generation and mobile intents, not every API route.
Sign out everywhere is DELETE /api/settings/sessions: it needs CSRF and a step-up proof, ends all other provider sessions, then the current one, and revokes every device refresh credential.
Product session cap defaults to 30 days from creation (SESSION_ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME_HOURS), on top of the provider's idle expiry.
The provider-side session length is not in the repository.
evidence: apps/web/lib/auth/session-policy.ts comment says the provider's expiry renews on use

key_facts.fact: Linked devices are rows in device_registrations created by POST /api/devices/heartbeat and managed through /api/settings/devices.
CLI credentials sit in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) or an owner-only file when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1; VS Code uses SecretStorage.
apps/cli/src/trust/identity.rs is workspace identity for trust grants (git remote key), not account sign-in.
CLI logout posts to /api/auth/logout, which revokes the token id and the whole session family, or the family named by a refresh token.
Enabled web sign-in providers come from AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS among google, github, microsoft, apple; default google and github.
Sign-in, device approval and token issue do not check a plan; plan gating happens after identity.
No document in the repository was found recording a real run of these sign-in flows.

doc.summary: Every cloud request resolves a user, then a workspace (Personal, or one organization the user actively belongs to). The database repeats that check with row-level security (RLS) for the restricted app_rls role. Inside a workspace, roles bundle permissions and projects, chats, artifacts and connectors can be shared. Source-reading guards keep server code from skipping RLS. Nothing here has been run by this page's author.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers who may do what in the cloud side of AGI Workforce, and how the server ties a request to a person and a workspace.

**Terms.**
- **Account**: one person. The account id is the identity provider's subject mapped to an internal id (`userId`).
- **Organization**: the billed tenant (a team or company). Table `table:organizations`.
- **Workspace**: the container content lives in. Two kinds: Personal (the row has `organization_id` NULL) and Organization. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/workspace.ts:1-6, apps/web/lib/server/workspace-scope/index.ts:47-50). Migration 0234 adds a `workspaces` table, but the live code scopes by `organization_id`; see Gaps.
- **Membership**: a row in `table:organization_members` with a `role` and a `status`. Only status `active` carries access. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/workspace.ts:40-47).
- **RLS (row-level security)**: the database refuses rows the caller may not see, even if the application forgets a `where` clause.

**Why it exists.** The product sells team and enterprise controls (admin visibility, shared projects, governed content, removal of departed members). Personal content must stay personal, and an admin may read only the active workspace's content, never personal content. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0110_active_workspace_content_scope.sql:1-14, apps/web/lib/server/workspace-scope/index.ts:98-105).

**Scope of the model.** [inferred] This is a server and database model. The six apps do not enforce it themselves; they send a bearer token (or the web session cookie) and, optionally, a workspace selector header. Local content on a device (mode:local) never reaches this layer; see Rules.

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline (turns run under the scope resolved here).

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Who is calling (authentication)
`getClerkAuthUser` in apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:427 accepts three credential kinds:
1. **API key** (`sk_live_` or `sk_test_` prefix). Allowed only on routes that declare an `apiKeyScope`, and only if the key carries that scope. [code] (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:436-448)
2. **Bearer token**: a developer (device) token, an identity-provider session token, or a native session token. A session token that itself carries a surface claim is refused as a bearer. [code] (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:~340-420)
3. **Cookie session** (web), through `getCookieSessionAuthUser` (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:494).

After the credential is accepted, the same gates run: absolute session lifetime, account lifecycle active (`assertAccountActive`, :205), account-security step, workspace MFA policy, IP allow list, tenant lockdown. [code] (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:205-230, 449-520)

### 2. Which workspace (the active organization)
`resolveActiveOrganizationId` (apps/web/lib/services/active-workspace-service.ts:63) decides it in this order:
1. Request header `x-agi-organization-id` (constant `MANAGED_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION_HEADER`, packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversation-contract.json:5). The value `personal` means Personal (NULL). A malformed value gives 400. A value for an organization where the caller has no `active` membership gives 403 `You are not a member of that workspace`.
2. A cached selection (re-checked against membership; a stale one is cleared).
3. The saved selection in `user_settings.settings.workspace.activeOrganizationId`, joined to an `active` membership.
If the lookup itself fails, the request is denied with 503 (fail closed). [code] (apps/web/lib/server/rls-db.ts:56-68)

The selection is changed with `PUT /api/settings/organization/active` (body `{organizationId: uuid|null}`), under an advisory lock, with CSRF and a rate limit. [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/active/route.ts:11-40)

### 3. How the database learns the scope
`getUserScopedDb(request, options)` (apps/web/lib/server/rls-db.ts:116) returns `{db, userId, organizationId, surface}`:
- For a session token or cookie, it builds a pooled adapter `getRlsCapableDb().withUser(token).withOrg(organizationId)`. Inside each transaction the data layer runs `SET LOCAL ROLE app_rls` and sets `request.jwt.claim.sub` and `request.jwt.claim.org_id`. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/rls-db.ts:81-105, packages/platform/data-layer/src/adapters/sql-session.ts:52-56)
- `withUser` decodes the token subject without checking the signature, so it is default-deny: it throws unless the adapter was built with `unsafeAllowUnverifiedJwtSubject: true`, and the web code verifies the token first. [code] (packages/platform/data-layer/src/adapters/neon.ts:504-522, apps/web/lib/server/rls-db.ts:30-37)
- For an API key, or for an owner policy recovery route, it uses `createClaimedUserScopedDb`, which runs the same `set local role app_rls` and `set_config` calls on the service connection. It cannot be rebound to another user. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/claimed-user-scope-db.ts:20-72)
- The other handle, `getNeonDb()` (apps/web/lib/server/neon-db.ts), is the privileged owner connection. It bypasses RLS. Code using it must carry the user and workspace predicate by hand. [code] (apps/web/scripts/../../../scripts/check-rls-boundary.mjs:13)

### 4. What the database enforces
The current rule for the content tables (`web_conversations`, `user_projects`, `web_artifacts`, `user_memories`, `scheduled_tasks`, `cloud_agent_runs`, `user_connectors`, `user_custom_connectors`, `search_history`, and more) is `app_row_is_visible(user_id, organization_id)` as last defined in migration 0272:
- The owner sees a row only when its `organization_id` equals the active org (NULL equals NULL for Personal), and, for an org row, only while still an active member.
- Someone else sees an org row only if it belongs to the active org and they hold the `content.govern` permission.
- Personal rows are never visible from inside an organization, and the reverse. An admin cannot read personal content.
[code] (apps/web/db/neon/0272_active_membership_authorization.sql:76-90). `app_row_is_writable` (migration 0110, lines ~34-45) lets a caller write only their own row, in the active workspace, and only if a member of it. [code]

If the GUCs are unset, the helper functions return NULL and every comparison fails closed. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0073_tenancy_foundation.sql, header "Fails closed")

### 5. Roles and permissions
A role is a named set of permissions. Built-in roles live in `table:organization_roles` with `organization_id` NULL: `primary_owner`, `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0200_organization_permission_grid.sql:~96-140)
- The membership column `organization_members.role` holds `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `viewer`. `owner` means the single **Primary Owner** (unique index from 0085). Only the Primary Owner holds `ownership.transfer`, `workspace.delete`, `billing.contracts.manage`; a check constraint forbids any other role from carrying them. [code] (0200 constraints `organization_roles_primary_owner_permissions`)
- A member's permissions are the union of: the built-in role for their membership role, extra roles in `organization_member_roles`, and roles of every SCIM directory group they belong to. Only `status = 'active'` members get any (migration 0272). [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0272_active_membership_authorization.sql:5-58)
- SQL helper `app_has_org_permission(org, key)` (0200:328) answers policies. TypeScript `requireMemberPermission` (apps/web/lib/services/organization-permission-service.ts:95) answers routes, calling `evaluateAuthorization`.
- Permission keys exist in two forms: legacy (`content.read`, `sharing.manage`, `members.manage` ...) stored on grants and used by RLS, and canonical (`feature.content.view`, `admin.members.manage` ...). A resolved set carries both and `manage` implies `view`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/permissions.ts:1-80, apps/web/db/neon/0248_permission_namespaces_and_scim_group_membership_lock.sql header)
- A role grant is refused unless the granter holds every permission in it (no self-escalation), enforced in WITH CHECK of the grant tables and in TypeScript (`permissionsBeyondGranter`). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/authorization.ts:~85-100)
- `evaluateAuthorization` runs five stages in order and the first refusal wins: membership, entitlement (plan features), permission, policy (feature switches, allowed surfaces, allowed countries, reasoning-effort cap), rollout. Personal scope (organizationId null) is allowed outright. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/authorization.ts:20-26, 180-290)
- Team administration also needs the plan capability `team_admin` (plans team, team_premium, enterprise); SSO, SCIM and admin controls need `enterprise_controls` (enterprise only). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:362-363, apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts:21)

### 6. Workspace administration routes
About 48 route files under `/api/settings/organization/*` manage the workspace (members, invitations, roles, groups, policy, audit, shared items, keys, retention, legal holds, spend limit, plugins, MCP, data region, ownership transfer, leave). Most call `resolveWorkspaceApiCaller(request, route, method)`, which looks the route up in `WORKSPACE_ROUTE_ACCESS` (route, method, one permission, whether workspace API keys are allowed). A route absent from the table is closed to automation. Order inside: member check, `team_admin` entitlement, then permission. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/service-principals/caller.ts:39-75, apps/web/lib/server/service-principals/route-access.ts:24)

Workspace admin API keys have the prefix `agiadm_` and carry permission scopes. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/admin-api-keys.ts:19)

### 7. Joining, leaving, removal
- **Invitations**: 7-day lifetime, at most 10 resends, token stored hashed; roles invitable are admin, member, viewer. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/organization-invitation-service.ts:16-19)
- **Leave**: a non-owner leaves by deleting their own membership. The Primary Owner must name an active successor who passes an entitlement check; the old owner becomes admin first. A sole owner cannot leave. Advisory locks serialise it. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/organization-membership-service.ts:117-226)
- **Removal by an admin**: `DELETE /api/settings/organization/members/{userId}` runs `removeMember`, drops the cached active-workspace entry, then `deprovisionMember`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/members/[userId]/route.ts:96-140)
- **Deprovision** revokes what this workspace issued: provider sessions (only if the member's recorded selection was this workspace), device refresh-token families for the (user, organization) pair, mobile Siri/intent tokens, API keys for that pair, and unshares connectors the leaver shared. Each step is independent; failures are returned as `errors`, not thrown. Personal credentials are not touched. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/deprovision-service.ts:176-291)

### 8. Sharing
| Thing | Audience options | Who may change | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project | whole workspace (`default_access` read), invited members only (`none`), per-member `read`/`write` grants | someone with `sharing.manage`, or the project's owner if their role holds `content.share` | `table:organization_shared_projects`, `table:organization_project_access`; RLS 0086/0200/0315/0316 |
| Project edit (write) | only an explicit per-member `write` grant, and only while the member still holds `content.share` | as above | RLS policies 0217, re-stated in 0358; the share's default never confers write |
| Conversation (shared session) | `public` (anyone with the 24-character token, until expiry) or `organization` (members holding the grant row) | the share's owner | `table:shared_sessions`, `table:organization_shared_sessions` (0186) |
| Artifact, connector, schedule, skill | workspace-wide shares | owner with `content.share` or admin | `organization_shared_artifacts` (0184), `organization_shared_connectors`, `scheduled_task_shares` (0311), skill share route |
[code] (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:72-130, 216-270; apps/web/db/neon/0315_private_shared_projects.sql, 0316_project_owner_sharing.sql, 0358_shared_project_editor_needs_share_permission.sql, 0186_organization_shared_sessions.sql)

A project is readable if the caller owns it in the active workspace, or it is shared into the active org and the caller's effective access (`coalesce(grant, default_access)`) is `read` or `write`. That rule is written once as `READABLE_PROJECT_SCOPE_SQL` for statements on the privileged connection. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/project-read-access.ts:7-46)

Reading a shared session: `GET /api/share/{token}` tries the public row first on the privileged connection (needs `visibility = 'public'`), then falls back to the signed-in cookie user's RLS connection for organization-only shares. Expired shares answer 410. [code] (apps/web/app/api/share/[token]/route.ts:46-100)

### 9. Platform admin (operators) is separate
Platform operators are user ids listed in the environment variable named `AGI_PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS`. An organization `owner` or `admin` never qualifies. A non-operator, or a device token, gets 404, not 403. An unset list denies everyone. [code] (apps/web/lib/auth-guards.ts:26-52, apps/web/features/admin/lib/platform-admin-access.ts:6-24). Routes under `/api/admin/*` are checked by `check:admin-route-guards`. Operator access to a customer's content goes through time-limited support access grants with scopes (conversations, files, projects, connectors, billing, audit_logs, workspace_settings, background_jobs) and a hash-chained trail. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/support-access-service.ts:11-30)

### 10. Identity provisioning
SSO and SCIM 2.0 exist under apps/web/lib/server/sso and apps/web/lib/server/scim, with the SCIM endpoints under `/api/scim/v2`. SCIM-owned group membership may only be written by the provisioner (migration 0248). [code] (docs/compliance/directory-sync.md:1-25, apps/web/db/neon/0248_permission_namespaces_and_scim_group_membership_lock.sql header)

**Database roles.** `app_rls` is a NOLOGIN role without BYPASSRLS; user queries run as it. The owner role bypasses RLS and is used by `getNeonDb()`. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0037_rls_user_isolation.sql:60-80)

[code] (apps/web/lib/services/active-workspace-service.ts:90-100, apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/members/[userId]/route.ts:118) The IP allow list has its own cache (apps/web/lib/services/organization-ip-allow-list-cache.ts). Guard `check:workspace-cache-scope` covers cache keys.

**Device stores.** [unknown] No device store holds authorization decisions in the files read. Mobile reads and sets the workspace through `/api/settings/organization` and `/api/settings/organization/active` (apps/mobile/src/features/team/service.ts:68,123). The CLI caches the effective workspace policy in a sealed file keyed through the OS keychain service name `com.agiworkforce.cli.workspace-policy`, refreshed hourly, usable up to 7 days old. [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/workspace_policy.rs:14-24)

**What a workspace switch changes.** `WORKSPACE_SWITCH_SURFACES` lists each surface as partitioned (chat history, projects, artifacts, memory, and others), account-wide, or organization-only. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/workspace-scope/switch-surfaces.ts:25-60)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Plan rules.** [code]
- Creating or administering a team needs plan capability `team_admin`: plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:362). SSO, SCIM and admin controls need `enterprise_controls`: plan:enterprise only (billing-catalog.ts:363).
- When an organization has no subscription of its own, team administration follows the owner's personal plan; handing ownership to someone whose plan lacks the capability fails with 409 `ORG_TRANSFER_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/organization-membership-service.ts:60-80)
- Individual plans are not gates for Personal scope: personal scope allows everything the entitlement system allows; `evaluateAuthorization` returns allowed for a null workspace. Quotas and usage accounting are a different layer; see SYS-chat-turn-pipeline and the subscription pages. [inferred]
- Product decision (owner memory, not a project document): no subscription sales on any surface before 2027-01-01. That bears on who can hold paid team seats today. [unknown] whether code gates this; not read.

**Mode rules.**
| Mode | Authorization behavior |
|---|---|
| mode:cloud | Full model on this page. Every request is authenticated, scoped to a user and a workspace, and the database enforces RLS. |
| mode:own-key | [inferred] A request that still goes through our server (account, sync, sharing) is authorized the same way. A call straight from the device to a provider is outside this layer. The requirement is that Local-to-BYOK is an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label (AGENTS.md section 6, [requirement]). Not traced in this page. |
| mode:local | [requirement] Local inference on mobile and desktop does not require a paid plan (task brief). [unknown] What the code requires for sign-in in local mode was not read here. Nothing in this layer is consulted for content that never leaves the device. |

**Trust boundary rule.** Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6).

**Hard rules the code enforces.**
1. Inactive members get nothing: `suspended`, `deprovisioned` and `invited` memberships give no permissions and no workspace content. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0272_active_membership_authorization.sql:5-20, 62-73)
2. An admin sees other members' rows only in the active organization, never personal rows. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/workspace-scope/index.ts:98-125)
3. Only the Primary Owner can transfer ownership, delete the workspace, or manage the billing contract. [code] (0200 constraints; packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/authorization.ts:~228)
4. Viewer is read-only: `content.read` and nothing else; a viewer cannot share into the workspace or hold write access on a shared project. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0200_organization_permission_grid.sql header; 0358 header)
5. A role grant cannot exceed what the granter holds. [code] (authorization.ts:85-100)
6. Platform operator access is by an environment allowlist, not by org role; customer admins cannot confirm the operator surface exists (404). [code] (apps/web/lib/auth-guards.ts:10-14)
7. Workspace API keys reach only routes listed in `WORKSPACE_ROUTE_ACCESS`, at the same permission a person needs. [code] (route-access.ts:18-24)
8. A public share link is a bearer capability: anyone with the token reads it until expiry; `organization` visibility closes the anonymous page. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/org-shared-session-service.ts:15-21)
