sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
**Deadlines** (all in apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts) [code]

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Function limit (`CHAT_COMPLETIONS_FUNCTION_LIMIT_MS`) | 300 s | Matches route `maxDuration` |
| Teardown reserve | 60 s | Kept for cleanup |
| Tool loop budget / provider stream deadline | 240 s | Limit minus reserve |
| Tool call deadline | 120 s | Per tool, clamped to remaining loop budget (`nestedDeadlineMs`, floor 1 s) |
| Turn first-token budget | 40 s | Whole turn across attempts |
| Provider first-token deadline | 25 s | Per attempt, clamped by what is left of the 40 s |
| Durable stream silence | 150 s | Tool-call deadline plus 30 s margin; silent runs end with code `run_stream_silent`, 'nothing further was charged' |
| Durable stream detach | 240 s | Connection is detached with `x_run_detached` reason `function_budget`; the run continues and the client follows by run id |
| SSE heartbeat | every 2 s | Keeps intermediaries from timing out |

**Provider failures before the first byte**: `startProviderStreamWithinTurnDeadlines` peeks the first chunk. A retryable error is retried on the SAME route with backoff (up to 2 attempts; overload class has its own larger limit; never for auth or context overflow) while the first-token budget has room. If that fails, `failover.next` may rotate to the next planned route, only if the first-token budget is not spent. (lib/provider-deadlines.ts:27-312; route.ts:1284-1325)

**Failover rules** (lib/managed-failover.ts) [code]: rotate on availability classes (connection, server error, overload, capacity off-switch, timeout, rate limit, quota exhausted, empty response, unsupported input) and on a rejected credential (that provider account is skipped). Never rotate on billing exhausted, safety or content-blocked, or aborts. A pinned model may cross providers but is never answered by another model; Auto may change model. Once a provider minted tool-call ids the turn stays on it (from the second step). An unfunded account gets at most one Auto rotation. Rotation happens only before any content reaches the client, so failed-attempt text cannot leak. All attempts share one reservation; settlement is priced by the serving model.

**When no route works**: the reservation is refunded (`refundFailedReservation`, settles a free-trial or finalizes managed usage as failed with zero cost), a failed-turn record is stored (`recordFailedTurn`), and an upstream error response is built with provider-neutral copy. (route.ts:1301-1330; lib/failed-turn-record.ts; lib/upstream-error-copy.ts)

**Errors after streaming began**: the stream cannot change status, so the error is sent as a frame, billing settles as failed (zero), the partial answer is saved as truncated, and the stream errors. (stream-transform.ts:700-760)

**Stop**: closing the request aborts the provider call. For plain streams `cancel()` settles billing as failed-cancelled (billed on delivered text only) and saves the partial answer with `truncated` true. For runs, `stopGeneration` aborts locally and calls the cancel endpoint, then confirms; if not confirmed it shows 'Cloud task has not confirmed it stopped'. The finish reason of a stopped turn is `STOPPED_FINISH_REASON` and it keeps a Continue action. (stream-transform.ts:921-940; useChatStream.ts:5390-5460, 3793-3830)

**Client recovery**: on a dropped connection with a run handle the client replays the durable run; without one it resumes from the persisted turn by cursor; frames carry a sequence envelope, duplicates are skipped, and a gap makes the client wait for cursor replay instead of trusting `[DONE]`. An empty answer with no tool call and no error gets one silent retry (`-retry` idempotency suffix). A 401 or terms/passkey requirement parks the unsent draft and redirects. (useChatStream.ts:3232-3262, 3780-3830, 4440-4460, 4795-4830)

**Other refusals**: 413 payload too large, 400 validation or `secret_detected`, 403 policy/spend/terms, 429 `concurrent_turn_limit_reached`, 503 `user_message_persistence_failed`, `billing_unavailable`, `attachment_load_unavailable`, `mcp_context_unavailable`, project-context failure. (code citations above)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Status labels: [requirement] means a project document states it; [proposed] is this page's suggestion.

- **One metered path**: Cloud is the only mode that reaches the completions route and the AGI Subscription ledger; Local and own-key never route to it silently, and a move from Local to cloud is an explicit fork with consent. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6; trust-mode matrix)
- **Routing order**: workspace policy, commercial status, trust mode, harness reachability, lifecycle stage, zero data retention and capabilities admit routes; health, credentials and cost then rank them. An explicit model choice rotates among same-model routes first. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md)
- **Billing follows the model, cost follows the route**: the user is debited the model's official price, the served route's price is recorded as provider cost. [requirement] (same document); implemented in settleStreamBilling [code]
- **Every managed turn survives the connection**: the route header comment says a turn holding a free-tier or managed reservation starts on the durable transport. [requirement-in-code-comment] Today only tool-loop turns do (see Gaps). [proposed] Either make plain chat durable, or correct the comment.
- **Execution boundaries made visible**: the client should show which of Device, AGI servers or an outside provider ran each part of a turn (tool runs on our sandbox, connector calls to outside services, model on a provider). [proposed]
- **Cost as a design constraint**: routing weighs cost and quality; a stronger model is not a default. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 7)

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Implementation status (is it there and connected) is separated from verification (has anyone run it).

**Implementation gaps** [code unless noted]

1. The route's header comment says a managed or free-tier turn starts on the durable Workflow transport 'whatever the tier'. In the code read, the durable attempt sits inside the tool-loop and research branches only; the plain adapter stream and non-stream branches are request-scoped and die with the connection (the server still saves what it had, as truncated). (route.ts:162-196 vs 898-1024, 1239-1345)
2. The web client contains a Local turn path while the policy matrix says Web has no Local. It is only reachable when a host bridge answers `local_chat_start`; the public Electron shell refuses these commands, so the reachable host is the internal Tauri build. (runtime-client.ts:621-646; dispatcher.ts:3235-3244; trust-mode matrix)
3. The harness catalog lists `vscode/byok-chat` and `vscode/local-chat` as unwired and `cli/local-chat` as partial, though policy permits them. (docs/generated/trust-mode-surface-matrix.md)
4. Deep Research is paid-only and its durable path starts only after a plan is approved (`approvedResearchRun`); an unapproved research run uses the request-scoped loop. (route.ts:628-700)
5. Title generation is skipped for free-quota offering models, which keep the truncated title. (persist-message.ts:198)

**Verification gaps** [unknown]

- No project document read records a real end-to-end run of this pipeline. No test, build or app was run for this page, so every statement is from reading code, not execution. Tests exist for failover, first-token deadline, stream parity, memory and persistence (see Implementation map), but their pass state is unknown.
- Real provider behaviour under outage, durable transport breaker behaviour in production, and the 500 ms durable first-event default under load are unverified.

**Documentation maintenance**: the pipeline spans files of 7000 and 8000 lines (request-processor.ts, tool-loop.ts); there is no single maintained architecture page for it before this one. [inferred]

2. Failover and deadlines: run test:apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/__tests__/route.managed-failover.test.ts, route.first-token-deadline.test.ts and lib/managed-failover.policy.test.ts through the apps/web package script (not the root vitest; AGENTS.md section 12 warns the versions differ). [requirement]
3. Wire stability: stream-transform.byte-parity, openai-byte-parity and response-builder.golden tests. Persistence: assistant-turn-persistence tests; memory: request-processor.memory.test.ts and turn-context.test.ts.
4. Local boundary: test:apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.local.test.ts and each surface's `trust-boundary.test.ts`; the guard `pnpm check:trust-boundaries`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)

[proposed] (owner memory notes on local testing; not executed)
6. Deadline math: DEADLINE_HIERARCHY in deadline-policy.ts is the machine-readable parent/child list; a guard or test comparing it to the route's `maxDuration` is [unknown].

key_facts.fact: Only Cloud (Managed Cloud) turns reach api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions; Local and BYOK never do.
The route has maxDuration 300 s; the tool-loop and provider stream budget is 240 s (300 s minus a 60 s teardown reserve).
The whole turn has a 40 s first-token budget; each provider attempt gets 25 s, clamped to what is left of the 40 s. Each tool call has a 120 s deadline.
Request order in the route: auth gate (rate limit, identity, CSRF, terms, age, subscription), turn slot, policy and spend gates, processRequest, secret gate, provider-start mark, dispatch.
The user message is persisted before any model call; if that fails the route returns 503 user_message_persistence_failed and sends no model request.

Context building (account memory, past chats, project files) runs in resolveInteractiveTurnContext; a loader failure continues without that source, but a project context failure fails closed with no model request.
Memory is off for temporary chats and, on the API surface, only on when memory_enabled is true; past-chat recall is never used on the API surface.
Provider dispatch goes through the ADAPTER_PROVIDERS table to adapters in packages/ai/providers/*; a provider not in the table fails as unsupported-provider and the reservation is refunded.

Failover rotates only before the first byte reaches the client, only on availability-class errors (and credential rejection), never on billing, safety or content-blocked; a pinned model is never answered by a different model; all attempts share one reservation settled at the serving model's price.
Same-route retry happens first: up to 2 attempts (overload class has its own limit), never for auth or context-overflow errors, and only while the 40 s first-token budget has room.

Tool loop default step budgets are 10 (chat), 100 (AGI Work), 20 (caller tools); exhausting the budget pauses the run on a checkpoint rather than killing it; manual approval saves a signed checkpoint before emitting x_tool_approval_request.

Tool-loop and research turns start on the durable Workflow transport unless AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS is off, the breaker is open, or the first event misses a 500 ms default budget (AGI_DURABLE_FIRST_EVENT_BUDGET_MS); then they fall back to an inline stream with the same wire. Plain chat is always inline.
A detached durable stream ends the connection with x_run_detached (reason function_budget) while the run continues; the web client and mobile follow the run by id.

Managed usage uses one reservation per turn (table managed_usage_requests) keyed by the Idempotency-Key; settlement bills list price of the serving model and records the served route's price as provider cost; failed turns bill zero; a stopped turn bills on delivered text only.

The server saves the assistant row (upsert by client-supplied assistant_message_id) at stream end, marking cancelled or incomplete turns truncated with reason stream_cancelled; temporary conversations are not saved.
The web client also saves its own copy through api:POST /api/chat/conversations/{id}/messages; a server-side edit guard returns a content-changed conflict, and a failed save marks metadataNotSaved.

Titles are two-stage: a truncated first-message title is set synchronously by the server; a fire-and-forget utility-model call (6 words, 24 output tokens, via managed route admission, cache and a conversation_title usage lease) replaces it; failures keep the truncated one.

Concurrent managed turns are capped per plan (billing catalog maxConcurrentTurns); over the cap returns 429 concurrent_turn_limit_reached and a limiter outage returns 503 concurrency_limiter_unavailable.

Local turns are decided from the model id prefix local:, run through a desktop-host bridge command local_chat_start (Ollama or LM Studio), accept text only, and never call the route, reserve compute or persist to the cloud.
The public Electron Desktop refuses on-device inference commands for chat; its local coding sessions use the bundled CLI.
Own-key (BYOK) is available in CLI by policy, permitted but marked unwired for VS Code in the harness catalog, and absent on Web, Desktop chat, Mobile and Chrome.
A conversation that holds Local turns cannot be continued with a cloud model from the web client, so local content is never uploaded.

Auth gate: a missing subscription is the Free website plan; a lapsed paid plan is served as Free; an unpaid enterprise plan gets 403 subscription_inactive; terms and adult-eligibility checks apply to session callers.
The route comment claims every managed turn starts durable; code shows only tool-loop and research branches try the durable transport.
Secret-looking content is blocked (400 secret_detected, reservation refunded) or redacted before dispatch, and the count is returned in a header.
No document read records an executed end-to-end run of this pipeline; this page is from code reading only.

doc.summary: Beyond answering, the assistant calls tools through one server loop in the web app. Web search, sandboxed code, Office files, images, schedules and AGI Work all run on our servers (mode:cloud) and are charged to the subscription. sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
The assistant can act, not only reply. This page covers the "beyond answering" abilities: a catalog of tools the model may call, web search, code in a sandbox, Office file creation, image generation, artifacts, multi-step Work, approvals, scheduled tasks and their runner, event triggers, the cloud coding agent, browser actions through the Chrome extension, and computer use.

Why: the product competes with Claude and ChatGPT, which ship the same abilities. Cost and risk differ per ability, so each has its own gate. Established rules that shape this page: execution boundaries are explicit, subscription rules come from one AGI Subscription system, and local inference is free of any paid subscription [requirement] (task brief; AGENTS.md section 6 on Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud trust boundaries).

Plan names. Plan tier ids and display labels differ. `free`=Free, `basic`=Basic, `pro`=Premium, `max`=Max, `max_15x`=Ultra, `team`=Team, `team_premium`=Team Premium, `enterprise`=Enterprise, plus `local-only` (Local Mode) and `byok` (Local Mode + BYOK) [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:169-227). This page uses tier ids in relationships and labels in prose.

Path note: the brief names `apps/web/lib/chat/tool-loop.ts`, which does not exist. The real loop is `apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts` (7,993 lines) [code].

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### The tool loop (all hosted tools)
The hosted chat endpoint `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` (route.ts:1526) builds a tool list per turn, calls the model, and runs `runToolLoop`. The loop streams the model, pauses on tool calls, gates each call, executes it, appends results and calls the model again, up to a step budget. A step budget is cumulative; exhausting it pauses the run on a checkpoint instead of killing it [code] (tool-loop.ts:1-20).

Step limits are separate numbers: chat 10, caller-driven 20, Work 100, Cloud Code 12/24/48 (default 24), device steps per pause 8, tool calls per step 32 [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-call-limits.ts:2-5; device-steps.ts:17; packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:310-311). Planned Work steps are a different thing: the model plans up to 6 steps (`AGIWORK_PLAN_MAX_STEPS`, cloud-agent-runs.ts:84, minimum 3 in agiwork-plan.ts) and a stored plan holds up to 32 (work-plan-service.ts, `MAX_WORK_PLAN_STEPS`).

### Approvals: one gate, nine ranked rules
Every call goes through `resolveToolCallGate`. First matching rank wins [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-call-gate.ts:68-125):
1. User saved level `deny`: deny.
2. A device host is present and the tool is a device step: allow (the device side holds its own grant, see computer use below).
3. Saved level `allow` but the call completes the "lethal trifecta" (untrusted content in context, a reachable private source, and a tool that opens an outbound path): escalate.
4. Saved level `allow`: allow.
5. Saved level `ask`: ask.
6. Manual mode, no trifecta, and the account policy auto-approves this tool: allow.
7. Manual mode: ask.
8. Trifecta: escalate.
9. Otherwise: allow.

Escalate means ask a person; in an unattended run that cannot pause it means deny (tool-call-gate.ts:150-157).

The account policy has three values: `ask_every_time`, `auto_approve_read_only`, `autonomous` [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:3-7). If nothing is stored, a signed-in cloud account gets `autonomous` (line 13, used by `parseToolApprovalPolicy`, apps/web/shared/types/toolApprovalPolicy.ts:40-48). `ask_every_time` is the fail-closed value: no user, unreadable setting, or a workspace that forbids autonomy [code] (tool-approval-policy.ts:11, 93-101; web `loadToolApprovalPolicy` catch path, lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:56-62). Every workspace the user belongs to must permit autonomy (lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:33-41).

What the policy auto-approves (`policyAutoApprovesTool`, tool-metadata.ts:1083-1100): never a device step or a browser command; any tool flagged `autoInReadOnlyMode` (web search, page fetch, sandboxed code, places and maps); under `autonomous` any tool not destructive; under read-only any declared tool that is a read, reversible, and opens no outbound path. Destructive means: delete or external send, or a write or execute that cannot be undone (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-primitive.ts:163-176). So even under `autonomous`, `run_command`, `write_file`, `edit_file` and `delete_file` still ask (tool-metadata.ts:190-216, all `reversible:false`). MCP and connector tools are undeclared, so they force manual mode (tool-loop-routing.ts:56-65).

### Tool catalog (declared metadata)
`PLATFORM_TOOL_METADATA` declares each platform tool's action class, reversibility, whether it returns untrusted content, and whether it opens an outbound path (tool-metadata.ts:101-700+). Groups seen: directory and reconnect; web_search, url_fetch, search_maps, search_places, plan_itinerary, compare_products, render_answer_ui, ask_clarifying_questions; sandbox tools execute_code, run_command, write_file, edit_file, read_file, list_files, delete_file, create_folder; create_office_file; generate_image and edit_image; skill; memory tools (save, search, forget); search_files and open_file; create_schedule; draft_plugin; agi_work; `device_*` tools (files, calendar, reminders, shell, screen, mouse, keyboard, browser); and `browser_*` tools for the Chrome extension; then GitHub review tools. The listing was read to line 686 of 1,100; the tail is [unknown].

### Web search
Tool `web_search` returns up to 5 results per call, max 3 calls per turn (10 in a Work turn), query up to 400 chars, 15 s timeout (web-search-tool.ts:39-58). The configured backend is Perplexity's search API (web-search-providers.json; `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`). Some providers also offer their own native search; a gated function tool replaces it when approval is needed (required-search.ts:336-368). Cost: paid plans and automated callers (API, CLI, VS Code, scheduled, Work, research) are charged to managed credits per call; Free is limited to 20 calls per rolling 30 days and also held against Free usage windows (search-budget.ts:32-33, 58-64, 109-123, 129-141).

### Code in a sandbox
Tools `execute_code`, `write_file`, `read_file`, `edit_file`, `list_files`, `create_folder` run in an E2B sandbox when `e2bProvisioningReady()` is true: needs `AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1`, `E2B_API_KEY`, and a priceable compute rate (`AGI_E2B_COMPUTE_MICROUSD_PER_SECOND`) (lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-27). Otherwise, if the model supports it, the provider's own hosted code tool is used and code runs at the model provider, not in our sandbox (execution-tools.ts:204-266). One sandbox and kernel is reused per conversation, stored in Redis, paused at turn end, killed on conversation delete (runtime.ts header). Plan limits: Free 2 sandboxes and 60 min; Basic 5; Premium 10; Max and Ultra and Enterprise 20; all paid runs up to 24 h (billing-catalog.ts:531-532, 569-721; 473-476). Sandbox time is metered (`sandbox_compute`, compute-metering.ts). Unavailability causes shown to the user: not-configured, no-capacity, policy, over-quota, provider-error (e2b/unavailability.ts:10-16).

### Office files
Tool `create_office_file` builds Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV in the server process (docx, pptxgenjs, jsPDF libraries), verifies the package, and can edit an attached docx or xlsx; max generated file 20 MiB (managed-office-file-service.ts:123-155, 253; generated-file-persist.ts:17). Spreadsheets support real formulas and charts; recalculation and rendering use the sandbox template when configured (`officeRendering: e2bChatTemplate() !== null`).

### Image generation as a tool
`generate_image` and `edit_image` (one image per call) are offered only on surfaces web, desktop, mobile and chrome, only on plans with the `image_generation` capability (Premium and up), and only if image storage and a default provider are configured (image-chat-tools.ts:50-55, 107-130; billing-catalog.ts:341, 356). Each call uses account credits (tool description text). Results render as an interactive card.

### Artifacts
HTML, React, SVG, Mermaid, Markdown, text and code artifacts render in a separate-origin iframe (`infrastructure/sandbox/index.html`, deployed as its own Vercel project; web reaches it via `NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN`), speaking postMessage; the page's CSP blocks all network connections (index.html header; lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:3-14). Published artifacts get an unguessable URL stored in `public.published_artifacts`; they may use AI calls and saved data after publishing, up to 20 MB shared data and 20 MB per viewer, with plan caps on AI calls per app (50 Free to 600 Ultra) (chat-system-prompt.ts:130-146; billing-catalog.ts:530). Connected-app access in artifacts needs Premium+ (`artifact_connectors`).

### Work (AGI Work)
A chat request with `work_mode: 'agiwork'` needs Premium or higher (`agi_work`) or the server returns code `agi_work_plan_required` (request-processor.ts:1486-1503). `applyWorkMode` forces streaming, turns web search, fetch and code on unless the goal excludes them, and tells the model to always use tools (request-processor.ts:1463-1477). The run is a durable cloud run (tables `cloud_agent_runs`, `cloud_agent_events`); the plan is stored with revisions (`work_plans`, `work_plan_steps`, `work_plan_revisions`). Runs are listed via `api:GET /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs`; a stalled run is reaped by `/api/cron/reap-agent-runs` every 15 minutes (vercel.json).

### Approving a paused run
When a gated call needs a person, the server persists a checkpoint first, then streams an approval request. The client resumes with `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve` carrying the run id and per-call decisions. Pending approvals expire after 24 hours (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:457). Device results come back on `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/resume-device`; the server re-checks device pairing, presence and capability at resume (device-clearance-step.ts).

### Scheduled tasks and the runner
A task is a saved prompt with timing (once, interval, daily/weekly/monthly, cron, rrule, or event) plus caps, retries (0 to 5), a missed-run policy (`run_once` or `skip`), and a credit cap (schedule-service.ts:86-102, 139-167). Plan caps on tasks: Free, Local and BYOK 0; Basic 3; Premium 5; Max 15; Ultra 25; Team 10; Enterprise custom (billing-catalog.ts:584-721). Vercel cron calls `/api/cron/run-schedules` every 15 minutes (vercel.json:50-51). The route claims due rows 10 at a time in waves (max 50 per sweep, 55 s budget, 40 s per wave) and executes them inside that same request (cron route; schedule-service.ts:2471-2531). A claim uses `for update skip locked`, a 45 s lease, an idempotency key, and skips owners who may not run unattended or are not active workspace members (schedule-service.ts:1341-1400). Run now is `api:POST /api/schedules/{id}/runs`, executed in the request with a 40 s limit.

The executor (`scheduled-agent-executor.ts`) builds a tool plan from the model's capabilities, plan policy, connectors, web-domain policy, and the same account approval policy. A tool that would need approval is either withheld or the run pauses with status awaiting approval and a checkpoint, approved through `api:POST /api/schedules/{id}/runs/{runId}/approval`; an unanswered approval stops the run after 24 h (schedule-service.ts:80, executor lines 237-372, 374-400). Scheduled runs always use a managed cloud route (`admitManagedCloudRoute`, kind unattended; executor 783-822).

### Event triggers
Sources: gmail, slack, google_calendar, github, connector (cloud-contracts triggers.ts:9-15). A trigger binds an event to an existing scheduled task. Receivers: `api:POST /api/github/webhook`, `api:POST /api/webhooks/gmail`, `/api/webhooks/slack`, `/api/webhooks/google-calendar`, `api:POST /api/webhooks/connectors/{triggerId}` (signed). Ingest records the delivery (dedupes), checks verification, field conditions and debounce, enforces caps of 30 runs per hour and 720 per day per owner, then queues a job; the job creates a run keyed by event id and attempt and appends the event to the prompt (trigger-ingest.ts:361-420; trigger-fire.ts:85-170; billing-catalog.ts:480-482). Limit 50 triggers per account (trigger-service.ts:26). Gmail and Calendar triggers are refused while connectors are "coming soon" (`CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE = 'coming_soon'`, connector-release.ts:14; trigger-types.ts:22-30).

### Cloud coding agent (Code)
A Code session owns an E2B sandbox. `api:POST /api/code/sessions/{id}/agent` starts a turn in mode `agent` or `plan` with 12, 24 or 48 steps. The loop runs in `cloud-code-agent-loop.ts`; each shell command is classified: safe (read-only commands), requires approval (rm, mv, installs and builds, find with action flags), or denied (sudo, curl and wget, git push, hard reset, credential files) (cloud-code-agent-tools.ts:74-190). Approvals are stored in `cloud_code_agent_approvals` and decided via `api:POST /api/code/sessions/{id}/agent/approvals`. Network access setting: none, trusted, full (cloud-code.ts:4). Plan access: sandboxes above 0 and a daily harness ceiling above 0, so Basic and up (billing-catalog.ts:839-841); daily ceiling 1 USD Basic, 5 Premium, 25 Max, 75 Ultra (billing-catalog.ts:584-721). Stalled turns are reaped by `/api/cron/reap-code-turns`.

### Browser actions (Chrome extension)
Two paths. (1) Chat handoff: the web turn offers `browser_*` tools; the extension runs them on the user's tab and returns the result (extension chatBrowserTools.ts: at most 4 calls per handoff, 15 minute timeout). (2) Browser task: the extension's own agent loop (agentLoop.ts, default 20 steps) takes screenshots and acts through the Chrome DevTools Protocol debugger. The model call goes to our cloud, never to a local model, and the model must support tools, vision and streaming (cloudAgentClient.ts:60-100). Permission modes: `ask`, `auto` (default), `full`, `yolo` (askBeforeActing.ts:3-45). Some actions always ask (download, upload, sensitive input, banking/health/identity sites, payment, publish, purchase, terms, permission changes), and crucial ones ask even in auto mode (approvalPolicy.ts; crucialActions.ts). Site grants: the user approves origins and Chrome shows a debugging banner (browserControlConsent.ts:12-20).

### Computer use (desktop)
The Electron desktop captures the screen and sends input through a signed macOS helper; other platforms report unsupported (computerUseService.ts:1-20, 226-231). The cloud turn pauses with `device_*` steps; the desktop carries them out and posts results. The device needs the `computer.use` permission grant, shows a stop shortcut, and stops if the user touches the mouse or keyboard (computerUseSession.ts:96-100, 124-130, 255).

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
Modes. All hosted abilities in this page run in mode:cloud (our servers, charged to the AGI Subscription). Scheduled tasks and event triggers are cloud-only: the CLI client returns a `NotManaged` error outside managed cloud mode (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs:42-43, 234) [code]. The public Desktop is the hosted web app plus a device-capability host; it rejects local inference and accepts no provider key, per a repository document [requirement] (docs/architecture/desktop-local-runtime.md:7-12; not verified in electron code by me). A desktop-only Local routines panel exists (apps/web/features/schedules/components/LocalRoutinesSection.tsx) [code]; what it runs and how is [unknown]. mode:own-key (BYOK) and `local-only` plans get 0 sandboxes and 0 scheduled tasks (billing-catalog.ts:584-615).

Subscription entitlements by ability (tier ids):

| Ability | Free | Basic | Premium (`pro`) | Max / Ultra / Team Premium / Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat tools (search, fetch, code, office) | yes (`chat_tools`) | yes | yes | yes |
| Web search | 20 calls per 30 days, held against Free windows | credits | credits | credits |
| Sandbox code | 2 sandboxes, 60 min | 5 | 10 | 20 (Team 10) |
| Image generation | no | no | yes | yes |
| AGI Work | no | no | yes | yes |
| Scheduled tasks | 0 | 3 | 5 | Max 15, Ultra 25, Team 10, Enterprise custom |
| Connectors | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Cloud coding agent | no | yes (1 USD/day ceiling) | yes (5) | Max 25, Ultra 75 |
| Video generation | no | no | no | Ultra and Enterprise only |

Source: billing-catalog.ts:323-370 (capability tiers) and 584-726 (limits) [code]. Connectors are globally "coming soon" except a short list of exact ids (connector-release.ts:14-33), so connector tools and Gmail or Calendar triggers are not live today [code]. Hosted tool use also requires the model to support tools (`capabilities.tools`) and the plan policy `allowToolUse` (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:250-251).

What approves what:
- Read-only tools (search, fetch, sandboxed code, maps): auto-approved under read-only and autonomous policies.
- Destructive sandbox tools and shell: always ask (even autonomous), unless the user saved `allow`.
- Connector and MCP tools: manual mode; user-saved level decides.
- Device steps: the server allows when a cleared device host is present; the device's own `computer.use` grant and stop control govern the action (tool-call-gate.ts:76-80; computerUseSession.ts).
- Browser commands from chat: never auto-approved by the policy (tool-metadata.ts:1086-1090); the extension applies its own permission mode.
- Scheduled and triggered runs: the same account policy applies; a tool that asks is withheld or pauses the run for approval; a trifecta escalation denies when the run cannot pause.
- Cloud coding agent: command classifier plus stored approvals.
- Workspace policy: a workspace can forbid autonomous approvals (then `ask_every_time`), restrict models, spend, event triggers and managed compute (lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:33-41; managed-compute-gate.ts).

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
- Sandbox unavailable: the model gets a message naming the cause and is told not to retry on that turn (unavailability.ts:35-52). It does not fall back mid-turn to the provider's code tool.
- Search budget unreadable or Free quota used: the call is refused (`blocked`, search-budget.ts:129-141). Reserved charges use a 300 s lease and an idempotency key `search:{request}:{call}`.
- Approval never answered: the run stops after 24 h with a message (schedule-service.ts:80).
- Scheduled run fails: retry up to 5 times with backoff 60 s to 24 h (default 300 s); missed runs follow `run_once` or `skip`; stale claims are recovered at the next sweep (schedule-service.ts:84-90, 2471-2495).
- Sweep too long: the cron route logs that schedules are still due and returns `drained:false`.
- Policy refusal in a background run is recorded as a cancelled run with a reason (`managed_compute_access_denied`, `secret_handling_blocked`) (schedule-service.ts:225-258).
- Trigger delivery: states filtered, fired, failed, dead; a debounced event notes the cap; duplicate deliveries are ignored (trigger-ingest.ts:361-420).
- Device step: pairing revoked, device missing or remote work off gives `withdrawn` with a reason; the turn pauses, not fails (device-registry.ts:396-420).
- Chrome: model must support tools, vision and streaming or the task refuses; step limit message at 20 steps (agentLoop.ts:1294-1296).
- Computer use: user input or stop shortcut stops the run; unsupported OS returns a reason.

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
[requirement] The product requirement ledger lists items per area. Relevant files: knowledge-base/10-requirements/capabilities/057-tool-catalog-and-invocation-experience.md, 059-approvals-and-human-in-the-loop-ui.md, 060-agentic-work-product.md (34 items), 063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md, 064-browser-assistant-experience.md, 065-computer-use-experience.md (29 items). The ledger records these as acceptance criteria, for example computer use needs guided setup, app allow and block lists, monitor choice and a stop control. Per its own status lines, web is missing for computer use and the desktop covers most items.

[requirement] Execution boundaries must be explicit and Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud stay separate; nothing silently moves a Local chat to cloud (AGENTS.md section 6). Today every tool on this page is mode:cloud, so the boundary is clear for them.

[requirement] An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence (AGENTS.md section 9). The metadata table follows this: irreversible writes, deletes and sends always ask.

[proposed] State one boundary table in product copy: which tools leave the device (all hosted tools, Chrome model calls, device-step screenshots) and which stay (CLI local tools, device grants). [proposed] Make the fallback explicit: if the sandbox is off, say the code runs at the model provider.

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Open audit rows (document-based, not re-verified here; code wins if they disagree) in audit/registers/known-flaws.md:
- WEB-E2B-UNSCOPED-COMPUTE-01 (High): a completion with no conversation id can run code with no sandbox quota check or billing.
- WEB-CODE-WILDCARD-EGRESS-APEX-ONLY-01 (High): a `*.example.com` extra host resolves only the apex, so private subdomains could be allowed.
- WEB-CODE-RUN-LEASE-SHORTER-THAN-TURN-01 (High): a Code turn may run 740 s while the session lease expires at 420 s.
- WEB-TRIGGER-WORKSPACE-POLICY-BYPASS-01 (Medium): workspace Event triggers switch gates only creation; existing triggers keep firing.
- WEB-DEPARTED-MEMBER-SCHEDULES-01 (Medium): removed members' schedules stay enabled and never run silently.
- SCHEDULE-POLICY-REFUSAL-AS-SUCCESS-01 (Medium): source fixed, runtime acceptance open.
- WEB-TOOL-RISK-TIER-MISMATCH-01 (Medium): two functions rate the same connector tool differently.
- WEB-AGENT-RULES-IN-BACKGROUND-RUNS-01 (Medium): scheduled runs skip the agent's effort level.

Other gaps seen in code: connectors are coming soon, so Gmail and Calendar triggers and connector tools are not live [code]. Computer use is macOS only. The public Desktop has no local inference, which sits against the requirement that local inference on desktop is free [requirement vs code, see open questions]. No verification run is recorded for any ability here.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Implementation status (code present and connected) is separate from verification status (anyone ran it). Everything above is read from code; nothing is [executed]. The audit checks that a document records a real run was not found for these abilities (the live-check files were listed, not opened).

Read-only checks an engineer can do:
1. Gate order: read tool-call-gate.ts:68-125 and its tests under apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/__tests__.
2. Tool metadata: tool-metadata.ts:101 onward; policy function at 1083.
3. Schedule claim and quota: schedule-service.ts:868-903, 1341-1412; tests test:apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.test.ts, schedule-service.policies.test.ts, scheduled-agent-executor.test.ts, scheduled-agent-executor.tools.test.ts.
4. Search allowance and pricing: test:apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.test.ts, web-search-tool.test.ts, required-search.test.ts, web-search-pricing.test.ts.
5. Office: test:apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.test.ts, managed-office-preservation.test.ts.
6. Triggers: tests under apps/web/lib/triggers/__tests__.
7. Cron registration: apps/web/app/api/cron/cron-registration.test.ts against vercel.json.
8. Chrome: tests under apps/extension/__tests__ and src/features/computer-use.

To run it for real (the owner's call, nothing here did): build the compiled web app against a local database, seed Free and Premium accounts, trigger `/api/cron/run-schedules` with the cron secret, and drive Desktop and Chrome with a human-style check, per project guidance (memory: local testing, human-style verification).

key_facts.fact: The hosted tool loop lives at apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts; the path given in the brief (apps/web/lib/chat/tool-loop.ts) does not exist.

Account tool-approval policy has three values: ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous. A signed-in cloud account with nothing stored defaults to autonomous; ask_every_time is the fail-closed fallback.
A workspace that forbids autonomous approvals drops a member from autonomous to ask_every_time (not to read-only); every workspace the user belongs to must allow autonomy.
The per-call gate is a nine-row ranked table; escalation to a person becomes a deny in an unattended run that cannot pause.
Even under autonomous, irreversible writes, deletes, external sends and shell commands still ask; web search, page fetch and sandboxed code are flagged to run without asking under read-only.
Device steps and browser commands are never auto-approved by the account policy; when a cleared device host is present the server gate allows device steps, and the device holds its own grant.

Step limits differ: chat 10, caller-driven 20, Work 100, Cloud Code 12/24/48 (default 24), 8 device steps per pause, 32 tool calls per step; Work plans hold 6 planned steps in the agent plan and up to 32 stored steps.
Web search uses a Perplexity search backend, returns at most 5 results per call and 3 calls per turn (10 in Work).
Free plan web search is capped at 20 calls per rolling 30 days; paid plans and automated callers (API, CLI, VS Code, scheduled, Work, research) are charged to managed credits per call.

Code execution uses our E2B sandbox only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, an E2B key and a compute price are set; otherwise a capable model gets its provider's own hosted code tool, so code then runs at the model provider.
Sandbox limits by plan: Free 2 sandboxes and 60 minutes; Basic 5; Premium 10; Max, Ultra and Enterprise 20; paid runs up to 24 hours; Local and BYOK 0.
create_office_file produces docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf and csv on the server, can edit an attached docx or xlsx, with a 20 MiB generated file cap.
The image tools are offered only on web, desktop, mobile and chrome surfaces, only on Premium and above, and only when image storage and a default provider are configured.
AGI Work needs Premium or higher; the server answers agi_work_plan_required otherwise. Work mode forces streaming and turns search, fetch and code on unless the goal excludes them.
Scheduled tasks are run by Vercel cron every 15 minutes; the run executes inside the cron request in waves of 10 (max 50 per sweep, 55 s budget).
Scheduled task caps by plan: Free, Local and BYOK 0; Basic 3; Premium 5; Max 15; Ultra 25; Team 10; Enterprise custom. Create is refused above the cap.
A paused scheduled run waits for approval for 24 hours, then stops; retries allowed 0 to 5 with backoff from 60 seconds to 24 hours.
Scheduled runs use a managed cloud route and are cloud-only; the CLI returns NotManaged outside managed cloud mode.
Event trigger sources are gmail, slack, google_calendar, github and connector; at most 50 triggers per account and 30 runs per hour / 720 per day per owner.
Connectors are in the coming_soon state, so Gmail and Google Calendar triggers are refused at creation and connector tools are not generally live.
Cloud Code agent classifies each shell command as safe, requires approval, or denied (sudo, curl, wget, git push, hard reset, credential files); Basic and up include it.

Chrome browser actions call our cloud model (never a local one), require a model with tools, vision and streaming, and have four permission modes: ask, auto (default), full, yolo; payment, purchase, publish, upload, sensitive-site and similar actions always ask.
Desktop computer use works only on macOS through a signed input helper, needs the computer.use grant, and stops on a stop shortcut or any user mouse or keyboard input.
Artifacts render in a separate-origin sandbox page whose CSP blocks all network connections; published artifacts live in published_artifacts under an unguessable URL.
Three High audit rows are open for this area: unscoped sandbox compute with no quota check, wildcard egress resolving the apex only, and a Code lease shorter than the turn.
No document read records a real run of any ability on this page; implementation status is code-read only.

doc.summary: Outside apps plug in through the web app's connector broker: OAuth with PKCE, tokens sealed with AES-256-GCM in Postgres, and MCP servers from a directory or a custom URL. Today 13 connectors are released; the full launch is switched to coming_soon. Plugins and skills install from a directory, and the skills folder is also customer content. Desktop and CLI run MCP through a Rust crate with local token stores. Slack is a separate app.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how outside apps and extensions plug into AGI Workforce. There are five parts.

- **Connectors.** A connector lets the assistant read or act in an outside app such as Notion or Linear. Most are remote MCP servers. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for giving an AI tools and data. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/catalog.ts:161-275)
- **The MCP directory and custom MCP servers.** The directory lists many vendor servers. A user can also add any HTTPS MCP server by URL.
- **Plugins.** A plugin is a bundle, mostly skills. It installs from a built-in registry, a public directory, or a marketplace the user registers.
- **Skills.** A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file that teaches the assistant a procedure. The folder `.agents/skills` is both developer tooling and customer content. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5) [code] (apps/web/lib/services/skill-catalog-service.ts:192)
- **The Slack app.** One Slack app installs per Slack workspace so people can message the assistant in Slack. It is separate from the `slack` connector, which signs in to Slack's own MCP server. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:275-320)

The goal is parity with the leaders: sign-in works in one click. Claude's and ChatGPT's connectors are the stated reference. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:11-60)

Execution boundary. Web connectors run on our servers: the server holds the tokens and calls the outside service. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/mcp/route.ts:23-100) Desktop and CLI run MCP clients on the device through the Rust crate `agiworkforce-mcp`. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:44, apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:36) Device-local connectors (filesystem, terminal, browser automation, screen vision, Ollama) are marked desktop-only, and the cloud does not run them. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/catalog.ts:207-211)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. What is released

- The full-launch switch `CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE` is `coming_soon`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14)
- Only 13 connector ids are released, through `SELECTIVELY_RELEASED_CONNECTOR_IDS`: airtable, canva, clickup, cloudflare, confluence, datadog, jira, linear, monday, notion, posthog, sentry, todoist. [code] (connector-release.ts:16-30)
- `connectorReleased(id)` is true only for that exact set while the switch stays `coming_soon`. A directory alias or a custom server does not inherit it. [code] (connector-release.ts:52-58) [requirement] (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:11-30)
- The 13 ids work in ordinary account chat and Settings (the `allowSelective` path). Agent, voice, schedule, artifact and generic custom/plugin setup keep the full-launch restriction. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:19-22) [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/connector-capability.ts:44-55)

### 2. The catalog

`CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES` has about 90 records. There are three kinds.

| Kind | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| first-party | We implement a fixed tool list. | github (3 tools), outlook, onedrive, teams, sharepoint, bank-accounts |
| operator-configurable | A generic remote-MCP client. The vendor's server decides the tools, discovered at connect time. | notion, linear, gmail, slack |
| device-local | The desktop runtime owns the tools. | local-filesystem, terminal, ollama |

[code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/catalog.ts:12-65, 161-275)

The catalog also ranks execution channels: a structured connector beats browser automation, which beats screen control. [code] (catalog.ts:298-319)

### 3. Directory

- `GET /api/connectors/directory` serves a snapshot built by the ingest. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/directory/route.ts)
- The ingest crawls the official MCP registry at `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io`. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/registry-client.ts:3)
- It merges in three checked-in source files. `first-party.json` has 32 entries, `vendor-directory.json` has 401, and `hand-checked.json` is empty. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/sources/*.json, counted)
- The ingest probes each server's auth mode and its site icon. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/ingest.ts:1-60)

A directory entry connects in one of these modes. [requirement] (docs/development/connectors-setup.md:17-30)

| Mode | What happens |
|---|---|
| connect, open | Lists the server's tools and saves a custom row. |
| connect, OAuth | `POST /api/connectors` answers 409 with `oauthStartPath`. |
| api-key-form | `POST /api/connectors/<id>/credentials` tests the tools list, then saves. |
| needs-setup | The entry names the missing environment variables. |
| desktop-and-cli | Nothing on the web. |

### 4. Sign-in (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE)

1. The browser opens `GET /api/connectors/oauth/start?connectorId=...`. It checks sign-in, the region, token-storage readiness and the workspace connector policy. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/oauth/start/route.ts:187-198)
2. Discovery picks a client identity in this order: a pre-registered app, then a client-ID metadata document hosted by us, then dynamic registration. [requirement] (docs/development/connectors-setup.md:94-110)
3. PKCE `S256` is mandatory. A server that does not advertise it is refused. [requirement] (connectors-setup.md:111-118)
4. A pending row stores the state hash and the sealed code verifier. It expires after 600 seconds. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-store.ts:11, 52-80)
5. The vendor redirects to `/api/connectors/oauth/callback`. The callback checks `iss` and exchanges the code, in `finishConnectorAuthorization`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/oauth/callback/route.ts:61-70)
6. If a native app started the flow, the callback hands `state`, `code` and `iss` back to the app. The app then calls `POST /api/connectors/oauth/complete`. [code] (callback/route.ts:35-45; apps/mobile/app/(app)/connectors/oauth.tsx)
7. Refresh is single-flight: an in-process map plus a row lock (`for update`). [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:37, 145, 173; oauth-store.ts:476)
8. Scopes above a per-connector ceiling are dropped. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-scope-allowlist.ts:20-30)

### 5. Custom MCP servers

- The user gives an HTTPS URL. [code] (apps/web/lib/mcp-url-validation.ts:6-27)
- The URL must resolve to a public host, and embedded credentials are refused. [code] (mcp-url-validation.ts:19-26)
- The server probes the URL and lists its tools. If the server answers with an auth challenge, the row is saved as `sign_in_required` and OAuth starts. [requirement] (connectors-setup.md:32-53)
- A custom row carries either a bearer or header credential, or an OAuth client. Never both. [requirement] (connectors-setup.md:46-50)
- The number of custom servers is capped per plan. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/mcp-custom-connections.ts:212-225)

### 6. Calling a tool

- `POST /api/connectors/<id>/mcp` takes `callTool`, `readResource`, `getPrompt` and the task operations.
- It checks per-tool permission levels (allow, ask, deny) and a critical-risk tier. A call that is not allowed, or is critical, returns `approvalRequired` until the client sends `approved`.
- It writes an audit event. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/mcp/route.ts:36-135)
- MCP text used as chat context is fenced as untrusted. [code] (apps/web/lib/connectors/mcp-context-service.ts:13-14)

### 7. Plugins and skills

There are three install paths. [requirement] (docs/development/plugins-directory.md:152-160)

| Path | Route | Table |
|---|---|---|
| built-in pack | `POST /api/plugins/installations` | table:plugin_installations |
| public directory plugin (an inspected official or public marketplace entry) | `POST /api/plugins/marketplace-installations` with `pluginId` | table:plugin_marketplace_installations |
| account's own marketplace entry | the same route with `entryId` | table:plugin_marketplace_installations |

- A directory plugin is web-installable only if it ships at least one skill and declares no hooks, no language server and no stdio MCP server. Otherwise the entry points to the desktop app or CLI. [requirement] (plugins-directory.md:41-60)
- The directory is refreshed by cron `/api/cron/refresh-plugin-directory`. [code] (vercel.json:158)
- Installs resolve declared dependencies, up to 8 levels and 32 plugins. [requirement] (plugins-directory.md:228-260)
- Skills reach chat through `loadSelectableSkillCatalog`. It merges managed skills, the account's own skills (table:user_skills), installed directory skills and plugin-enabled skills. [code] (skill-catalog-service.ts:597-627)

### 8. Slack app

- An admin installs the app per workspace through `/api/slack/install` and `/api/slack/oauth/callback`. The bot token is stored sealed with purpose `slack-bot-token`. [code] (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-installations.ts:11; db/neon/0330_slack_app.sql:31-42)
- Slack events arrive at `/api/webhooks/slack`. The route verifies the Slack signing secret, answers the URL handshake, then hands assistant events to `after()` so it acknowledges in under 3 seconds. [code] (apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts:36-90)
- Each person links their Slack user to their account through `slack_link_requests`. [code] (0330_slack_app.sql:63,82)
- Approvals for risky actions expire after 24 hours. [code] (slack-config.ts:30)

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
### Tables (all Postgres on Neon)

| Table | Holds | Source |
|---|---|---|
| table:connector_oauth_authorizations | In-flight sign-ins: state hash, sealed code verifier, issuer, endpoints, 10-minute expiry. | oauth-store.ts:52-80 |
| table:connector_oauth_grants | Settled grants: sealed access and refresh token, scopes, expiry, account key, default flag, revoked_at. Row-level security by user. | 0097_connector_oauth_broker.sql:92-132 |
| table:mcp_oauth_clients | Dynamic client registrations, one per issuer. | 0115_mcp_oauth_discovery.sql:49; connectors-setup.md:103-107 |
| table:user_custom_connectors | Custom server rows, with a sealed auth header, `sign_in_required` and an optional sealed OAuth client secret. | 0052; 0313 |
| table:connector_tool_permissions | Per-tool allow, ask or deny. | 0069 |
| table:plugin_registry_entries, table:plugin_installations | Built-in packs and their installs. | 0096 |
| table:plugin_marketplace_sources, table:plugin_marketplace_entries, table:plugin_marketplace_installations | Marketplaces and their installs. Directory installs use shadow rows. | 0159 |
| table:user_skills | Skills the user authored. | 0157 |
| table:slack_installations, table:slack_link_requests, table:slack_account_links, table:slack_assistant_runs | The Slack app. | 0330 |
| table:slack_channel_policies | Per-channel rules. | 0374 |

The column and constraint details come from the migration files above; I did not open every one.

### Token storage

- Tokens are sealed with `sealEnvelope(..., 'hex-triple', purpose)`, which is AES-256-GCM. The key ring comes from `CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (64 hex characters). [code] (custom-connector-crypto.ts:49; apps/web/lib/crypto/envelope.ts:8)
- The purpose is bound into the auth tag. The purposes are: custom-connector-auth-header, oauth-client-secret, oauth-code-verifier, oauth-access-token, oauth-refresh-token, slack-bot-token, plaid-access-token. [code] (connector-secret-reseal.ts:13-21)
- Without the key, connecting is refused with a clear message. [code] (custom-connector-crypto.ts:34-41)
- A revoked grant must hold no secret, and a live grant must hold a token. These are database constraints. [code] (0097 migration:117-120)
- Disconnect revokes the token at the vendor where possible. [code] (oauth-access.ts:284-460)

### Device stores

- store:cli-keyring. The CLI keeps MCP OAuth tokens in the OS keyring. The old file `~/.agiworkforce/mcp-oauth.json` is read only for migration. [code] (apps/cli/src/mcp/oauth_store.rs:1-5)
- store:cli-mcp-registry. The CLI registry is `~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json`. Disabled servers are parked in a `disabledServers` object that the loader ignores. [code] (apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs:1-50)
- store:desktop-settings-db. Desktop encrypts MCP OAuth credentials with `encrypt_oauth_token` into its settings database. [code] (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/mcp/oauth.rs:42-57)
- store:cli-skills. CLI skills load from the project `.agiworkforce/skills/`, `~/.agiworkforce/skills/` and `~/.agiworkforce/account-skills/`. [code] (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:1-8)
- store:cli-plugins. CLI plugins are tracked in `~/.agiworkforce/plugins/installed.json`. [code] (apps/cli/src/marketplace.rs:4)

### Skills integrity

- `skills-lock.json` (version 2, algorithm `agiskill-sha256-v1`) lists 113 skills: 64 `product` and 49 `developer`. [code] (skills-lock.json, counted)
- Any edit to a skill fails CI until `node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate` runs. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md)
- `getManagedSkillDirectory` filters by audience, so only `product` skills reach customers. It caches the result. [code] (skill-catalog-service.ts:239-259)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Plans (internal tier ids)

The plan table is `BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:343-362)

| Capability | Tiers allowed |
|---|---|
| connectors | basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. Not free. |
| skills | free and every paid tier. |
| slack_app | pro and above. |
| artifact_connectors | pro and above. |
| agi_work | pro and above. |

- Plugin installs pass the workspace feature gate `plugins`, and authored skills also pass `skills`. [code] (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-gate.ts:11-12, 29-40)
- Custom MCP server count comes from `customMcpServers` in the plan limits: a number, `unlimited` or `custom`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:526-717; free-plan-entitlements.ts:14)
- I did not map each number to its plan name. Read billing-catalog.ts. [unknown]
- A limit of 0 refuses custom servers. [code] (mcp-custom-connections.ts:218)
- A single user may have at most 32 connector tools. [code] (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:135)
- Plan names shown to people were renamed. The code ids above are internal. [requirement] (memory: product-direction)

### Order of checks when connecting

1. Sign-in, rate limit and CSRF. [code] (apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:533-539)
2. The workspace access gate. [code] (route.ts:239, 539)
3. The release check, then plan, then the kill switch `canUseConnectors`. A kill-switch read failure withholds tools. [code] (connector-capability.ts:23-60)
4. The workspace connector policy. A policy read failure refuses the connection. [code] (connector-policy-gate.ts:78-110)
5. Region refusal for sensitive-data connectors and token-storage readiness. [code] (oauth/start/route.ts:169-172)

### Modes

- mode:cloud. Web connectors, the Slack app and directory plugin installs are server-side and need an account. [code]
- mode:own-key and mode:local. Connectors are a cloud feature and need a paid account. But desktop and CLI MCP servers (stdio, HTTP, SSE) are configured and run on the device. Whether that needs sign-in or a subscription I did not establish. [unknown]
- Local inference is free of subscription. Nothing in the connector path makes it depend on one. [inferred]

### Trust boundaries

- Custom URLs must be HTTPS and public. [code] (mcp-url-validation.ts)
- OAuth fetches run through an egress guard. [code] (mcp-oauth-fetch.ts) In Rust the OAuth flow always validates endpoints. [code] (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/security.rs:1-9)
- The directory page says no Local session routes silently to the cloud. A device-local connector is never run by the cloud. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)
- An own-marketplace plugin entry never enables a first-party pack. [requirement] (plugins-directory.md:217-227)

It is not a connector client. | Absent | Absent | [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts:80-84; apps/extension/src/webmcp.ts) |

The Slack app is web-only and has no client in the other apps. [inferred]

Mobile and desktop native OAuth: the native app opens the browser, the web callback redirects back to the app, and the app calls `oauth/complete`. [code] (callback/route.ts:35-45)

Native clients use separate hosted metadata documents (`/.well-known/oauth-client-metadata/cli` and `/desktop`) with loopback redirects, so no local process can pose as the hosted web app. [requirement] (connectors-setup.md:80-92)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
- **Token storage not configured.** Connecting returns 503 with `CONNECTOR_TOKEN_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. [code] (custom-connector-crypto.ts:28-29; oauth/start/route.ts:171)
- **Lost key.** Grants sealed with a lost key cannot be opened. The user must reconnect. [requirement] (connectors-setup.md:73-76) [code] (`ConnectorGrantDecryptionError`, oauth-store.ts:441)
- **Refresh failure.** The outcomes are `reauthorization-required` (expired, refresh-failed, undecryptable) or a transient 'unreachable' state that leaves the grant intact. [code] (oauth-access.ts:56-75)
- **Authorization server changed.** The start route answers `reauthorize`. A server without `S256` returns `error`. A refused registration returns `registration_rejected`. [code] (oauth/start/route.ts:67-76, 256-270)
- **Callback problems.** A malformed state redirects with `invalid_state`. A vendor denial redirects with `denied`. A wrong or missing `iss` is rejected. [code] (callback/route.ts:61-70; connectors-setup.md:123-126)
- **Policy unreadable.** The connection is refused with 503, never allowed. [code] (connector-policy-gate.ts:101-109)
- **Probe failure on add.** The add path returns `McpProbeError` codes: unreachable or edge-blocked. [code] (route.ts imports `CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_CODE`, `CONNECTOR_UNREACHABLE_CODE`)
- **Disconnect.** Vendor revocation is attempted and the result is reported to the user and logged in the audit trail. [code] (route.ts:883-960; oauth-access.ts:476-495)
- **Connectors not released.** Reads show 'Coming soon' for ids outside the released set. [code] (connector-release.ts:36-44)
- **Plugins.** A blocked install answers 409 with the runtime note and the CLI command. If migration 0159 is missing, install routes answer 503. [requirement] (plugins-directory.md:140-150) I did not recheck this against the code.
- **Truncated GitHub tree.** A truncated tree with no skill counts as a failed inspection, not as an empty plugin. [requirement] (plugins-directory.md:57-62)
- **Slack.** A missing signing secret returns 503. A bad signature returns 401. A payload over 256 KB returns 413. Settings says the app is not set up until the three variables exist. [code] (webhooks/slack/route.ts:36-62) [requirement] (connector-oauth-apps.md:316-319)
- **Skill catalog unreadable.** `SkillCatalogUnavailableError`. Optional sources (plugins, user skills) degrade to empty with a warning. [code] (skill-catalog-service.ts:161, 576-620)

key_facts.fact: Full connector launch is switched off: CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE is coming_soon.
Exactly 13 connector ids are selectively released: airtable, canva, clickup, cloudflare, confluence, datadog, jira, linear, monday, notion, posthog, sentry, todoist.
The connector catalog has about 90 records of three kinds: first-party declared tools, operator-configurable remote MCP with runtime-discovered tools, and desktop-only device-local.
Connectors need a paid plan: free is not in the connectors tier list. slack_app, agi_work and artifact_connectors need pro or above. Skills are open to free.
Connector OAuth uses mandatory PKCE S256. A discovered server that does not advertise S256 is refused.
Pending authorizations live 600 seconds and store a hash of the state and a sealed code verifier.
Access and refresh tokens are sealed with AES-256-GCM, with a purpose bound into the auth tag. The key ring is read from CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
Grants are stored in table connector_oauth_grants, which has row-level security, and a revoked row must hold no secret.
Token refresh is single-flight per grant: an in-process map plus a row lock.
Custom MCP servers must use HTTPS and resolve to a public host, with no embedded credentials. The count is limited by the plan's customMcpServers limit.
A tool call through /api/connectors/<id>/mcp checks allow, ask or deny and a critical risk tier, returns approvalRequired until approved, and writes an audit event.
A user can have at most 32 connector tools.
The workspace connector policy is checked at connection time. If the policy cannot be read, the connection is refused.
The directory snapshot merges the official MCP registry crawl with first-party.json (32 entries) and vendor-directory.json (401 entries); hand-checked.json is empty.
Plugins install through three paths. Built-in packs go to plugin_installations. Directory and own-marketplace plugins go to plugin_marketplace_installations.
A directory plugin is web-installable only if it ships a skill and declares no hooks, language server or stdio MCP server.
skills-lock.json lists 113 skills (64 product, 49 developer). Only product skills reach customers through the managed skill catalog.
Editing any skill file fails CI until the lock is regenerated with node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate. Skills must not be installed with npx skills add.
The Rust MCP crate speaks protocol 2026-07-28 and four legacy versions, over stdio, SSE and HTTP. It is used by desktop (Tauri) and CLI.
CLI MCP OAuth tokens go in the OS keyring; the old JSON file is read only for migration. Desktop encrypts them into its settings database.
The Slack app is installed per workspace. The bot token is sealed with purpose slack-bot-token. Events arrive at /api/webhooks/slack, verified by signing secret.
The Slack assistant refuses a user whose plan lacks slack_app (reply slack_plan_required) and refuses task mode without agi_work.
Slack bot scopes the code requests: app_mentions:read, channels:history, chat:write, groups:history, im:history, reactions:write, users:read. Approvals expire after 24 hours.
The Slack app is configured only when the signing secret, client id and secret, app origin and token storage are all present.
Mobile finishes connector OAuth through an app-return route that calls oauth/complete. The web callback hands state, code and iss to the app when the app started the flow.
The Chrome extension has no connector client. It reads the canUseConnectors capability and shows the coming-soon state, and it exposes page-declared WebMCP tools.
Setup readiness is not authorization: no connector may be marked connected from a redirect alone.
No document I read records a real run of a connector connect.

doc.summary: Files enter through four upload paths on the web API, are checked by structural, credential and ClamAV scanning (fail closed in production), and are stored in private R2-style object storage with a media_assets row. The Library lists those rows. Scripted artifacts render on a separate sandbox origin; published artifacts get a token URL. Plan limits come from one billing catalog.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how a person's files and artifacts are accepted, checked, stored, shown and given back, in all six apps. Basis for the overall shape is [code]; the paths are in the Implementation map section.

- **Upload**: a file is sent to our web API. Small chat files go in one request; large chat files go in parts (a resumable upload). [code] (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/route.ts)
- **Upload scanning**: every uploaded byte is checked before it is usable. There are three layers: file structure (executable signatures, active content in SVG and PDF), secrets in the text, and ClamAV (a malware scanner) run as our own service. [code] (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:601; services/upload-scanner/src/server.ts) [requirement] docs/security/upload-scanning.md
- **Library**: the person's list of stored files and generated images, video and saved artifacts. It is a view over the table:media_assets table. [code] (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts)
- **Artifact**: a model-made piece of HTML, React, SVG, Mermaid, Markdown, text or code that is shown in a side panel. Scripted kinds run inside a page on a different web origin (a different site address) so their code cannot touch the app. [code] (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts)
- **Published site / published artifact**: an artifact turned into a link anyone (or invited people) can open. The Sites page is the owner's list of them. [code] (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts; apps/web/features/sites)
- **Downloads and exports**: a stored file is served back with safe headers and counted against a monthly download allowance; account, usage and memory exports are separate routes. [code]

Why it exists: users bring files into a model chat and keep what the model makes. The product must stop malware and leaked secrets, bound storage cost per plan, and never let model-written code reach the signed-in app. These rules come from AGENTS.md section 6 (trust boundaries) and the scanning document. [requirement] AGENTS.md; docs/security/upload-scanning.md

This page is the file/artifact view. For how an attached file reaches the model see SYS-chat-turn-pipeline. For plan and quota rules see the AGI Subscription pages of this knowledge base (ids not established here: [unknown]).

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Small chat attachment (web API, mode:cloud)

1. Client calls `api:POST /api/uploads/presign` with kind `chat-attachment`, file name, type, byte count. The route checks CSRF, a rate limit, the file type and size, then admits the upload against the plan (size limit and, on Free, a daily upload count kept in the key-value store). It returns either a presigned PUT URL (valid 300 seconds) straight to the private bucket, or, for origins the bucket's CORS does not allow (for example a Chrome extension origin), a same-origin relay URL `api:PUT /api/uploads/chat-attachment/put`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/upload-transport.ts; apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts, admitAttachmentUpload)
2. Client uploads the bytes.
3. Client calls `api:POST /api/uploads/chat-attachment/complete`. The server reads the stored object (bounded to the declared size), then in order: checks stored type equals declared type; matches a hash denylist of known illegal media; checks the SHA-256 the client sent; reuses an existing identical asset if one exists; checks storage space (skipped for temporary chats); runs `scanUploadBytes`; runs a data-loss check (`inspectOutboundContent`) under the workspace secret policy; copies the object to a sealed key; inserts a table:media_assets row; deletes the staging object. Any refusal deletes the staged object. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:302-506)
4. The file is then addressed as `/api/files/<id>`. [code] (chat-attachment-completion.ts, return value)

### 2. Large chat file (over the inline limit)

Only when the readiness check passes: flag `CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED` is `on`, the plan allows it, the caller's origin can reach storage, the intake tables exist, and the scanner answers the protocol 2 capability probe. Otherwise the API answers `chat_large_files_unavailable`. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/chat-file-intake/readiness.ts; apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts)

- `api:POST /api/files/uploads` opens a multipart upload; parts go in through `api:PUT /api/files/uploads/{uploadId}/parts` or the relay `api:PUT /api/files/uploads/{uploadId}`; `api:POST /api/files/uploads/{uploadId}` completes; `api:DELETE` aborts; `api:GET` reports progress. [code] (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:573-576)
- Completion creates an intake row (table:chat_file_intakes) that a step runner advances: head inspection (`inspectUploadHead`), then a source scan (`submitSourceScan` to the scanner's `/v2/scans`), then preparation (table:chat_file_preparations) and sealing. A cron sweeps stuck intakes every 5 minutes. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/chat-file-intake/steps.ts:181,689; vercel.json:66)
- Part sizes and concurrency come from `upload-contract.json` (5 MiB parts, 8 MiB parts for files over 100 MiB, 4 parallel on web, 2 on mobile). [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/upload-contract.json)

### 3. Project knowledge files

Presign kind `knowledge-file` needs a SHA-256 (older clients get 409 `UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`) and a project the user owns. Bytes go to project-knowledge object storage (a local-signed upload URL when no private bucket exists), then `project-knowledge-extraction.ts` scans them (`scanUploadBytes`), extracts text, and seals the object. [code] (presign route; apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:359)

### 4. The scan

`scanUploadBytes` runs, in one call: structural inspection (only for the leading bytes of an object), credential scan, then `runExternalScanner`, which POSTs the bytes with a bearer token to `UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL` with a 15 second timeout. Only `{safe:true}` passes. In production the scanner is required unless `UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false`; with no URL it returns a `scan_unavailable` finding and the upload is refused. [code] (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-455,601-611) [requirement] docs/security/upload-scanning.md

### 5. Serving a file

`api:GET /api/files/{id}` loads the asset in the caller's workspace, then serves bytes with `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `nosniff`, and `servedByteHeaders`, which forces HTML, SVG and XML types to download as `application/octet-stream` attachments. Files over 30 MiB (videos 256 MiB) are refused inline; a sealed large chat file over the limit gets a 5 minute redirect to a presigned URL, only for navigations or clients declaring the large-file capability. Video supports a single byte range. Download bytes are charged to the monthly allowance except for the owner's own AI-generated media. [code] (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts; apps/web/lib/security/served-bytes.ts; apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:472)

### 6. Library

`api:GET /api/library` lists media_assets (filters: kind, sort, surface, origin, search, deleted) plus storage and download meters on the first page. `api:POST /api/library` saves an artifact (up to 1,000,000 characters; html, svg, md, json, csv) as a file via `persistGeneratedFileBytes`. Delete, restore, and permanent delete go through `/api/media` (soft delete sets `deleted_at`; restore only within 30 days; a nightly cron purges after 30 days). [code] (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:693-756; apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-deleted-media/route.ts; vercel.json:82)

### 7. Artifacts and the separate origin

- The chat panel frames `NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN` (the app in `infrastructure/sandbox`, a static page with no build) and posts the artifact to it with `postMessage`. The sandbox page only accepts messages from an exact allowlist of parent origins and only from its actual parent window. [code] (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:134-195,942-952; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:140-230)
- The sandbox's response headers set a strict CSP: `connect-src 'none'`, scripts only from the page itself and pinned CDN hosts, no forms, and `frame-ancestors` limited to our web hosts. [code] (infrastructure/sandbox/vercel.json)
- If no sandbox origin is configured the UI falls back to a same-document `srcDoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-modals"` and a CSP meta tag; React artifacts need the origin. [code] (artifact-sandbox.ts:3,buildSandboxedHtml; apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-preview-capability.ts)
- Desktop (Tauri build) serves the same renderer file on an `artifact://` URI scheme compiled into the binary. [code] (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/ui/artifact_sandbox.rs:1-40)
- Artifacts can call back to the host for AI, connectors and small storage through `postMessage` requests that the host turns into `api:POST /api/artifacts/runtime/{token}/complete`, `/connectors`, `/storage` (published) or `/api/artifacts/runtime/live/{artifactId}/...` (live). AI there only works for artifacts made in a managed-cloud chat. [code] (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts, ownedArtifactOriginRefusal)

### 8. Publishing

`api:POST /api/artifacts/publish` takes artifactId, title, kind (html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code), content (up to 1,000,000 characters). It runs the external-sharing gate, usage-policy moderation and outbound content inspection, then inserts or updates table:published_artifacts and appends table:published_artifact_versions (unchanged content adds no version). Max 200 publications per user. The share URL is `<SITE_URL>/shared-artifact/<24-char token>`. Html, react and mermaid render in the sandbox frame; other kinds render inline. Visibility is `public` or `organization`; only `public` is readable anonymously by token, and a publication that uses connectors cannot be made public. [code] (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:50-110,289-296,824; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts)

### 9. Exports

`api:POST /api/artifacts/export/google-docs` (builds a .docx and creates a Google Doc), `api:POST /api/artifacts/save-to-drive`, `api:POST /api/artifacts/save-to-onedrive`, `api:GET /api/user/export` and `api:POST /api/user/export` (account data; media appears as authenticated download links, not inlined bytes), `api:GET /api/usage/export`, `api:GET /api/memory/export`. [code] (route files under apps/web/app/api)
