sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Access.** Every route uses the user-scoped database (row-level security) so a person reads only their own or their workspace's rows. Writes need a CSRF token and a rate limit bucket. Published content: anonymous read only for `public` visibility; owner can also be blocked from unattended publication when their account status is in a denied list. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:824-840; presign route)

**Sizes** [code] (chat-attachment-policy.json; billing-catalog.ts)

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Inline chat file, per file | 25 MiB (26,214,400 bytes) |
| Inline chat image | 20 MiB; models get an image re-encoded under 5,000,000 base64 bytes and 8,000 px |
| Per message | 25 MiB total, 20 files |
| Client with no handshake (for example the CLI) | 12 MiB per file, 10 files |
| Large chat file | 500 MiB per file, 20 files, 2 GiB per message (policy ceilings) |
| Avatar | 5 MiB |
| Generated or saved file persisted | 20 MiB |
| Inline serve cap | 30 MiB, video 256 MiB |
| Published content | 1,000,000 characters; 200 publications per user |

**Per plan** (plan tier ids from the billing catalog; display names may differ). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:536-720)

| Plan | Daily uploads | Large chat files | Storage shared by Library and project sources | Monthly downloads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plan:local-only, plan:byok | unlimited | none | unlimited (counted nowhere server-side) | unlimited |
| plan:free | 5 a day | none | 500 MiB | derived from the free daily egress cap |
| plan:basic | unlimited | yes, 2 GiB a day, 3 at once | 4 GiB | 1 GiB |
| plan:pro | unlimited | yes, 10 GiB a day, 3 at once | 20 GiB | 3 GiB |
| plan:max | unlimited | yes, 25 GiB a day, 5 at once | 50 GiB | 15 GiB |
| plan:max_15x | unlimited | yes, 50 GiB a day, 5 at once | 100 GiB | 30 GiB |
| plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise | unlimited | team yes; team_premium as max; enterprise not read | team 25 GiB; team_premium from price; enterprise custom | team and team_premium from price; enterprise custom |

Every plan's per-file inline limit is the same constant; the scanner limit is pinned to it by `limits.test.ts`, and the scanning document states `billing-catalog.test.ts` fails a plan above it. [requirement] docs/security/upload-scanning.md [code] (services/upload-scanner/__tests__/limits.test.ts exists)

Plan tier is resolved server side by `resolveEntitledPlanTier`; this is the one AGI Subscription entry used by uploads. [code] (attachment-allowance.ts)

**Modes.**
- mode:cloud: uploads go to our servers and are scanned there; plan limits apply. [code]
- mode:local: on mobile, attachments are read on the device with a device-memory ceiling and no plan count or server upload. [code] (attachmentValidation.ts, attachmentLimitsFor 'local')

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
All of these are [code] unless marked.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| No scanner configured in production, scanner down, 401, 413, 503, timeout | Upload refused with "We couldn't check this file for safety. Try again later." (fail closed) |
| Malware or unsafe finding | Staged object deleted; message "failed a safety check" |
| Password-protected archive, PDF or Office file | Refused; asks the person to remove the password |
| Archive too deep or large | Refused as too complex to check |
| Declared size or type differs from stored object | Validation error; oversize object purged |
| Checksum mismatch | Purged; "bytes do not match the file you selected" |
| Object has no entity tag after inspection | Refused as changed during the check |
| Not enough storage | Refused with message to delete Library files; staged object purged |
| Daily upload count cannot be kept | Refused rather than counted loosely |
| Over plan size | 413 with upgrade hint when a bigger plan exists |
| Large files not ready (flag, plan, origin, schema or scanner) | `chat_large_files_unavailable`: "Files this large aren’t available yet." |
| Scanner queue full or hourly byte budget spent (protocol 2) | 429 with Retry-After; scan retried, never treated as safe |
| Abandoned multipart uploads and relay segments | Swept by the purge-deleted-media cron |
| Library storage cannot store a saved artifact | 503, nothing saved |
| Sandbox frame does not connect | UI arms a timeout and activates a fallback `srcDoc` frame; if scripts are blocked there it says so |
| Sandbox origin equals the app's own origin | `getArtifactSandboxOrigin` returns null and the fallback is used |
| Artifact AI switch off, connectors not released, concurrent-turn ceiling | 403 or 429 with a stable code |
| Publish over 200 items, content over limit, ownership or policy refusal | Conflict, validation or forbidden error |
| Scanner machine unhealthy | Fly stops routing; the service exits after 5 minutes without detecting its test string and restarts; stale signatures show as `stale` but scanning continues |
| Storage config missing | 500 "Object storage is not configured" |

key_facts.fact: Chat attachments upload through api:POST /api/uploads/presign, a PUT to private storage (or a same-origin relay api:PUT /api/uploads/chat-attachment/put), then api:POST /api/uploads/chat-attachment/complete, which scans and seals the file.
Upload scanning has three layers in scanUploadBytes: structural inspection, credential scan, and an external ClamAV call to UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL with a 15 second timeout; only {safe:true} passes.
In production the external scanner is required unless UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false; an unconfigured production deployment refuses every upload (fail closed).
The scanner is our own ClamAV service (Fly.io) that streams bytes to clamd and never writes them to disk; it refuses encrypted and too-complex archives; unauthenticated calls get 401.
Inline chat file ceiling is 25 MiB per file and per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files; clients without the handshake (CLI) use 12 MiB and 10 files.

Large chat files (up to 500 MiB) use a resumable multipart upload under /api/files/uploads, an intake pipeline with a protocol 2 source scan, and are available only on paid plans when CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED is on and the scanner answers the capability probe.
Free plan: 5 attachment uploads per UTC day, 500 MiB storage, no large chat files. Paid tiers: unlimited uploads, large files on, storage 4 GiB (basic) up to 100 GiB (max_15x).
Storage used is one number shared by the Library and project knowledge files, computed over table:media_assets and table:project_knowledge_files; temporary-chat files are mostly excluded.

Files live in S3-compatible object storage, default Cloudflare R2, configured by AGI_STORAGE_* (legacy CLOUDFLARE_R2_*); the private bucket must differ from the public bucket and holds chat attachments and project knowledge.
The Library is a view over table:media_assets served by api:GET /api/library; delete is a soft delete with 30 day recovery and a nightly purge cron at 04:00; permanent delete respects legal holds.

api:GET /api/files/{id} serves bytes with no-store caching and nosniff; HTML, SVG and XML types are forced to download as octet-stream; files over 30 MiB (video 256 MiB) are not served inline; downloads spend the monthly allowance.

Scripted artifacts render in infrastructure/sandbox/index.html on the separate origin named by NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN; the page accepts messages only from an exact allowlist of parent origins and only from its own parent window.
The sandbox's response CSP sets connect-src 'none', no forms, scripts only from itself and pinned CDNs, and frame-ancestors limited to our web hosts.
Without a configured sandbox origin the web falls back to a same-document srcDoc iframe with sandbox allow-scripts allow-modals, where scripts may not run and React artifacts need the origin.
The Tauri desktop build serves the same renderer from an artifact:// scheme compiled into the binary; the public Electron desktop shows the hosted web app.

Publishing uses api:POST /api/artifacts/publish; kinds html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code; content up to 1,000,000 characters; 200 publications per user; 24-character token; URL path /shared-artifact/<token>; html, react and mermaid render in the sandbox.
Publication runs the external-sharing gate, usage-policy moderation and outbound content inspection; a publication that uses connectors cannot be made public.
Anonymous read of a published artifact needs visibility public plus the token; organization visibility is limited to members with a grant row.

AI and connector calls from artifacts go through api:POST /api/artifacts/runtime/... and are allowed only for artifacts made in a managed-cloud chat, subject to an AI switch and concurrent-turn limits.
Project knowledge uploads require a SHA-256; older clients get 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.
Chat attachments are checked against a hash denylist of known illegal media and a workspace data-loss policy before storage.
docs/security/upload-scanning.md says no web code calls the scanner's /v2 routes yet, but source-scan-client.ts and chat-file-intake/steps.ts do.
Account export is api:GET/POST /api/user/export; media inside it is given as authenticated download links, not inline bytes.
A guard script lists every route that stores upload bytes and the files that finish them, and requires each to inspect the bytes.
Mobile local mode parses documents on the phone with a device-memory ceiling and no plan count; cloud mode uses the server limits from the handshake.
Whether production currently has the sandbox origin, the scanner and large files switched on is not established by any file read.

doc.summary: The assistant's per-turn context comes from five stores: account custom instructions, saved Memory, past-chat recall, project instructions and files, and the chat's own instruction. A shared engine checks each source against the user's switches, the workspace policy and the temporary-chat rule. Everything is ordered by one six-layer hierarchy, and the model treats Memory and project files as reference only. Web and Cloud mode do this on the server. Local mode on mobile and CLI uses on-device copies.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how the assistant remembers things and how the text the model reads for one turn is built.

**Five kinds of personal context** [code]:

| Kind | What it is | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| Custom instructions | The account's standing instructions and response style, plus name, work and an "about you" text | The user |
| Saved memory | Short facts in table:user_memories | The user, or the assistant (automatic learning, the `save_memory` tool, a typed "remember ...") |
| Past-chat recall | Excerpts of the user's earlier chats | Read from table:web_conversations and table:web_messages |
| Project context | Project instructions, knowledge files, and excerpts of sibling chats in the same project | The user, who uploads the files |
| Chat instruction | An instruction attached to one conversation (`conversation_instruction`) | The user |

**Temporary chat** is a conversation with `is_temporary = true`. It skips memory, past-chat recall, learning and the stored context manifest. A temporary chat cannot be inside a project (`lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts`).

**Why it exists** [requirement]: `docs/product/requirements.md` section 18 requires memory that can be viewed, edited, switched off, bounded to a project and excluded from temporary chats. The product competes with ChatGPT and Claude, which ship Memory and Projects.

**One contract for all surfaces** [code]: the taxonomy of context kinds and the instruction hierarchy live in `packages/contracts/context`. The engine that applies the checks lives in `packages/platform/context-engine`. The web app uses both through `apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts`.

**Trust rule** [code]: only layers that are instructions (system, developer, project, personalized) can instruct the model. Memory and past chats are reference. Project knowledge files, uploads, connector and web results are untrusted data. The code derives each layer from the source's trust level and a test helper reports any mismatch (`instructionLayerTrustMismatches`, packages/contracts/context/src/instruction-precedence.ts:219).

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. The request arrives

The chat route is `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` (`request-processor.ts`). Three request fields matter [code]:
- `memory_enabled` (request-processor.ts:712) is the per-chat Memory switch.
- `personalization` (request-processor.ts:713) is the per-chat custom-instructions switch.
- `conversation_id` ties the turn to a stored conversation.

If `personalization === false`, the server also sets `memory_enabled = false` (request-processor.ts:3523). The clients send `personalization: false` only for a temporary chat whose "personalized" toggle is off. The toggle defaults to on (web-chat-store.ts:1030; apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:138).

### 2. The conversation row is read

The ownership step loads the conversation. It gets `is_temporary`, `project_id`, the chat instruction and the agent config (request-processor.ts:3760-3980). If the conversation has a project, `loadProjectContext` runs. A missing, archived or deleted project returns HTTP 409 `project_context_unavailable`. A load error returns a project-load failure and no model call is made.

### 3. The Memory policy is read

- For a temporary chat the policy is the disabled constant and nothing is read (request-processor.ts:4126-4131).
- Otherwise two layers are read. The workspace layer is `organization_admin_policies.allow_memory`. The personal layer is `user_settings.settings.capabilities` (`readUserMemoryCapabilities`, managed-memory-context-service.ts:258).
- Memory is on only if `capabilities.memory === true`. The default is off (use-capabilities-preferences.ts:62).

### 4. `resolveInteractiveTurnContext` decides what to load

At turn-context-service.ts:105-242:
- **Memory** is included if the policy is enabled, the chat is not temporary, and `accountMemoryRequested` is true. On the web surface that is `memory_enabled !== false`. On the `api` surface memory is opt-in (`=== true`) (lines 70-75, 124-127).
- **Past chats** are included if the policy has `searchPastChats`, the surface is not `api`, `memory_enabled !== false`, the chat is not temporary, and the query is not empty (lines 128-131).
- The loaders are the project loaders, the past-chat loader and the memory loader. All go to `resolveContext`.

### 5. The engine applies its checks

In `packages/platform/context-engine/src/engine.ts`, for each loader, in budget-priority order [code]:
1. **Class admission** (`classAdmission`, line 114-133): a switched-off toggle gives `source_disabled`. A temporary chat gives `temporary_chat` for classes marked `excludedFromTemporaryChat`. A shared project gives `personal_scope` for personal-sensitivity classes.
2. **Per-candidate checks:** `permissionCheck` (owner, workspace, project must match, and an external source can never be an instruction) and `policyCheck` (the workspace flags allowMemory, allowPastChats, allowConnectorResults, allowWebResults).
3. **Stale, duplicate and budget limits.** Stale items are dropped only if the loader sets `dropStale`. Duplicates are found by a normalized text key. Each loader has a character cap.
4. **Output:** items sorted by authority order (`CONTEXT_SOURCE_PRECEDENCE`) and a manifest of counts and ids, with no text.

The budget is spent in a different order from the reading order. `CONTEXT_BUDGET_PRIORITY` keeps instructions first, then user uploads, then account memory, then project files, sibling chats, past chats, library files, connector results and web results last (context-source.ts:154-169).

### 6. Project blocks are trimmed

`admittedProjectContext` (turn-context-service.ts:87-103) drops any class the engine withdrew. It drops sibling chats when past chats are not allowed. It then fits the rest into `MAX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_CHARS`, giving up the lowest-authority blocks first (`fitProjectContextBlocks`, project-context-service.ts:554).

### 7. The system message is assembled

The stable, cacheable part is built by `composeManagedSystemPreamble` (request-processor.ts:2107-2137). It orders blocks with `orderInstructionBlocks`:

| Rank | Layer | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | system | The capability preamble |
| 2 | developer | Study instruction |
| 3 | project | Project name, description and instructions |
| 4 | personalized | Account custom instructions, then the chat instruction |

The dynamic part comes after `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`. It is built from the system messages added during the turn (request-processor.ts:4270-4345, 6218-6240):
- project knowledge files (layer untrusted_context)
- project sibling chats, past-chat excerpts and account memories (layer memory)
- connector context (layer untrusted_context)

Those blocks are ordered by layer rank with a stable sort. Within one layer they keep message-array order, and later-added blocks sit earlier in the array [inferred].

### 8. Conflict outcomes

`INSTRUCTION_CONFLICTS` (instruction-precedence.ts:156-172) defines what a losing layer becomes:
- A losing instruction layer is **narrowed**: kept, but applied only where it does not contradict the winner.
- A losing memory layer is **ignored** for the contested subject.
- A losing untrusted layer is **quoted**: reported as data and never followed.

The pairwise ranking is system > developer > project > personalized > memory > untrusted. This table is executable. How well a model obeys it is [unknown] (no run in the repo evidence I read).

### 9. After the answer

- Automatic learning (`prepareManagedAutoMemoryFacts`, request-processor.ts:~2410) takes up to 5 pattern-matched facts from the user's message. It runs only if all of these hold: policy enabled, `generateFromHistory`, not temporary, `memory_enabled !== false`, not the `api` surface, and (unless `allowToolAssistedGeneration`) a tool-free turn.
- Optionally a model re-reads the message (`AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION`, on unless set to 0, false, off or no). It runs after the response, on a cheap utility route, metered as feature `memory_extraction`. It is skipped for zero-data-retention turns. Any failure falls back to the pattern facts.
- Each fact passes `writeConsolidatedMemory`, which runs the eligibility gate (see Rules).
- The context manifest is written to table:context_manifests in the background, unless the chat is temporary.

### Other paths

- **Memory tools:** `save_memory`, `search_memory` and `forget_memory` are offered only on stream turns, only if the message asks about memory, and never in a temporary chat (applyMemoryToolCapability, request-processor.ts:1123-1152).
- **Project file search tool:** `applyFileSearchToolCapability` (line 1154) offers a file-search tool when the project has knowledge files, except in temporary chats.
- **Typed commands:** "remember ..." and "forget ..." go through `api:POST /api/memory/commands` or `memory_command` on the chat request. Both use the same eligibility gate and the never-remember list (memory-commands.ts).
- **Free offering path:** `resolveFreeOfferingPersonalContext` (turn-context-service.ts:338) builds the same blocks for the free quota route. It refuses the turn if a project cannot be loaded.

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Who can have Memory and Projects

- The `projects` and `memory_personalization` capabilities are on for the tiers free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise (billing-catalog.ts:322-350). These are Cloud-chat tiers. `local-only` and `byok` are not in that list. [code]
- Project count limit: free 5; basic, pro, max_15x and team unlimited; enterprise by contract (billing-catalog.ts, free-plan-entitlements.ts:10). The limit is enforced in `api:POST /api/projects`.
- Knowledge storage is shared with the Library: free 500 MiB, basic 4 GiB, pro 20 GiB, max_15x 100 GiB (billing-catalog.ts). Over the limit the upload is refused.
- I found no plan gate on reading memory in chat beyond the user and workspace switches. Plan gates were [unknown] for `max` and `team_premium` project limits (not read).

### Switches, in order of authority

1. **Workspace admin:** `allow_memory` off closes Memory and past chats. No policy row, or an unreadable row, means closed (managed-memory-context-service.ts:123-215). `allow_connector_context` and `allow_web_result_context` govern the other two classes.
2. **User setting:** `capabilities.memory` (default off), `searchPastChats` (default off), `generateFromHistory` (default on once memory is on), `includeSensitiveTopics` (default off), `allowToolAssistedGeneration` (default off).
3. **Per project:** `uses_global_memory` false means the project reads only its own memories (memoryScopePredicate, managed-memory-context-service.ts:1085). `uses_account_instructions` and `uses_account_style` false remove the account's custom instructions and style for chats in that project (user-identity.ts:213-247).
4. **Per chat:** `memory_enabled=false`, `personalization=false`, or a temporary chat.

### Memory write eligibility (`memoryEligibilityGate`)

A fact is refused if:
- it is in a prohibited category (credential, payment instrument, government identifier, biometric, precise location, criminal history, immigration status);
- the chat is temporary;
- the workspace has memory off;
- the user's Memory switch is off;
- it touches a sensitive topic (health, race or ethnicity, religion, politics, sexual orientation, gender identity, union membership) and the user has not opted in, unless the user explicitly asked to save it;
- the source class cannot generate memory (project files, uploads, connector and web results cannot);
- the trust mode is not `managed`;
- it matches the user's never-remember list.

An explicit "remember" does not bypass the never-remember list or the prohibited categories (memory-commands.ts).

### Modes

- **mode:cloud:** the server builds all context (turn-context-service.ts). Memory is stored in table:user_memories and the turn is metered. Memory extraction and summary are metered as separate quota features.
- **mode:own-key and mode:local:** not read by the server. `docs/product` and `memory-content-policy` state that managed storage may not hold local or BYOK content (memory-eligibility reason `trust_mode_outside_managed_storage`, managed-memory-context-service.ts:650-660). On the web client with a local model, `useChatStream.ts:4460-4510` fetches account instructions and memory through `api:GET /api/memory/local-context` and injects them locally. Memory is withheld for a temporary chat or a turn with memory off. Whether this crosses the Local-to-managed boundary by the AGENTS.md section 6 standard is [unknown]; it needs a signed-in account and a network call, and the content flows from the server to the device, not the reverse.
- Local inference needs no paid plan. Reading account memory for a local model needs a sign-in because the memory is fetched from the account [inferred].

### Temporary chat promise

[code] (temporary-chat-policy.ts:1-80, plus the engine): no history, no search, no memory read, no learning, no Library files, a connector asks before each call, and no sharing. Project instructions and files are not marked temporary-excluded in the taxonomy. A temporary chat can never be inside a project, so the combination does not arise in Cloud mode.

| Memory policy read fails | Treated as disabled; the turn continues without memory | turn-context-service.ts:292-301; request-processor.ts (UNREADABLE_MEMORY_POLICY) |

| One context loader throws | That class is dropped and the manifest marks it failed; the turn continues | engine.ts:142-150; turn-context-service.ts:190-195 |
| Whole assembly throws, no project | Logs an error; continues without memory and past chats | turn-context-service.ts:320-326 |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
The sections below mark which parts of the design are already met and which are proposals.

**Already met in code** [code]:
- One hierarchy and one set of checks for every context source, with a manifest that explains each turn.
- Memory, past chats and project files are fenced and treated as data, not commands.
- Temporary chats are excluded and cannot be in projects.
- Workspace policy overrides the user, and fails closed.

**Requirements the code should keep meeting** [requirement: docs/product/requirements.md sections 9.6 and 18]:
- Memory is viewable, editable, deletable, switchable, project-bounded and importable.
- Temporary chats do not update or reference memory.
- Browser data never enters global memory.
- Local-only sensitive data never silently enters synced memory.

**Proposals** [proposed]:
1. Pass a real token budget (`budget`) to `resolveContext` in the web turn, so the engine's token ceiling and compaction apply. Today only character caps apply.
2. Set `actor.sharedProject` when the project is shared, so personal memory cannot be drawn into a shared project. Nothing sets it today.
3. Show the manifest to the user ("why did this reach the turn?"). The taxonomy has an `explanation` sentence per class, but I found no user-facing viewer.
4. State per surface, in one place, whether a Local or BYOK turn may receive account memory, and make every surface follow it.

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Each gap is [code] unless marked.

1. **Token budget not used on the web turn.** `resolveContext` is called without `budget` (turn-context-service.ts:179-196), so only per-loader character caps and the project character cap bound the context. The engine's token ceiling and `compactable` path are unused here.
2. **`sharedProject` is never set.** No caller sets `actor.sharedProject`, so the `personal_scope` exclusion cannot fire (engine.ts:130; grep over apps and packages). Separately, `loadProjectContext` selects only projects where `user_id` is the caller (project-context-service.ts:206-209). How chats of a non-owner member of an org-shared project get their project context is [unknown].
3. **Taxonomy classes with no producer.** `library_file`, `user_upload`, `connector_result`, `web_result`, `security_policy`, `template_instruction` and `local_repository_instruction` have `producedBy: []` in the taxonomy (context-source.ts:171-end). They are declared but not emitted as typed sources by the engine path I read. Connector context is added by a separate path (request-processor.ts:4283-4300).
4. **Project instruction and knowledge files in temporary chats.** Both classes are not marked temporary-excluded. This is safe today only because temporary chats cannot join a project. The local-model path says chats with a local model are temporary and cannot be saved in a project (`LOCAL_MODEL_PROJECT_REFUSAL`).
5. **Doc metadata understates surfaces.** `lib/support/doc-metadata.ts:219` lists the help topic `memory` for web and desktop only, while the surface feature matrix and code show memory on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
6. **CLI Local sessions read all boundaries' memory.** The CLI comment says a Local session's prompt carries all three merged memory files (memory_pipeline.rs header). That is by design, but it should be checked against AGENTS.md section 6 (no silent cross-boundary routing). [unknown] whether this is intended.
7. **Web local-model path fetches account memory.** See "Rules" above: whether this honors the trust boundary rules is [unknown].
8. **Within-layer order is implicit.** Blocks of the same layer keep message-array order, which depends on `unshift` call order in request-processor.ts. A test locks cross-layer order (system-assembly-order.test.ts), but I did not confirm a test for same-layer order.
9. **No verification record.** I found no document recording a real run of these paths. Nothing here is [executed].

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
I did not run anything (read-only task). These are the checks to run, using the commands inventory at `docs/agent-context/commands.json` and the rules in AGENTS.md section 12.

1. **Contract tests:** run the vitest suites in `packages/contracts/context` and `packages/platform/context-engine` (instruction order, trust mismatches, engine admission, budget and boundary cases).
2. **Web service tests:** run through `apps/web` package scripts (apps/web uses its own Vitest major, so never the root binary): `lib/services/__tests__/context-resolution-engine.test.ts`, `managed-memory-context-service.test.ts`, `memory-eligibility-gate.test.ts`, `memory-lifecycle.test.ts`, `past-chat-context-service.test.ts`.
3. **Chat route tests:** `request-processor.memory.test.ts` (temporary chat, per-chat toggle, past chats, API surface), `request-processor.project-precedence.test.ts`, `request-processor.system-assembly-order.test.ts`.
4. **Custom instructions reach the model:** `apps/web/lib/server/__tests__/personalization-reaches-model.test.ts`.
5. **Local-model path:** `apps/web/features/chat/lib/LocalPersonalContext.test.tsx` and `packages/contracts/types/src/__tests__/memory-wire.test.ts`.
6. **Guards:** `pnpm check:llm-operability` (includes `check:mock-exports`) and `pnpm check:trust-boundaries`.
7. **By hand, as a person would** (per the owner's preference for human-style verification): with a seeded account, turn Memory on, say "remember that I prefer short answers", open a new chat and ask what you prefer; repeat in a temporary chat and confirm nothing is recalled or saved; set a project to "only its own memories" and confirm global facts do not appear; add a long file to a project and ask about a late passage.
8. **Manifest check:** after a turn, read the row in table:context_manifests and confirm included, excluded and exclusion reasons match the settings used (no row for a temporary chat).

key_facts.fact: Instruction hierarchy has six layers, highest first: system, developer, project, personalized, memory, untrusted_context. Memory and untrusted_context are reference-only.
Project instructions outrank the account's custom instructions; a losing instruction layer is 'narrowed', a losing memory layer is 'ignored', a losing untrusted layer is 'quoted'.
Project knowledge files map to the untrusted_context layer; project instructions to project; account memory, past chats and sibling project chats to memory.
The stable system preamble is ordered system, developer(study), project, personalized (custom instructions then chat instruction); recalled and untrusted blocks go after the cache boundary.
Memory is off by default for a user: capabilities.memory must be true. generateFromHistory defaults on, searchPastChats off, includeSensitiveTopics off, tool-assisted generation off.
A temporary chat reads no account memory, no past chats and learns nothing; no context manifest is stored for it.
A temporary chat cannot be in a project; conversation create rejects projectId with isTemporary, and the policy file states the refusal text.
Temporary chat rows are purged after 30 days by a cron, unless a legal hold applies.
Temporary chats keep custom instructions by default; a 'personalized' toggle (default on) turns them off by sending personalization=false, which also forces memory_enabled=false.
Memory read caps per turn: 30 memories, 1,000 chars each, 8,000 total, from up to 500 candidates ranked by pinned then relevance.
Project limits: name 200, description 2,000, instructions 10,000 chars; up to 40 knowledge files; 16,000 chars per file and 48,000 total in a turn.
Custom instructions text is capped at 2,000 chars; 'about you' at 1,500; preferred name 60; work description 120.

A project can opt out of account custom instructions and style (uses_account_instructions, uses_account_style) and out of global memory (uses_global_memory); memory written in a project is project-scoped.
The workspace policy row governs memory, past chats, connector results and web results; a missing or unreadable row closes everything.
The engine spends the budget in a different order than it reads: user uploads and account memory outrank project files and past chats when space is short.
The web turn passes no token budget to the engine, so only character caps bound context.
No caller sets actor.sharedProject, so the 'personal_scope' exclusion is never triggered in current callers.
Memory and Projects capabilities are in the Cloud chat tiers (free through enterprise); local-only and byok tiers are not in that list. Free allows 5 projects and 500 MiB of knowledge storage.

Memory writes are refused for prohibited categories, temporary chats, workspace or user memory off, sensitive topics without opt-in, non-generating source classes, non-managed trust modes, and never-remember terms.

Automatic memory learning takes at most 5 pattern-matched facts per turn; a model-based extractor is on unless AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION is 0/false/off/no, runs after the response, and is metered as feature memory_extraction.
The API surface is opt-in for memory, never recalls past chats, and skips custom instructions.
Mobile Cloud mode lets the server assemble context; mobile local and own-key modes inject on-device memory_facts and personalization and skip memory in temporary chats.

The CLI keeps instruction files per trust boundary (CLAUDE.md for Local, CLAUDE.byok.md, CLAUDE.managed.md) and merged memory files per boundary; BYOK and Managed sessions read only their own boundary's file, a Local session reads all three.

With a local model on the web client, account instructions and memory are fetched from api:GET /api/memory/local-context and cached for 60 s; memory is withheld when the chat is temporary or memory is off.
Model-assisted auto-memory is a recorded founder decision and temporary chats, Memory-off sessions, API and ZDR traffic stay excluded.
Project knowledge files are fenced as untrusted data with an instruction not to follow text inside them; files with no extracted text or that did not fit are named so the model says so.
No document in the project records a real run of the memory or project-context paths; nothing here is verified by execution.

doc.summary: Voice, images and video are managed-cloud features served by the web app's API routes. Live voice, dictation and read-aloud use the voice routes. Images use durable jobs polled by id. Video uses a durable workflow polled by id. Free gets 10 voice minutes a month and a capped daily offer of 10 images and 5 videos from a separate free-quota route. Paid image generation starts at Premium; video is Ultra and Enterprise only. Mobile dictation runs on the device. No run is recorded.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
Three families of capability share one backend in `apps/web/app/api`:

- **Voice**: live voice conversations (a two-way spoken chat), dictation (speech to text for the message box) and read-aloud (text to speech for one reply).
- **Images**: generate, and edit (edit, inpaint, outpaint, variation) from an uploaded or stored image.
- **Video**: text to video, and image to video (first frame or reference images).

Every one of them spends money at an outside provider, so every one goes through the AGI Subscription system: entitlement lookup, plan gate, usage reservation, settlement and monthly or daily limits. [requirement] `AGENTS.md` section 7 (cost is a first-class constraint) and section 9 (an irreversible action asks first).

Provider choice is not hard-coded in the routes. Voice and media models are resolved from routing slots (`voice_live`, `voice_transcription`, `voice_speech`, `image_generation`, `video_generation`) and the model catalog. Model identifiers live in `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` and `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json`, not in this page. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1252-1392 lists the slots each plan may use)

Execution boundary in one sentence: live voice, read-aloud, image and video generation always need AGI servers and an outside provider (mode:cloud). The one fully on-device voice path is mobile dictation. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:438, :493 set `requiresOnDeviceRecognition: true`; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts, LIVE_VOICE_LOCAL_MODE_REASON)

Status split used in this page: **implementation** means the code exists and is connected. **Verification** means someone ran it. Nothing here is verified by a recorded run; see How to verify.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Live voice (api:POST /api/voice/live/sessions)

The browser or phone sends a WebRTC offer (SDP, the connection description) to AGI. The server checks many gates, asks the voice provider to create a session, and returns the provider's answer so the client can connect audio directly to the provider. [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts)

Order of checks in the create handler, [code] (same file):
1. CSRF token, rate limit bucket `voice-live-session`, signed-in user, 18+ adult gate (`gate: 'voice-live'`).
2. The `voice_live` routing slot must resolve to a live model on a managed provider, else a server error.
3. Managed-compute gate, organization policy gate, spend limit gate, model policy gate.
4. Body must parse (`sdp`, optional `voice`, `conversationId`, `language`, `pace`, `reasoning`, `surface`, `memoryEnabled`, `clientHandoffs`). A `conversationId` is required (`voice_conversation_required`).
5. The provider key env var must be set (`OPENAI_API_KEY`), else 503 `live_voice_not_configured`. The live model must declare a per-minute session rate, else 503 `live_voice_unpriced`.
6. Entitlement and subscription access, the `canUseVoice` flag, then the plan flag `allowVoice`.
7. Training opt-out: if the live or backend model may train on inputs and the user opted out (or the chat carries Google user data), refuse with `model_may_train`.
8. Funding, described below.

Two models work together. The live model speaks. A text backend model (chosen by plan through `getVoiceLiveBackendModel`) does the thinking and tool calls, with the reasoning effort set server-side. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts, `getVoiceLiveBackendModel`; the Free tier lists slot `voice_live_backend_free`, paid tiers list `voice_live_backend`)

The browser is untrusted. The server sends an allow-list of data-channel events (`FRONTEND_CLIENT_EVENTS`: mute, unmute, instruction append, response create, session close) so the client cannot swap model, tools or reasoning. [code] (route.ts:138)

**Billing in one-minute blocks.** `LIVE_VOICE_BLOCK_SECONDS` is 60. Paid plans reserve one block at start and extend block by block through `POST /api/voice/live/sessions/{sessionId}/extend`. The session settles on close at what it used, capped at what was reserved. A session with no check-in for `LIVE_VOICE_LEASE_SECONDS` (600) counts as abandoned and a sweep closes and settles it. [code] (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:20, :28; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/voice-session-settlement.ts)

Other session routes: `GET /api/voice/live/sessions/active` (resume a session, optional history), `POST .../{sessionId}/settings` (voice, language, pace), `POST .../{sessionId}/tools` (run a tool call the voice model asked for, with approval handling and an audit event), `POST .../{sessionId}/close`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/**/route.ts)

A new session for the same conversation supersedes and settles the older one. Context (recent turns, project prompt, memory) is loaded into the instructions; a failed context load starts the session without it. [code] (route.ts; lib/live-voice-context.ts)

### Dictation (api:POST /api/voice/transcribe)

A thin wrapper. It checks the `dictation` kill switch, then runs the shared handler of `/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts)

The shared handler: region check (HTTP 451 when blocked), CSRF, rate bucket `audio-transcription`, auth, file size at most 25 MiB, MIME allow-list (mp3, mp4/m4a, wav, webm, ogg, flac), magic-byte check, upload scan, privacy check on the provider, model policy gate, then the funding step. The `model` form field is honored only if it is a live speech-to-text catalog model; otherwise the `voice_transcription` slot is used. Duration is estimated from file size. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:271-660)

### Read-aloud (api:POST /api/voice/speech)

Text (1 to 4000 characters), optional voice and speed (0.25 to 4), an `Idempotency-Key` header is required, returns `audio/mpeg`. It uses the `voice_speech` slot, which must be an OpenAI text-to-speech model. Cost is estimated from characters and settled as completed. It reserves and settles through the managed usage service, but it does not call the voice-minutes allowance check. [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts)

### Image generation (api:POST /api/media/image/generate)

1. Gates: CSRF, rate bucket `image-generation`, auth, 18+ gate (`media-image`), managed-compute gate, organization policy, spend limit. [code] (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts)
2. `generateManagedImage` then requires an active subscription (403 `subscription_required`), subscription access, and the plan capability `image_generation` (403 `plan_upgrade_required`), then the `canUseImages` flag. [code] (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts)
3. Body validated by `ManagedMediaImageGenerationRequestSchema`. Prompt moderation runs before any billing or provider call; a refusal returns 422 `content_policy_violation` and is never charged. Uploaded edit images are hash-checked against a denylist and structure-checked before billing.
4. Model and provider resolved from the catalog; only the OpenAI and Google adapters can run. Edits need an image API that supports edits (OpenAI only today). [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts, `MANAGED_MEDIA_IMAGE_EDIT_APIS`)
5. A usage reservation is made under a required `Idempotency-Key` that must be a managed-media key for operation `image`. A durable job row is created in `image_generation_jobs` and a background drive is queued.
6. Without `async: true` the request runs the first attempt inline and returns images (or an error). With `async: true` it returns HTTP 202 with a job snapshot and runs the attempt after the response.

The job runs up to 3 attempts (`IMAGE_JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS`). One reservation covers all attempts, so a retry costs nothing extra. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/image-generation-jobs.ts:84-86)

### Video generation (api:POST /api/media/video/generate)

Same front gates (rate bucket `video-generation`, 18+ gate `media-video`). Then the plan capability `video_generation`, prompt moderation, model and input-image resolution, and `assertTierUnitAllowance` for `video_seconds` (clip seconds times candidates). Each candidate (`n` up to 4) is its own durable job in `video_generation_jobs` with its own reservation. Submission takes a short per-user admission lock, then the provider task is started and a Vercel Workflow reconciles it. The route returns `task_id` (plus `task_ids`). [code] (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:982-1245; apps/web/lib/workflows/video-generation-workflow.ts)

Video providers in the wire contract are runway, google and openrouter. OpenRouter can also push completion through a signed webhook. [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:4; apps/web/app/api/media/video/openrouter-webhook/route.ts)

### Polling routes

| Route | Method | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/media/image/status?job_id=` | GET | Snapshot of a durable image job | Owner only. A due job is re-driven after the response. Rate bucket `image-generation`. |
| `/api/media/image/cancel` | POST | Cancel by `job_id` or `idempotency_key` | Releases the reservation. |
| `/api/media/image/retry` | POST | Retry a failed retryable job | 409 `image_job_not_retryable` when attempts are used up. |
| `/api/media/video/status?task_id=` | GET | Snapshot of a durable video job | Rate bucket `video-status`; task id must be a job UUID. Reconciles with the provider. |
| `/api/media/video/cancel` | POST | Cancel a video job | Reports provider cancellation as requested or unconfirmed. |
| `/api/media/availability` | GET | Which image and video models are admitted and what they support | No-store. |
| `/api/media/jobs` | GET | Job history for the user and workspace | |
| `/api/media` | GET, DELETE, POST | List library assets, soft or permanent delete, restore | |
| `/api/media/keep` | POST | Move a temporary-chat asset into the Library | |

[code] (apps/web/app/api/media/**/route.ts)

Client polling cadence: web video every 5 s for up to 5 min; mobile image every 2 s for up to 170 s; mobile and Chrome video constants 5 s and 5 min. [code] (apps/web/lib/hooks/useMediaGeneration.ts:94-95; apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/imagegen.ts:36-37; apps/mobile/src/features/video/services/videogen.ts:49-50; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:11-12)

### What Free gets

- **Voice**: Free has `allowVoice: true` and `voiceMinutesPerMonth: 10`. Live voice and dictation draw on the same monthly pool, in seconds, funded from a per-user usage-events log (`free_voice_seconds_granted` and `free_voice_seconds_settled`). Free uses the cheaper backend slot. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1252-1256; apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47)
- **Image and video through the normal routes**: not available. Free fails `canUseBillingPlanCapability` and gets 403 `plan_upgrade_required`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:356-357; managed-image-generation.ts)
- **Image and video through the free-quota route**: a separate, limited offer. `limitedMediaOffer.dailyCapPerUser` is 10 images and 5 videos per user per UTC day, admitted only for plans that have managed chat but not the paid capability. The turn is served by `serveFreeQuotaTurn` on `/api/models/free-quota/completions`, only when a free quota offering of that kind is ready (terms review current, console check, allowance left). [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json:3501-3503; apps/web/lib/server/free-quota-catalogue.ts:81-93; apps/web/features/models/lib/free-media.ts:49-57)
- `GET /api/models/free-quota/media-offer` publishes whether each is `offered`, `not_offered` or `unknown`. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/free-media-offer-reader.ts)

sections.markdown:
### Database tables

| Table | Holds | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| table:voice_sessions | One row per live session: provider session id, conversation, surface (web, mobile, desktop), voice, language, pace, active tools, last turn id, status (active or closed), close reason, timestamps | [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/voice-session-store.ts; migration apps/web/db/neon/0260_voice_sessions.sql) |
| table:usage_events | Free voice grants and settlements (`free_voice_seconds_granted`, `free_voice_seconds_settled`), keyed by session id and calendar month, under a per-user advisory lock | [code] (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts) |
| table:managed_usage_requests | Reservations and settlements for paid voice, dictation, read-aloud, image and video. Monthly voice minutes are summed from rows whose `usage.operation` is `transcription` or `voice_live_session` | [code] (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts, voice_minutes query) |
| table:managed_usage_request_extensions | One row per extra voice block (extension) | [code] (voice-session-budget.ts, `readVoiceReservation`) |
| table:image_generation_jobs | Durable image jobs: status, attempts (max 3), claim, lease, public error, cancel request, billing outcome, `temporary_chat` flag | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/image-generation-jobs.ts; migrations 0226, 0339) |
| table:image_generation_job_assets | Links a job to its stored images | [code] (image-generation-jobs.ts references it) |
| table:video_generation_jobs | Durable video jobs: provider task, duration, status, cancellation, settlement and incident-alert state | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/video-generation-jobs.ts; migrations 0339, 0392) |
| table:media_assets | Stored images and videos; library, soft delete, temporary-chat assets | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts) |
| table:web_conversations | Owner check for `conversation_id` on image requests and temporary-chat marking | [code] (managed-image-generation.ts) |

A background job kind `media-generation.image-attempt` is queued per image attempt, keyed by job id and attempt count, so a killed request still finishes. [code] (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-drive-queue.ts)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Plans

Plan names in the code are `free`, `basic`, `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`. Display labels: Free, Basic, Premium (`pro`), Max, Ultra (`max_15x`), Team, Team Premium, Enterprise. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-14, :176-230) The tier policy used for voice limits folds several plans together: `pro`, `team`, `basic` become product tier pro; `max`, `max_15x`, `team_premium` become product tier max; `enterprise` stays; anything else is free. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1691-1710)

| Capability | plan:free | plan:basic | plan:pro (Premium) | plan:max | plan:max_15x (Ultra) | plan:enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live voice and dictation | Yes, 10 min per calendar month shared pool | Yes, paid usage budget | Yes, paid usage budget | Yes, paid usage budget | Yes, paid usage budget | Yes, paid usage budget |
| Image generation (normal route) | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Video generation (normal route) | No | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Video seconds per month | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable | 300 | no cap in policy (null) |
| Free daily offer via free-quota route | 10 images, 5 videos per UTC day when an offering is ready | same offer shape (managed-chat plans without the paid capability) | not needed for images; videos: offer shape | offer shape for video | not needed | not needed |

Sources: voice flags and minutes [code] (model-catalog.ts:1252-1256 free; :1288-1290 pro; :1336-1343 max; :1387-1392 enterprise); capability tiers [code] (billing-catalog.ts:356-357: image `PRO_TIERS` = pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; video = max_15x, enterprise); video seconds [code] (model-catalog.ts:1343, tier-unit-quota-service.ts:57-58). The `team` and `team_premium` plans pass the image capability; only `team_premium` folds to product tier max for voice and video seconds, and neither passes the video capability. The Free-plan voice allowance applies to any plan for which `isFreeBillingPlanTier` is true, which is `free` only. [code] (free-voice-allowance.ts:47; billing-catalog.ts:260)

The last row of the table is [inferred] from `freeMediaPlanStanding` (included if the paid capability is held, offer-eligible if the plan has managed chat) together with the runbook's note that the offer is for eligible managed-chat plans. [code] (apps/web/features/models/lib/free-media.ts:49-57) Basic and Premium videos going through the offer was not traced to a test. [unknown]

A concrete consequence worth knowing: Max (not Ultra) has video slots in its tier policy and a 300 second monthly cap defined, but fails the video capability gate, so only Ultra (and Enterprise) can actually generate video. [code] (model-catalog.ts:1336-1343 vs billing-catalog.ts:357)

### Paid voice funding

For any plan that is not Free: `assessVoiceBudget` checks the rolling five-hour and weekly usage caps and credits; if the plan cannot fund one block, 402 `voice_usage_not_in_plan`. Then `assertTierUnitAllowance` for `voice_minutes` (a hard limit only when the plan sets `voiceMinutesPerMonth`, null for all paid tiers), then a one-block reservation. [code] (voice-session-budget.ts; route.ts)

For Free: before granting, abandoned sessions are settled so their seconds return; then `grantFreeVoiceSeconds` grants 60 s, refusing with the allowance-used error and a reset time (first of next UTC month) when the pool is spent. An unsettled grant counts only for 660 s (lease plus block) so a dead attempt does not burn the month. [code] (free-voice-allowance.ts:24, :47; route.ts)

### Gates every managed media or voice request passes

18+ adult-eligibility gate, managed-compute gate (surface and platform), organization policy gate, workspace spend limit, workspace model policy (checked on the resolved catalog model), provider training opt-out, feature flags (`canUseVoice`, `canUseImages`, kill switch `dictation`). [code] (route files cited above)

### Modes

- mode:cloud: live voice, read-aloud (server voice), dictation through the server, all image and video generation.
- mode:local: mobile dictation is on-device; mobile read-aloud uses the device voice (`expo-speech`) when the conversation is not Cloud; live voice is refused in Local Mode with the text 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceOutput.ts, tts.ts, liveVoiceAvailability.ts)
- mode:own-key: the CLI can transcribe with a user's own OpenAI key or a local `whisper` program, and Local privacy mode suppresses the OpenAI path. Whether any app lets a user bring their own key for live voice, image or video is [unknown]; the managed routes read server keys only. [code] (apps/cli/src/voice.rs header and lines 72-141)
- Local features need no paid plan. Whether mobile dictation and device read-aloud need sign-in was not established. [unknown]

Nothing in these routes moves a Local chat to the cloud on its own; mobile live voice and server read-aloud check that the conversation's mode is Cloud first. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:155; voiceOutput.ts)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are product requirements and my proposals, kept apart.

- [requirement] Subscription capabilities on every app must connect to one AGI Subscription system. The web routes already do this through entitlement, tier policy, `assertTierUnitAllowance` and managed usage reservations, and the other apps call the same routes. (AGENTS.md section 7; billing-catalog.ts)
- [requirement] Local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription. Mobile dictation and device read-aloud follow this. A consistent Local read-aloud and dictation story on every app that claims it is not shown in this code review.
- [requirement] Execution boundaries must be explicit. The mobile app does this for live voice (a reason string per refusal). The other apps' wording was not reviewed.
- [requirement] Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters (owner decision recorded in project memory). The Free voice allowance and Free daily media caps are enforced server-side; whether any screen shows a meter was not checked.
- [proposed] Give image status polling its own rate bucket or exempt it from the 10 per minute image bucket, so a 2 second poll cannot trip the limit it shares with submission (see Gaps).
- [proposed] Make the tier policy and the capability table agree about video. Today Max carries video slots and a 300 second cap in `TIER_POLICIES` while the capability table admits only Ultra and Enterprise. One owner should decide, and the other should be derived from it, per AGENTS.md section 3.
- [proposed] Let `GET /api/media/availability` or the capability handshake publish voice minutes, image and video limits per plan for every app, so clients stop carrying their own copies. A capability handshake already lists `voice_minutes_per_month`. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/capability-handshake-service.ts:319-324)

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Implementation gaps and risks found by reading code. Each is a lead to confirm, not a proven defect.

1. **Image status polling shares the submission rate bucket.** `/api/media/image/status` calls `withRateLimit(request, 'image-generation')` with no plan tier, so the base limit is 10 per minute (times a global scale), and the mobile client polls every 2 s, up to 85 polls. [inferred] (apps/web/app/api/media/image/status/route.ts; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:384-388, :962-965; apps/mobile/src/features/image/services/imagegen.ts:36). Whether the identifier is per user or per address, and whether `rateLimitScale` is above 1 in production, were not checked. [unknown]
2. **Plan table and tier policy disagree on video** (see How it should work). [code]
3. **Free media offer depends on a promotional pool that mostly expired.** In `free-pools.json`, 244 of 279 inventory entries carry `expiresOn` 2026-10-21, and today is after that date. The terms-review and console-check gates decide whether anything still serves, and those records were not read. [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json) [unknown] for what serves today.
4. **Mobile video is shipped but switched off** (`videoGen: false`). The runbook says mobile video UI is paid-only; the flag hides it entirely. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:28)
5. **Mobile has no consent notice for the named-provider Free quota models**, so those turns are refused until the account agrees on web. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/free-quota-models.md)
6. **Read-aloud is not counted against voice minutes.** It reserves usage money but never calls the voice-minutes allowance. A Free user's read-aloud is not capped by the 10-minute pool; what does cap it is the managed-compute access check and the reservation. [code] (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts) Whether this is intended is [unknown].
7. **Surface matrix is stale** (see outdated_documents).
8. **Stability image provider** is in the wire contract but its adapter throws 'not supported'. [code] (image-generation-provider.ts `getApiKey`, `isProviderAvailable`)
9. **No recorded run** of live voice, image, video or the free media path. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/free-quota-models.md says no tests, probes or deployment validation were performed for the reconstructed free media changes).

key_facts.fact: Free plan voice is 10 minutes per calendar month, one pool shared by live voice and dictation; paid plans have no monthly voice-minute cap and pay from the usage budget in 1-minute blocks.
Live voice billing block is 60 seconds; a session with no check-in for 600 seconds is treated as abandoned and settled at its last check-in.
Live voice uses two models: a live speaking model from the voice_live slot and a text backend chosen by plan (a cheaper slot for Free); the browser may send only an allow-list of data-channel events.
Live voice requires a conversationId, an 18+ adult-eligibility pass, the canUseVoice flag, allowVoice on the plan, and the OPENAI_API_KEY server setting; Local Mode on mobile refuses live voice.
Dictation endpoint /api/voice/transcribe wraps /api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions behind the dictation kill switch; max 25 MiB, MIME allow-list, 20 requests per minute base.
Read-aloud (/api/voice/speech) takes up to 4000 characters, requires an Idempotency-Key, returns mp3, and is not checked against the monthly voice-minutes allowance.

Image generation on the managed route needs a subscription and the image_generation capability: pro (Premium), max, max_15x (Ultra), team, team_premium, enterprise. Free and Basic get 403 plan_upgrade_required.
Video generation capability is limited to max_15x (Ultra) and enterprise; Max does not pass it even though the Max tier policy has video slots and a 300 second monthly cap.
Video seconds are capped at 300 per month for the max product tier (which includes Ultra); enterprise has no cap in policy. The cap counts non-failed jobs this month.
Free users get limited image and video through a separate route: 10 images and 5 videos per user per UTC day, only when a free quota offering of that kind is ready.
Most free-quota inventory entries carry an expiry of 2026-10-21; whether anything still serves depends on terms-review and console-check gates not read for this page.

Image jobs are durable: up to 3 attempts on one reservation, claim 180 s, lease 3600 s; with async true the route returns 202 and the client polls /api/media/image/status; the status call also re-drives a due job.

Image requests accept prompt up to 4000 characters, up to 4 images (1 for the Gemini image API), up to 3 edit reference images, and operations generate, edit, inpaint, outpaint, variation; only the OpenAI image API supports edits.
Video requests accept a prompt up to 2000 characters, clip 2 to 30 s (default 4), up to 4 candidates each billed as its own job, and optional first-frame or reference images (not both).
Video is processed by a durable Vercel Workflow; the client polls /api/media/video/status (web and Chrome every 5 s for 5 min); OpenRouter can call a signed webhook.
Prompt moderation and uploaded-image hash and structure checks run before any billing reservation or provider call, so a refused image request is never charged.
Base rate limits per minute: image 10, video 5, video status 30, transcription 20, read-aloud 30, live session create 10; all but video status fail closed.

Mobile dictation runs fully on the device through expo-speech-recognition with on-device recognition required; mobile read-aloud uses server speech in Cloud conversations and the device voice otherwise.
Mobile live voice needs a native build with react-native-webrtc, an https server, a signed-in Cloud conversation; otherwise voice stays turn based.
Mobile image generation is enabled (imageGen true) and uses async jobs polled every 2 s for up to 170 s; mobile video generation code exists but the videoGen flag is false.

Chrome extension wires video generation (start and poll) and dictation through the browser Web Speech API; VS Code only dictation to /api/voice/transcribe?surface=vscode; CLI has push-to-talk voice and image generation.
Live voice session records accept only surfaces web, mobile and desktop.
Image status polling uses the same rate bucket as submission (base 10 per minute) while mobile polls every 2 seconds, so mobile could hit 429 during a long job; not confirmed.
No document in the project records a real run of live voice, image or video generation; the free media changes are explicitly recorded as unvalidated.

Voice and media data lives in voice_sessions, image_generation_jobs, image_generation_job_assets, video_generation_jobs, media_assets, managed_usage_requests and usage_events; jobs started in temporary chats carry a temporary_chat flag purged with the chat.

doc.summary: Chat history syncs through one cursor-based endpoint, api:POST /api/chat/sync (and GET), used by mobile and CLI, and pulled by Chrome. Remote Control lets a phone steer a code session on a computer through a WebSocket relay with signed messages; it is paid-plan gated and hidden in mobile v1. Notifications go to an in-app feed, email (Resend) and push (Expo for phones, Web Push for browsers).

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how the AGI apps stay in step. It has four parts:

1. **Chat sync**: one account's conversations, messages and artifacts are copied between devices through the hosted web app. The conversations are stored in `table:web_conversations`, `table:web_messages` and `table:web_artifacts`.
2. **Remote Control and its relay**: a phone (the companion) watches and steers a coding session that runs on a computer (the host). A small relay server passes signed messages between the two. The relay never holds the session. [requirement] (docs/architecture/remote-control.md:14-21)
3. **Notifications by channel**: an in-app feed, email, and push. Push goes to phones through Expo and to browsers through Web Push.
4. **What mobile v1 hides**: Remote Control and Send to Desktop are switched off in the first phone release.

Sync is for cloud-backed chat only. A Local-mode chat on the device is not copied (see SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for modes). The mobile sync loop runs only when the app is in cloud mode and signed in. [code] (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:97-107)

Why it exists: the product promise is one account across six apps. The research file records that the leaders sync cloud conversations across devices while local ones stay on the computer. [requirement] (docs/research/cross-surface-continuity-2026-09-21.md:25-33). That file is dated research, not authority.

The hand-off idea has no single feature. In code it appears as three things. (a) Cloud history shows in every client. (b) A local code session reports activity to the server, which pushes a notice to the phone (api:POST /api/code/local-sessions/activity). (c) Remote Control lets the phone steer the host.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Chat sync (implementation status: code present and connected)

- One route, `file:apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts`, exports GET (pull) and POST (push) (route.ts:1020-1021).
- **Pull**: the client sends `since`, a version cursor. The server returns conversations, messages and artifacts whose `server_version` is greater than the cursor. Limits are 500 conversations, 1000 messages and 500 artifacts per page. `hasMore` is true when any list is full. Temporary chats are excluded. A `scope=conversations` query returns conversations only. [code] (route.ts:49-51, 104-195)
- **Push**: the client sends rows with a `baseVersion`. A row with `baseVersion` 0 is an insert. A row with a higher base is an update that applies only when the stored version still equals the base. Otherwise the row comes back in `conflicts` with the server copy. Deletes are tombstones (`deleted_at`), not hard deletes. [code] (route.ts:222-340 for the SQL, 543-600 for the handler)
- **Order of checks on push**: CSRF, rate limit bucket `chat-conversation`, workspace policy gate `chat_sync`, a no-op shortcut for old empty pushes, protocol version check, schema check, project ownership check, then the free daily allowance check. [code] (route.ts:543-583, 940-956)
- **Protocol version**: `SYNC_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 2 and the minimum is 2. A client below the floor gets a client-update-required error. A client above it gets a validation error. [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/sync.ts:33-41; route.ts:940-947)
- **Threading**: new assistant and user rows are chained to the conversation's active leaf under a lock, so branches stay consistent. [code] (route.ts:470-535)
- **Side effects**: pushing assistant messages schedules artifact indexing, fire and forget. A push also clears the stored compaction summary for touched conversations. [code] (route.ts:715-740, 532)

### Clients of chat sync

- **Mobile** pushes then pulls, then syncs memory, projects and settings, in one `syncNow`. It runs every 30 seconds while the app is active and on return to the foreground. Each step records its own failure. [code] (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1007-1077)
- **CLI** reads and writes the same `/api/chat/sync` records so a CLI turn shows in the other apps. [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs:1-14)
- **Chrome extension** pulls the conversations scope with an alarm-driven sweep and keeps a local cursor. It checks a local cloud-mirroring switch first. [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts:62-65, 131). How it pushes is [unknown]: it was not traced.
- **Web and Electron desktop**: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5). The web app's own chat uses the conversation routes. The only `chat/sync` caller found in `apps/web/features` is artifact sync. [inferred] (apps/web/features/chat/services/artifact-cloud-sync.ts)

### Remote Control (implementation status: code present; deployed relay not live)

1. **Pairing**. A host asks the web app for a pairing: api:POST /api/pair/initiate. The route checks CSRF, a rate limit (`device-link`), then `remoteControlStandingRefusal` (workspace policy, plan, kill switch). It calls the relay (`POST /pairings`) with an internal bearer secret. It returns a code, expiry, relay URLs and one role token. Default life is 300 seconds, allowed range 30 to 900. [code] (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:20-25, 47-70, 100-175)
2. **Claim**. The phone calls api:POST /api/pair/claim with the code. The web app proves the account and tells the relay which account to mint for. The relay refuses a different account (403, `pairing_belongs_to_another_account`). [code] (apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:30-47, 146)
3. **Connect**. Both peers open a WebSocket to the relay and register with their role token. Each registration consumes the token and returns a fresh one. [requirement] (services/signaling-server/README.md, section Pairing credentials)
4. **Signed messages**. Both sides derive a key from the pairing code, a session salt and a secret that the relay never sees. Each message is an envelope with version 3, a timestamp, a nonce and an HMAC. The message is signed, not encrypted. [code] (packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/dispatchEnvelope.ts:4, 38-60, 118)
5. **Allow-list**. The relay forwards only listed actions: approvals, agents, heartbeat, cancel, receipts, code-session verbs and four dispatch-task verbs. Normal control messages are capped at 4 KB. Code-session, dispatch and large snapshot messages are capped at 48 KB. [code] (services/signaling-server/src/control-payload.ts:9-77; constants.ts:25-27)
6. **Standing recheck**. While a pairing lives, the relay asks api:POST /api/pair/standing about every 60 seconds whether the account, workspace policy, plan, switch and paired devices still allow it. If the web app cannot answer, the relay keeps the last answer for at most 5 minutes, then closes the sockets. The relay's pairing lifetime cap defaults to 7 days. [code] (apps/web/app/api/pair/standing/route.ts:18-35; services/signaling-server/src/constants.ts:101-105; README.md section Pairing lifetime and standing)
7. **Hosts**. Three hosts exist: Electron desktop (`apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts`), the VS Code extension (`apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts`) and the CLI command `agi remote-control` (`apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs`). The CLI needs a login token, shows a QR payload `agiw3:<code>:<secret>` and reconnects with back-off. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6659-6678; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:759-815)
8. **Activity push**. While a CLI host runs, it posts session activity to api:POST /api/code/local-sessions/activity. The server records a feed notice and sends a push to the user's phones only (Expo, not browser). [code] (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:24-25, 621-654; apps/web/app/api/code/local-sessions/activity/route.ts:18-35; apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:374-405)

### Notifications

| Channel | Where it is produced | Provider or store | Consent |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-app feed | `recordNotification` writes `table:notifications`; the web bell polls api:GET /api/notifications every 60 seconds | Neon Postgres | None; always recorded. Duplicates are dropped by `(user_id, dedupe_key)`. |
| Email | Security alerts, schedule completion, spend alerts, data export, billing notices | Resend, needs `RESEND_API_KEY` and `AGI_NOTIFICATIONS_FROM_EMAIL` | Per-key settings, for example `emailSecurityAlerts`, `emailScheduleDone`. Marketing email has a signed one-click unsubscribe at api:POST /api/email/unsubscribe. |
| Mobile push | `sendPushToUser` fans out to Expo | Expo push service (`https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send`), tokens in `table:mobile_devices` | Device registers a token and per-event preferences with quiet hours. |
| Browser push | Same fan-out, Web Push with VAPID keys | `table:web_push_subscriptions`, `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_SUBJECT` | Browser opt-in from settings; subscription at api:POST /api/web-push. |

[code] (apps/web/lib/services/notification-service.ts:58-120; push-notification-service.ts:25, 281-383; notification-email-service.ts:13; apps/web/app/api/notifications/route.ts:94-95; apps/web/features/notifications/hooks/use-notification-feed.ts:8; web-push-service.ts:107-109)

Producers: agent run events, research reports, cloud code turns, local code sessions, chat reply ready (phone-started runs, phone push only), schedule completion, product updates, identity security events, new device. [code] (agent-notification-service.ts; chat-reply-notification-service.ts:30-50; identity-events/catalogue.ts:5-33)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Chat sync

- Plan: `cloud_sync` is available to `plan:free`, `plan:basic`, `plan:pro`, `plan:max`, `plan:max_15x`, `plan:team`, `plan:team_premium` and `plan:enterprise` (the cloud-chat tier list). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:322-352). Whether the route itself checks this capability is [unknown]: the route checks the workspace policy and the free daily allowance, not `cloud_sync` by name.
- Free accounts: new conversations and new messages count against a daily allowance. Over the limit, push is refused. [code] (route.ts:575-583)
- Workspace: an organization policy can refuse sync per surface. Mobile shows the refusal as a sync-off reason. [code] (managed-compute-gate.ts:262-281; cloudSyncEngine.ts:996-1000)
- Mode: sync is for `mode:cloud` only. Mobile checks that the app is in cloud mode with a signed-in account. `mode:local` has no server copy. `mode:own-key` sync behaviour is [unknown]; AGENTS.md section 6 says a Local-to-BYOK move must be an explicit fork with consent. [code] (cloudSyncEngine.ts:97-107) [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)
- Local inference is not tied to this system, so it needs no subscription. Cloud sync needs an account.

### Remote Control

- Plan: `remote_control` needs a paid tier: `plan:basic` and above. `plan:free` is refused with a 403 `plan_upgrade_required`. If the plan cannot be read, the answer is 503 and pairing is refused. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:352; remote-control-gate.ts:50-77; apps/cli/src/plans.rs:98)
- Another gate: the feature registry lists Remote Control as `experimental`, kill switch `screen_share`, entitlement `developer_surfaces`, host `desktop`. The route uses the plan capability `remote_control`, not `developer_surfaces`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/feature-registry.json:175-199)
- The workspace policy `remote_control`, the plan and the kill switch are asked together at create, at claim and at every relay recheck, so a pairing cannot outlive them. [code] (remote-control-gate.ts:97-130)
- Authority stays on the host. The phone sends control messages only. Permissions, path limits and approvals run on the computer. [requirement] (docs/architecture/remote-control.md section Where authority actually lives)
- Privacy: the CLI host refuses to start if the account privacy mode forbids cloud (`CloudClient::admit`). [code] (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:767)
- This is a `mode:cloud` account feature (the relay and plan check are our servers), even though the session runs on the user's device.

### Notifications

- Email: security alert email goes out unless the user turned `emailSecurityAlerts` off. A user enrolled in advanced account security cannot opt out. [code] (account-activity-notifications.ts:57-91)
- Phone push: an agent-activity switch (`mobilePushAgentActivity`) is opt-out. `product_update` push is opt-in. Quiet hours hold push unless the type is exempt. If quiet hours cannot be read, the notice is queued as job `notifications.deferred-push` and the feed copy is kept. [code] (agent-notification-service.ts:25-96; mobile-push.ts:38-52; push-notification-service.ts:281-330)
- Browser push is consented separately from phone push. The caller names which transports it checked. [code] (push-notification-service.ts:255-280)
- Account binding: each Expo push carries a hash of the account id. The phone drops a push whose hash is not for the current account, or that has no hash. [code] (push-notification-service.ts:157-165; apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:68-100)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are requirements from documents, not claims about running behaviour.

- **Execution boundaries are explicit.** Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries. Nothing may silently move a Local chat to the cloud. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6). Chat sync must therefore stay cloud-mode only.
- **One AGI Subscription system.** Plan limits must come from the shared entitlement code, not from per-app copies. [requirement] (AGENTS.md sections 3-4). Remote Control already reads the shared capability table.
- **Remote Control exit criteria.** A pairing can be revoked from either side and takes effect on the next request, and a controlled device shows that it is being controlled for as long as it is. [requirement] (packages/contracts/types/src/feature-registry.json:187)
- **Relay is a dependency, not a trust anchor.** It can read payloads but cannot forge them, and local work must continue when it is down. [requirement] (docs/architecture/remote-control.md)
- **Adding a control verb** is a three-place change: relay list, host controller, companion. [requirement] (docs/architecture/remote-control.md)
- **Irreversible actions ask first.** Disconnecting a phone names its consequence (it can no longer follow or steer sessions). The web panel does this. [code] (RemoteControlSection.tsx, `DISCONNECT_CONSEQUENCE`)
- **Free usage screens show Upgrade only, never meters** (owner decision recorded in project memory; not a repository document). [unknown] as to a repo path.
- **Mobile v1 should hide Remote Control until the relay host is live.** [requirement] (docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md:50-56). To ship it later, both flags must flip and the relay host must answer a health check with a phone pairing a desktop. [requirement] (audit/decisions/founder-actions.md:285)
- **[proposed]** Keep a single table of push event types shared by server and phone. The phone's code comment still says only the schedule service sends push, while several producers now do (see Gaps).
