sections.markdown:
Nothing was run for this page. These are the checks a person can run, and the tests that already exist. Heavy jobs run through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh` and scoped tests through `scripts/dev/light-job.sh` (CLAUDE.md).

**Existing tests (not run here)**

- Sync: test:apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/__tests__/route.contract.test.ts, route.metadata-object.test.ts, route.turn-ending.live.test.ts, plus `route.artifact-index.test.ts`, `route.compaction-cache.test.ts`, `route.google-user-data.test.ts` beside the route. Run web tests inside `apps/web` with its own Vitest (AGENTS.md section 12).
- Pairing: test:apps/web/app/api/pair/__tests__/remote-control-switch.test.ts, standing-recheck-policy.test.ts, workspace-client-policy.test.ts.
- Relay: test:services/signaling-server/__tests__/control-payload.test.ts, pair-token.test.ts, standing.test.ts, device-revocation.test.ts, expired-pairings.test.ts, connection-manager.test.ts, plus folders `relay/`, `websocket/`, `http/`.
- Notifications: test:apps/web/app/api/notifications/__tests__/route.test.ts, test:apps/web/app/api/web-push/__tests__/route.test.ts, test:apps/web/app/api/mobile/push-token/__tests__/route.test.ts, test:apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/push-notification-service.test.ts, test:apps/web/app/api/email/unsubscribe/route.test.ts, identity events under apps/web/lib/services/identity-events/__tests__.
- Mobile: test:apps/mobile/__tests__/push-preference-sync.test.ts, notification-auth-gate.test.ts, NoPurchasesFeatureGates.test.tsx (the "Remote Control hidden in version 1" case), RemoteCompanion.test.tsx, connection-relay-retry.test.ts, manual-pairing.test.ts.
- Desktop host: test:apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/remoteControlHost.test.ts.

**What a person should check by hand**

1. Sync: sign in on two apps in cloud mode, write a message on one, and confirm it appears on the other within about 30 seconds on mobile. Watch for a conflict on edits to the same message.
2. Hidden features: build the phone app and confirm the Remote control row is missing and `/(app)/companion` shows the unavailable screen.
3. Relay: `curl` the relay health address and confirm healthy JSON, then pair a desktop with a phone (the founder-actions check). This needs `FEATURES.companion` and `FEATURES.dispatch` true and the relay deployed. Do not deploy without the owner's word.
4. Push: register a phone, trigger an agent run finishing, and confirm one banner. Turn on quiet hours and confirm the notice is held but the feed row remains.
5. Email: with Resend configured, change a sign-in setting and confirm a security email; turn `emailSecurityAlerts` off and confirm it stops unless advanced account security is on.
6. Instrument check (AGENTS.md section 1): when testing push, make sure your own test sends are not counted as product traffic, and that a phone signed in as another account drops the push.

key_facts.fact: Chat sync is one route with GET (pull by version cursor) and POST (push with baseVersion and conflicts), exported from apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts.
Pull pages are capped at 500 conversations, 1000 messages and 500 artifacts; hasMore is true when any list is full; temporary chats are never synced.
Sync protocol version is 2 with minimum 2; older clients get a client-update-required error, newer ones a validation error.
Push checks, in order: CSRF, rate limit, workspace chat_sync policy, protocol version, schema, project ownership, free daily allowance.
Mobile syncs chats, memory, projects and settings every 30 seconds while active and on foreground, only in cloud mode with a signed-in account.
CLI and Chrome use the same hosted sync records; CLI pushes and pulls through /api/chat/sync, Chrome pulls the conversations scope.
Remote Control pairing is created by api:POST /api/pair/initiate (default 300 s, 30 to 900 s) and claimed by api:POST /api/pair/claim; the relay refuses a claim from another account.
Remote Control needs a paid plan (basic and above); free gets 403 plan_upgrade_required, and an unreadable plan gets 503.
The relay rechecks live pairings through api:POST /api/pair/standing about every 60 s, tolerates a web outage for 5 minutes, and caps pairing life at 7 days by default.
Relay messages are signed envelopes (version 3, HMAC, nonce, timestamp), not encrypted; the relay cannot forge them.
The relay forwards only allow-listed actions; normal control payloads max 4 KB, code-session and dispatch payloads max 48 KB.
Three hosts exist for Remote Control: Electron desktop, VS Code extension and the CLI command agi remote-control.

In mobile v1 the switches companion, dispatch, billing, videoGen, bankLinking, pluginMarketplaceAdmin, appLanguage and linkBrowser are false, so Remote Control is hidden and its routes show an unavailable screen.
The stated reason for hiding Remote Control is that signaling.agiworkforce.com is not deployed; the live relay is at a Fly address.
Notice channels are in-app feed (table notifications), email via Resend, Expo push for phones and Web Push for browsers; the two push transports are consented separately.
The in-app feed is served by api:GET /api/notifications and marked read by api:PATCH /api/notifications; the web bell polls every 60 s.
Feed rows are de-duplicated by (user_id, dedupe_key) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; terminal agent events use a run-based key.
Phone push tokens are stored by api:POST /api/mobile/push-token in table mobile_devices; a device id owned by another account gets 403.
Browser subscriptions are stored by api:POST /api/web-push in web_push_subscriptions; the endpoint must resolve to a public host.
Expo push goes to a fixed Expo endpoint in batches of 100 with a 10 s timeout; DeviceNotRegistered clears the token.
Quiet hours hold push; if quiet hours cannot be read the notice is queued as job notifications.deferred-push and the feed row stays.
Each Expo push carries a hash of the account id; the phone drops a push bound to another account or with no binding.
Security email for identity events is sent unless emailSecurityAlerts is off, and users in advanced account security cannot opt out.

Identity events (27 keys, e.g. new_sign_in, password_changed) write a feed notice, an email, an audit event and a risk observation; a compromise assessment triggers session and device-credential revocation.
A CLI host reports local code-session activity to api:POST /api/code/local-sessions/activity; the server records a feed row and pushes to phones only (Expo, not browser).
A first heartbeat from a new device (api:POST /api/devices/heartbeat) triggers a new-device notice.
Marketing email has a signed one-click unsubscribe at api:GET and api:POST /api/email/unsubscribe, linked to Settings > Privacy on expiry.
No document in the project was found that records a real run of sync, Remote Control or push; all verification status is unknown.

How does the Chrome extension write conversations to the account? Only its pull of the conversations scope was traced.
Does the VS Code extension sync chat history, and does it get any push or email? Not traced.
Does mobile read the server notification feed (api:GET /api/notifications) or only its local store of 50 items? Only the web client of the feed was found.
How does the Electron desktop chat sync? It shows the hosted web app, and the conversation routes it uses were not traced.
Is sync allowed in mode:own-key? Code does not say; AGENTS.md section 6 requires an explicit consent fork between Local and BYOK.
Which plan should gate Remote Control: developer_surfaces (Pro and above, per the feature registry) or remote_control (Basic and above, per the code)?

Should browsers also get push for local code-session activity? The code sends phones only.
The relay README says initiator defaults to desktop while the web pairing route defaults to mobile; which default is intended?

doc.summary: The web app (Next.js on Vercel) is watched by Pino logs with redaction, Sentry plus optional OTLP traces, OpenTelemetry metrics, and a health endpoint. 47 Vercel crons do background work, and some also detect outages and burning error budgets. Alerts go through one dispatcher (email, pager, channel, out-of-band). Rate limits live in one table backed by Redis. Capacity figures are unmeasured targets. Other apps have only partial telemetry.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how the **running hosted system** (the Next.js web service, surface:web, which also serves the API used by every other app) is watched and kept alive. It answers: where do logs go, what is traced, what is measured, which scheduled jobs exist, what limits requests, how health is reported, how errors are classed, and where to look when something fails.

Why it exists [requirement]: `docs/runbooks/incident-response.md` says that until 2026-08-09 nothing in the repository could reach a human when production broke; the probe, burn-rate alerting and dispatcher were added to fix that. `AGENTS.md` section 8 says scale is a target and a concurrency figure may never be claimed without a live run (also stated in `docs/runbooks/capacity-and-load-testing.md`).

Scope note: everything below is the **hosted** service. Local inference on desktop and mobile is not watched by any of it [inferred: none of these routes or crons see on-device work]. See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for the turn path and the subscription pages for quotas and credits.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
All statements are [code] unless marked.

### Logs
- `apps/web/lib/logger.ts` builds a Pino logger. Every record gets `service`, `version` (release SHA), `region`, `deploy_env`, and, inside a request, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `request_id`, `organization_id`, `user_id` (`traceLogFields` in `apps/web/lib/observability/trace-context.ts:96-104`).
- Deployed runtimes refuse `trace` and `debug` however `LOG_LEVEL` is set; the floor is `info` (`logger.ts` `resolveLogLevel`, `MINIMUM_DEPLOYED_LEVEL`). Development defaults to `debug` with `pino-pretty` unless `AGI_DEV_LOG_FORMAT=json`.
- Strings and records are redacted by key and by secret pattern before output (`redactLogRecord`, `redactSecrets`; key denylist in `apps/web/lib/observability/log-field-policy.ts`: prompt, body, token, email, password and similar). A repo guard `scripts/check-log-redaction.mjs` loads that policy file (comment at the top of `log-field-policy.ts`).
- Where logs are shipped is [unknown]: the logger writes to the platform stream; no log drain is configured in the repository.

### Traces and spans
- `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` `register()` runs once at server start. In Node it installs trace storage and the provider tracer, validates environment (fails boot in production unless `AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV=1`), asserts a pooled database endpoint, preloads platform keys, and records configuration states.
- Sentry starts only when `NODE_ENV=production` and a DSN exists (`apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts` `isSentryConfigured`). Release is the commit SHA; environment comes from the Vercel environment so previews are not filed as production.
- OTLP export is **off unless** `AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT` is a valid URL (`apps/web/lib/observability/otel-config.ts:15-20, 71-86`). Other settings: `AGI_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (default `agiworkforce-web`), `AGI_OTEL_HEADERS`, `AGI_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO`, `AGI_OTEL_SLOW_SPAN_MS` (default 1000 ms).
- Sampling is **tail-biased** (`otel-sdk.ts:55-85`, `trace-sampling.ts`): every span is recorded; at span end it is exported if it errored, ran at least the slow threshold, or its trace id falls in the sample ratio (decided on the last 8 hex digits, so a trace is kept or dropped whole). With OTLP on, Sentry records all traces (rate 1) so this tail filter decides (`otel-config.ts` `sentryTracesSampleRate`).
- Spans use closed domains: approval, billing, database, external, http, model, queue, retrieval, sandbox, task, tool (`apps/web/lib/observability/span.ts:15-27`). A span can be closed as a deliberate refusal so refusals are not counted as success (`ActiveSpan.refuse`).
- Incoming `traceparent` is parsed and a request id header `x-request-id` is used (`trace-context.ts` `parseTraceparent`; `packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/header-names.ts:11`). `apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts` wraps routes, records the HTTP metric, and returns the request id with errors.
- Exported spans pass a privacy filter (`PrivacyFilteredSpanExporter` in `sentry-otel-export.ts`).

### Metrics
`apps/web/lib/observability/metrics.ts` defines the OpenTelemetry instruments (names in `METRIC_NAME`, lines 21-62): HTTP request count and duration, span count and duration, tool calls, browser tasks, notification deliveries, `agi.failures` (kinds: api, browser, client, connector, database, mcp, model, notification, remote, tool, worker), database operation count and duration, queue depth, wait, age and stuck, routing decisions, turn counts, time to first token, duration, cost and retries, completions and false-success, denials (layers: capability, policy, entitlement, surface), rejections, client failures, configuration state, media generation. Label values are bounded so series cannot explode (`cardinality.ts`: enumerated, bounded with a default limit of 50, overflow label `other`). `apps/web/lib/observability/dashboards.ts` declares 20 dashboards as data (for example http-traffic, job-health, turn-latency-and-cost, database-health, client-health, completion-truth); rendering them in a vendor tool is [unknown].

### Client failures
Browsers send closed-vocabulary failure classes (no free text, strict schema) in batches to `api:POST /api/telemetry/client`; it needs CSRF, the `client-telemetry` limit (30 per minute, fail closed), and the user's telemetry consent (`apps/web/app/api/telemetry/client/route.ts`; sender `client-failure-transport.ts`, 20 reports per page budget, 5 s timeout, one attempt).

### Scheduled jobs
47 crons are registered in `vercel.json` (`crons`), one per route directory under `apps/web/app/api/cron/`; `apps/web/app/api/cron/cron-registration.test.ts` fails if a route is unscheduled, a schedule points nowhere, a path repeats, or an expression is not five fields. Each route checks `verifyCronRequest` (bearer `CRON_SECRET`, constant-time compare, 10 failures per minute per client throttle, fail closed when no secret; a dev bypass works only with `CRON_DEV_BYPASS=1` on a loopback host in development; `apps/web/lib/server/cron-auth.ts`). Full cadence table is in Data and state.

### Detection and alerting
- `api:GET /api/cron/health-probe` (every 10 min) runs `runHealthChecks()` directly with an 8 s timeout, tracks a failure streak in the key-value store (`agi-health-probe:consecutive-failures`, TTL 1800 s) and pages only on the **second consecutive** miss (`route.ts:21-25, 146-160`). Healthy clears the incident. `unhealthy` maps to critical, `degraded` to warning; a thrown or timed-out check pages critical as `probe_failed` with HTTP 500.
- `evaluate-slo-burn` (at :05 and :35) evaluates error-budget burn and cost or latency anomalies. Fast window 1 h at 14.4x burn is critical; slow window 6 h at 6x is warning; fewer than 20 samples stays silent (`apps/web/lib/server/slo/attainment.ts:210-215`).
- `page-security-anomalies` (every 30 min), `reconcile-credits` (email on terminal settlements) and `remind-free-quota-renewal` also reach humans [requirement: incident-response.md detector table].
- `apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts` is the one exit: email to the on-call responder (or `AGI_SUPPORT_FALLBACK_EMAIL`), pager webhook (`PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL`), incident channel webhook (`INCIDENT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL`), and, only if none delivered, an out-of-band webhook (`INCIDENT_OUT_OF_BAND_WEBHOOK_URL` plus token) and a status mirror write (`AGI_STATUS_MIRROR_*`). Escalation level rises with how long the same incident key keeps firing (default 15 min per level), held in the key-value store for 6 hours as `agi-incident:<key>`.

### Health and status
- `api:GET /api/health` is public, rate limited (`health-check`, 30 per minute), `Cache-Control: no-store`. It serves a cached result (60 s render cache, stale after 120 s). A stale result triggers one shared refresh bounded to 8 s; if that fails it answers 503 with `stale: true`. `unhealthy` also answers 503; `healthy` and `degraded` answer 200 (`app/api/health/route.ts:81-111`). Public check messages are reduced to `unavailable` or `not configured` so no component name leaks.
- `/status` (`apps/web/app/status/page.tsx`) renders the same checks plus SLO attainment, and says a passing check does not verify a model response.
- Core checks (database, environment, cache) failing means `unhealthy`; Stripe, chat routing, work queues, voice routing, search, vector and identity failing means `degraded` (`apps/web/lib/server/health-check.ts:474-500`). The key-value store is core on purpose: rate limiting fails closed, so turns cannot be served without it.

### Rate limits
`apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts` holds `rateLimitConfigs` (147 named buckets, each with a limit, a window and `failClosed`). Limits are enforced in Redis-compatible shared storage with an 800 ms limiter budget. Key points are in Rules.

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
### Cron cadence (from `vercel.json`, UTC)

| Cadence | Routes |
| --- | --- |
| Every 5 min | `drain-background-jobs`, `sweep-chat-file-intakes` |
| Every 10 min | `health-probe`, `index-retrieval-documents` |
| Every 15 min | `live-artifacts-refresh`, `run-schedules`, `recover-reservations` (:00/:15/:30/:45) |
| Four times an hour, offset | `notify-upgrade-waitlist` (:04,:19,:34,:49), `reap-code-turns` (:05,:20,:35,:50), `reap-agent-runs` (:10,:25,:40,:55) |
| Every 10 min offset | `run-auto-reloads` (:07,:17,...:57) |
| Every 30 min | `drain-audit-streams`, `page-security-anomalies`, `evaluate-slo-burn` (:05,:35) |
| Hourly | `remind-trials` (:13), `reclaim-sandboxes` (:11), `replicate-object-backups` (:06), `expire-code-trials` (:06), `evaluate-model-rollout` (:05), `remind-free-quota-renewal` (:05) |
| Daily | `reset-credits` 00:00, `reconcile-credits` 00:07, `expire-bonus-credits` 00:12, `enforce-billing-retention` 01:00, `expire-purchased-credits` 01:06, `grant-referral-rewards` 01:10, `reconcile-provider-costs` 01:03, `reconcile-billed-plans` 01:11, `expire-support-handoffs` 02:00, `expire-support-access-grants` 02:03, `purge-security-audit-logs` 02:07, `roll-up-product-metrics` 02:10, `purge-temporary-chats` 03:00, `expire-memories` 03:05, `purge-deleted-media` 04:00, `purge-deleted-accounts` 04:07, `enforce-workspace-retention` 04:05, `purge-soft-deleted-resources` 04:10, `purge-deleted-organizations` 04:12, `enforce-domain-retention` 04:14, `expire-organization-invitations` 05:00, `enforce-billing-collection` 05:05, `report-enterprise-usage` 05:10, `refresh-connector-directory` 06:03, `refresh-plugin-directory` 06:08, `renew-gmail-watches` 06:13 |
| Monthly | `allocate-infrastructure-costs` (06:00 on the 5th) |

Max durations seen: `drain-background-jobs`, `reap-agent-runs`, `reap-code-turns`, `recover-reservations`, `reclaim-sandboxes` 300 s; `run-schedules` 60 s; `health-probe` 30 s; `evaluate-slo-burn` 60 s. The drain has a 250 s budget and at most 12 jobs in flight (`drain-background-jobs/route.ts:15-18`). `run-schedules` claims waves of 10 with a 40 s wave timeout and a 55 s sweep budget (`run-schedules/route.ts:12-20`).

### Low-power mode
`AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1` makes any cron call after minute 14 of the hour return `{"skipped":"db_low_power"}` (`cron-low-power.ts`, window 15 minutes). Crons that call `lowPowerCronSkip` then run only in the first 15 minutes of each hour, so the 15-minute and 30-minute crons effectively run hourly. `docs/runbooks/capacity-and-load-testing.md` says to set it in Production on the Neon Free plan; whether it is set now is [unknown].

### Service level objectives (`apps/web/lib/server/slo/catalogue.ts`)
Objectives are computed from named production tables over a 30-day window. Examples: authentication 99.9% (`authentication_attempts`), chat 99% (`routing_decision_traces`, served turns reaching success), first token 95% within 3000 ms, completion 95% within 120000 ms, tool execution 99% (`agent_tool_executions`), work 99% (`background_jobs`), research 95% (`research_reports`), search 99% (`search_history`), file upload and parsing 99% (`product_analytics_events`, consented accounts only), remote control 95%, notifications 99% (declared, instrument missing), billing events 99.9%. Some are `audience: 'internal'` (billing-usage, entitlement-activation) and never published. A definition may carry `missingInstrument` instead of a source.

### Stores
- Key-value store (Upstash Redis REST, or Vercel KV names): rate limit counters (prefix `agi-rl:<bucket>`), managed turn slots (`agi-turns:<userId>`, TTL 360 s), health streak, incident state.
- Postgres (Neon): the SLO source tables above, `credit_settlement_jobs`, `background_jobs`, `mcp_response_cache`. Table list for observability itself is [unknown] beyond these.
- Domain events (`docs/standards/domain-events.md`): 29 catalogued events named `<namespace>.<object>.<verb>`, each with data class, PII fields, retention class and consumers (audit-log, siem-export, product-analytics, notifications, read-model). Retention class is set by the catalogue, not the producer. Delivery is at least once; consumers dedupe on `dedupeKey`.
- Device stores: none are used by this subject on the server. CLI crash reports go to a local `crash-reports` folder (max 20 pending) before upload (`apps/cli/src/crash_reports.rs:13-20`).

### Configuration names (purpose only)
`LOG_LEVEL`, `AGI_DEV_LOG_FORMAT`, `AGI_OTEL_*`, `SENTRY_DSN` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_RELEASE`, `CRON_SECRET`, `CRON_DEV_BYPASS`, `AGI_DB_LOW_POWER`, `AGI_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE` (ignored in production), `AGI_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_OUTAGE_POLICY`, `AGI_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN` (or `KV_REST_API_*`), `PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL`, `INCIDENT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL`, `INCIDENT_OUT_OF_BAND_*`, `AGI_STATUS_MIRROR_*`, `AGI_ONCALL_*`, `AGI_SUPPORT_FALLBACK_EMAIL`, `AGI_SUPPORT_FROM_EMAIL`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV`.

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Who may call what
- Cron routes: only with `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`; 401 otherwise; also fail closed when no secret is set (`cron-auth.ts`). Calling one by hand is the same call the scheduler makes (`incident-response.md`).
- `api:GET /api/health` and `/status` are public. Public payloads hide component names and error text.
- `api:POST /api/telemetry/client` needs CSRF and telemetry consent; a browser that refused telemetry sends nothing (`client-failure-transport.ts` `mayReport`).

### Rate limit rules
- Production **requires** shared-store credentials: importing `rate-limit.ts` throws `SEV-WEB-13` in a production runtime without them (`rate-limit.ts:22-30`).
- Each bucket is `failClosed` true or false. When the shared store errors or times out (800 ms) a fail-closed bucket refuses with 429 and `Retry-After: 60` and a fail-open bucket admits. The deployment policy `AGI_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_OUTAGE_POLICY` can force either; default is fail-closed when credentials exist or in production (`redis-outage-policy.ts`). If the store's request quota is exhausted the limiter falls back to per-instance counting and sets `X-RateLimit-Degraded: shared-store-quota` (`rate-limit.ts` catch block).
- Examples [code]: `chat-message` 20 per minute fail open; `llm-completion` 30 per minute per user fail closed; `llm-completion-ip` 1500 per minute fail closed; `chat-conversation` 60 per minute; `health-check` 30 per minute; `client-telemetry` 30 per minute fail closed; `guest-chat-device` and `guest-chat-ip` per day from `GUEST_CHAT_CONFIG` fail closed; `default` 100 per minute.
- **Plan scaling:** keys in `TIER_SCALED_KEYS` (`llm-completion`, `chat-message`, `chat-conversation`, `chat-conversation-read`, `chat-conversation-list`, `image-generation`, `video-generation`, `audio-transcription`, `voice-speech`, `voice-live-session`) multiply the base limit by the plan's `maxConcurrentTurns` from `BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS` in `@agiworkforce/types` (`rate-limit.ts` `resolveTierRateLimit`). Plan names and values live in that package, not here. Whether every caller passes the plan tier is [unknown].
- **Concurrent turns:** `acquireManagedTurnSlot` admits a managed turn only under the plan's concurrent limit; denial reasons are `plan-excluded`, `ceiling-reached`, `limiter-unavailable`. Slots expire after 360 s, just above the 300 s maximum chat duration (`rate-limit.ts` comment on `MANAGED_TURN_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`; `app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:161` sets `maxDuration = 300`).
- A 429 body has `error.code = RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `retry_after_seconds`, `reset_at` and an appeal path; the block is audit logged (`logRateLimitExceeded`).
- The client IP source is configurable (`x-real-ip` default, `xff-rightmost`, `xff-hop:N`) so a caller cannot dodge limits by editing `x-forwarded-for`.
- Developer API limits are tabulated in `docs/standards/api-rate-limits.md`; API-key traffic falls back to the IP bucket.

### Modes and plans
- mode:local: nothing on this page governs on-device inference. It has no server limit, quota or health check [inferred].
- mode:own-key and mode:cloud: turns that reach the hosted API are subject to the limits above. Whether the managed turn slot applies to own-key turns is [unknown].
- Free usage screens show only Upgrade, not meters [memory note, not a repository document]; the free quota gate renewal is watched by `remind-free-quota-renewal`.
- Telemetry that carries user data follows consent: product analytics SLOs read consented accounts only; client failures need consent; CLI crash reports need privacy mode `Managed` and the setting or `AGI_CRASH_REPORTS`.
- Trust boundary: health and telemetry payloads must carry no prompts or content (`log-field-policy.ts`, strict client schema).

The shared `@agiworkforce/observability` package (error reporting port, scrub step, Sentry envelope adapter) is described as shared by browser-adjacent surfaces (package.json). Which apps import it was not verified.

The `/status` page and the `surface-status.ts` map (`apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts`) are different things: the status page reports service checks; `SURFACE_STATUS` is marketing availability labels (web Available now, others Coming soon).

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
### Error categories
User-visible errors carry a code, a class, an HTTP status, `retryable`, a suggested action and a request id (`packages/contracts/types/src/error-taxonomy.ts` `UserFacingError`). The 23 classes and their retry flag from `error-taxonomy.json`:

| Retryable | Classes |
| --- | --- |
| yes | rate_limit, provider_unavailable, timeout, network, offline, storage, database, search, tool, connector, sandbox, internal |
| no | authentication, authorization, policy, entitlement, validation, unsupported, conflict, not_found, deleted, quota, safety |

Only provider_unavailable, storage, search, tool, connector and sandbox may show the upstream's name and status; all other classes hide provider detail. `scripts/check-error-model.mjs` fails a code with no class (comment at the top of `error-taxonomy.ts`). A route error handler hides internal messages behind generic text except a safe list of codes such as `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `CREDIT_REQUIRED`, `SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED` (`apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts`).

Note: `docs/agent-context/llm-failure-taxonomy.json` (28 categories such as `error-handling-failures`, `reliability-scalability-failures`, `webhook-failures`) is **not** a runtime error list. It is a guardrail vocabulary for agents and repository checks about code defects [code: its `purpose` field]. Do not use it to classify production errors.

### Severity and response (from `incident-response.md`, matches code)
| Condition | Overall status | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Database unreachable or no database URL | unhealthy, critical | Page now |
| Key-value store does not answer one read | unhealthy, critical | Page now; turns refuse |
| Harness threw or dependency hung beyond 8 s | `probe_failed`, critical, HTTP 500 | Page now |
| Stripe unreachable | degraded, warning | Billing only |
| Retrieval or embedding index missing | degraded, warning | Search over own content blind; chat unaffected |

### Where to look
1. `/status` or `api:GET /api/health` for which check fails.
2. Logs: search by `request_id` (given to the user) or `trace_id`; key messages: `Cache health check failed`, `Stripe health check failed` (field `step`: client, products.list, prices.retrieve, price.usable), `Health probe alert dispatched`, `Incident alert could NOT be delivered · no human has been told`, `Rate limit exceeded`, `Rate limit check failed, allowing request (fail-open)`.
3. Vercel cron log: an undeliverable alert returns HTTP 500 so the failed invocation shows there.
4. Neon dashboard (suspended compute, pool, region), Upstash dashboard (request quota), `status.stripe.com`.
5. Queue trouble: `evaluateJobHealth` warns when the oldest due job waited 15 min or 1 lease lapsed, and goes critical at 60 min or 5 lapsed (`slo/job-health.ts`). SQL for terminal credit settlements is in the runbook (`credit_settlement_jobs` where status is terminal).
6. Data integrity: run the reconcilers (`reconcile-credits`, `reconcile-billed-plans`, `recover-reservations`, `reconcile-provider-costs`, `purge-deleted-accounts`, `replicate-object-backups`, `drain-background-jobs`) before closing an incident; a 500 means unfinished.
7. Bad release: revert first (`docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md`, `scripts/release/rollback.mjs`); a rollback does not revert the database.

### Built-in resilience
- Health probe holds the first miss and pages on the second; detection latency is up to 20 minutes.
- `/api/health` shares one refresh among concurrent callers and refuses to call a stale result ready.
- Status page and health payloads never expose vendor errors.
- Retries are bounded (CLI crash upload: 5 s, one try; client failure post: one try) so telemetry cannot add load during an incident.
- Reapers and recoverers clean after dead turns: `reap-agent-runs`, `reap-code-turns`, `reclaim-sandboxes`, `recover-reservations` (returns held quota), `drain-background-jobs` (re-queues or dead-letters when a worker died).

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
[requirement] `AGENTS.md` section 8: horizontal scaling with bounded resources, backpressure, graceful degradation and observability; rate limits are configuration, never constants; 100,000 concurrent users is a target never to be claimed without a live run. Section 9: no silent failures. Section 6: security fails closed. `docs/runbooks/capacity-and-load-testing.md`: load tests never run against production, a failing threshold is the result, one variable per run, and a capacity figure may be promoted to the SLO catalogue only after a recorded run in `docs/research/`.

[proposed] Items worth deciding, each owned elsewhere if accepted: (1) a cross-process backpressure signal, since there is none today; (2) an alert on database connection pool exhaustion; (3) one documented place for where logs and metrics are viewed; (4) a shared, consent-gated crash and failure report path for desktop, mobile, VS Code and Chrome like the CLI and web ones; (5) instruments for the SLOs still declared without a source.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Nothing here was executed by this page's author; the project folder was read only. The checks below are what the repository provides.

- Cron registration: `apps/web/app/api/cron/cron-registration.test.ts`; worker registry: `deployable-components.test.ts`; low-power windows: `apps/web/__tests__/cron-low-power-window.test.ts`.
- Health probe and alert decisions: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web exec vitest run app/api/cron/health-probe lib/server/incident` (from the runbook). It does not test real delivery.
- Alert path drill (real): follow the numbered drill in `docs/runbooks/incident-response.md` on a preview deployment; expect `"alerted":true,"delivery":"delivered"` on the second call.
- SLO logic: `apps/web/lib/server/slo/__tests__/{catalogue,attainment,anomaly,job-health,degradation}.test.ts`.
- Logger: `apps/web/lib/logger.test.ts`; tracing: `apps/web/lib/observability/__tests__` and the `*.test.ts` files beside `otel-sdk.ts`, `trace-sampling.ts`, `trace-context.ts`.
- Rate limits: `apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/__tests__/developer-api-contract.test.ts` pins the developer table.
- Domain events: `packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/__tests__/domain-events.test.ts`.
- Live: `curl` the public `api:GET /api/health` (expect 200 or 503 and `Cache-Control: no-store`); call a cron with the bearer secret (expect 401 without it).
- Load: `tools/load-test/README.md`; record results in `docs/research/` before updating the capacity table.

key_facts.fact: 47 crons are registered in vercel.json, one per directory under apps/web/app/api/cron, and a test enforces that they match.
Every cron route requires a bearer CRON_SECRET, compared in constant time, throttled at 10 failures per minute per client, and fails closed when no secret is configured.
The health probe runs every 10 minutes, times out its checks at 8 s, and pages only on the second consecutive failure, so outage detection takes up to about 20 minutes.
Core health checks are database, environment and key-value cache; failing any means unhealthy. Stripe, chat routing, work queues, voice, search, vector and identity failing means degraded.
GET /api/health is public, no-store, rate limited to 30 per minute, caches results 60 s, treats results older than 120 s as stale and answers 503 for unhealthy or stale.
Public health payloads reduce messages to 'unavailable' or 'not configured' so component names and vendor errors do not leak.
Burn-rate alerting: fast window 1 h at 14.4x is critical, slow window 6 h at 6x is warning, and fewer than 20 samples stays silent; evaluated at :05 and :35.

SLOs are defined only in apps/web/lib/server/slo/catalogue.ts over a 30-day window (for example chat 99%, first token 95% within 3000 ms, completion 95% within 120000 ms, authentication 99.9%); some are declared with a missing instrument.

All incidents leave through one dispatcher: email to on-call (or support fallback mailbox), pager webhook, incident channel webhook, then an out-of-band webhook and status mirror if none delivered; escalation levels rise every 15 minutes by default while the condition persists.
Logs use Pino with redaction; deployed runtimes force a minimum level of info, whatever LOG_LEVEL says.
Every log line inside a request carries trace_id, span_id, request_id, organization_id and user_id when known.
OTLP trace and metric export is enabled only when AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT is a valid URL; default service name is agiworkforce-web.
Trace export is tail-biased: errored spans and spans over the slow threshold (default 1000 ms) are always exported; others are kept by trace-id ratio so a trace is whole.
Sentry initialises only in production with a DSN; production boot fails on invalid environment unless AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV=1.
The rate limiter has 147 named buckets; each is fail-closed or fail-open, and production throws at import if shared store credentials are missing.

Rate limit shared-store calls have an 800 ms budget; on failure fail-closed buckets answer 429 with Retry-After 60, and when store quota is exhausted the limiter counts per instance and sets X-RateLimit-Degraded.
Chat-related rate limits scale by the plan's maxConcurrentTurns for ten tier-scaled buckets; the AGI_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE override is ignored in production.
Managed turn slots live in the key-value store with a 360 s TTL, just above the 300 s chat maxDuration, and can be denied as plan-excluded, ceiling-reached or limiter-unavailable.
There is no global backpressure; admission is per conversation, per user and for video, so saturation first shows as latency.
All capacity targets are unmeasured; four dimensions have no load scenario, and no concurrency figure may be claimed without a recorded run.
With AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1 crons answer {skipped: db_low_power} after minute 14 of each hour, so frequent crons effectively run hourly.
Runtime error classes are 23 (authentication through internal), each with a retryable flag decided server side; only six classes may show upstream provider name and status.
llm-failure-taxonomy.json is a guardrail vocabulary of 28 code-defect categories for agents, not a runtime error list.
Browser failure telemetry is a strict closed schema posted to /api/telemetry/client, needs CSRF, consent and a 30 per minute limit, with one attempt and a 20-report page budget.
CLI crash reports are stored as local JSON files (max 20) and uploaded with a 5 s timeout only when privacy mode is managed and enabled.
Job queue health warns at 15 minutes oldest-due age or 1 lapsed lease and goes critical at 60 minutes or 5 lapsed leases.
Domain events: 29 catalogued durable events with data class, retention class and consumers, written once and consumed idempotently by dedupeKey.
Metrics label cardinality is bounded (default 50 values, overflow label 'other') and enforced by a test.

doc.summary: AGI Workforce guards secrets with a repo-wide scanner and encrypted key rings. Cloud-bound egress is blocked in Local mode by shared host rules and per-surface guards. Uploads get structural, credential and ClamAV checks that fail closed in production. Users get export (24-hour link), 24-hour delayed deletion, 30-day recovery, 2FA, passkeys and step-up. Public claims are tied to tests, and no SOC 2, ISO or pen-test is claimed.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers the security model of AGI Workforce and the privacy controls a user can reach. It exists so that public copy, settings screens and engineering rules all say what the code does.

**Core idea.** Rules are enforced by guards (scripts that fail CI) and by claim ledgers (files that tie each public sentence to code and a test). A document that disagrees with code is a bug in the document. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 2; docs/security/security.md:5-13)

**Three trust boundaries.** Local, BYOK (bring your own key) and Managed Cloud are separate. Nothing may silently move a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or cloud. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)

**Why the claim ledgers exist.** An earlier audit found marketing copy that described a permission model the code did not implement. The fix was one matrix that copy is rendered against. [code] (docs/security/security.md:34-39)

**Honesty about certification.** The public trust page says no SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate or third-party penetration test exists. [code] (apps/web/app/trust/page.tsx:87, 289). The ledger rows are in docs/compliance/trust-claims.json (39 rows: EVIDENCE, COMPLIANCE, POSTURE) and are reviewed on a 90-day cadence. [code] (docs/compliance/trust-claims.json:2-3)

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline (tool loop that calls the approval gate), and any page on billing, connectors and the model catalog.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Secrets handling

- **Repository scan.** `pnpm check:secrets` runs scripts/check-secrets.mjs. It reads files tracked by git and matches named credential shapes: PEM private keys, Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq, xAI, Stripe live, Slack, GitHub, Google, AWS, Supabase, OpenRouter, Perplexity and generic `sk-` keys, plus Postgres/Redis URLs with passwords and JSON private keys. [code] (scripts/check-secrets.mjs:25-62). Obvious fakes are masked (words like EXAMPLE, counting runs of six or more characters). [code] (scripts/check-secrets.mjs:10-13, 64-120). Reviewed exceptions live in scripts/secret-scan-allowlist.json, keyed by path and credential format; stale entries are reported. [code] (scripts/secret-scan-allowlist.json:1-20). `--history` also scans git history objects with no allowlist. [code] (scripts/check-secrets.mjs:429-471; package.json:433). It runs inside `pnpm check:llm-operability`. [code] (package.json:397)
- **Other secret guards.** check-client-bundle-secrets (secrets in shipped client bundles), check-cli-local-secret (no literal credential in CLI local servers), check-connector-secret-reseal (every connector secret class has a re-seal column), check-crypto-context-binding. [code] (scripts/check-cli-local-secret.mjs:1-6; scripts/check-connector-secret-reseal.mjs; package.json:233,311)
- **Encryption at rest.** Connector tokens, GitHub installation tokens and TOTP secrets are AES-256-GCM sealed by a key ring: an active key, an id and a retired list (`<NAME>`, `<NAME>_ID`, `<NAME>_RETIRED`). [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:657-714). Three keys are on a 12-month rotation, next due 2027-08-17. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:750-754). Keys live only in deployment environment variables; the doc records this as an accepted risk (no KMS, no escrow). [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:761-790). KMS adapters for AWS, GCP and Azure exist behind a provider seam but the default is `env`. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:819-827)
- **Where each client keeps credentials.** CLI: OS keychain on macOS and Windows; owner-only files on Linux or when `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING` is set. [code] (apps/cli/src/secure_store.rs:1-6). Mobile: the database key is held in expo-secure-store, accessible only when unlocked and this device only. [code] (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:2,45-52). Chrome extension: `chrome.storage.local` holds settings such as the site allowlist. [code] (apps/extension/src/background.ts:4118-4138). Desktop: the hosted web session lives in an app-only browser profile; the CLI keeps the sign-in in the OS store; Desktop accepts no provider keys. [requirement] (apps/web/app/trust/page.tsx:179-182). VS Code: [unknown] where provider keys are stored (a providerSetup grep for `secrets.` returned nothing).

### 2. Egress rules

- **Local mode must never reach our cloud.** The shared package `@agiworkforce/trust-boundaries` holds `OUR_CLOUD_HOSTS` (agiworkforce.com, vercel.app, neon.tech and four Clerk domains) and `isOurCloudHost`, a suffix match. BYOK provider hosts are deliberately not on the list. [code] (packages/contracts/trust-boundaries/src/egress-policy.ts:33-72)
- **Per-surface chokepoints.** Desktop's `guardedFetch` throws before any network call when the workspace is Local and the host is ours. [code] (apps/desktop/src/lib/egressGuard.ts:1-60). Mobile has its own `apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts` with a path allowlist (account deletion, data export, step-up and similar). [code] (apps/mobile/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts:21-37)
- **Guards that enforce it.** check-desktop-local-egress (every renderer outbound call must be `guardedFetch`, files enumerated from the tree), check-rust-egress-boundary (Rust HTTP use outside an allowlist of 22 files fails), check-security-egress-inventory (every server outbound target is a repo-chosen host or resolved and refused before the socket opens), check-mcp-dial-egress (every MCP dial names `MCP_EGRESS_POLICY`). [code] (scripts/check-desktop-local-egress.mjs; scripts/check-rust-egress-boundary.mjs:10-33; scripts/check-security-egress-inventory.mjs; scripts/check-mcp-dial-egress.mjs)
- **Server-side limits.** Remote MCP endpoints pass DNS-resolution SSRF validation. Code sandboxes (E2B) default to no network or a fixed allowlist of code hosts, and extra hosts are resolved and refused if private. A raw managed provider key never enters a sandbox. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:309, 358-392)

### 3. Tool approval and the lethal-trifecta gate

`resolveToolCallGate` evaluates nine ranks: a saved `deny` wins, a saved `allow` is overridden by the trifecta, and an escalation never becomes an allow (unattended runs pause at a checkpoint or deny). [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-call-gate.ts:138-159). The trifecta is: untrusted content in context, plus a reachable sensitive source, plus a call that creates an egress path. Pasted user text is not counted as untrusted. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:201-217). A saved Block is enforced at execution, not by hiding the tool from the model. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:219-229). The website account default is `autonomous`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:13)

### 4. Upload scanning

Every route that materialises user-uploaded bytes runs the same three steps: structural inspection, credential scan, external scan. [requirement] (docs/security/upload-scanning.md:5-30). The external scanner is our own ClamAV service (services/upload-scanner). In production the scanner is required unless `UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false`; with no `UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL` and required, every upload is refused with `scan_unavailable`. [code] (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-436). A non-OK scanner reply, a timeout (15 s on the web side) or an unsafe verdict all refuse the file. [code] (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:442-480). Password-protected files are refused with a dedicated message. [requirement] (docs/security/upload-scanning.md:77-85)

### 5. Account security

Step-up (fresh reverification) is demanded for account deletion, 2FA changes, identity unlink, email change, password change, API-credential reveal, passkey enrolment and change, and workspace ownership transfer. The window is 300 s (120 s for revealing an API credential). [code] (apps/web/lib/server/step-up/actions.ts:15-58). Settings shows sessions, a log-out-everywhere action behind step-up, a session timeout, passkeys, 2FA and linked devices. [code] (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx:49-130, 192-214; apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:154-206). Suspended or banned accounts get 403 on every authenticated request, failing closed after one retry. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:345)

### 6. Privacy controls (web settings)

The Privacy section offers: crash and error reports (default off), "Only use models that do not train on your chats" (default off), two model-improvement switches for chats and voice (default off; the screen says nothing is used for this today), product-analytics and marketing-email consent, named-provider consent rows, a US-only routing panel, shared links, archived chats, Recently deleted, bulk conversation controls, temporary-by-default chats, a privacy-requests page, a Library link for uploaded files, and data export. [code] (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:46-122, 560-870). A Lockdown mode panel stores a preference. [code] (apps/web/features/settings/components/LockdownModePanel.tsx:1-40); what lockdown enforces server-side is [unknown].

### 7. Export and deletion

- **Export.** `GET/POST /api/user/export` and `/api/user/export/archives` build a JSON export or a zip archive by background job; the download link works for 24 hours, then an expire job removes the archive. [code] (apps/web/app/api/user/export/route.ts:3456-3458; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/data-export.ts:7; docs/architecture/RETENTION_MATRIX.md:84)
- **Deletion.** `DELETE /api/user/delete-account` requires step-up, refuses while the account is sole owner of a workspace (409), and schedules erasure 24 hours ahead; the user can cancel in that window. [code] (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:440-481). Erasure sweeps rows, object-store bytes, caches and email-keyed tables, and reports `complete` only when every store cleared. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:1158-1168)
- **Soft delete and temporary chats.** A deleted chat sits in Recently deleted for 30 days (`RESOURCE_RECOVERY_WINDOW_DAYS = 30`). Temporary chats and attachments are purged after 30 days (`RETENTION_DAYS = 30`). [code] (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:8; apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:24). The soft-delete purge cron only deletes when `SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED` is `true`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-soft-deleted-resources/route.ts:15)

### 8. Legal hold

The hold predicate sits inside every destructive WHERE clause; account and workspace erasure refuse outright when a hold applies. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:1170-1180). A hold beats the temporary-chat promise. [requirement] (docs/security/security.md:1199-1202)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Modes.**

| Mode | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| mode:local | Chats, files, telemetry and account data must not reach our cloud hosts; the guard blocks before the socket opens and fails closed when the mode is unknown | [code] (egress-policy.ts:1-20; egressGuard.ts:36-60) |
| mode:own-key | Client-direct to the user's own provider; provider hosts are not blocked; our servers never see the key traffic | [code] (egress-policy.ts:24-28) |
| mode:cloud | Server-side tool gate, sandbox limits, upload scan, connector grants and retention all apply | [code] |

The privacy screen says hosted Web and Desktop have neither Local nor BYOK, so everything sent there is a Cloud request. [code] (PrivacySection.tsx:486-500). A move from Local to BYOK must be an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)

**Plans.**
- Free plan: the privacy screen warns that free-model providers may train on chats unless "Only use models that do not train on your chats" is on. [code] (PrivacySection.tsx:508-514)
- Connectors and Remote Control are paid capabilities (`BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS`); `/api/pair/initiate` and `/api/pair/claim` refuse plans without `remote_control`. [requirement] (security.md:300-305)
- Per-plan caps: connector tool count, concurrent sandboxes, attachment size (every plan's max equals the scanner limit). [requirement] (security.md:307; upload-scanning.md:96-100)
- Rate limits: LLM 30 per minute per user, 1500 per minute per IP, both failClosed; conversation ops 60 per minute. [requirement] (security.md:347-349)

These are the same Subscription rules that apply on every app; security controls do not vary by plan, except the capability gates above.

**Claims the product may make.**
- Allowed: only what a ledger row proves. `check-security-claims` fails on a sentence with no entry or whose proof moved; `check-trust-claims` fails when text changes after review, a review is older than 90 days, or a proof moved. [code] (docs/security/security-claims.json:2-3; docs/compliance/trust-claims.json:2-3)
- Not allowed: SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, third-party pen-test claims; the ledger records none exist. [code] (trust/page.tsx:87)
- Must be said together: any claim about approval must also say write_file, execute_code and similar tools act in the conversation's own sandbox, not the user's device. [requirement] (security.md:192-199)
- Do not claim blocked tools are withheld from the model's offered catalog. [requirement] (security.md:225-229)
- Temporary-chat copy must carry the legal-hold exception. [requirement] (security.md:1199-1202)
- Public copy must not guess the GitHub App permission list; it is configured on GitHub and not declared in this repo. [requirement] (security.md:287-289)
- Local/BYOK public claims must be named by surface: the privacy screen assigns them to the CLI. [code] (PrivacySection.tsx:486-492)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
| Situation | Behaviour | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Scanner not configured in production | Every upload refused (`scan_unavailable`), unless `UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false` | [code] (upload-scan.ts:408-436) |
| Scanner error, non-2xx, or timeout | Upload refused; file deleted, never registered | [code] (upload-scan.ts:442-480); [requirement] (upload-scanning.md:12-14) |
| Unknown app mode on a client | Treated as Local; our-cloud egress blocked | [requirement] (egress-policy.ts:12-14) |
| Tool gate escalation, nobody to ask | Pause at checkpoint if possible, else deny; never allow | [code] (tool-call-gate.ts:150-155) |
| Unreadable tool-policy data | Falls back to `ask_every_time` | [requirement] (security.md:75-79) |
| Chrome approval unanswered | Denied after 30 s | [requirement] (security.md:333) |
| Suspended or banned account | 403, fail-closed after one retry | [requirement] (security.md:345) |
| Sandbox needs E2B | Both `AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1` and `E2B_API_KEY` required | [requirement] (security.md:358-359) |
| Account deletion with sole-owned workspace | 409, nothing deleted | [code] (delete-account/route.ts:452-465) |
| Workspace ownership or plan-renewal stop fails | 503, nothing deleted | [code] (delete-account/route.ts:440-446, 481-499) |
| Step-up missing or stale | Request refused with a step-up error; settings shows a dialog, cancel leaves state unchanged | [code] (delete-account/route.ts:461-475; SecuritySection.tsx:60-78) |
| Erasure of one store fails | Not reported as complete; object bytes deleted before rows so a failed delete leaves a retryable row | [requirement] (security.md:1158-1168) |
| Restored DB backup brings back erased rows | `erasure_tombstones` and `syncErasureLedger` re-arm suppression | [requirement] (security.md:1203-1209) |
| Scope above connector ceiling | Dropped with a warning; provider still loads. Marker `needs-vendor-specific-review` passes scopes through unchanged | [requirement] (security.md:527-541) |
| Lost key bytes | Restored TOTP secrets unrecoverable; users re-enrol 2FA | [requirement] (security.md:770-777) |
| Secret found by scanner | CI fails; rotate first because it is already in git history | [code] (check-secrets.mjs:498) |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are the target behaviours stated by project documents, not new proposals.

- Every public sentence traces to a ledger row, and every row has a proof that fails when the behaviour changes. [requirement] (security.md:28-39)
- A user can undo or review what they delete: files go to the OS Trash, chats to Recently deleted, and permanent removal only follows an explicit user action that names what is lost. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 9)
- A hold, once placed, must win over any purge or erasure. [requirement] (security.md:1172-1177)
- Key material should move from deployment env to a KMS-backed provider once provisioned, with its own review. [requirement] (security.md:791-827)
- A rotation on suspected exposure should take the exposed key out of service; today for `CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` it does not, because six columns are not swept. [requirement] (security.md:912-918)
- [proposed] Finish re-sealing the six unswept connector columns and the two legacy-unbound call sites so `_RETIRED` can be dropped.
- [proposed] One page-level table per surface for where credentials are stored, including VS Code, so public copy can cite it.

| Is erasure complete over the schema? | `pnpm check:retention-graph`, `pnpm check:legal-hold-coverage`; the matrix test is deletion-manifest.test.ts [code] |
| Are connector scopes within ceilings? | `pnpm check:connector-scopes` [code] (package.json:148) |

A guard reads the working tree, not HEAD, so stage first and run second. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12). A guard that fails beside others counts as green only if it passes alone. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12)

**Live checks a human should do** (not yet recorded as run): set a temporary chat and confirm it is absent from history; request an export and confirm the link dies after 24 hours; schedule and cancel account deletion within 24 hours; upload a password-protected PDF and an EICAR test file against a configured scanner; in Local mode on Desktop and Mobile confirm a request to an our-cloud host is blocked.

key_facts.fact: check:secrets scans git-tracked files for named credential shapes (PEM, Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq, xAI, Stripe live, Slack, GitHub, Google, AWS, Supabase, OpenRouter, Perplexity, generic sk-, DB URLs with passwords) and --history scans git history with no allowlist.
The secret-scan allowlist is keyed by (path, credential format), not a wildcard; stale entries are reported and must be deleted.
OUR_CLOUD_HOSTS is the one shared list of our hosts (agiworkforce.com, vercel.app, neon.tech, four Clerk domains); BYOK provider hosts are deliberately excluded.
Desktop guardedFetch throws before any network call when in Local mode and the host is ours; unknown mode is treated as Local.
check-trust-boundaries runs seven proofs (web, extension, mobile, vscode, types classifier, two desktop Rust tests) and fails if desktop gains Sentry; no CLI entry is in the list.
In production the external upload scanner is required unless UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false; with none configured every upload is refused with scan_unavailable.
The upload scanner is our own ClamAV service (services/upload-scanner), so user files do not go to a third party; password-protected files are refused.
Data export download link lasts 24 hours (DATA_EXPORT_DOWNLOAD_HOURS = 24).
Account deletion schedules erasure 24 hours ahead, requires step-up, and is refused with 409 when the account is sole owner of a workspace.
Step-up freshness is 300 seconds for most sensitive actions and 120 seconds for revealing an API credential.
Deleted resources have a 30-day recovery window, and temporary chats and attachments are purged after 30 days.
The soft-delete purge cron only deletes when SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED is 'true'; otherwise recovery windows do not end on schedule for conversations, messages, artifacts and projects.
security_audit_logs are kept at most 90 days, usage_events 730 days, credit_transactions 2922 days, signaling_sessions 8 days.
The tool gate never lets an escalation become an allow; unattended runs pause at a checkpoint or deny.
The website account default tool-approval policy is 'autonomous'; the shared fail-closed default is ask_every_time.
The trifecta check ignores text the user pasted, and a saved Block is enforced at execution, not by removing the tool from the model's catalog.
Public pages claim no SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA or third-party pen test; the ledger records that none exists.
trust-claims.json has 39 rows and a 90-day review cadence; security-claims.json has 111 claims; guards fail when text, date or proof moves.
Encryption keys live only in deployment env vars (no KMS, no escrow); rotation is every 12 months, next due 2027-08-17, and no rotation has ever been run.
CLI secrets use the OS keychain on macOS and Windows and owner-only files on Linux or when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING is set.
Mobile stores its database key in expo-secure-store with WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY.

pages.title: Shared interface code and design system

doc.summary: Five workspace packages under packages/ui hold shared interface code: unified-chat (chat components, stores and headless helpers), ui (primitives), design-tokens (colour, type, motion, z-index), i18n (12 catalogues, only English and Spanish selectable) and icons. Desktop mounts the full chat; web, Chrome, VS Code and mobile use parts. Surface differences enter through injected seams, and guards enforce tokens and imports. One web-only assumption remains in the chat memory store.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
Five pnpm packages live under `packages/ui`. Together they are the interface code that more than one app shares. [code] (packages/ui/design-tokens/package.json, packages/ui/i18n/package.json, packages/ui/icons/package.json, packages/ui/ui/package.json, packages/ui/unified-chat/package.json)

| Package | Name | One-line job (from its package.json description) |
|---|---|---|
| file:packages/ui/unified-chat | `@agiworkforce/unified-chat` | Surface-neutral chat UI, stores and hooks |
| file:packages/ui/ui | `@agiworkforce/ui` | Shared presentation primitives with no business logic |
| file:packages/ui/design-tokens | `@agiworkforce/design-tokens` | The only sanctioned source of colour, spacing and type values |
| file:packages/ui/i18n | `@agiworkforce/i18n` | Locale catalogues and message resolution; parity enforced by `check:i18n-parity` |
| file:packages/ui/icons | `@agiworkforce/icons` | Hand-authored icon family with a lucide-compatible API |

Why it exists: AGI Workforce must feel like one product on every app. The product rule is "the ChatGPT and Claude apps, feature for feel, with two differences only, any model and any API provider". [requirement] (.agents/skills/agiworkforce-design/SKILL.md, step 1). So chat rendering, tokens, copy and primitives have one owner each. AGENTS.md section 3 says every mutable concept has one canonical owner, and section 5 says `packages/ui/unified-chat` is shared by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code, so "nothing in it may assume one surface's routing, billing, or account model". [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5)

Both statements need two corrections from the code, covered below. Mobile also depends on unified-chat (apps/mobile/package.json:73), and Chrome and VS Code use only its non-React helper modules, not the chat screen.

The design contract adds the layering rule: `surface composition -> presentation adapter -> headless/contracts`, never reversed. Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome content scripts may use native presentation. [requirement] (docs/product/experience-contract.md, sections 2 and 3.2)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. unified-chat: one package, three kinds of export

The package has about 525 source files. [code] (find over packages/ui/unified-chat/src). Its `exports` map in file:packages/ui/unified-chat/package.json exposes the root barrel (`src/index.ts`) plus dozens of subpaths. Most subpaths are plain TypeScript with no React: `assistant-fence`, `tabular`, `message-sources`, `citation-markers`, `math-markup`, `deck-model`, `study-set`, `model-picker`, `ime-composition` and others.

1. **Full React chat.** `ChatInterface` takes a `runtime` (a `ChatRuntime` object) and an optional `hostBridge`, and renders the composer, message list, model selector, artifact panel and so on. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ChatInterface.tsx:111 RuntimeContext, :1040 provider)
2. **Stores.** Zustand stores are re-exported with a `Chat` prefix (`useChatStore`, `useChatModelStore`, `useChatUIStore`, `useChatProjectStore`, `useChatSettingsStore`, `useChatArtifactStore`, `useChatAgentControlStore`). [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/index.ts)
3. **Headless helpers.** Pure functions that any surface can call: fence classification, sanitising, continuation repair, regenerate replay, model admission, slash commands. Chrome, VS Code and mobile use only these.

### 2. How a surface plugs in

The package does not know which app hosts it. Four injected seams carry the differences:

| Seam | What the host supplies | Where defined |
|---|---|---|
| `ChatRuntime` | send, stop, load, create, delete, rename conversations; optional stream, supersede, upload | file:packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/runtime.ts |
| `ChatHostBridge` (React context `HostBridgeContext`) | conversation snapshot, `openUpgrade(requiredTier)`, `requestByokConversation`, `fetchPlanUsage`, `fetchCloudFile`, coding checkpoints, `compactConversation`, `fetchContextUsage`. Every member except `getSnapshot` is optional | file:packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/hostBridge.ts (lines 33-55) |
| `CapabilityProvider` | `platform` (a `SyncedAppSurface`) and an optional server capability document | file:packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx |
| Sinks and origins | `setClientFailureSink`, `configureArtifactSandboxOrigin` | file:packages/ui/unified-chat/src/index.ts |

Capability logic: `useCapability(c)` first asks `resolveCapabilityDocumentDecision` on the server document. If the document has no decision, it falls back to the static matrix `isCapabilityEnabled(platform, c)` from `@agiworkforce/types/capabilities`. [code] (Capabilities.tsx, `decideCapability`). The default context is `platform: 'web'` with no document. [code] (Capabilities.tsx, `DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_CONTEXT`)

Billing and plan UI follows the same pattern. A message that carries `metadata.paywall` renders a limit card. The Upgrade button appears only when the host gave `openUpgrade`. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx:938-943). The context-usage meter fetches plan usage only if the host supplies `fetchPlanUsage` and the conversation is cloud-managed. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ContextUsageMeter.tsx:69-77). The "use my own key" row in the model picker shows only if the host supplies `requestByokConversation`. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ModelSelector.tsx:591-594). Price and plan wording come from `@agiworkforce/types` helpers (`getBillingPlanPricing`, `paywallLimitHeadline`), not literals. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MessageLimitCard.tsx:1-8)

Execution mode is admitted by one pure function. `local_only` admits local models. `byok` admits non-local models that carry a user key. `cloud_managed` admits non-local, non-key models. [code] (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelAdmission.ts). Mapping to this knowledge base: local_only = mode:local, byok = mode:own-key, cloud_managed = mode:cloud. [inferred] (names match; the type is ChatExecutionMode at packages/contracts/types/src/suite-contracts.ts:24)

### 3. Primitives (`@agiworkforce/ui`)

The `src/primitives` folder holds about 45 components, including Button, Dialog, Sheet, Select, Tooltip, Tabs, Switch, Spinner, ConfirmAction, ConfirmDialog, PromptDialog, TrustBadge, ModelBadge, plus the keyboard hooks `useMenuKeyboard`, `useDialogKeyboard`, `useTablistKeyboard` and `useCombobox`. It also holds larger shared areas: `sidebar`, `settings-modal`, `directory` (connector, plugin and skill browser), and `auth-scene`. [code] (directory listing of packages/ui/ui/src). The index header states the boundary rule: only pure presentation and plain config live here, and anything that imports a store, calls `invoke()` or `fetch()`, or reads Next stays per-surface. [code] (packages/ui/ui/src/index.ts, header comment)

### 4. Design tokens

Three CSS files plus one TypeScript module own every design value.

- file:packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css has three layers: primitives (`--n-*`, `--hue-*`), semantic roles, and consumption. Components touch only layer 3. It also holds the corner scale (`--corner-detail` 2px to `--corner-hero` 32px and `--corner-pill`), the z-index scale (`--z-behind-far` up to `--z-skip-link`), and durations (`--duration-instant` 90ms, `--duration-quick` 160ms, `--duration-moved` 260ms, `--duration-reveal` 700ms). [code] (foundation.css:1-15, 270-352)
- file:packages/ui/design-tokens/src/chat.css is the `--chat-*` contract, light and dark, loaded by both web and desktop. Fonts are declared there with literal fallbacks, because a `var()` inside a custom property resolves on `:root`, where next/font variables do not exist. [code] (chat.css:1-40)
- file:packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css maps Tailwind names (`--radius-*`, `--text-*`, motion) to the semantic tokens.
- file:packages/ui/design-tokens/src/index.ts (1111 lines) mirrors the same values in TypeScript for hosts that cannot import a stylesheet: terminal palette, brand scale, chat variables, `agiExtensionCssVars` (Chrome), `agiVsCodeCssVars` (VS Code), `agiMobileColors` and high-contrast mobile colours. [code] (index.ts exports; consumers: apps/extension/src/tokens.ts, apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts)

A token names a role (fill, text, on-fill), not a hue. Do not dilute a text token with an opacity modifier. [requirement] (.claude/rules/ui-colour-and-interaction.md)

### 5. Translations

There are 12 language folders (`ar de en es fr hi it ja ko pt ru zh`), each with 8 namespaces (`common chat settings auth errors models pricing v3`) plus a `vscode.json`. [code] (packages/ui/i18n/locales; packages/ui/i18n/src/languages.ts). Only `en` and `es` are selectable by users. The others stay loaded for the strings they carry but are never offered, per decision D-2026-09-15-03. [code] (languages.ts, `SELECTABLE_LANGUAGE_CODES`). In shared components, `useUiTranslation(namespace)` returns `t(key, englishDefault, values)` and `plural`. English is passed in the call and used verbatim when the key or the i18next instance is missing. [code] (packages/ui/ui/src/i18n.ts)

### 6. Icons

Icons come from `lucide-react` or `@agiworkforce/icons` only. [code] (scripts/check-ui-icons.mjs, `ICON_SOURCES`). In practice `packages/ui` has 89 non-test files importing lucide-react and 3 importing the in-house package. [code] (grep count, this session). The in-house package has 9 glyph groups (Navigation, Actions, RowActions, Indicators, Composer, Media, Files, Account, Knowledge). [code] (packages/ui/icons/src/index.ts)

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
Shared state in unified-chat is held in Zustand stores in memory. A store persists only if its own code does so, and this was not checked store by store. [unknown]

| Store | Holds | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| chatStore | conversations, active id, messages; `replaceHostSnapshot` takes the host's list | The host owns the real conversation list and pushes a snapshot through `useHostBridgeSync`. [code] (hooks/useHostBridgeSync.ts) |
| modelStore | selected model id, catalog | Keeps the last verified same-boundary catalog during refresh. [code] (stores/modelStore.ts:158 comment) |
| tierStore | plan tier, current conversation provider | Default tier is `byok`. Selectors give `canSwitchProvider`, `isFreePlan`, and a provider-switch gate (`allow` or `upgrade-required`). [code] |
| budgetStore | budget snapshot, alerts, action trail | [code] |
| memoryStore | memories, synced to the server only on web | See Rules and Gaps. [code] |
| uiStore, settingsStore, projectStore, artifactStore, agentControlStore, checkpointStore, planModeStore, mediaModeStore | UI and feature state | [code] (file names only) |

Stores are exported under Chat-prefixed names so a host app can keep its own stores of the same name without clashing. [code] (index.ts)

Device or browser storage used for shared UI code:

- Web stores the language in a cookie and in `localStorage` under the key `agiworkforce-language`. [code] (apps/web/app/i18n/index.ts)
- The memory store caches a CSRF token and its expiry in module variables. [code] (stores/memoryStore.ts:114-125)

No database table is read or written by these packages directly. The one network path in the stores is `/api/memory` and `/api/csrf`. [code] (memoryStore.ts:94, :114). The server side of those routes was not read here, so table names are [unknown].

Configuration names: the unified-chat `exports` map; `SELECTABLE_LANGUAGE_CODES`; `NAMESPACES`; the `AGI_GUARD_CONCURRENCY` setting for the guard chain (AGENTS.md section 12).

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**What the shared code must not assume.** Per AGENTS.md section 5, unified-chat is shared by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code, "so nothing in it may assume one surface's routing, billing, or account model". [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5). The repo-wide dependency direction is surface composition, then adapter, then headless contracts. [requirement] (docs/product/experience-contract.md section 3.2). `packages/ui/ui` must not own account stores, runtime clients or navigation, and unified-chat must not own React Native, Rust TUI, Chrome content-script DOM or provider SDK logic. [requirement] (experience-contract.md section 3.1)

**How the code meets it.**

1. **Routing** goes through callbacks (`onNavigateView`, `hostBridge.openUpgrade`, `selectConversation`). `ChatInterface` takes `onNavigateView` as a prop. [code] (DesktopShellV3.tsx:169 passes `ChatInterfaceProps['onNavigateView']`)
2. **Billing**: plan facts come from `@agiworkforce/types`. The UI shows an Upgrade action only if the host supplies it. Free-plan wording is the owner's rule: Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters. [requirement] (owner memory note, free-usage-upgrade-only; test named there is UsageSection, not read here)
3. **Plan gates** are tier predicates from types (`canSwitchProviderInThread`, `canAccessAutoRoutingProfileForTier`, `isFreePlan`). The UI never encodes a price or a quota. [code] (stores/tierStore.ts). `check:plan-tier-predicates` exists for this. [code] (package.json:220; rule not read)
4. **Modes**: `isModelAdmittedForExecutionMode` filters the picker by mode. A model chosen for one mode is never silently valid in another. The Local to own-key move uses `LocalByokHandoffDialog` and `requestByokConversation`, the visible, explicit fork that AGENTS.md section 6 requires. [code] (modelAdmission.ts; ModelSelector.tsx:591-594) and [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)
5. **Provider names**: capabilities from the model registry decide controls, never a provider name. [requirement] (agiworkforce-design SKILL step 2). `LOCAL_PROVIDER_IDS` in modelAdmission.ts names local runtimes (`ollama`, `local`, `lmstudio`, `llamacpp`, `vllm`) as a literal set. That is a classification of local engines, not a cloud provider, but it is a hardcoded list. [code]
6. **Local inference needs no paid plan.** The shared chat code has no plan check in `isModelAdmittedForExecutionMode` for `local_only`. [code] (modelAdmission.ts). Whether sign-in is required is a host decision and was not established here. [unknown]

**Design rules enforced by guards and the design skill:**

- Use `useConfirmAction` for anything irreversible, `useMenuKeyboard` for any `role=menu` panel, `Spinner` for loading. [requirement] (.claude/rules/ui-colour-and-interaction.md; AGENTS.md section 9)
- A new token needs a case in theme-contrast.test.ts. [requirement] (same rule file)
- Never edit `models.json` by hand, and no model ID literal in UI code. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4; enforced by `check:model-id-literals`)
- Product names come from `packages/contracts/types/src/product-names.ts`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)
- No explanatory comments in product code. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 9). The shared tree has many long explanatory comments (for example foundation.css, chat.css, runtime.ts). See Gaps.

**Skills lock.** `.agents/skills` is product content, and skill edits need `node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate`. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md section 5). This applies to the design skill file as well.

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
- **Render crash in chat.** `ChatInterface` wraps its tree in an error boundary class. It shows "Something went wrong in the chat." and a Try again button, and logs the error outside production. [code] (ChatInterface.tsx:80-110). These strings are plain English, not routed through `useUiTranslation`. See Gaps.
- **Missing translation.** `useUiTranslation` returns the English passed at the call site when the key or the i18next instance is absent. [code] (packages/ui/ui/src/i18n.ts)
- **Unknown locale resource.** `loadLocaleNamespace` throws for an unsupported language or namespace, and the lazy backend passes the error to i18next. [code] (packages/ui/i18n/src/lazy.ts)
- **Network errors.** `toUserMessage`, `toUserMessageWithStatus`, `httpStatusMessage` and `networkErrorMessage` turn failures into user text, and exist in both ui and unified-chat. [code] (both index.ts files). Duplicate definitions exist: `network-error.ts` appears under both packages. Whether one re-exports the other was not checked. [unknown]
- **Client failures** are classified and sent to a host-supplied sink: `reportClientFailure`, `setClientFailureSink`, `CLIENT_FAILURE_CLASSES`. With no sink set, behaviour is [unknown].
- **Optional host methods** (`openUpgrade`, `fetchPlanUsage`, `requestByokConversation`) are optional, and the UI hides the control instead of showing a dead one. [code] (MessageBubble.tsx:942, ContextUsageMeter.tsx:77, ModelSelector.tsx:594). This matches the product rule that a hidden control beats an enabled no-op. [requirement] (experience-contract.md section 2, rule 4)
- **Memory sync** gives up quietly in a non-web host: `canSyncToServer()` is false in Tauri and React Native. [code] (memoryStore.ts:77-84). Failure text: "Could not reach your memory. Nothing changed." [code] (memoryStore.ts:96). Switching accounts aborts in-flight requests through an account generation counter. [code] (memoryStore.ts:98-111)
- **Artifact preview when scripts are blocked** uses `getSameDocumentScriptSupport` and shows `SCRIPTS_BLOCKED_NOTICE`. [code] (index.ts exports)
- **Token or CSS drift** fails the guard chain and does not fail at runtime. A `var()` with no declaration "is dropped and the element renders unstyled". [code] (check-css-tokens.mjs, error text)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are the stated targets, not claims about the code.

1. **One owner for every visual and shared behaviour value**, with the dependency direction surface composition, then adapter, then headless contracts. [requirement] (experience-contract.md section 3)
2. **The product UI feels like ChatGPT and Claude**: sidebar 260 wide, 34px rows, one 768 column, 48px header, one-row composer, hover-gated action row, Stop in the send slot. [requirement] (agiworkforce-design SKILL step 2, citing docs/research/leader-ui-measurements-2026-09-04.md section 9)
3. **Public pages are black, white and neutral grey with the logo accents**, Geist for text, no decorative amber. [requirement] (SKILL step 3). The public pages live in apps/web and are only touched here through the token files.
4. **Browser comparison is the acceptance test**: screenshot at 1440, 1024, 390 and 320 in both themes, and run the web specs. [requirement] (SKILL step 8)
5. **Guards before commit**: css-tokens, em-dash, hardcoded model IDs, theme-only text colours, web typecheck, eslint and prettier. [requirement] (SKILL step 9)
6. **Capability honesty**: a hidden or disabled control is better than an enabled no-op. [requirement] (experience-contract.md section 2)
7. **Languages are offered only when a catalogue is complete and reviewed.** [code] (languages.ts comment citing D-2026-09-15-03)
8. **[proposed]** Move the memory store's web-origin fetch (`/api/memory`, `/api/csrf`) behind a host-supplied client, like `fetchPlanUsage`, so the package has no URL knowledge. Keep the existing runtime checks until then.
