doc.summary: The repo is one monorepo: pnpm and Turborepo for JavaScript, one Cargo workspace for Rust. A lane map assigns write ownership. A hook chain guards commits and pushes. A 229-step guard chain (check:llm-operability) runs in a clean worktree before every push. Generated files (model catalog, Rust-to-TypeScript types, agent-context indexes) have owners and check commands. Implementation is present; no run was executed in this review.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how the AGI Workforce repository is laid out and how it is protected from bad changes. It serves six product apps (surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:cli, surface:vscode, surface:chrome) from one codebase, so shared behaviour lives once and drift is caught by machines, not by memory.

The design has four parts.

1. **Workspace layout.** pnpm workspaces for JavaScript/TypeScript, a Cargo workspace for Rust, Turborepo to run tasks across packages.
2. **Ownership lanes.** A machine-readable map of who may write which paths, so many agents or people can work in parallel without collisions.
3. **Generated files.** Some files are produced from a single source (model catalog, Rust protocol types, agent-context indexes). They must be regenerated, never hand-edited.
4. **Guards.** Small scripts (`scripts/check-*.mjs`) that fail when a rule is broken. A runner called the guard chain runs them all. Git hooks and CI call the chain.

Why: AGENTS.md says prose is the lowest-ranked source and that a rule "worth never violating belongs in a guard, not in prose" [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 2 and section 11). Source-of-truth precedence is: schemas and enforced config, then implementation, then tests/hooks/CI, then docs, then training knowledge [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 2).

Product context: the guards protect the established requirements (model agnostic, provider agnostic, one AGI Subscription system, free local inference, explicit execution boundaries). Examples are `check:model-id-literals` (no model ID outside the catalog), `check:entitlement-entry-point`, `check:usage-pool-is-shared`, `check:provider-call-reservation` and `check:trust-boundaries`. Each is a script that exists and is wired; what each one proves about product behaviour is covered by the pages that own those subjects.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Workspace layout

[code] pnpm workspaces include `apps/*`, `packages/*/*`, `packages/ai/providers/*`, `services/*`, `infrastructure/*` (pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-6). The package manager is pinned to pnpm 10.34.7 and Node `>=24.15.0 <25` (package.json:12 and engines). pnpm also sets `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` (minutes, i.e. 7 days), so a new package version must age a week before install, with a named exclude list (pnpm-workspace.yaml:8-10).

[code] The Cargo workspace members are `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, `apps/desktop/gpui`, `apps/cli` and `crates/*` (Cargo.toml:2-7). The Rust toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` with clippy and rustfmt components (rust-toolchain.toml:9-10). A workspace clippy lint table denies a long list of patterns; per-crate files inherit it (Cargo.toml). Release profile uses LTO, size optimisation, strip and `panic = abort`.

[code] Turborepo (turbo.json) defines tasks `transit`, `build`, `lint`, `test`, `typecheck` and others, with `build` depending on `^build` and `lint`/`test` depending on `transit`. Root scripts: `pnpm typecheck` covers only desktop; `pnpm typecheck:all` runs `turbo run typecheck` for everything (package.json:418; AGENTS.md section 12). `pnpm test` runs Turbo with concurrency 2.

### Ownership lanes

[code] `docs/agent-context/lanes.json` lists 19 writer lanes plus 4 review/verify/integrator lanes (lanes.json; `recommendedParallelism.writerLanes` is 19 at line 6). Each lane has `ownedWritePaths`, `readOnlyContextPaths`, `blockedPaths`, `requiredChecks` and `escalationOwners`. Shared files (root manifests, lockfiles, `.github/**`, `docs/agent-context/**`, `packages/contracts/types/**`, `apps/web/db/neon/**`) go only through the integration lanes `repo-operability` and `release-ci` (lanes.json `sharedFilePolicy`). `scripts/check-lane-ownership.mjs` validates the file (unique ids, owned paths exist, at least 15 writer lanes) and can test a staged change against one lane with `--lane <id> --staged`.

[code] `.github/CODEOWNERS` is provisional: every path routes to one founder account until real teams exist (CODEOWNERS:1-5). `pnpm check:codeowners` locks coverage.

### Generated files

| Generated output | Source | Regenerate | Drift check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model catalog `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` | `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` and other catalog files | `pnpm sync:models` (package.json:386) | `pnpm sync:models:check`, `check:model-catalog` |
| Rust protocol types in `packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol` | Rust crate `crates/agiworkforce-protocol` via ts-rs | `pnpm generate:protocol-types` (package.json:420) | `pnpm check:protocol-types` (renders to a staging dir and diffs) |
| `docs/agent-context/generated/` (contract registry, dependency graph, module summaries, knowledge graph) | repository scan | `pnpm generate:agent-context-indexes` | `pnpm check:agent-context-indexes` |
| `apps/web/AGENTS.md` and `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` | written by `next dev` | commit them | none specific |
| iOS project in `apps/mobile/ios` | Expo prebuild and config plugins | prebuild | gitignored |

[code] `check-generated-artifacts.mjs` fails a tracked file that is git-ignored and unclassified, loose root images or scratch markdown, Playwright MCP captures, and archive files not on an allowed asset list (scripts/check-generated-artifacts.mjs:34-80).

### The guard chain

[code] `pnpm check:llm-operability` is `node scripts/run-guard-chain.mjs "<229 pnpm steps joined by &&>"` (package.json:397; I counted 229 entries). The runner (scripts/run-guard-chain.mjs):

- accepts only steps shaped like `pnpm [--filter @x/y] script` and rejects empty or repeated steps (lines 11 and 33-50);
- runs the `EXCLUSIVE` set alone first: `check:protocol-types`, `check:cross-version-matrix`, `check:script-tests`, `check:rust-fmt` (lines 18-23), because they run cargo or rewrite tracked files temporarily;
- runs the rest concurrently, default 4 (cores permitting), set with `AGI_GUARD_CONCURRENCY` from 1 to 16 (lines 25-26 and `concurrencyFrom`);
- reruns each failure alone; one that then passes is reported as "recovered", one that still fails counts as failed (`runChain`);
- gives every guard its own process group and stops them all on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, force-killing after 5 s (`stopGuards`);
- keeps only the last 4 MiB of each guard's output; exit code 0 only if nothing failed.

[code] `check:guard-inventory` enumerates every `scripts/check-*.mjs` and fails when nothing runs it, taking the closure of the chain plus workflow `run:` steps (scripts/check-guard-inventory.mjs:1-12, 50-60). A baseline lives in `scripts/config/guard-inventory.json`.

### What the important guards protect

| Guard (pnpm script) | Protects | In the chain? |
|---|---|---|
| `check:model-id-literals` | no model ID literal outside the generated catalog; Rust side via `scripts/check-no-hardcoded-models.sh`, which now only calls the Node guard | yes |
| `check:model-catalog`, `sync:models:check` | catalog is internally consistent and in sync with curation | yes |
| `check:protocol-types` | generated TypeScript matches Rust types | yes (exclusive) |
| `check:boundaries` | imports do not reach past a package's published entrypoints; vendor SDKs only via port adapters (allowlist file) | yes |
| `check:neon-migrations`, `check:migration-dependencies` | append-only checksummed migration chain in `apps/web/db/neon` | yes |
| `check:db-isolation`, `check:rls-boundary` | database tenant isolation and row-level security | yes |
| `check:secrets` | no committed secrets | yes |
| `check:hardcoded-endpoints` | no endpoints the repo already models | yes |
| `check:css-tokens`, `check:ui-*`, `check:no-hex-*` | design values come from tokens | yes |
| `check:mock-exports` | a `vi.mock()` factory must keep every real export its subject imports | yes |
| `check:tauri-wiring` | desktop frontend and Tauri commands agree both ways (`apps/desktop/check-wiring.sh`) | yes |
| `check:lane-ownership` | lane map is valid | yes |
| `check:entitlement-entry-point`, `check:usage-pool-is-shared`, `check:provider-call-reservation`, `check:plan-tier-predicates` | subscription and usage rules go through one place | yes |
| `check:llm-failures` (and `:staged`) | known LLM failure patterns per `llm-failure-taxonomy.json` | chain: full; staged only in pre-commit |
| `check:hooks` | Husky hook wiring and commitlint policy | yes |
| `check:trust-boundaries` | Local, own-key and cloud trust separation | NOT in the chain; run by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (line 932) |
| `check:rust-egress-boundary` | desktop Rust network calls only through an allowlisted transport | NOT in the chain; CI (ci.yml:130) |
| `check:hardcoded-arrays` | no hardcoded arrays of modelled data | NOT in the chain; CI (ci.yml:149) |
| `verify-skills-lock.mjs` | skill content hashes match `skills-lock.json` | NOT in the chain; `repo-operability.yml:163` |

### Commit and push rules

[code] Hooks live in `.husky/` and install via `prepare` (package.json:140).

- `commit-msg`: commitlint, conventional commits, header at most 100 characters, subject must be lower-case (commitlint.config.cjs; .husky/commit-msg).
- `pre-commit`: `lint-staged` (eslint fix and prettier on code; prettier on json/md/css/yaml; an em-dash copy check on many file types), then `check:audit-inventory`, `check:executable-docs`, `check:structure-conventions`, `check:llm-failures:staged` (.husky/pre-commit; package.json lint-staged block).
- `pre-push`: skipped when `SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`. By default it runs `scripts/prepush-clean-worktree.sh`, which makes a detached git worktree of HEAD, links dependencies, runs the whole chain there, then runs `turbo run lint typecheck --affected` (against `origin/main` when present) and `git diff --check` over the push range. With `AGI_PREPUSH_ON_TREE=1` it runs the same checks on the live tree instead (.husky/pre-push; scripts/prepush-clean-worktree.sh).
- Lockfiles are never hand-edited; change the manifest and run pnpm or cargo. A Claude Code hook (`.claude/hooks/block-lock-files.sh`) blocks writes to `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `Cargo.lock` [requirement] (CLAUDE.md).
- `scripts/commit-pathspec.sh -m <subject> [-m <body>]... -- <path>...` commits exactly the listed paths (scripts/commit-pathspec.sh:1-9).
- New root files must be registered in `scripts/check-repo-organization.mjs` [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- Most guards read the working tree (`git ls-files -co`), not HEAD, so stage first, then run, then commit [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).

### Machine limits for agents

[code] `.claude/hooks/heavy-job-gate.py` denies unwrapped heavy commands (build, dev, test, lint, tsc, vitest, cargo build/test/check/clippy, `git push`, some check scripts) when the machine has 24 GB RAM or less (heavy-job-gate.py:9-12, 96). `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh` takes a machine-wide lock and waits for at least 3 GB free memory (`AGI_HEAVY_MIN_FREE_GB`, up to 900 s). `scripts/dev/light-job.sh` is the scoped-job wrapper.

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
This subject has no runtime plan or mode gating. It governs how code is changed, not what a user may do. Relevant rules:

- **Write access by lane.** A lane may write only its `ownedWritePaths`; shared files need the integrator lanes [code] (lanes.json `sharedFilePolicy`). Do not let two agents write the same file at once [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, Delegation).
- **Production-affecting commands.** `git push` is treated as a heavy job and must go through the lock wrapper on small machines [code] (heavy-job-gate.py). A deploy happens only when the owner asks in that message [requirement] (owner memory notes; not a repository file).
- **Mode and plan rules are protected, not defined, here.** Trust-boundary rules (mode:local, mode:own-key, mode:cloud must never route silently across) are in AGENTS.md section 6 [requirement] and enforced by `check:trust-boundaries`, `check:rust-egress-boundary`, `check:db-isolation`, `check:rls-boundary` [code]. Plan and quota rules are protected by `check:entitlement-entry-point`, `check:usage-pool-is-shared`, `check:plan-tier-predicates`, `check:provider-call-reservation` [code] (package.json chain). See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for how a turn uses them [unknown: that page was not read here].
- **Never weaken a guard.** AGENTS.md section 9: do not weaken validation, tests, security, lint or guards to make a change pass [requirement].
- **Skills.** Editing any skill, even a reformat, breaks `skills-lock.json` until `node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate` is run; never install with `npx skills add` [requirement] (CLAUDE.md). The web catalog ships every skill marked `audience: product`, so a skill edit changes what customers get [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5).

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
- **A guard fails beside others.** The runner retries it alone; a pass is reported as recovered, a second failure is final. The run ends with the list of failures, exit 1 [code] (run-guard-chain.mjs `runChain`, `summarize`).
- **Guard steps that touch tracked files** are run alone first so they do not corrupt what others read [code] (EXCLUSIVE comment, lines 14-17).
- **Cancelled run.** Signals stop every guard process group, with a 5 s grace and 8 s limit, then exit `128 + signal` [code].
- **Local green does not mean committed green.** Guards read the working tree; the pre-push clean worktree checks HEAD instead, which catches unstaged-file passes [code] (prepush-clean-worktree.sh) and [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- **Loaded machine.** Long suites time out under load and report as assertion failures; check `uptime` and rerun alone before chasing [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- **Hook skipped.** `SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` skips the push checks (.husky/pre-push:5-8). CI still runs its own jobs [code] (workflows); whether branch protection requires them is [unknown].
- **Branch name case clash** (`Fix/` vs `fix/`) can lose a ref; restore with `git branch -m`, never reset [inferred from owner notes, not a repository file].
- **Unregistered guard.** `check:guard-inventory` fails a `check-*.mjs` script nothing executes [code].

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
[proposed] Items that follow from the established requirements and the gaps below:

1. Every guard named in AGENTS.md as "Enforced by" should run in the same pre-push chain, or the docs should say which run only in CI. Today `check:trust-boundaries`, `check:rust-egress-boundary`, `check:hardcoded-arrays` and the skills-lock check run only in CI.
2. Guard counts and lists in docs should be generated, not typed, so they cannot drift (the chain has 229 steps and 251 `check:*` scripts; no doc states this).
3. The Cargo member list in AGENTS.md should include `apps/desktop/gpui`, since Cargo.toml has it.
4. Provider and model changes must stay catalog-only edits (curation file, then `pnpm sync:models`), which keeps the model-agnostic and provider-agnostic requirements cheap to hold.

doc.summary: The web app (apps/web) is a Next.js 16 App Router site plus the server API (apps/web/app/api) that every other app and third parties call. It hosts Cloud chat, accounts, billing, admin and marketing pages, and it is the UI the public Electron desktop loads. Sign-in is Clerk behind an identity port. Web is Cloud-only (Free and paid plans); Local runs only inside the Electron host; BYOK is not on web.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `apps/web` is two things in one deployable: (1) the Next.js web application (marketing pages, sign-in, chat, projects, artifacts, settings, billing, admin) and (2) the server API under `apps/web/app/api` (88 top-level route folders) that Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and third parties call. [code] (apps/web/app/api; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:29 describes the API as 'the HTTP surface under apps/web/app/api that the other six and third parties call').

**Users.**
- Visitors: public marketing, legal, help, pricing and download pages. [code] (apps/web/app)
- Signed-in Free users: managed Cloud chat on the Free plan. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:323, `free` is in `CLOUD_CHAT_TIERS`)
- Subscribed users: the same chat plus paid capabilities (connectors, deep research, image and video generation, developer surfaces, team admin). [code] (billing-catalog.ts:346-361)
- Admins and workspace owners: `apps/web/app/admin`, `apps/web/features/admin`, `apps/web/features/workspace-console`.
- Guests: a small anonymous chat route exists, off unless a feature flag is on. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest/route.ts; apps/web/lib/guest-chat/guest-chat-access.ts)
- Public Electron Desktop users: the Electron window shows the hosted web app, so they use web UI. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md, 'The desktop is two shells'; docs/architecture/overview.md 'Public Electron Desktop uses the hosted web settings surface')

**Role in the product.** suite.md names Web as: account, projects, synced app chats, artifacts, admin, Free managed access, and the owner of waitlist/access-code-gated paid acquisition. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:31)

**Published state label.** The website marks only Web as 'Available now'; Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome read 'Coming soon'. [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13)

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
| Layer | Choice | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framework | Next.js 16, App Router, React 19 | [code] (apps/web/package.json: next ^16.4.5, react 19.3.0; ARCHITECTURE.md Surfaces table) |
| Routing middleware | `apps/web/proxy.ts` exporting `proxy` (not `middleware.ts`) | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5); [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts) |
| Identity | Clerk (`@clerk/nextjs`) behind an `IdentityProvider` port; default provider name `clerk`, chosen by env `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:9-11; apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts) |
| Database | Neon Postgres via `@neondatabase/serverless` and `@agiworkforce/data-layer`; migrations in `apps/web/db/neon` (577 entries in the folder) | [code] (apps/web/package.json; apps/web/db/neon) |
| Payments | Stripe (checkout route); Apple store library also a dependency (mobile IAP route `apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap`) | [code] (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts; package.json `@apple/app-store-server-library`) |
| Storage | S3-compatible object storage (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `@agiworkforce/object-storage`) | [code] (package.json) |
| Code sandbox | `@e2b/code-interpreter` | [code] (package.json) |
| Providers | One adapter per provider under `packages/ai/providers/*` (anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, groq, minimax, moonshot, nvidia, ollama, lmstudio, openrouter, perplexity, qwen, zhipu, workers-ai, vercel-gateway, factory); web also depends on `@agiworkforce/provider-runtime`, `providers-factory`, `providers-vercel-gateway`, `routing` | [code] (ls packages/ai/providers; apps/web/package.json) |
| Models | Not written in web code; the generated catalog and family slots own them: `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json`, `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json`, generated `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4) |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry packages, Sentry shared helper, pino-style logger | [code] (package.json; apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts; apps/web/lib/logger.ts) |
| Hosting | Vercel (`vercel.json`: build via `apps/web/scripts/build-with-chat.sh`, cron list, git auto-deploy disabled); also a container build `apps/web/Dockerfile` (standalone output, node 24) | [code] (vercel.json:3,9-11; apps/web/Dockerfile) |
| Tests | Vitest 5 (jsdom) plus Playwright e2e | [code] (apps/web/vitest.config.ts; package.json) |

**Chat turn path (managed Cloud).** The client calls `POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions`. The route runs an auth gate (`lib/auth-gate.ts`), the managed-compute kill switch, workspace policy gates, spend limits, and then dispatches through the shared provider adapters; usage is accounted in `managed-usage-accounting-service`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:40; lib/auth-gate.ts; apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts; apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-accounting-service.ts). See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for the full pipeline.

**Public API.** The same adapters back a public OpenAI-compatible v1 route. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Provider strategy')

sections.heading: Folder map and entry points
sections.markdown:
| Path (under apps/web) | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `app/` | App Router pages (about 130 route folders: chat, agi-work, agi-code, code, settings, billing, pricing, admin, connectors, skills, plugins, download, help, legal, login, signup, device-auth, share, shared-artifact, waitlist, upgrade...) and `app/api/*` handlers |
| `app/layout.tsx`, `app/Providers.tsx`, `app/ProductRuntimeProviders.tsx` | Root layout and client providers |
| `app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx` | Chat route; renders `features/chat/components/WebChatRoot.tsx`, which mounts `features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx` (the main chat screen) |
| `proxy.ts` | Request middleware: identity session, CSP nonce, region gate, API-host rewrite, CORS and security headers |
| `features/` | Product features by area (chat, projects, settings, billing, admin, agents, connectors, code, media, memory, study, workspaces, marketing, desktop-host, remote-dispatch...) |
| `shared/` | Web-wide components, stores (`shared/stores/web-chat-store.ts`), hooks, services, config |
| `lib/` | Server and client helpers: auth, billing, guest-chat, managed-compute-gate, free-chat-surface-policy, surface-status, connectors, moderation, rate-limit, `lib/server/*`, `lib/services/*` |
| `db/neon/` | Append-only, checksummed SQL migration chain (never edit an applied file) |
| `config/` | `free-pools.json`, `free-model-promotion.json` (free inference pools and promotion) |
| `content/` | `api-docs`, `legal`, `support` content |
| `e2e/` | Playwright specs (164 files in the folder) |
| `__tests__/`, `*.test.ts` beside code | Vitest tests |
| `scripts/` | Build helpers (`build-with-chat.sh`, `verify-built-css.mjs`, notices, support corpus) |

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Provider.** Clerk, accessed only through the identity port `getIdentityProvider()` so the provider can be swapped by environment plus one adapter. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts:11-24; packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:9-11; adapters `clerk.ts`, `clerk-sessions.ts`)

**Web sign-in screens.** `app/login` (combined log-in or sign-up entry `AuthEntryScreen.tsx`), `app/signup` (with `TermsGate`), `app/auth/*` (callback, sso-callback, reset-password, update-password, desktop, device, chrome-extension). [code] (apps/web/app/login, app/signup, app/auth)

**Middleware.** `proxy.ts` takes the identity middleware from the port. Public API routes served without identity are only `/api/health`, `/api/download`, `/api/models`, `/api/waitlist/public` and the OG image. Product routes and `/api/(.*)` run through the identity session. [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:155-164, 170-200)

**How other apps sign in.**
- Browser-origin tokens: the token's authorized party (`azp`) decides the bound surface; `chrome-extension://` origins bind to `chrome`, other origins to `web`. Mobile mints tokens from a Clerk JWT template that carries a surface claim. A token with neither binds to nothing and the plan gate fails closed. [code] (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:53-67)
- Desktop (Electron) and Chrome carry a web-minted token and may refine the surface by header `x-agi-surface`. [code] (free-chat-surface-policy.ts:31-33, 97-112)
- CLI and VS Code: device code flow (`api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `/token`, `/approve`, `/refresh`) and API keys; the page `app/device-auth`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/device; apps/web/app/device-auth)
- Desktop sign-in handoff: `/api/auth/desktop/grant` and `/redeem`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop)

**Account rules checked on the chat route.** Terms version standing, adult (18+) eligibility, MFA/passkey policy, IP allow list, CSRF and rate limits are checked in the auth gate. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:5-35)

**Anonymous use.** A guest chat route (`api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest`) exists with bot challenge, per-device and per-IP daily caps (defaults 20 and 100 messages) and spend caps; it is available only when bot protection is ready and the flag `guest.chat` is enabled. [code] (apps/web/lib/guest-chat/config.ts:3-30; guest-chat-access.ts:15-33)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The product names three modes. Here is what the web app does with each. Implementation status is separate from verification status; no run is recorded in the documents read, so every row is unverified by execution.

| Mode | Web in a plain browser | Web inside the Electron desktop host | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:cloud (managed Cloud) | Supported and the only inference path. Free and all paid plans can use managed chat. | Same hosted UI | [code] (billing-catalog.ts:346 `managed_chat: CLOUD_CHAT_TIERS`; free-chat-surface-policy.ts:97-112 maps `web` to `managed_chat`) |
| mode:local | Not supported. Local calls need the desktop host bridge; with no bridge `startLocalChat` throws `DesktopHostUnavailable`. | Supported through the host bridge (`local_chat_start`) to local model servers; text only, attachments refused; a chat that holds local turns cannot continue on a cloud model | [code] (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/runtime-client.ts:621-646; apps/web/features/chat/lib/local-turn.ts:15-70) |
| mode:own-key (BYOK) | Not supported. Web never stores a provider key; BYOK belongs to the CLI and VS Code. | Same: Desktop chat takes no provider keys | [code] (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:224); [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:44 'Must not: expose BYOK/free env-key chat or pretend Local compute is available in-browser without a connected host') |

**Local to own-key crossing.** Web contains the handoff dialog and preview logic for a Local conversation moving to a BYOK model as an explicit fork (`routeLocalToByokSend`, `LocalByokHandoffDialog`). This is code for the consent step; it does not mean web holds keys. [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:81-103; WebChatPage.tsx:412) Whether the BYOK target is reachable from web at all is [unknown].

**Free vs subscribed on web.**
- plan:free: managed chat, tools, projects, memory, skills, cloud sync. Not included: connectors, remote control, AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API, developer surfaces. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:322-361)
- Paid plans (ids `basic`, `pro` labelled Premium, `max`, `max_15x` labelled Ultra, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`): `connectors` from all paid; `agi_work`, `deep_research`, `image_generation`, `managed_api`, `developer_surfaces` from `pro` up; `video_generation` only `max_15x` and `enterprise`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-232, 346-361)
- Plan ids `local-only` and `byok` exist as free-of-charge plan tiers; they carry no managed Cloud capability. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:168-179, 296-299)
- Paid acquisition is staged: checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time switch opens it (`AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1` forces it open). [code] (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-52; checkout route.ts:300-308) The doc says the same. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:19-24)
- Kill switch: env `AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA`; unless set to 0, false or off the gate allows managed compute; when off, chat returns 403 `public_launch_blocked`. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40,50-83)

**Subscription system.** Entitlements are resolved on the server (`lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts`, `effective-subscription-service.ts`) and returned by `api:GET /api/me`; usage accounting is in `managed-usage-accounting-service.ts` and `credit-service.ts`. Clients do not compute quotas. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:20; apps/web/lib/services); [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Data ownership across surfaces')

**Free inference pools.** `apps/web/config/free-pools.json` lists promo pools with terms review fields (`reviewedBy` is null in the first entry read). [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json:1-30)

| Shared piece | Used by | Evidence |

| `packages/ui/unified-chat` | Desktop, web, Chrome, VS Code (must not assume one surface's routing or billing) | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5); [code] (WebChatPage.tsx:91,412) |

sections.heading: Build, run and test
sections.markdown:
Commands come from `docs/agent-context/commands.json` (surfaces.web) and `apps/web/package.json`. They were not run for this page. [code] (docs/agent-context/commands.json:125-135)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Dev server | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web dev` |
| Build | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web build` (runs `pnpm notices` then `next build`) |
| Typecheck (web only) | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web typecheck`; whole repo `pnpm typecheck:all` |
| Unit tests | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test` (Vitest, workers set by `AGI_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`, default 2) |
| One test | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test <file-or-pattern>` |
| End to end | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test:e2e` (Playwright) |
| Lint | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web lint` (max-warnings 0) |
| Container | `docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile .` from the repo root |
| Guard chain | `pnpm check:llm-operability` (runs on pre-push) |

**Gotchas.** [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12)
- `apps/web` uses its own Vitest major; run through the package script, never the root binary.
- `tsc --noEmit` in apps/web needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` or it dies with SIGABRT.
- Guards read the working tree, so stage first, then run.
- Migrations: `pnpm db:migrate -- status`, `apply --target <env>`; production apply needs `--confirm-production`.
- On the owner's 16 GB machine, heavy jobs (builds, full suites, tsc, dev servers, browsers) must go through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`; a hook denies unwrapped ones. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md 'Delegation')

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
The intended unified product is one experience across six apps over one contract layer, with Local, own-key and Cloud as separate trust boundaries. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md; ARCHITECTURE.md)

| Area | Unified intent | What web does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat UI | Shared `unified-chat` package | Uses `unified-chat` pieces but keeps a very large web-only screen, `features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx`, plus its own store `shared/stores/web-chat-store.ts` [code] |
| Modes | Local, own key, Cloud everywhere it fits | Cloud only in a browser; Local only through the Electron bridge; no own-key [code] (see Modes) |
| Local-free promise | Local inference on desktop and mobile needs no paid plan | Web itself has no local inference; the Electron-hosted web UI reaches local models through the host bridge. Whether signing in is needed for Local in that host is [unknown] |
| Plan names | One AGI Subscription | Server plan ids differ from labels: `pro` is shown as Premium, `max_15x` as Ultra [code] (billing-catalog.ts:192-206) |
| Developer work | Host-owned runtime for Desktop Code, CLI and VS Code | Web has its own cloud code sessions (`api/code/sessions`, `lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts`); the matrix marks terminal use and git as absent on web [code]; [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:414-444) |
| Screen and device tools | present on desktop | Web cannot capture the screen; terminal absent [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:344, 434) |
| Copy about other apps | One truth | Web marketing and settings copy states availability of other apps from `surface-status.ts`, so those labels must be edited there [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts) |

Web is also the policy owner for entitlements, usage and moderation for all apps, so it carries server logic the other apps only consume. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services)

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Largest known gaps, each with its basis.

1. **Open Web defects.** `audit/registers/known-flaws.md` has a Web section with many rows, mostly account and workspace erasure, export and session revocation (several rated High, for example WEB-WORKSPACE-DELETION-LIFECYCLE-01, WEB-WORKSPACE-ERASURE-LOCKDOWN-01, WEB-ACCOUNT-EXPORT-ERASURE-CUSTODY-01, WEB-SESSION-REVOCATION-CLASSIFICATION-01). Most say 'runtime acceptance open'. [requirement] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md:15-40)
2. **Nothing recorded as run.** The feature matrix says no cell was produced by running the feature; whether the release workflow has ever run is not in the tree. [requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:7-13, 23)
3. **No browser Local, no own-key.** By design in the browser; users wanting Local or BYOK must use CLI, VS Code or the desktop host. [code] (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:224)
4. **Large chat files.** The large-file path (up to 500 MiB) is built but was off when documented: `CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED` unset, scanner protocol not live. Current state is [unknown] (the doc date is 2026-11-15, the migration ledger is now 425). [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md 'Chat File Uploads')
5. **Paid acquisition gated.** Waitlist or access code required unless the switch is open. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts)
6. **Free pool terms.** The first pool entry in `free-pools.json` has `reviewedBy` and `verifiedAtMs` null and an expiry timestamp, so its terms review is not recorded there. [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json)
7. **Web size.** Many routes and features in one app (88 API folders, 164 e2e specs, 577 migration-folder entries); a single chat screen file holds most chat logic. [inferred] (folder counts; WebChatPage.tsx imports)
8. **Matrix cells unverified for web:** Chat, Library, Search, slash commands, attachments and repository context are marked unverified by the matrix generator (a limit of its import search, not a proven absence). [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:44-60, 154, 194, 214, 334, 424)

key_facts.fact: apps/web is both the Next.js web app and the server API that all other apps and third parties call.
Stack is Next.js 16 App Router with React 19; routing middleware is proxy.ts exporting proxy, not middleware.ts.
Sign-in uses Clerk behind an identity port; default provider is clerk, selected by env AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER.

A verified token is bound to a surface from signed claims: chrome-extension origin to chrome, other origins to web, mobile via JWT template claim; no claim means unbound and the plan gate fails closed.
Web chat is managed Cloud only for all signed-in tiers including free; managed_chat capability is granted to free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise.
Web never stores a provider key; own-key (BYOK) belongs to the CLI and VS Code.
Local model chat from web works only when the Electron desktop host bridge exists; without it startLocalChat throws DesktopHostUnavailable. Local turns are text only.
Plan ids differ from display labels: pro is labelled Premium, max_15x is labelled Ultra; local-only and byok plan ids exist and are free.
Capability tiers: connectors from any paid plan; agi_work, deep_research, image_generation, managed_api, developer_surfaces from pro up; video_generation only max_15x and enterprise.
Paid checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time flag opens upgrades or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1.
Env AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA acts as an incident kill switch: only values 0, false or off block managed compute with 403 public_launch_blocked.

A guest chat route exists (POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest) with defaults of 20 messages per device and 100 per IP per day; it is on only when bot protection is ready and flag guest.chat is enabled.
Only /api/health, /api/download, /api/models, /api/waitlist/public and the OG image are served without identity.
Website surface labels mark Web 'Available now' and Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome 'Coming soon'.
Hosting is Vercel with git auto-deploy disabled; a container build via apps/web/Dockerfile also exists; deploy workflow runs after CI and has a daily drift alarm and a rollback input.
Committed migration ledger says production migrations applied through 425 as of 2026-11-21.
Chat screen mount chain is app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx to WebChatRoot to WebChatPage.
Public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so apps/desktop/src changes never reach it.
Web test commands: pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test (Vitest, jsdom), test:e2e (Playwright); typecheck needs 8 GB heap; web uses its own Vitest major.

apps/web/db/neon is an append-only checksummed migration chain; tables seen include profiles, subscriptions, conversations, messages, usage_events, media_assets, chat_file_intakes, feature_flag_definitions, feature_flags, beta_invites, beta_redemptions, api_keys, organizations.
Entitlements, quota and plan values are computed on the server and returned by GET /api/me; clients never compute them.
Open Web defects are tracked in audit/registers/known-flaws.md (Web section), many rated High on erasure, export and session revocation, with runtime acceptance open.
No document in the tree records a real run of the web release or features; feature-matrix 'Present' means located, not exercised.
Large chat file path (up to 500 MiB) was built but gated off (CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED unset) when documented on 2026-11-15.
Model identifiers are not written in web code; the catalog files own them.

open_questions: Is web chat currently serving production users, and at which commit? Only GET /api/version or the deploy workflow run history can say; the tree records no run.
Does the Electron-hosted web UI require sign-in for Local chat? The web code reaches local models through the host bridge but the sign-in requirement for that path was not traced.
Can a BYOK target ever be reached from web? The handoff dialog exists in web but no web key storage was found.
Is CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED on in production now, and is the scanner at protocol 2? Documented as off on 2026-11-15; ledger has since advanced to migration 425.
Has the first free-pool entry in apps/web/config/free-pools.json been reviewed? Its reviewedBy and verifiedAtMs are null.
Product choice left open: when to open paid acquisition on web to everyone (the waitlist switch is a run-time flag).
Whether the guest chat flag guest.chat is on in production is unknown.
Which of the surface-feature-matrix 'Unverified' web cells (Chat, Library, Search) are truly absent or only missed by its import search was not settled.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**Basis summary.** The public Desktop is the Electron app in `apps/desktop/electron`. It opens a window on the hosted web app and adds device powers the web cannot have. [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-15-04; apps/desktop/README.md:1-20).

**Users.** People who want the AGI chat app as a Mac app, plus developers who want AGI Code on local folders (Code sessions, terminal, git, browser pane, iOS simulator pane, computer use, dictation). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseService.ts; apps/desktop/electron/voiceDictation.ts; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md lines 325, 415, 435, 515).

**Three codebases live in `apps/desktop`:**

| Name | Host process | What the window shows | Public? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electron | `apps/desktop/electron` (Node) | The hosted web app | Yes, the public Desktop [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md; ARCHITECTURE.md:43-56) |
| Tauri | `apps/desktop/src-tauri` (Rust) + `apps/desktop/src` (Vite/React) | The Vite app in `src` | Retained internal code [requirement]. A 2026-10-24 decision note says the owner chose to ship it as a second public app later; the code and README do not show that happened [unknown] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-95) |
| GPUI | `apps/desktop/gpui` (Rust, native, no webview) | Native UI over the shared CLI app-server protocol | Opt-in migration host, does not replace either shell [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md:17-27) |

Product definition: Account-synced Cloud shell plus Desktop Code on the shared host-owned developer runtime [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:32).

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
- **Electron main process** in TypeScript, built by `electron/build-main.mjs` into `electron/dist/bootstrap.cjs` (package.json `main`). [code] (apps/desktop/package.json; scripts `build:electron`, `dev:electron`).
- **Window.** `BrowserWindow` with `contextIsolation: true`, `sandbox: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, and a persistent session partition `persist:agi-cloud` so the site login survives restarts. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1104-1116; apps/desktop/electron/config.ts REMOTE_SESSION_PARTITION).
- **Where it loads.** `CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` defaults to the production web origin. A packaged build ignores the `AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` environment variable; only an allowlisted `--agi-cloud-app-origin=` argument can change it (localhost or first-party hosts only). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts, `cloudAppOriginFrom`).
- **One bridge.** `preload.ts` exposes a single object, `agiHost`, to the page. All privileged work goes through `electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts`, which checks a capability grant (`permissionManager.ts`) and contains paths (`pathGuard.ts`). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts:201; ARCHITECTURE.md:79-91).
- **Code sessions** run in the bundled `agi` CLI (the CLI app-server) started per approved folder; the dispatcher talks to it over JSON lines. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts `startDeveloperSession`, `readyServer`; apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml extraResources `agi-cli/agi`).
- **Packaging.** electron-builder, app id `com.agiworkforce.desktop.cloud`, mac targets dmg and zip, security fuses (no runAsNode, asar integrity). [code] (apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml).
- **Chrome native-messaging host** is the same binary started with `AGI_NATIVE_MESSAGING_HOST=1`. [code] (electron-builder.yml fuse comment).
- **Tauri** is Rust (`src-tauri`) with a React/Vite renderer; `check-wiring.sh` fails drift between the renderer and registered Tauri commands in both directions. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:79-81).

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Electron.** Sign-in happens in the user's browser, not in the window. A signed-out window shows a local `data:` screen with Start and Cancel buttons. Start opens the system browser at the web sign-in path with a PKCE-style challenge (random verifier, SHA-256 challenge); a pending sign-in lasts 10 minutes; the shell completes it from a deep link using scheme `agiworkforce-cloud`. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts:1-14; apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:1-40; apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml `protocols`).

The web app's own identity provider is Clerk. The main process only allows navigation through the Clerk host named by this build's publishable key variable `VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (development hosts only) plus first-party hosts. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts `clerkDevelopmentHost`).

**Bundled CLI account.** After the shell is signed in, `developerAccountSync.ts` reconciles the bundled CLI's account (`account/*` calls, device-code approval) with the shell identity before a Code thread starts. Sign-out without a running app-server runs `agi logout --account-only`, which forgets only the account grant and keeps provider keys the user saved in the terminal. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerAccountSync.ts; developerSessionService.ts:1203-1222, 1279-1300; cliAccountStore.ts).

**Required?** The signed-out screen replaces the site's sign-in pages, so chat needs an account [inferred]. Whether Code on a local folder works fully signed-out is [unknown]; the code comment says a thread started before the CLI is signed in is pinned to the user's own provider keys (developerSessionService.ts:2770).

**Tauri** has its own account module (`src-tauri/src/sys/account`) and refresh-token flow; a known flaw says a lost refresh reply revokes the sign-in family (DESKTOP-REFRESH-LOST-REPLY-01 in audit/registers/known-flaws.md:270).

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
| Mode | Electron Desktop chat | Electron Desktop Code (bundled CLI) | Retained Tauri |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode:cloud | Yes. Every chat request is Managed Cloud by construction (hosted web app) [code] (config.ts header comment; dispatcher.ts:3244 comment) | Yes, when the CLI is signed in to the account; the thread takes its model route at start [code] (developerSessionService.ts:2770) | Yes (`AppMode = 'local' \| 'cloud'`) [code] (src/stores/appModeStore.ts:9) |
| mode:own-key | No in chat. The dispatcher refuses on-device inference; own-key chat is not described for Electron [inferred] | Yes via provider keys saved in the CLI terminal, which survive account sign-out [code] (developerSessionService.ts:1203-1213, 2770 comment) | Retained BYOK code in `src/features/byok`, `src/api/byok.ts` [code] |
| mode:local | **No.** Commands in `LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS` return an `unsupported-platform` failure. The device profile reports `localModels: false` [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244-3246, 3366-3368; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:3; dispatcher.ts ~2297) | Local models reachable through the bundled CLI, not through the shell commands [code] (dispatcher.ts:3238-3243 comment) | Yes; local mode only when `supportsLocalAppMode` (Tauri) [code] (src/lib/runtimeEnvironment.ts:21) |

**Free versus subscribed.** The Electron shell code contains no plan check. Plan limits live in the hosted web app and the managed gateway, not in the shell [inferred]. Which plans can use Desktop Code, and what a Free user gets from the bundled CLI, is [unknown]; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:245 marks plan status on desktop "unverified".

**Requirement mismatch to flag.** The established requirement says local inference on desktop is free of any paid subscription. The Electron chat refuses local inference by decision D-2026-09-15-04 ("Inference stays Managed Cloud"), so that requirement is met on Electron only through local coding sessions in the CLI, and in retained Tauri. [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-95) vs [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244).

MCP: the Electron shell reports `localMcp` from whether the bundled CLI serves MCP; connectors for chat use the hosted account connector service. [code] (dispatcher.ts:2299; docs/architecture/overview.md:136).

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
The Electron shell shows `apps/web`, so the whole chat UI is shared with surface:web, and with mobile through the shared contracts. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:53; docs/architecture/overview.md:24-26).

`apps/desktop/package.json` workspace dependencies (all [code]): `@agiworkforce/local-runtime-contract` (commands, deep-link and sign-in paths, `LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS`, env protections; used by Electron and GPUI), `@agiworkforce/types` (product names, model catalog), `@agiworkforce/ui` and `@agiworkforce/unified-chat` (shared chat UI, also used by web, Chrome, VS Code per AGENTS.md section 5), `@agiworkforce/client-runtime`, `ide-runtime`, `cloud-contracts`, `design-tokens`, `desktop-command-client`, `i18n`, `mcp`, `providers-ollama`, `providers-lmstudio`, `routing`, `skills`, `sync`, `trust-boundaries`, `artifacts`, `apply-patch`, `utils`, `observability`.

Rust: the bundled CLI binary (`apps/cli`, surface:cli) is the Code engine; GPUI and Tauri path-depend on shared `crates/*` (ARCHITECTURE.md:22, 114). Release feeds come from `apps/web` routes `/api/download` and `/api/releases/desktop-cloud/*` [code] (apps/web/app/api/download/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/releases/desktop-cloud).

sections.markdown:
- **Implementation status.** A release workflow exists: `.github/workflows/release-desktop-cloud.yml` on tags `v-cloud-desktop-<semver>`. Version comes from the tag. Never attach these assets to `v-desktop-*` releases (Tauri feed). [code] (workflow header).
- **Platform.** Public platform list for desktop is macOS only: `SURFACE_PLATFORMS.desktop = ['macOS']`. Auto-update is supported only for packaged macOS builds. [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:42; apps/desktop/electron/desktopAutoUpdate.ts `autoUpdateSupported`). electron-builder.yml defines only a `mac:` section (dmg and zip) [code].
- **Updates.** Daily check against `/api/releases/desktop-cloud/update/<arch>/<version>`; first install is `/api/download?platform=mac&app=cloud&arch=<arch>`. [code] (desktopCloudUpdate.ts; desktopAutoUpdate.ts:AUTO_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS).

Some pieces have recorded checks: the simulator service was run in a real Electron process on 2026-11-13, and the installed apps were observed on 2026-11-23 (audit/flows/desktop-code-tab-parity-2026-11-13.md). sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
- **Chat is the web app**, so chat features match surface:web by construction. Gaps are device features the web lacks and web features the shell blocks.
- **No on-device chat models** on Electron (web and Electron chat are Cloud only), whereas mobile and the retained Tauri app offer local inference. [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244; docs/product/suite.md:33).
- **Feature matrix cells for desktop** (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md): present for projects, library, tasks, skills, memory, voice dictation, terminal, git, diff viewer, computer use, BYOK settings (Tauri), deep research (Tauri `src`), media tools (Tauri Rust). Absent: study mode, video generation, local MCP in chat (public Electron reports `localMcp` through the CLI separately), hosted app publishing in the window, renderer browser automation (deleted). Unverified: search mode, camera, plan status, help centre, context handoff. Many "present" cells point to retained Tauri files under `apps/desktop/src`, which the public Electron window does not show [requirement] (matrix line 24 and apps/desktop/README.md), so check the cell path before treating a feature as public.
- **Device registry.** Desktop sends no heartbeat, so a Desktop sign-in never shows in the devices panel (WEB-DESKTOP-DEVICES-NEVER-WRITTEN-01, known-flaws.md:50) [requirement]; `describeDeviceForRegistry` exists in dispatcher.ts:~2290 [code]. Treat the flaw row as possibly stale [unknown].
- **Two continuity domains.** Desktop chats join Account Cloud sync; Desktop Code sessions join the Host Developer domain with CLI and VS Code and are never merged implicitly. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:45; ARCHITECTURE.md:172-176).

sections.markdown:

key_facts.fact: The public Desktop is the Electron shell; its window shows the hosted web app, so changes in apps/desktop/src never reach it.
Tauri (src-tauri + src) is retained internal code; GPUI (apps/desktop/gpui) is an opt-in native migration host that replaces neither.
The web status map labels Desktop 'Coming soon' and lists macOS as its only platform.
Electron chat is Cloud-only: dispatcher refuses every command in LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS with an unsupported-platform failure.
The device registry profile reports localModels false and localMcp from whether the bundled CLI serves MCP.
Window security: contextIsolation true, sandbox true, nodeIntegration false, persistent partition persist:agi-cloud.
A packaged build ignores AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN; only an allowlisted --agi-cloud-app-origin argument can redirect the window; default is production origin.
Sign-in happens in the system browser with a verifier/challenge and a 10-minute pending window; the window shows a data: sign-in screen with no bridge; deep link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud.
Code sessions run in a bundled agi CLI app-server per approved folder; the shell syncs the CLI account to the shell identity before thread start.
Sign-out without an app-server runs the CLI's logout --account-only, which keeps provider keys saved in the terminal.
A single bridge object agiHost is exposed by the preload; privileged commands pass through dispatcher.ts, permissionManager.ts and pathGuard.ts.
Packaging is electron-builder with app id com.agiworkforce.desktop.cloud, mac dmg and zip only, fuses runAsNode off and asar integrity on.
Release workflow release-desktop-cloud.yml triggers on tags v-cloud-desktop-*; whether it has ever run is not in the tree.
Auto-update works only in packaged macOS builds, checks daily, and uses /api/releases/desktop-cloud/update/<arch>/<version>.
The Electron shell has no plan or entitlement check in the files read; plan gating is not established for Desktop Code.
Retained Tauri app has AppMode local|cloud and allows local mode only in Tauri (supportsLocalAppMode).
Local MCP in the public Electron Desktop runs through the bundled agi app-server, managed on a Developer settings page; project servers need approval.
Feature matrix desktop cells often cite retained Tauri files, which are not shown in the public Electron window.
Known flaw: installed Electron builds fall back to command mode on the interactive workspace terminal protocol.
Known flaw: Electron test files are not typechecked.
Known flaw: remote-control messages are signed but not encrypted, so the relay can read them.
Desktop Code tab trails Claude's: no side-by-side panes, task panel, sign-in import, or agent in browser pane; checks owed on the running app.
Desktop chats sync in Account Cloud; Desktop Code sessions share the Host Developer domain with CLI and VS Code and are not merged implicitly.
The relay host for remote control is allowlisted to the fly.dev signaling host or first-party hosts; ws only for local origin.
Build commands: dev:electron, dist:electron, typecheck, test; the Rust CLI engine is bundled via bundleBinaries.mjs.

doc.summary: The mobile app (surface:mobile) is an Expo and React Native client for iOS and Android under apps/mobile. It chats with on-device models in Local mode with no sign-in, and with AGI Cloud after Clerk sign-in and consent. It has no own-key mode. Not published: the release registry and the web surface-status file both say "Coming soon", with no store listing verified. Native purchases are off.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**Purpose.** AGI Mobile is the phone client of AGI Workforce, a Claude/ChatGPT-style assistant. The display name under the icon is "AGI Mobile" (apps/mobile/app.config.js APP_DISPLAY_NAME) [code]. Bundle id and Android package are both `com.agiworkforce.app` (apps/mobile/app.config.js:165, :299) [code].

**Users.** Two groups [code/inferred]:
- People who want private chat on the phone itself (Local mode, the default). No account is needed to reach the app after the age gate and onboarding (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts `resolveRootRedirect`, signed-out path goes to the app) [code].
- Signed-in people who switch to Cloud mode to use AGI-managed models, projects, sync, tasks, connectors, schedules and the Code companion. Free and paid accounts both can; the plan decides which cloud models and limits apply (apps/mobile/lib/models.ts `getCloudModelsForTier`; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts reads /api/me) [code].

**Product role.** docs/product/suite.md says Mobile must ship a small Local LLM default, public-alpha Cloud (sign-in gated), preview/share of generated files, and clear privacy labels, and must not expose BYOK in v1 [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:46).

**Status in one line.** Implemented in code, unpublished in stores, never recorded as run on a store build [code: apps/mobile/src/features/release-state/mobileReleaseState.json].

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
| Layer | What | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86, React 19, TypeScript 5.9 | [code] apps/mobile/package.json |
| Routing | Expo Router, file-based routes in `app/`; a Drawer shell in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` | [code] |
| Styling | NativeWind + Tailwind; tokens from `@agiworkforce/design-tokens` | [code] package.json, tailwind.config.js |
| State | Zustand stores, persisted in MMKV (encrypted key kept in SecureStore) | [code] apps/mobile/lib/mmkv.ts |
| Local database | expo-sqlite `agi_mobile.db` with a SQLCipher key held in SecureStore | [code] apps/mobile/storage/db.ts |
| Auth | Clerk (`@clerk/expo`), native AuthView, Apple/Google/GitHub providers | [code] apps/mobile/src/integrations/clerk.ts, app/(auth)/login.tsx |
| On-device inference | iOS system model (`AGIFoundationModels` native module, runtime `foundation_models`), Android `aicore`, plus downloadable models run by react-native-executorch or llama.rn | [code] packages/platform/local-llm/src/tier1.ts; apps/mobile/package.json |
| Cloud chat | HTTPS streaming to the web API `POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` (paid/managed) and `/api/models/free-quota/completions` (Free quota route) | [code] apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:402, :847; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/free-quota-paths.ts:4 |
| Native projects | Generated by prebuild and gitignored; changes go through config plugins in `native/` | [code/requirement] apps/mobile/README.md |
| Build service | EAS Build with profiles development, preview, preview-simulator, beta, production | [code] apps/mobile/eas.json |

**Boundary enforcement.** All calls that can reach our servers go through `guardedFetch` in apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts. In Local mode it blocks our cloud hosts (`EgressBlockedError`) except named account and withdrawal controls; in Cloud mode all hosts are allowed only while the person has a current permission to share with AI providers (`managedCloudOpen()`, egressGuard.ts:124) [code]. TLS pinning is applied by `native/withAGITlsPinning.cjs` and checked by `check:tls-pins` [code].

sections.heading: Folder map and entry points
sections.markdown:
**Entry chain.** `index.ts` imports `./polyfills`, initialises ExecuTorch with the Expo resource fetcher, then `expo-router/entry` [code: apps/mobile/index.ts]. `app/_layout.tsx` mounts ClerkProvider, the app-mode door, cloud sync loop, notifications, biometric lock and the root redirect. `app/index.tsx` sends the user to the age gate, onboarding or `/(app)` [code].

| Path (under apps/mobile) | Holds |
|---|---|
| `app/(app)` | Signed-in-or-local main shell: tabs, chat/[id], chats, projects, artifacts, library, voice, camera, scan, translate, study, schedules, tasks, connectors, skills, plugins, agents, companion (Code threads), cloud-code, models, search, settings/* |
| `app/(auth)` | login, reset-password |
| `app/(public)` | age-gate, onboarding |
| `app/legal` | legal pages (incl. article-50) |
| `src/features/*` | About 50 feature folders: auth, chat, billing, model-picker, age-assurance, release-state, rollout, waitlist, voice, memory, projects, settings, companion, siri, share-preview, and others |
| `src/integrations` | clerk.ts, universalLinks.ts, controlAckTracker.ts |
| `src/lib/runtimeMode.ts` | Fail-closed dev/release classification |
| `services/` | Device-side services: api.ts, streaming.ts, cloudSyncEngine.ts, modelDownload.ts, executorchModels.ts, llmGate.ts, providerConsent.ts, notifications.ts, secureFetch.ts |
| `storage/` | SQLite repositories: conversations, messages, memory, installedModels, migrations |
| `stores/` | Zustand stores (chat, settings, agent, dispatch, connection) |
| `lib/` | egressGuard.ts, pinning.ts, mmkv.ts, sendQueue.ts, constants.ts (API_URL, GATEWAY_URL, WS_URL), v1FeatureFlags.ts |

| `store-listing/` | Store metadata and reviewer notes |
| `app.config.js`, `eas.json` | Expo config and EAS profiles |

**Key switches.** `lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts` FEATURES: cloudChat true, auth true, projects true, schedules true, connectors true, skills true, billing false, dispatch false, companion false, videoGen false [code]. `app.config.js` reads `dispatch` and `companion` from this file to decide background tasks and pairing links [code].

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Provider.** Clerk via `@clerk/expo`. The publishable key comes from `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`; preview and production builds throw unless it starts with the live-key prefix (apps/mobile/src/integrations/clerk.ts, app.config.js:41-47) [code]. Session tokens are minted from a Clerk token template named by `MOBILE_SESSION_TOKEN_TEMPLATE` in `@agiworkforce/types` [code].

**Methods.** Native `AuthView` plus custom `MobileSignIn` and `MobileSignUp` (email and password flows) and social providers named by `EXPO_PUBLIC_AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS` (beta and production EAS profiles set google, github, apple) [code: eas.json]. On iOS the app shows either all third-party providers with Sign in with Apple or none (loginProviders.ts, App Store rule 4.8) [code].

**Gates before Cloud.** Age gate (region thresholds, e.g. 18 in India and Brazil; `ageGate.ts`), accepted Terms (`termsAcceptanceStore`), adult eligibility (`adultEligibilityStore`), and a Cloud provider-sharing consent (`services/providerConsent.ts`) [code]. Memory notes say 18+ on every surface with a server-held decision [requirement: owner notes, not a repo file].

**Signed-out use.** `resolveRootRedirect` lets a signed-out person who finished onboarding into `/(app)`; Local mode works without an account [code: rootRouting.ts]. A session that ends while Cloud was active owes a sign-in (`endedSession.ts`) [code].

**Other.** Optional biometric app lock (`useBiometricGate`, expo-local-authentication), step-up checks, a second account on one device (accounts feature) [code]. Review accounts need password sign-in [requirement: owner notes only].

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The persisted mode value is only `'local' | 'cloud'` (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts:6); default `'local'` (line 62) [code]. There is no third mode value for own key.

| Mode | Supported? | Who | Where it runs | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mode:local | Yes, default | Anyone past the age gate and onboarding; no account, no payment | On the phone: system model (iOS Foundation Models, Android AICore) or a downloaded model via ExecuTorch / llama.rn. Chats stored in encrypted SQLite and MMKV. Model files download from a public model host (URLs in the local-llm catalog) | [code] tier1.ts, catalog.ts, storage/db.ts |
| mode:own-key | Not exposed | Nobody | No provider-key entry screen exists in the app. The only API-key sheet is for connectors (`ConnectorApiKeySheet.tsx`). `RemoteChatFeatureFlags.byokKeys` is accepted and never consulted. The egress guard comment still mentions BYOK; suite.md forbids BYOK in v1 | [code] services/remoteChatGate.ts:8-11; [requirement] docs/product/suite.md:46 |
| mode:cloud | Yes, after gates | Signed-in Clerk users with age, Terms and provider-sharing consent. Free and paid | AGI servers: `/api/llm/v1/chat/completions` and, for the Free quota catalogue, `/api/models/free-quota/completions` | [code] cloudModeDoor.ts:94-100, streaming.ts |

**Switch rule.** Every write to the mode store passes `admitAppMode`: Cloud is admitted only when a current provider-sharing consent exists; otherwise the app stays Local and starts the consent flow (cloudModeDoor.ts:94-100). Withdrawing consent returns the app to Local [code].

**Free vs subscribed in Cloud.** The tier store starts every account at Free, then `/api/me` confirms the plan (billing/store.ts, planCheck.ts). The cloud model list is filtered by tier for surface `mobile/cloud-chat` (lib/models.ts:117). Free-quota models come from a catalogue endpoint (model-picker/freeQuotaCatalogue.ts). Limits and entitlements are the server's AGI Subscription system; the phone only reads them (`/api/usage`, `/api/usage/limits`, services/usage.ts) [code]. Which plan names exist is in `@agiworkforce/types`; see the model catalog `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` (generated) and `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json`. No model IDs are written here.

**Local is free of payment.** Local chat has no plan check in the route or egress path read; `mapBillingPlanToUIPlan` maps free, byok, basic and local-only to the `local` UI tier (tierGuard.ts) [code]. Local also needs no sign-in [code].

**Selling.** `nativePurchases: false` in src/features/billing/storePurchases.json: no purchase, upgrade, top-up or restore control, no store connection, no Play Billing permission. `FEATURES.billing` is also false. So no subscription is sold inside the app; existing plans are managed on the web [code]. docs/product/suite.md:20 matches [requirement].

sections.heading: Build, run and test
sections.markdown:
Commands come from apps/mobile/README.md and package.json [code]; docs/agent-context/commands.json lists dev, typecheck, test and testSingle for mobile [code]. None were run for this page [unknown as executed].

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Dev server | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile dev` |
| Run iOS / Android | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile ios` / `android` |
| Real iPhone | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile ios:device:dev` |
| Typecheck | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile typecheck` (app and scripts configs) |
| Lint | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile lint` (max-warnings 0) |
| Tests | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile test`: Node script tests and Python IPA test first, then Jest in shards of 120 files per process (scripts/run-jest-shards.mjs) |
| One test | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile test <pattern>` |
| Detox smoke (iOS sim) | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile test:e2e:ios:ci` |
| EAS builds | `build:dev`, `build:preview`, `build:prod` |
| Guards | `check:expo-deps`, `check:tls-pins`; from root `pnpm check:no-hex-mobile`, `pnpm check:mobile-hygiene` |

**Native on-device models need a dev or release build.** The app uses native modules (llama.rn, ExecuTorch, WebRTC, MMKV), so Expo Go cannot run it [inferred: expo-dev-client dependency, native modules].

**Machine rule.** Heavy jobs on the 16 GB owner laptop go through scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh [requirement: CLAUDE.md].

**Tests.** About 868 entries in apps/mobile/__tests__ (for example test:apps/mobile/__tests__/age-gate-guards-cloud-not-local.test.ts, test:apps/mobile/__tests__/age-check-before-cloud.test.ts) plus colocated tests under src/features/*/__tests__ [code]. Root CI lane `mobile` runs `pnpm test:affected --filter=@agiworkforce/mobile` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:454-455) [code]. CI mobile end-to-end runs on the iOS simulator only; no Android E2E job (known flaw MOBILE-ANDROID-E2E-ABSENT-01) [code].

sections.heading: Release state
sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** Release machinery is in the repo: `.github/workflows/release-mobile.yml` (triggered by `v-mobile-*` tags or manual dispatch with a protected-environment publish step), scripts/release/* verifiers (store listings, privacy declarations, associations, IPA check, bundle scan, preflight), and runbooks docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md, mobile-store-products.md, mobile-eas-signing.md [code].

**Verification status.** The registry file src/features/release-state/mobileReleaseState.json says `released: false`, `statusLabel: Coming soon`, maturity experimental, channel nightly, availability unavailable; Apple and Google both `unpublished` with `listingId: null`, evidence "Zero v-mobile-* tags in this repository and no ... listing has been verified" [code]. apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts sets `mobile: COMING_SOON_LABEL` (line 10) and the mobile download action has `onNotifyList: true` [code]. docs/product/suite.md calls Mobile an "Unpublished client" [requirement]. The workflow's ever having run is not in the repo [unknown].

**Native purchases off** in this build (storePurchases.json). Changing it needs a new store build and review.

**Build identity.** package version `0.0.1`; EAS appVersionSource is remote; production and beta profiles set auto-increment [code].

**Known release blockers on record.** No Android store screenshot has ever been captured (audit/blockers/36-android-store-screenshots.md); export-compliance wording versus WebRTC and MMKV crypto (MOBILE-EXPORT-COMPLIANCE-WEBRTC-01); llama.rn memory entitlements not guarded in release check (MOBILE-LLAMA-ENTITLEMENT-UNGUARDED-01); share extension and widget targets missing from EAS appExtensions (MOBILE-EAS-APP-EXTENSIONS-01); reviewer notes far longer than the field (MOBILE-REVIEW-NOTES-LENGTH-01); no operator action to comp the App Review account (MOBILE-REVIEW-ACCOUNT-PLAN-GRANT-01) [code: audit/registers/known-flaws.md].

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Largest known gaps, from the code and the registers (all [code] unless noted):

1. **Unpublished.** No store listing, no `v-mobile-*` tag, no verified App Store Connect or Play record; release workflow never evidenced as run.
2. **No proof on devices.** audit/live-check/mobile-feature-gaps-2026-11-13.md says 21 features were built and checked only by unit tests and typecheck, not on a simulator or phone [requirement/document].
3. **Android.** No Android screenshots, no Android E2E in CI, Android share-intent plugin needs clean prebuild (README).
4. **Account and push lifecycle defects** (open, source-corrected but not runtime-accepted): MOBILE-PUSH-REVOCATION-ORDER-01 (High), MOBILE-LOGOUT-SESSION-LIFETIME-01 (High), MOBILE-SIRI-ROTATION-DISABLE-01 (High), MOBILE-LOCAL-WIPE-CLEANUP-ORDER-01 (High), MOBILE-COLD-START-CLOUD-DEMOTION-01 (Medium: slow start demotes a Cloud user to Local), MOBILE-NOTIFICATION-OTHER-ACCOUNT-TAP-01.
5. **Privacy copy mismatches.** Web privacy policy and Play data-safety notes omit mobile on-device inference and Read aloud via Cloud (MOBILE-PRIVACY-PAGES-LOCAL-01, MOBILE-READ-ALOUD-PRIVACY-COPY-01); store copy says Local chats stay on device while a manual copy to Cloud exists (MOBILE-LOCAL-CHATS-STORE-COPY-01).
6. **Local-model packaging.** llama.rn version range mismatch with `@agiworkforce/local-llm` (MOBILE-LOCAL-LLM-PEER-RANGE-01); memory entitlement unguarded.
7. **Feature gaps vs the leaders.** No study mode, video, Fast mode, local tools; library filters, a push on plain Cloud replies, files in live voice and some coding-session states are left out because the server or a native module is missing (audit/live-check document).
8. **Test suite size.** Full Jest run needs sharding to avoid heap exhaustion (run-jest-shards.mjs; MOBILE-TESTS-RED-ON-MAIN-2026-10-23).
9. **No own-key mode** by decision (suite.md), so users with their own provider keys have no mobile route.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Run from the repo root; all are read-only checks except the test and build commands, which are heavy and go through scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh.

- Release state: read `apps/mobile/src/features/release-state/mobileReleaseState.json` and `apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts`; `git tag -l 'v-mobile*'` should list nothing while unpublished.
- Modes: read `apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts`, `cloudModeDoor.ts` and `apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts`. Confirm no provider-key UI: search `apps/mobile` for a screen that stores a model-provider key.
- Sign-in routing: `apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts` and its tests under apps/mobile/__tests__.
- Purchases: `apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json`.
- Feature flags: `apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts`.
- Local model catalog: `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts` (`shipsInV1`).
- Run tests (heavy): `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile test`; a single test with the `<pattern>` form. Real behaviour needs a simulator or device build (`ios`, `android`) and is not evidenced in the repo.
- Release scripts: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile release:preflight` and the `release:verify-*` scripts.

doc.summary: The cli app is "agi", a Rust terminal coding agent (crate agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary). It runs Local (Ollama, LM Studio), own-key and Managed Cloud modes. Sign-in is a browser device code. Managed Cloud needs Premium or higher; Free and Basic fail closed, while Local and own key need no plan. It also hosts the app-server that VS Code and Desktop use. No signed release is published yet.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `agi` is the terminal coding agent of AGI Workforce. It is a Rust program with a full-screen terminal UI (TUI), a plain line mode (REPL), and a non-interactive `agi exec` / `--print` mode for scripts and CI. Its package description says it is a multi-provider agentic CLI. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:4; apps/cli/README.md:21-28)

**Who uses it.** Developers who work in a repository and want an AI agent in the terminal, including teams that run it in CI/CD. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:21-28). Account features (usage, library, projects, invites) are for signed-in Managed Cloud users only. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:~195-205)

**Role in the product.** The suite doc calls the CLI the "Developer agent surface and Rust engine proving ground", scoped to a workspace or session by default. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:34). The requirements doc lists it fifth in development order, with local transcripts, resume/branch, approvals, shell tools, MCP/plugins/skills/hooks, subagents and review flows. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:1148-1181)

**Developer domain.** The CLI, Desktop Code and VS Code share one host-owned developer-session runtime. CLI sessions are not merged into Web/Mobile/Desktop Cloud chat without an explicit handoff. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md:49; docs/product/requirements.md:1183). The README repeats this: CLI and VS Code share `~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/` and do not join Cloud chat sync. [code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Architecture section)

**Commands.** Primary command `agi`; `agiworkforce` is a backward-compatible alias (second binary). [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:15-21)

sections.markdown:
| Item | Value | Basis and source |

| Language | Rust, edition 2021 | [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:6) |

| Async runtime | tokio multi-thread runtime built in `run_to_exit_code` | [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8797-8810) |
| Command parsing | clap 4 derive; `Command` enum in src/lib.rs and src/cli_options.rs | [code] (Cargo.toml dependencies) |
| Terminal UI | ratatui 0.30 + crossterm 0.29; line mode uses rustyline | [code] (Cargo.toml dependencies) |
| HTTP | reqwest; local servers via axum (ws) and tokio-tungstenite | [code] (Cargo.toml dependencies) |
| Credential storage | `keyring` crate (OS keychain), with an owner-only file fallback | [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92-120) |

This page names no model IDs for that reason.
