sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Two kinds of sign-in, both through `agi login`.** [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288)

1. **AGI account (device code).** `agi login` with no provider runs `login_agiworkforce`, which calls `oauth::device_code_login`, saves the grant, and sends a device heartbeat. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1051). The CLI POSTs `api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `api:POST /api/auth/device/token` and `api:POST /api/auth/device/refresh` on the web origin; the `surface` it sends must be one the endpoint accepts (`cli`, `vscode` or another listed one). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:69-75, 133, 229; apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016-1018). The user opens the verification page `/auth/device` in a browser and enters a code (example `ZED3-E49H`). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:285-291). The browser target is checked against trusted AGI hosts. [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:309-312 test name)
2. **Own provider key.** `agi login <provider>` prompts for an API key. The accepted list in the error text: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, ollama-cloud, openrouter, nvidia, plus brave or tavily for web search. GitHub Copilot sign-in is refused as unavailable. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288, 1060-1090)

**Where credentials live.** One OS-keyring entry per provider under service `com.agiworkforce.cli.auth`, plus a non-secret index. With `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` they go in an owner-only file. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92-120, 175). The managed token can also come from env `AGIWORKFORCE_JWT`, then the keyring, then a legacy `~/.agiworkforce/auth.toml`. [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:20-22)

**Account identity.** After sign-in the CLI calls `api:GET /api/me` for the plan tier and email, and caches the tier on disk for 5 minutes (`~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml`, 3-second timeout, trusted `*.agiworkforce.com` HTTPS hosts only). [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:264-275; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:1-50, 195-210). `AGI_AUTH_BASE` overrides the device-grant base for a trusted host. [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:287-292)

**Other commands.** `agi logout` signs out of the account; `agi logout --all` also removes every saved provider key after a confirmation; `agi auth-status` reports state. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7275-7300). The README says the sign-in system behind the account is shared with the web app (the endpoints are in apps/web). [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016)

**Sign-in not needed for Local or own key.** README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan." Whether a Local session can start with no account at all is not stated in one line of code I opened. [unknown for the no-account case; code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Subcommands section)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The CLI names its three trust boundaries with `PrivacyMode`: `Local`, `Byok`, `Managed`. Their words for people are "Local", "Your key", "Managed". [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:253-290). Arguments accepted include `local|offline|device`, `byok|cloud-byok|provider`, `managed|agi|agi-cloud|cloud`. [code] (session.rs:~285-294)

| Mode | Meaning in code | Who can use it | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode:local | "no prompt, chat, or file context should leave this device". Providers are Ollama and LM Studio probed on this computer, plus a custom endpoint with no key on a local URL. | Any user, no subscription | [code] (session.rs:~270; apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:69-119; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1835-1855; README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan") |
| mode:own-key | "selected context may be sent directly to the user's configured provider key". Providers: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, mistral, openrouter, nvidia, user-defined OpenAI-compatible endpoints from `[providers.<name>]` in config.toml | Any user with a key; never gated by plan tier | [code] (session.rs:~272; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-935 comment; apps/cli/README.md custom provider section) |
| mode:cloud (`Managed`) | "selected context may be sent through AGI managed cloud"; requests go to `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` with a bearer token, an `Idempotency-Key` header and client-surface headers | Premium (pro) and higher: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. Free and Basic fail closed | [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:501-551; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-945; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 359) |

**Free and subscribed users, in one table**

| Plan | Local | Own key | Managed Cloud in the CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan:free | yes | yes | no. `can_access_model_for_tier` returns false for Free, Basic and BYOK | 
| plan:basic | yes | yes | no, "Basic can use the economy roster in Web/Mobile/Desktop chat, but not from the CLI" |
| plan:pro (shown as Premium) | yes | yes | yes, economy plus pro-additions models |
| plan:team | yes | yes | yes, as Premium roster |
| plan:max, plan:max_15x (shown as Ultra) | yes | yes | yes, all three slots for Max/Ultra |
| plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise | yes | yes | yes |

Source for the table: [code] (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-960; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:206-215, 244-253; apps/cli/src/plans.rs:96-104; billing-catalog.ts:359). The capability is named `developer_surfaces`, labelled "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code". [code] (billing-catalog.ts:417)

**Subscription link.** The CLI uses the one AGI subscription system: it reads plan and entitlements from `api:GET /api/me`, plan-capability tables from `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts`, credit windows (5 hours, week, month) from `packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts`, and a paywall body from the gateway when quota is exceeded (150 percent of tier quota per the code comment). `pnpm check:protocol-types` keeps the CLI plan table equal to the billing catalog. [code] (apps/cli/src/plans.rs:14-16; apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:309-315; apps/cli/README.md Subcommands). Usage accounting itself happens on the server. [inferred]

**Boundary rules.** Account commands (`usage`, `invite`, `library`, `projects`, ...) run only in Managed and refuse in Local and own-key before any request. [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:4, 212, 900-968; README). A Local chat "stays on this device and is not saved to your account history". [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:111, 1487). The gateway base must be a trusted AGI HTTPS host before the bearer token is attached. [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:465-480)

**Fallback chains.** `-m a,b,c` lists models; on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect the next takes over with the provider switched automatically. Whether a chain can cross from Local into own key or Managed without consent is not established here. [code-doc] (README; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs) [unknown for the consent question]

[code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:36-46). The Tauri crate also depends on agent-core, execpolicy, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy and worktree. [code] (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32-39). ARCHITECTURE.md says crates/ is "Shared Rust used by both the desktop and the CLI". [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:22)

[code-doc + code] (apps/cli/README.md Architecture; grep of apps/extension-vscode/src)
- surface:desktop (Electron) bundles its own `agi` for local coding sessions and talks to it with `DeveloperSessionClient` over stdio. [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md Install section; ARCHITECTURE.md:57-64)

Nothing under `packages/ui/unified-chat` is used by the CLI; the CLI renders its own terminal UI. [inferred]

sections.heading: Release state
sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** The code is broad and connected: the Cargo manifest, command dispatch, auth, managed gateway client, app-server, TUI and REPL are all present (see Folder map). Version is 0.0.1. [code]

**Release status.** [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13) `SURFACE_STATUS` marks only web "Available now"; `cli` is "Coming soon". The public CLI download link is `/download#cli-downloads`. [code] (surface-status.ts:62)

**Pipeline exists, first release unconfirmed.**

- `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml` triggers on tags `v-cli-*` (tag must equal the Cargo version) and on manual runs. A tag run validates, builds six archives (macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Windows x64 and arm64), signs `SHA256SUMS` with a P-256 key held in the protected `cli-release` environment, and publishes a GitHub release. A manual run builds and stops. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/cli-release.md:1-50; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:1-30)
- The binaries have no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; the signed checksum manifest is the integrity check. [requirement] (cli-release.md)
- `apps/web/public/install.sh` pins a public release key (line 31) and stops with "No signed AGI CLI release is published yet" when GitHub answers 404. [code] (install.sh:31-35, 133)
- The README says the installer stops with that message until the first signed release exists. The surface matrix says "Whether it has ever run is not in this tree." [code-doc] [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md; docs/product/suite.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:26). So whether any release is live is [unknown].

**Install channels.** Only the curl installer is advertised; `agi update --install` self-updates; the VS Code extension and Desktop installer bundle or fetch `agi`. Homebrew, npm, WinGet, apt, native Windows installer: none advertised (Homebrew writes to a private tap). [requirement] (cli-release.md, Install channels)

**Verification status.** No document I read records a real end-to-end run of the CLI against production. The audit register records some Electron-to-CLI acceptance work, but it is isolated and not a CLI release check. [unknown / code-doc] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md line 224)

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Only read-only checks were done for this page; run nothing below unless you intend to.

1. Build state: `cargo check -p agiworkforce-cli` and `cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib` (commands.json:143-145).
2. Release state: read `SURFACE_STATUS` in apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts; check GitHub for a `v-cli-*` release; run `bash apps/web/public/install.sh` only on a throwaway machine.
3. Plan gate: read `can_access_model_for_tier` in apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs and `developer_surfaces` in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts; run `agi plans` signed in to see which plans include "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code".
4. Sign-in: run `agi login`, then `agi auth-status`; for own key run `agi login <provider>`.
5. Modes: run `agi --privacy local` (or the `--privacy` argument) and `agi doctor` with Ollama running; see apps/cli/src/local_models.rs probes.
6. Doc drift: compare surface-feature-matrix.md cli rows to `pub mod` lines in apps/cli/src/lib.rs.
7. Guards: `pnpm check:protocol-types`, `pnpm check:llm-operability`, and `node apps/cli/scripts/generate-third-party-notices.mjs --check`.

key_facts.fact: The CLI is a Rust crate named agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary, not published to crates.io.
Two binaries: `agi` (primary, default-run) and `agiworkforce` (backward-compatible alias).
main.rs only calls agiworkforce_cli::run_to_exit_code(); the real command dispatch lives in src/lib.rs (about 11,000 lines).
Sign-in to an AGI account uses a browser device code against /api/auth/device/code, /token and /refresh on the web origin.
Credentials are stored in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) with an owner-only file fallback when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1.
The CLI has three trust boundaries in code: PrivacyMode Local, Byok, Managed.
Managed Cloud in the CLI requires the developer_surfaces capability, granted to pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise; Free and Basic fail closed.
Local (Ollama, LM Studio) and own-key modes are never gated by subscription tier, so a Free user can use them.
Managed chat requests go to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions on a trusted AGI HTTPS host with a bearer token and an Idempotency-Key header.
Plan tier is read from GET /api/me and cached in ~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml for 5 minutes with a 3-second timeout.
Account commands (usage, library, projects, invite and others) run only in Managed mode and refuse in Local and own-key mode before any request.
The web release-status table marks the CLI 'Coming soon'; only web is 'Available now'.

A release workflow exists (tags v-cli-*, six archives, signed SHA256SUMS), but the installer says 'No signed AGI CLI release is published yet' on a 404, and the matrix says whether the workflow ever ran is not in the tree.
Binaries carry no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; integrity relies on a signed checksum manifest.
Build and test commands: cargo check/test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib, cargo build --release -p agiworkforce-cli.
CI runs cargo test --locked -p agiworkforce-cli under xvfb-run, then workspace lib tests excluding desktop and cli.
The CLI shares 11 path-dependency crates with the Tauri desktop backend (agent-core, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy, execpolicy, worktree and more).
`agi app-server` is the local developer-session runtime used by VS Code and the Electron Desktop; CLI and VS Code share ~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/ and do not sync into Cloud chat.
The model catalog is compiled in from packages/contracts/types/src/models.json; model IDs are not hardcoded in the CLI.
Sandbox: macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap, none on Windows; no in-process fallback; --no-sandbox is the only workaround.
evidence: apps/cli/README.md Runtime requirement and Sandbox defaults sections

key_facts.fact: Voice (push-to-talk) is an optional Cargo feature off by default because cpal links ALSA on Linux.
The CLI has a remote-control command and module, although the surface matrix reports remote control absent for the CLI.
The CLI plan credit windows are read at compile time from managed-usage-limits.ts; plan labels show pro as Premium and max_15x as Ultra.
Custom OpenAI-compatible providers are added with [providers.<name>] in ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml; names that collide with built-ins are ignored.
The README claims 35 hook events; I did not verify the count in code.
A multi-model fallback chain (-m a,b,c) switches model and provider on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect.
About 4,578 test markers exist under apps/cli/src; this is a grep count, not a run result.
evidence: grep count of #[test] and #[tokio::test] in apps/cli/src

open_questions: Has any signed CLI release ever been published? The tree does not say; the installer reports none and the surface status is Coming soon.
Can Local mode start with no AGI account at all? README says Local and own key need no plan, but I did not find the single code check for the no-account case.
May a fallback chain cross from Local to own key or Managed without a consent step? AGENTS.md requires explicit consent for such moves; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs was not read.
Product choice: should Free and Basic users get any managed model in the CLI? Code excludes them; billing-catalog sets developer_surfaces to PRO_TIERS.
Are the hook events really 35, and are all three MCP transports connected? Only the README states this.
Do the packages ai/providers folders map to CLI providers? The CLI uses the Rust crate agiworkforce-llm, so provider:<package folder> edges are only approximate.
What real verification (manual run, CI results) exists for Managed mode on production? None is recorded in the documents read.
Does the Desktop (Electron) installer currently ship the CLI binary in a released build, given Desktop is also Coming soon?

doc.summary: The VS Code extension (display name AGI Code, package agi-workforce, version 0.0.2) is a chat and agent panel inside VS Code. It does not run the agent itself: it starts the AGI CLI's local app-server per workspace. It supports Local, own-key and Cloud, but Cloud models need a Pro-or-higher plan. It is a preview. The Marketplace release is unproven, and the web page marks it Coming soon.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** AGI Code is the VS Code surface (surface:vscode) of AGI Workforce. It gives developers a sidebar chat, an editor-tab chat, and an `@agi` participant in VS Code's own Chat view. It also adds editor helpers: explain, fix, refactor, tests, docs, code review, terminal help, hover, CodeLens and inline completions. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:2-4, 62-70; apps/extension-vscode/README.md)

**Who uses it.** Developers who want an agent scoped to the repository they have open. Chat, agent runs and history are scoped to the workspace folder and run through the AGI CLI on the user's machine. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/README.md:19-24; apps/extension-vscode/docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Purpose)

**Where it sits in the product.** The suite doc calls it the IDE-native developer assistant, workspace scoped. It belongs to the "Host Developer" domain with Desktop Code and the CLI. It is not part of the consumer "Account Cloud" domain. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:35; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:19)

**Platforms.** The web status helper lists macOS, Windows and Linux. The manifest needs VS Code `^1.100.0`, runs in the workspace extension host (`extensionKind: workspace`), and does not support virtual workspaces. [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:45; apps/extension-vscode/package.json:34-39, 107-111)

**Names.** Display name is "AGI Code", marketplace id `agiworkforce.agi-workforce`, publisher `agiworkforce`, pricing field "Free", flagged `preview: true`. Command titles start with "Code:". [code] (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:3,6,31-33; .github/workflows/release-vscode-extension.yml publish job url)

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
**Language and host.** TypeScript, bundled by esbuild into one Node CommonJS file (`out/extension.js`, target node18, `vscode` external). Two browser bundles are built for the webviews: `out/webview/render.js` and `out/webview/dictation.js`. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/esbuild.js:20-60)

**The agent lives in the CLI, not the extension.** The extension spawns `agi app-server` (a local JSON-RPC style process of the Rust CLI) once per workspace root through `LocalRuntimePool` and `LocalRuntimeClient`. That process owns threads, turns, streamed output, approvals, cancellation and session history. Multi-root windows keep one runtime per root. Changing `agiWorkforce.cliPath` disposes the processes. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:2575; src/extension.ts:104-122; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Developer-session architecture)

**Three UI paths share one pool.** The `@agi` chat participant, the sidebar webview (`agi-workforce.sidebar`) and the editor chat panel all use the same `LocalRuntimePool`. [code] (docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md; src/extension.ts:44-58 imports)

**Cloud-backed editor utilities.** Inline completions, code review, suggest-terminal-command, feedback, memory, usage and dictation call AGI web APIs directly with the account token. Completions stream from `<apiEndpoint>/chat/completions` (default endpoint `https://agiworkforce.com/api/llm/v1`). [code] (src/utils/api.ts:1115, 324, 1545; package.json:1214-1218)

**Activation is fault tolerant.** `activate()` guards `setupProviders` and `setupChat` separately, records failures in subsystem health, and falls back to a degraded provider state so the sidebar view always registers. Tests lock this in. [code] (src/extension.ts:76-90, 117-135; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Activation contract)

**Size.** 149 commands are contributed. The extension contributes one Activity Bar container `agi-workforce-sidebar` and one chat participant `agiworkforce.agi`. `src/extension.ts` is 526 lines and `ChatStateManager.ts` is the largest UI file. [code] (package.json contributes; src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts)

**Workspace trust.** In an untrusted workspace the local runtime is not started, and settings such as API endpoint, CLI path, model and inline completion cannot be overridden by workspace settings. [code] (package.json:49-90)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Sign-in is optional for Local and own-key use.** The README says an AGI Cloud account is needed only for Managed Cloud and cloud-backed extras (inline completions, memory, feedback). Local models and provider keys work through the CLI without an AGI subscription. [code] (README.md:35-38; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Quick start)

**Command.** `agi-workforce.signIn` calls `signIn` in `features/surfaces/accountAccess.ts`. If the CLI can start the login (`account/login` over the app-server), the extension opens the verification URL and waits via `account/login/wait`. If the CLI cannot, it falls back to its own device flow. [code] (src/core/commandSetup.ts:1221-1230; src/features/surfaces/accountAccess.ts:27-67; src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:2091-2103)

**Device flow.** The extension requests a code with surface `vscode`, opens a browser approval page (on the user's own computer even in a remote window), and polls for the token. The paths and logic come from the shared `@agiworkforce/client-runtime` package. [code] (src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts:60-110, 190-230; packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts:24, 62-68)

**Where the credential lives.** In VS Code `SecretStorage`. The extension can also borrow the CLI's account token (`account/token`) when it holds none, after checking the owner through `GET /api/me?surface=vscode`. [code] (src/utils/api.ts:300-345, 380-395; src/extension.ts:111-123; README.md Privacy)

**Refresh and sign-out.** Expired sessions renew through the shared refresh endpoint. `agi-workforce.signOut` calls `POST /api/auth/logout`, clears the tier cache and memory cache, and also signs the CLI out. [code] (src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts:127-146; src/core/commandSetup.ts:1243-1256)

**Own-key sign-in.** `agi-workforce.signInProvider <id>` runs `agi login <id>` in a terminal. The id is checked against a strict pattern first because it reaches a shell. The app-server has no login call for providers. [code] (src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:383-404)

**Other credential.** `agi-workforce.setApiKey` stores an AGI API key in SecretStorage. [code] (src/core/commandSetup.ts:1259-1280)

**Provider.** Account identity is the AGI web account (identity handled by the web app; Clerk details are [unknown] from this folder).

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The code names the three modes as trust modes `local`, `byok` and `managed` (Managed Cloud). The chat header names the boundary before a request is sent. [code] (src/features/model-picker/reachability.ts:6; README.md Privacy)

| Mode | Supported | Who | How |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:local | Yes, through the CLI app-server. The runtime schema names Ollama and LM Studio providers. | Anyone, no AGI account or subscription. Free and signed-out users included. | The CLI runs local models on the device. [code] (README.md:35-38; src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:724-731) |
| mode:own-key | Yes (BYOK, bring your own key). | Anyone with a provider key, no AGI subscription. | Keys are held and used by the CLI. Calls go straight to the named provider. `signInProvider` runs `agi login <id>`. [code] (README.md Privacy; src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:383-404) |
| mode:cloud | Yes (Managed Cloud). | Plans that include the `developer_surfaces` capability: Pro, Max, Max 15x, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise. Free and Basic are blocked from managed models. | Models route through AGI servers. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 359; src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:100-109) |

**Free users.** Free can use Local and own-key. Managed models are refused for Free (the test names this) and Auto is kept off Free. Cloud-backed utilities such as inline completions need an account and a model the cloud picker offers. [code] (src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:67-109; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts:36-60)

**Unresolved tier.** With no known tier the extension treats the account as `byok`, which admits the whole catalog for provider admission by the app-server. [code] (src/integrations/tierResolver.ts:197-221; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts)

**Tier source.** `GET /api/me?surface=vscode` returns the tier and a capability document. The tier is cached for 300 seconds, matching the CLI's own cache. Plan labels the extension accepts include local, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. [code] (src/utils/api.ts:324, 1409; src/integrations/tierResolver.ts:14-39, 56)

**Boundary rules.** A Local default model is never swapped for a Cloud model. Cloud-only utilities (code review, suggest terminal command, inline completions) refuse and send nothing when the default is Local. Switching provider mid-thread across a boundary starts a new thread. Provider-switch inside one thread needs a plan that allows it (`canSwitchProviderInThread`). The privacy mode allows local only, local plus byok, or all three. [code] (src/core/cloudModelBoundary.ts:12-40; src/integrations/providerSwitchGuard.ts:19-43; src/features/model-picker/reachability.ts:30-34; README.md Privacy)

**Execution boundary.** Local runtime and tools run on the user's machine. Managed Cloud chat, inline completions, memory, usage, feedback, dictation and cloud tasks need AGI servers. Cloud dictation opens a browser page, since a webview has no microphone. [code] (README.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:328)

Whether the free Local use needs the CLI's own sign-in is decided inside the CLI, not here: [unknown] (apps/cli not read in depth).

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
**Workspace packages the extension depends on** (all `workspace:*`): agent-core, artifacts, client-runtime, cloud-contracts, design-tokens, i18n, ide-runtime, local-runtime-contract, observability, routing, sync, types, unified-chat, utils. [code] (package.json:1586-1600)

Import counts in `src/` show what is really used: `@agiworkforce/types` in 146 files (plans, model catalog, product names), `cloud-contracts` in 42 files, `local-runtime-contract` in 23, `ide-runtime` in 6, `agent-core` in 4, `client-runtime` in 3, and `routing`, `sync`, `artifacts` and `design-tokens` in 2 to 3 each. `i18n`, `observability`, `utils` have no direct import in `src/` ([inferred] they are declared but may be unused or reached through other packages). `unified-chat` is imported only by `src/webview/render.ts` (markdown plugins, math, assistant fences). [code] (grep of imports, apps/extension-vscode/src)

**Notable reuse.** Device sign-in logic in `client-runtime` is shared with CLI, Desktop and Chrome (surface type `cli|desktop|vscode|chrome`). The managed chat client comes from `cloud-contracts` (`createManagedCloudChatClient`). Memory sync uses `@agiworkforce/sync`. Task classification uses `@agiworkforce/routing`. Terminal, diagnostics and glob helpers come from `ide-runtime`. [code] (packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts:24; src/utils/managedCloudChat.ts; src/memory/accountMemoryClient.ts:9; src/integrations/routingTask.ts:1; src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:13)

**The biggest shared piece is the CLI.** The Rust `apps/cli` app-server is the same engine behind Desktop local sessions. The extension is a client of it. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:76; audit/overview.md:206)

**Model catalog.** Model IDs come from `@agiworkforce/types` (catalog owner: packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts, generated models file). The extension holds no model literal of its own in the code read. [code] (src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts; AGENTS.md section 4)

**Not shared.** The sidebar UI itself is its own webview (`ChatStateManager.ts`, `webviewContent.ts`), not the shared unified-chat React UI. [code] (src/features/sidebar-webview/; grep of unified-chat imports)

**Boundary.** The Marketplace listing is also the contributor's constraint: `README.md` ships in the VSIX, contributor notes do not. [code] (.vscodeignore; README.md header comment)

Commands come from `docs/agent-context/commands.json` (key `vscodeExtension`) and `package.json` scripts. The filter name is `agi-workforce`. [code] (docs/agent-context/commands.json:162-170; package.json:1568-1585)

| Goal | Command |

| Typecheck | `pnpm --filter agi-workforce typecheck` |
| Unit tests | `pnpm --filter agi-workforce test` (Vitest, `src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`, `vscode` aliased to a mock) |

**To run it by hand:** build, install the CLI so `agi` is on PATH (or set `agiWorkforce.cliPath`), open a trusted folder, open the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar. [code] (docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Quick start)

sections.heading: Release state
sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** Code is present and wired: the manifest, activation, sign-in, runtime pool, model picker, tree views and a release workflow all exist. [code] (package.json; src/extension.ts; .github/workflows/release-vscode-extension.yml)

**Version.** `package.json` is `0.0.2`, flagged preview. A git tag `v-vscode-0.0.1` exists. Tag format for releases is `v-vscode-X.Y.Z` (stable) or `v-vscode-X.Y.Z-<beta|rc|nightly|alpha|canary>.N` (pre-release channel), and the tag version must equal the manifest version. [code] (package.json:5; git tag list; release-vscode-extension.yml tag check)

**Release pipeline.** On a tag push or manual dispatch: typecheck, lint, tests, webview tests, release-guard self test, production package, `verify:package`, SHA-256, secret and dev-endpoint scan of the unpacked VSIX, install of the exact VSIX in a clean VS Code profile under xvfb, upload. Publish job (protected environment `vscode-marketplace`) logs in to Microsoft Entra by GitHub OIDC and runs `vsce publish`. An optional Open VSX job (for VS Code forks) stays off until the variable `OPEN_VSX_PUBLISH` is `true`. [code] (release-vscode-extension.yml)

**Is it published? [unknown].** The surface matrix says the workflow had no GitHub runs or matching release and that Marketplace publication was not independently proven. The web status map marks `vscode` as "Coming soon", and the web page `/vscode-extension` shows that label. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:27, 74; apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:11; apps/web/app/vscode-extension/page.tsx:34)

**Blocked by the CLI.** The extension chat needs the AGI CLI, which has no signed release yet. Until then VS Code chat works only from a source build. [requirement] (audit/blockers/14-desktop-and-vscode-need-unpublished-cli.md; docs/product/suite.md:72) The installer command `Code: Install AGI CLI` reads `/api/releases/cli/latest`. [code] (src/integrations/cliInstaller.ts:6)

**Verification status.** The 2026-09 audit judged VS Code "solid" for editor integration but "needs the local CLI". No live run is recorded in the files read. [requirement] (audit/overview.md:229, 398)

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
The product goal is one consistent experience across six apps. The extension differs on purpose and by gap.

**By design (Host Developer domain).**
- Sessions are workspace scoped and local. They are not synced into Web, Mobile or Desktop chat history. Any move to the cloud is an explicit handoff. [code] (README.md Privacy; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Purpose)
- Chat, history and tools depend on the local CLI process. The other consumer apps use Managed Cloud directly. [code] (src/integrations/localRuntimePool.ts)
- Cloud tasks, projects, schedules, connectors, artifacts and memory show as account tree views, not as the shared web UI. [code] (src/features/*/\*Tree.ts; surface-feature-matrix.md)

**Absent here (per the matrix).** Image, video, research reports, study mode, voice recording, camera, screen capture, skills, plugins, published apps, browser driving, desktop driving, provider Fast mode, in-editor auto-update (the Marketplace updates it), and library artifacts. [requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md lines 198, 268-348, 368-378, 408, 468, 518, 538)

**Unverified in the matrix.** Search interaction mode, MCP client role, settings and onboarding entry points, context handoff UI, git client role, hooks, account sign-in and config cells. These matrix cells are now outdated in part, see outdated documents. [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md lines 218, 238, 258, 388, 428, 448, 558, 588, 598)

**UI.** The editor has its own webview and theme tokens (checked by `check-vscode-theme-tokens.mjs`) rather than the shared React chat, using `unified-chat` only for markdown, math and fence helpers. [code] (src/webview/render.ts:2-12; package.json lint script)

**Plan gate difference.** Managed models need a Pro-or-higher plan (`developer_surfaces`), while Basic includes managed chat on web. Basic cannot use managed developer models here. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:341-359; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts:36-45)

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
1. **Manifest facts.** Read `apps/extension-vscode/package.json` (version, engines, activation, commands, settings, scripts).
2. **Entry point.** Read `src/extension.ts` `activate()`; confirm sidebar and runtime pool registration.
3. **Modes.** Read `src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:60-110` and `src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts`. Run that test with the single-test command above, through `scripts/dev/light-job.sh` on the owner's machine.
4. **Plan gate.** Read `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts` (`developer_surfaces`, `PRO_TIERS`).
5. **Sign-in.** Read `src/features/surfaces/accountAccess.ts`, `src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts`, and `packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts`.
6. **Release.** Read `.github/workflows/release-vscode-extension.yml`. Check `git tag` for `v-vscode-*`, the Actions run list, and the Marketplace page. Those last two were not available to this page.
7. **Whole-app check.** Run `pnpm --filter agi-workforce test:integration` for a real Extension Host, and install the VSIX with an `agi` binary on PATH, then try Local, own-key and Cloud with a Free and a Pro account. Not done by this page.
8. **Companion pages.** For the CLI runtime see the CLI surface page; for the plan system see the subscription pages of this knowledge base.

key_facts.fact: The extension is named AGI Code, package name agi-workforce, version 0.0.2, publisher agiworkforce, preview, pricing Free.
It requires VS Code ^1.100.0 and runs in the workspace extension host; virtual workspaces are not supported.
Entry point is src/extension.ts activate(), bundled to out/extension.js by esbuild (CJS, node18, vscode external).
Chat and agent runs run in a local `agi app-server` process of the AGI CLI, one per workspace root, managed by LocalRuntimePool.
Local models and own provider keys work without an AGI account or subscription; an account is needed only for Managed Cloud and cloud-backed extras.
Managed models in the editor need a plan with the developer_surfaces capability: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. Free and Basic are blocked.
Tier comes from GET /api/me?surface=vscode, cached 300 seconds (same as the CLI cache); an unresolved tier defaults to byok.
Sign-in uses a browser device-approval flow with surface 'vscode', preferring the CLI's account/login and falling back to the extension's own flow; the credential is kept in VS Code SecretStorage.
Sign-out calls POST /api/auth/logout and also signs the CLI out.
Own-key sign-in runs `agi login <provider>` in a terminal, since the app-server has no provider login RPC.
A Local default model is never swapped for a Cloud model; cloud-only utilities refuse and send nothing when the default is Local.
Inline completions are off by default and send surrounding code to AGI Cloud via <apiEndpoint>/chat/completions (default https://agiworkforce.com/api/llm/v1).

doc.summary: The Chrome extension (surface:chrome) is a Manifest V3 side panel that reads pages and, on sites the user approves, clicks and types. It signs in through Clerk, needs an AGI account (free or paid), and talks to Managed Cloud only. No own-key mode. Version 0.0.6. Web status shows Coming soon. Release workflow exists; no store release is proven in the tree.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
The Chrome extension is a browser side panel assistant. It chats, reads the current page, selected text and other tabs, and, on sites the user approved, clicks, types and fills forms. [code] (apps/extension/package.json:4 description; apps/extension/manifest.json:5)

**Users.** Anyone with an AGI account, free or paid. The store listing says "Needs a free or paid AGI account. Not available in incognito windows." [code] (apps/extension/docs/chrome-web-store-listing.md:91; apps/extension/manifest.json:7 `incognito: not_allowed`). The product suite page calls it a "Cloud-only browser assistant, page context, extension/native-host bridge". [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:36)

**Names.** Manifest name is "AGI Extension"; the package is `@agiworkforce/extension`; the release archive is named `agi-browser-companion-<version>.zip`. [code] (apps/extension/manifest.json:3; apps/extension/package.json:2; .github/workflows/release-chrome-extension.yml, metadata step). The name shown to users should come from the product-names registry (packages/contracts/types/src/product-names.ts). [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)

**Main features** (all [code], folders under apps/extension/src/features):
- Chat in the side panel with history, projects, memory, artifacts, voice, read aloud, share.
- Page context: current page, selection, several tabs (features/browser-tools, features/side-panel/tabContext.ts).
- Browser control by a Chrome DevTools Protocol driver (features/computer-use/cdpDriver.ts) with approval modes. Auto stops for crucial actions; Ask first confirms every action; no mode completes a purchase. [code] (apps/extension/docs/threat-model.md objectives; features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts, crucialActions.ts)
- Unattended tasks with `-yolo` or `--always-approve`, scheduled tasks, recorded shortcuts, job-application autofill (features/content/autofill, src/jobAutofill.ts). [code] (apps/extension/README.md; features/background/scheduled-task-runs.ts)
- Close finished tabs without reading them (features/browser-tools/tabCleanup.ts). [code] (README.md)
- A bridge to AGI Desktop through native messaging (features/native-bridge). [code]

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
- **Language and bundler.** TypeScript, built with Vite. Two passes: the main pass builds the service worker, side panel, options page and welcome page as ES modules; a second pass (`BUILD_TARGET=content`) builds the content script as a self-contained classic script. [code] (apps/extension/vite.config.ts:25-45, 70-85; package.json scripts `build`, `dev`)
- **Platform.** Chrome Manifest V3, `minimum_chrome_version` 132, service worker `src/background.js`, side panel `src/side_panel.html`, options page `src/options.html`, content script on all `http://*/*` and `https://*/*` top frames. [code] (apps/extension/manifest.json)
- **UI.** Plain DOM code, not React: `side_panel.ts` builds elements with helper functions (`el`). Markdown uses markdown-it, KaTeX and DOMPurify. [code] (package.json dependencies; features/side-panel/dom.ts) The shared chat package `@agiworkforce/unified-chat` is also imported (16 import sites). [code] (grep of src)
- **Size.** `src/background.ts` is about 9,300 lines, `src/side_panel.ts` about 16,800 lines, `src/content.ts` about 1,800 lines. [code] (wc -l)
- **Permissions.** activeTab, tabs, storage, nativeMessaging, alarms, contextMenus, sidePanel, scripting, cookies, notifications, tabGroups, debugger, downloads. Optional: history and any http(s) host. Fixed hosts: localhost, 127.0.0.1, agiworkforce.com, api.agiworkforce.com. [code] (manifest.json)
- **Security design.** The content script is treated as possibly compromised. Storage areas are set to trusted contexts only, so a page cannot read the session token or the approved-sites list. The agent refuses to operate the user's own AGI account origins. [code] (docs/threat-model.md; features/background/storageAccess.ts; features/computer-use/accountOrigins.ts; test:apps/extension/__tests__/content-storage-boundary.test.ts)
- **Package manager.** Node 24 or newer, pnpm workspace member. [code] (package.json engines)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
- **Provider.** Clerk, through `@clerk/chrome-extension`. The extension builds a Clerk client with the publishable key and a sync host, so it acts as the account already signed in on the web. [code] (src/features/cloud-bridge/clerkAuth.ts:1-80)
- **Flow.** The panel's sign-in opens a tab at the web app `/sign-in` with `redirectTo=/auth/chrome-extension`. The extension then reads the sync-host session. [code] (clerkAuth.ts:215-223). The `cookies` permission exists for this. [code] (docs/threat-model.md capability table)
- **Configuration names (no values).** `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `CLERK_FRONTEND_API`, `CLERK_SYNC_HOST`, `VITE_AGI_WEB_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_ARTIFACT_SANDBOX_ORIGIN`, `VITE_SENTRY_DSN`, `CHROME_EXTENSION_PUBLIC_KEY`. [code] (apps/extension/.env.example)
- **Fail closed.** If the key or sync host is missing or malformed, sign-in throws. [code] (clerkAuth.ts:60-70)
- **Stable extension ID.** Production builds need `CHROME_EXTENSION_PUBLIC_KEY` so the ID matches the store item; Clerk sync depends on it. [code] (.env.example; scripts/manifest-config.mjs) [requirement] (docs/runbooks/chrome-web-store-publish.md:33)
- **Token use.** Chat requests carry the Clerk session token. A development-only bearer token in local storage is honoured only when the build is a Vite dev build. [code] (features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:360-425)
- **Verification.** Register row EXT-CRX-KEY-MISSING-BLOCKS-CLERK-SYNC-01 says authenticated sign-in with the Store identity is not yet verified; only the signed-out bridge was answered in Chromium (2026-11-24). [requirement] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md:363)
- **Account changes.** Managed-cloud owner is tracked (`managedCloudAuthority.ts`) so a switch of account does not mix data. [code]

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
| Mode | Chat in this app | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| mode:cloud (Managed Cloud) | Yes. The only chat route. Chat posts to `/api/llm/v1/chat/completions` on the AGI web origin; models list from `/api/llm/v1/models`; usage from `/api/usage`. | [code] (freeTrialClient.ts:112-116) |
| mode:own-key (BYOK) | No. A leftover stored provider key is purged. The threat model says a failed cloud turn must not fall back to Desktop, Local or BYOK. | [code] (features/security/legacyProviderCredentials.ts:1-25) [requirement] (docs/threat-model.md objectives) |
| mode:local | No local inference in the extension. The Desktop bridge runs page actions requested by a paired desktop; it is not a chat model route. | [code] (features/native-bridge/desktopCommands.ts header comment) [inferred] |

**Free and subscribed users.** Both use Managed Cloud after sign-in. The server decides admission, plan, usage and model routing; the client shows plan notices and quota recovery (top up, upgrade, view usage). [code] (freeTrialClient.ts:122-160 quota types; features/side-panel/freePlanNotices.ts; docs/threat-model.md trust table: "Server admission, plan, usage and model routing remain authoritative"). The default model comes from the shared catalog helper `getDefaultModelFor` for the free tier, not a literal. [code] (freeTrialClient.ts:~60 FREE_TRIAL_MODEL) Model list comes from the catalog in packages/contracts/types/src/models.json (generated; do not edit by hand). [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4)

**Local-inference requirement.** The product requirement that local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any subscription does not apply to this app because it has no local inference. [inferred]

**Execution boundaries.** On the device: page reading, DOM actions, DevTools-protocol driver, approved-site list, conversation store (authoritative copy), recordings. On AGI servers: all model inference, usage and quota, memory, projects, schedules, skills, share, video generation. [code] (cloud-bridge clients; docs/threat-model.md)

**Sync rule.** A conversation is mirrored into the account store only when every turn has Managed Cloud provenance; unknown, Local or BYOK turns stay browser-local. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md:75; docs/product/suite.md:70-74) [code] (features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts)

The guard `check:no-cloud-ipc` stops cloud IPC calls outside the cloud-bridge folder. [code] (scripts/check-no-cloud-ipc-v1.mjs)

key_facts.fact: The Chrome extension is Manifest V3, version 0.0.6, minimum Chrome 132, with a side panel, options page, service worker and content script.
Chat is Managed Cloud only: it posts to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions on the AGI web origin; models from /api/llm/v1/models; usage from /api/usage.
There is no own-key (BYOK) or Local chat; a legacy stored provider key is purged from local, session and sync storage.
A failed cloud turn must not fall back to Desktop, Local or BYOK inference.
Sign-in uses Clerk (@clerk/chrome-extension) with a sync host; the panel opens web /sign-in?redirectTo=/auth/chrome-extension.
An AGI account (free or paid) is required; incognito is not allowed.
A development bearer token in local storage is honoured only in a Vite dev build.
Build is Vite in two passes: main (background, side_panel, options, welcome) then content as an IIFE.
The side panel is vanilla DOM TypeScript, not React; side_panel.ts is about 16,800 lines and background.ts about 9,300.
Most-used shared packages: types (64 import sites), cloud-contracts (51), unified-chat (16), utils (14), client-runtime (14).
Conversations are mirrored to the account store only when every turn has Managed Cloud provenance; Chrome keeps its local copy authoritative.
Browser control needs a per-origin Chrome host-permission grant plus stored consent; the AGI account origins are refused for every browser-control capability.
Approval modes: Auto (default) stops for crucial actions, Ask first confirms every action, no mode completes a purchase; -yolo runs routine actions unattended on approved sites.
Web surface status marks chrome as Coming soon with CTA href /chrome-extension and a notify list.
Release workflow triggers on tags v-ext-X.Y.Z, requires tag, package.json and manifest versions to match, and publishes only after protected-environment approval.
Whether the release workflow has ever run, or the extension is in the Chrome Web Store, is not established in the tree.
The first Chrome Web Store version must be uploaded manually in the Developer Dashboard; the API cannot create the item.
Unattended Chrome Cloud runs that fail, time out, are partial or cancelled are reported as success (High, open).
Production sign-in with the Chrome Web Store identity is unverified; only the signed-out bridge answered in Chromium on 2026-11-24.
The content script matches all http and https pages; on unapproved pages it injects no UI and only asks the worker whether the site is approved.

The extension has a desktop bridge over native messaging with HMAC-SHA256 envelopes after a negotiated session secret; desktop-issued actions are still held to the extension's own approved-sites and consent bar.
Features absent per the matrix: artifact library, research reports, study mode, image and video generation UI, camera, connectors, skills, plugins, apps, code sessions, Fast mode.
MCP is partial: webmcp.ts exposes page tools; no MCP server connection exists.
Unit tests are about 300 Vitest files in jsdom; a Chromium smoke test runs through e2e/smoke.mjs.
Free-tier default model is derived through getDefaultModelFor from shared types, not a literal in the extension.

doc.summary: How to set up a Mac for AGI Workforce development: Node 24, the pinned pnpm, the pinned Rust toolchain, then pnpm install. Lists the dev command for each of the six apps, local test accounts, the pre-push gate, and the rule that on a machine with 24 GB of RAM or less heavy jobs run one at a time through scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh. Also lists traps and stale documents.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page tells an engineer or an LLM what to install on a Mac and how to start each of the six apps (Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code extension, Chrome extension) for development. It also explains the rule that heavy jobs (builds, full test suites, type checks, cargo, dev servers, browsers, emulators, `git push`) run one at a time on a small machine.

Status words used here: *implementation status* means the script or file exists in the repository. *Verification status* means someone ran it. Nothing on this page was run by the author; the project records no run of the setup steps. Every command is [code] or [requirement] taken from the cited files.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
**1. Install the toolchain.**

| Tool | Required version | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `>=24.15.0 <25` [code] (package.json:14). `.nvmrc` holds `24` [code]. CI uses Node 24 [code] (.github/workflows/ci.yml:46). | `engine-strict=false` in `.npmrc:9`, so a wrong Node only warns; do not rely on pnpm to stop you [code] |
| pnpm | `>=10.16.0` in engines (package.json:15); exact pin `pnpm@10.34.7` in `packageManager` (package.json:12) [code] | use Corepack or Homebrew `pnpm` |
| Rust | channel `1.99.1` with `clippy` and `rustfmt` (rust-toolchain.toml) [code]; rustup provisions it by itself on first cargo call [inferred] | needed for CLI, GPUI and Tauri desktop, and for `pnpm check:protocol-types` |
| Xcode with the Metal toolchain | only for the GPUI desktop host: `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain` [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md:~159) | optional |
| `sandbox-exec` | ships with macOS; the CLI needs it to run sandboxed commands [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md, Runtime requirement table) | nothing to install on a Mac |
| Postgres 16 with pgvector | `docker compose up -d postgres` using `docker-compose.yml` (image `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, port 127.0.0.1:5432, database `agiworkforce_dev`) [code]. The runbook also mentions a Homebrew Postgres used for local work [requirement] (docs/runbooks/database-backup-restore.md:222). | needed for Web with a local database |

**2. Install packages.** From the repository root run `pnpm install`. A release younger than seven days will not install: `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` minutes in `pnpm-workspace.yaml:8` [code]. The `prepare` script runs `husky || true`, which installs the git hooks [code] (package.json:140).

**3. Create env files.** Copy `apps/web/.env.local.example` to `apps/web/.env.local` and fill the blank values (Clerk development keys, `DATABASE_URL`, random development secrets for `CSRF_SECRET`, `CRON_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET` and similar, Stripe test keys only if billing is under test). Keep `STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED=false` unless Stripe test webhooks and prices exist [code] (apps/web/.env.local.example). Copy `apps/mobile/.env.local.example` to `apps/mobile/.env.local` for Mobile. Never commit either file.

**4. Prepare the local database.** Start Postgres, then `AGI_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/agiworkforce_dev pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target local` [code] (docker-compose.yml header). The migration chain is append-only; see `pnpm db:migrate -- status` [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5 and 12).

**5. Seed test accounts.** `pnpm dev:accounts seed` makes one local account per plan and per app lane. Sign in at `http://localhost:3000/login` with `agi-dev-<name>+clerk_test@example.com` and the code `424242` [requirement] (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md). See the Commands section.

**6. Start the app you are working on** through the heavy-job wrapper (see Commands). For apps that talk to Cloud, start the Web app first, because Desktop (Electron), Mobile, Chrome and the CLI all call it [inferred] from the env examples (apps/mobile/.env.local.example points at `http://localhost:3000`).

**7. Before you push** run lint, `pnpm typecheck:all`, `pnpm test:affected` and `pnpm check:llm-operability` [requirement] (CONTRIBUTING.md, Before you push). `.husky/pre-push` runs the guard chain and an affected lint and typecheck for you [code].

sections.heading: Commands
sections.markdown:
**Run every command below with a wrapper on a machine of 24 GB or less.** Prefix a heavy command with `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`, and a scoped one (one test file or package, lint on touched files) with `scripts/dev/light-job.sh`.

| App | Start for development | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| surface:web | `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web dev` (runs `next dev`, apps/web/package.json:6) | default port 3000. For checks the project's QA notes prefer a compiled build, not `next dev` [requirement] (knowledge-base/70-qa/setup/web.md); `next start` is exempt from the gate [code] (.claude/hooks/heavy-job-gate.py is_heavy). Build: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web build` (runs `notices` first). |
| surface:desktop (public Electron) | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/desktop dev:electron` (builds main process then `electron .`, apps/desktop/package.json:16) | The Electron window loads the hosted web app; a change in `apps/desktop/src` never shows there [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md). An unpackaged build can point at localhost with `AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:18); a packaged build ignores it (config.ts:58). |
| surface:desktop (Tauri, retained internal) | `pnpm dev:desktop` at root, or `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/desktop dev` (`tauri dev`, package.json:414; apps/desktop/package.json:8) | renderer is the Vite app in `apps/desktop/src`; renderer only: `dev:vite` |
| surface:desktop (GPUI native host, opt-in) | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/desktop dev:gpui` | needs Node 24, Rust 1.99.1, Metal toolchain; closes the app before rebuild [requirement] |
| surface:mobile | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/mobile dev` (Metro), `... ios`, `... android`, `... ios:device:dev` for a real phone | `ios` and `android` run `expo run:*` and prebuild the native projects, which are gitignored and generated [requirement] (apps/mobile/README.md). On a real device set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to a LAN address, not localhost [code] (apps/mobile/.env.local.example). |
| surface:cli | `cargo install --path apps/cli --bin agi`, then `agi login` (AGI account) or `agi login <provider>` (own key) and `agi auth-status` | [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md). Binary is `agi`; `agiworkforce` is an alias. |
| surface:vscode | `pnpm --filter <vscode package name> watch` (`node esbuild.js --watch`, apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1570); package: `package` script (line 1571) | needs `agi` on PATH, or set `agiWorkforce.cliPath` [requirement] (apps/extension-vscode/README.md). I did not read the package name; use `docs/agent-context/commands.json` for the filter. |
| surface:chrome | `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/extension dev` (`BUILD_TARGET=content vite build && vite build --watch`, apps/extension/package.json:24); then load `apps/extension/dist` unpacked | Add the unpacked extension origin to `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES` to sign in from it [code] (apps/web/.env.local.example:11-13). Local artifact previews: set `VITE_ARTIFACT_SANDBOX_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3002` and run `node infrastructure/sandbox/dev.mjs --extension-id <id> --port 3002` [requirement] (apps/extension/README.md). |

**Repository-wide commands** [code] (package.json):

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `pnpm install` |
| Lint (all but the extension) | `pnpm lint` (line 141); extension: `pnpm lint:extension` |
| Typecheck desktop only | `pnpm typecheck` (line 401) |
| Typecheck everything | `pnpm typecheck:all` (line 418); Web needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12) |
| Tests | `pnpm test` (turbo, concurrency 2), `pnpm test:affected`, `pnpm test:l1`, `pnpm test:security` |
| One package's test | `pnpm --filter <workspace-package> test <file-or-pattern>` [requirement] (docs/agent-context/commands.json) |
| Build all except desktop | `pnpm build` / `pnpm build:all`; desktop: `pnpm build:desktop` |
| Guard chain | `pnpm check:llm-operability` (package.json:397) |
| Models | edit curation file then `pnpm sync:models` (line 386) |
| Protocol types | `pnpm generate:protocol-types` (line 420) |
| Rust | `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --lib -- -D warnings -D unsafe-code` [requirement] (commands.json) |
| Test accounts | `pnpm dev:accounts seed [name]`, `reset <name\|all>`, `list` (package.json:415) |

**The wrappers** [code]:

```
scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh pnpm typecheck:all
scripts/dev/light-job.sh pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/web test path/to/file.test.ts
```

- `heavy-job.sh` takes one machine-wide lock (`/tmp/agi-heavy.kernel.lock`) so only one heavy job runs at a time (scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh:31). It waits for free memory first: default 3 GB, set by `AGI_HEAVY_MIN_FREE_GB` (line 30). It polls every 15 seconds and gives up waiting after 900 seconds, then runs anyway (lines 34-39). It measures free memory with `vm_stat` (free, inactive, speculative, purgeable pages), falling back to `/proc/meminfo`. It is not re-entrant: never call it from inside a command it already runs (header comment).
- `light-job.sh` has two lock slots (`/tmp/agi-light.slot1.lock`, `slot2`), so two scoped jobs can run at once (scripts/dev/light-job.sh:9).
- Other scripts in `scripts/dev`: `reset-app-mac.sh` (deletes local Desktop app data under `~/Library/Application Support/com.agiworkforce.desktop` after a yes/no prompt; dev only) and `reset-app.ps1` for Windows [code].

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
**The one-at-a-time rule** [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, Delegation): the owner's laptop has 16 GB, so RAM, not tokens, is the limit. Reading, thinking and editing agents may run in parallel. Local heavy jobs (builds, full suites, `tsc`, cargo, dev servers, browsers, emulators, `git push`) go one at a time through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`; scoped tests or lint go through `scripts/dev/light-job.sh`.

**How it is enforced** [code] (.claude/hooks/heavy-job-gate.py, registered for the `Bash` tool in .claude/settings.json):
- It only runs inside Claude Code. A human in a plain terminal is not blocked; the wrappers are a convention there [inferred].
- It acts only when the machine has 24 GB of RAM or less (`SMALL_MACHINE_GB = 24`, line 9; it reads `sysctl hw.memsize`). If RAM cannot be read, it does not block (line 96).
- It splits the command on `&&`, `||`, `;`, pipes and newlines, and denies any segment that looks heavy and is not wrapped.
- Heavy means: a pnpm/npm/yarn/bun script whose name starts with `build`, `dev`, `test`, `e2e`, `typecheck`, `tsc`, `lint`, `knip` or `storybook` (with or without a `:suffix`), or `check:llm-operability`, `check:trust-boundaries`, `check:protocol-types`; the tools `tsc`, `vitest`, `jest`, `playwright`, `next`, `expo`, `eas`, `turbo`, `xcodebuild`, `gradle`, `electron-builder`, `vite`, `webpack`, `knip`, `storybook`; `cargo build|test|check|clippy|run|bench|nextest`; and `git push`. `next start` and `vite preview` are not heavy.
- A wrapped command passes (`heavy-job.sh`, `light-job.sh`, `heavy.sh`, `light.sh`).

**Other traps**
- Do not wrap a heavy-job inside a heavy-job (deadlock on the same lock) [code].
- The heavy-job wait is a floor, not a guarantee: after 900 seconds it starts the command even if memory is still short [code] (heavy-job.sh:34-39).
- A loaded machine fails tests that pass alone; check `uptime` and re-run in isolation [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- `apps/web` runs its own Vitest major: use the package script or `pnpm exec vitest` inside `apps/web`, never the root binary [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- Web `tsc --noEmit` dies with SIGABRT without `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` [requirement]. The pre-push hook sets that heap itself [code] (.husky/pre-push).
- Guards read the working tree, not HEAD. Stage first, run guards, then commit [requirement].
- `.husky/pre-push` normally builds a clean detached worktree of HEAD under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agi-prepush-worktree` and runs the chain there (`scripts/prepush-clean-worktree.sh`); `AGI_PREPUSH_ON_TREE=1` runs it on your tree; `SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` skips it [code].
- A Clerk `pk_test_` key forces a handshake redirect on every authenticated page; `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES` is required or sign-in fails with no clear error [requirement] (docs/development/troubleshooting.md).
- A value exported in your shell beats `.env.local`; check `env | grep AGI_` [requirement].
- If chat fails with a closed-lane error locally, set `AGI_KV_PROVIDER=memory` (or a local Redis with `AGI_KV_REDIS_URL`) so you do not use the shared key-value store [requirement].
- A dev server that slows down over an afternoon: stop it, delete `apps/web/.next` and the Turbo cache, restart. Do not reinstall dependencies under a running dev server [requirement].
- Lockfiles (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`) are never hand-edited; a Claude Code hook blocks writes [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, .claude/hooks/block-lock-files.sh).
- Mobile: stale Metro cache makes every `className` stop working; clear it. Generated `ios`/`android` folders are discarded by the next prebuild; never hand-edit them [requirement].
- `pnpm dev:accounts` refuses to run against a non-local database, a preview or production runtime, a production Clerk key or a live Stripe key; there is no override [requirement] (local-test-accounts.md; test:apps/web/scripts/__tests__/dev-accounts.test.ts).
- Local inference and local mode need no subscription, but the dev accounts and Cloud features need a Clerk sign-in; that is an account question, not a payment one [inferred]. Which mode each dev command exercises (mode:local, mode:own-key, mode:cloud) is not stated in the setup documents [unknown].
- Model names must not be written as literals; the only home is the generated catalog (`packages/contracts/types/src/models.json`, produced by `pnpm sync:models`) [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4).

sections.heading: Gaps in the documents
sections.markdown:
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` says Rust 1.94.0; the pin is 1.99.1 (see outdated documents).
- No document gives one end-to-end first-run recipe for a fresh Mac: no Homebrew list, no statement that Docker (or Homebrew Postgres) is needed, no ordering of env file, database, migrate, seed and start. This page assembles it from several files.
- The documents do not say which Node patch is required in prose; only `package.json` engines (`>=24.15.0`) does, while `.nvmrc` says `24`.
- `docs/development/README.md` does not link the heavy-job rule; it appears only in `CLAUDE.md` and some runbooks (chrome-web-store-publish.md:64, vscode-marketplace-publish.md, mobile-store-first-release.md).
- `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` do not mention `heavy-job.sh`; a contributor not using Claude Code is not told about it, and the gate hook does not apply to them [inferred].
- No document says how to run the Electron desktop against a local web server step by step (the env name exists in code only; the QA notes describe it).
- The documents do not state minimum Xcode or Android Studio versions for Mobile builds, or the macOS version needed.
- The dev-accounts document says a local database is needed but not how to start it; the compose file supplies it.
- `docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md` and the README do not state which local jobs count as heavy; only the hook regex does.
- Verification status: no document records a clean run of this setup on a new machine [unknown].

key_facts.fact: Node must be >=24.15.0 and <25; .nvmrc says 24; CI uses Node 24.
pnpm is pinned to 10.34.7 via packageManager; engines allow >=10.16.0.
Rust toolchain is pinned to channel 1.99.1 with clippy and rustfmt, in lockstep with CI.
engine-strict is false, so a wrong Node version only warns.
pnpm refuses package releases younger than seven days (10080 minutes), with exceptions listed by exact version.
heavy-job.sh holds one machine-wide lock, waits for 3 GB free memory by default (AGI_HEAVY_MIN_FREE_GB), polls every 15 s, and stops waiting after 900 s.
light-job.sh allows two concurrent scoped jobs through two lock slots.
A Claude Code PreToolUse hook denies unwrapped heavy commands only when the machine has 24 GB of RAM or less; if RAM is unreadable it does not block.
The owner's laptop has 16 GB; RAM, not tokens, is the limit, so reading/editing agents run in parallel but heavy jobs run one at a time.

Heavy commands include pnpm scripts starting with build/dev/test/e2e/typecheck/tsc/lint/knip/storybook, cargo build/test/check/clippy/run, git push, and tools like tsc, vitest, playwright, next, expo, turbo, xcodebuild.
Web dev command is next dev (apps/web package script dev); typecheck is tsc --noEmit and needs an 8192 MB heap.
Mobile runs through Expo: dev (Metro), ios, android, ios:device:dev; native ios/android folders are generated and gitignored.
The public Desktop is Electron showing the hosted web app; dev:electron builds the main process then runs electron; Tauri (tauri dev) is retained internal code.
An unpackaged Electron build can load a different web origin through AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN; a packaged build ignores it.
The CLI is built with cargo install --path apps/cli --bin agi; sandboxed commands need sandbox-exec, which ships with macOS.
The Chrome extension dev command is a watching vite build; loading it unpacked requires its origin in CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES.
The VS Code extension has a watch script (esbuild) and needs the agi CLI on PATH or agiWorkforce.cliPath.
pnpm dev:accounts seeds one local account per plan plus lane accounts; sign-in uses an agi-dev-<name>+clerk_test@example.com address and code 424242.
dev:accounts refuses non-local databases, preview or production runtimes, production Clerk keys and live Stripe keys, with no override; a test covers each.
A local Postgres 16 with pgvector comes from docker-compose.yml on 127.0.0.1:5432; schema is applied by pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target local.
Husky pre-push runs the guard chain in a clean detached worktree by default; AGI_PREPUSH_ON_TREE=1 runs on the working tree and SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 skips it.
CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES is required locally and a pk_test_ Clerk key forces a handshake redirect on authenticated pages.
A shell-exported variable beats .env.local; AGI_KV_PROVIDER=memory avoids the shared key-value store for local chat.
CONTRIBUTING.md states Rust 1.94.0 but rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.99.1; the code wins.
The commands inventory file docs/agent-context/commands.json lists per-app commands and was last updated 2026-11-09.
GPUI native desktop host needs Node 24, Rust 1.99.1 and the Xcode Metal toolchain on macOS.
No document records a clean first-run of this setup on a new machine.

doc.summary: Configuration in AGI Workforce is env-var driven per app. Each app owns a tracked .env.example. The web app has a typed key registry (apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts) that checks values at boot. scripts/env-doctor.mjs checks per-app contracts. Runtime feature flags live in the database (table:feature_flags), with env kill-switches beside them. Pages group names by sign-in, database, providers, billing, storage, connectors, observability and release. Names only, never values.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page lists where every setting of AGI Workforce lives and what each group of environment variable names is for. It gives names and purposes only, never values.

**Status labels.** Implementation status (the code exists) is kept apart from verification status (someone ran it). Nothing here is [executed]: no project document records a real run of the checks below, and this page did not run them. Every claim was read from files.

**Basis tags.** [code] = read in a source file (path:line). [requirement] = stated in a project document. [inferred] = reasoned from code. [unknown] = not established.

### The shape of configuration

| Layer | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Per-app example file | Tracked list of every name an app reads, with comments | file:apps/web/.env.example, file:apps/web/.env.local.example, file:apps/desktop/.env.example, file:apps/desktop/.env.local.example, file:apps/mobile/.env.example, file:apps/mobile/.env.local.example, file:apps/extension/.env.example, file:apps/extension/.env.local.example, file:apps/cli/.env.example, file:services/signaling-server/.env.example, file:services/upload-scanner/.env.example [code] |
| Contract checker | Per-app lists of required names, URL checks, forbidden production values | file:scripts/env-doctor.mjs (contracts at line 14 on) [code] |
| Web key registry | Typed description of web keys: secret or public, owner, allowed environments, validator | file:apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts (CONFIG_KEY_DESCRIPTORS, about 143 entries; registry built at line 1773) [code] |
| Optional-feature table | Which feature turns on when which names are set | file:apps/web/lib/config/optional-features.ts (OPTIONAL_FEATURES, line 36) [code] |

A name starting NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_ or EXPO_PUBLIC_ is compiled into client code and is public. Every other web name is server-only [code] (apps/web/.env.example:6-8; apps/desktop/.env.example:5-6; apps/mobile/.env.example:7-8).

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
## How to set up or change configuration

1. **Find the owner file.** Each app owns one example file (table above). Copy the `.env.local.example` to `.env.local` for local work. Production values live in the deployment secret store, never in a file [code] (apps/web/.env.local.example:1-2, apps/web/.env.example:6-8).
2. **Web is not loaded by the doctor.** `env-doctor` reads `process.env` only and never reads dotenv files or prints values, so export the variables in the shell first [code] (scripts/env-doctor.mjs:664-671). A value already exported in the shell wins over `.env.local` [requirement] (docs/development/troubleshooting.md:66-68).
3. **Mobile production builds** use EAS environment variables, because eas.json sets EXPO_NO_DOTENV=1 [code] (apps/mobile/eas.json base env; apps/mobile/.env.example:3-5).
4. **Signaling service** loads `.env` through dotenv, not `.env.local` [code] (services/signaling-server/.env.example:1-3). The **CLI** does not load `.env` itself; it reads the process environment [code] (apps/cli/.env.example:1-3).
5. **Add a new web name:** read it as a literal `process.env.NAME`, add it to apps/web/.env.example, and classify it in CONFIG_KEY_DESCRIPTORS (secret or published, owner, environments). A name reached through a constant is invisible to the scan; pin it in `documentedKeys` in scripts/env-doctor.mjs [code] (apps/web/.env.example:9-14; scripts/check-config-keys.mjs:1-8).
6. **Web boot check.** On the Node runtime, `register()` in file:apps/web/instrumentation.ts runs validateEnvironment(), then assertPooledDatabaseEndpoint(). If errors exist and NODE_ENV is production, boot throws unless AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV=1 [code] (apps/web/instrumentation.ts:40-64).
7. **Flags without a deploy.** Create or edit a flag definition through the operator or admin routes (for example api:GET /api/admin/upgrade-access exists for the upgrade switch) [inferred] (apps/web/app/api/admin/upgrade-access/route.ts exists; method not opened).

## Feature flags and switches (three kinds)

1. **Database flags.** Table table:feature_flags (per-user override rows, created in 0016_misc.sql) plus a definitions table added by migration 0211_feature_flag_targeting.sql. Definitions carry key, variants, default variant, rules, kill_switch, maturity, release channel, availability, owner, expiry [code] (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/flag-store.ts:20-33; apps/web/db/neon/0211_feature_flag_targeting.sql). Flag keys follow `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*([.:-][a-z0-9_]+)*$` [code] (flag-definition.ts:49).
2. **Key families.** capability.<name> kill switches, model.<id>, provider.<name>, tenant.lockdown, routing.* (observed_health, canary, shadow, response_assessment, response_assessment_apply, canary.<slot>), decision.<kind>, rollout rings, billing.upgrades_open [code] (kill-switches.ts:9-12; routing-flags.ts:10-16; billing-upgrades.ts:4). Extra kill-switch capabilities: dictation, screen_share, in_app_purchase, desktop_update, fast_mode [code] (kill-switches.ts:17-23).
3. **Flag tunables (env).** FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITION_CACHE_TTL_MS (0-300000, default 30000), FEATURE_FLAG_STALE_AFTER_DAYS (1-365, default 60), FEATURE_FLAG_STALE_CLEANUP_BATCH (1-200, default 25); a bad value keeps the default [code] (flag-config.ts:3-37).
4. **Env kill switches.** Defaults on: AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS, AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED, AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION, AGI_ROUTING_*, response caches, SUPPORT_AGENT_ENABLED, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_WIDGET_ENABLED, AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING. Defaults off: AGI_DURABLE_CODE_TURNS, AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED, SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED, AGI_SUPPORT_LIVE_HANDOFF_ENABLED, AGI_E2B_EXECUTION, CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED, MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED, STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED [code] (apps/web/.env.example comments).
5. **Build-time UI defaults.** NEXT_PUBLIC_COMPOSER_EDITOR (editor or textarea), NEXT_PUBLIC_MESSAGE_VARIANTS (on or off), NEXT_PUBLIC_FREE_LANE_UI (on or off); browser overrides by query parameter or localStorage [code] (apps/web/.env.example:866-890).
6. **Upgrade switch.** Paid upgrades are closed per account unless AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1 or flag billing.upgrades_open serves the on variant for that user; any read failure answers closed [code] (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/billing-upgrade-gate.ts:12-36).

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
- **Never put a secret in a public name.** NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*, EXPO_PUBLIC_* are public. The registry refuses a secret exposed to the client at boot (`secret_exposed_to_client` is source-fatal) [code] (apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts:1790-1796).
- **What fails boot (web, production):** missing DATABASE_URL/AGI_DATABASE_URL, missing Clerk, Stripe or app URL critical vars, missing Redis REST credentials, missing any of five individual-plan Stripe Prices (BASIC USD and INR, PRO, MAX, MAX_20X) [code] (validate-env.ts:36-139). Missing Team, enterprise and INR Pro/Max Prices only warn: checkout stays closed [code] (validate-env.ts:100-118).
- **Boot throws only when** NODE_ENV is production and AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV is not 1. The env-doctor treats AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV-style hatches as dangerous [code] (instrumentation.ts:60-64). ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN is an error in production, a warning elsewhere, and env-doctor also forbids it [code] (validate-env.ts:360-403; env-doctor.mjs productionForbiddenKeys).
- **Production forbidden values:** AGI_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_OUTAGE_POLICY=fail-open, and AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS set to 0, false or off [code] (env-doctor.mjs web contract).
- **Test keys, loopback URLs and placeholders in a deployed environment** warn loudly by default; AGI_ENFORCE_PRODUCTION_CONFIG=1 makes them refuse the boot. It is a deliberate two-step so a bad deployment is visible before it is allowed to block [code] (validate-env.ts:223-251; apps/web/.env.example:104-108). Whether production sets it is [unknown].
- **Stripe mode:** Production must hold live keys and preview/development test keys; secret and publishable keys must share one mode [code] (validate-env.ts:319-370).
- **Checkout gates must match:** STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED and NEXT_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT_ENABLED [code] (env-doctor.mjs web scope). Keep false locally unless webhooks and prices exist [code] (apps/web/.env.local.example:30).
- **Encryption key shapes:** connector and GitHub token keys are exactly 64 hex characters; TOTP key at least 32 characters; CSRF_SECRET and CRON_SECRET at least 32 characters [code] (apps/web/.env.example:110-111; validate-env.ts descriptors). Use independent random values per purpose.
- **Development runtimes cannot reach a non-loopback database** unless AGI_ALLOW_REMOTE_DATABASE equals the sentence the refusal prints [code] (apps/web/.env.example:78-83).
- **OAuth callback isolation:** development must redirect to loopback; deployed must use https and the same host as NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL [code] (validate-env.ts:1846-1905).
- **Sandbox origins must differ from the app origin.** NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN equal to the app URL is rejected. Unset in production is drift in env-doctor [code] (apps/web/.env.example:524-531 region; env-doctor.mjs web required list).
- **WORKFLOW_NODE_HTTP=1 is required** wherever durable turns run, or on Node 24 no durable step runs and AGI Work silently falls back to the inline turn [code] (apps/web/.env.example:57 of the workflow comment; env-doctor.mjs web required lists).
- **Mobile:** APP_ENV and EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV must be equal; production APP_ENV must be production; the Clerk key must be pk_live_ in production [code] (env-doctor.mjs mobile scope).
- **Egress allowlists:** CLI API hosts must be https and agiworkforce.com or a subdomain; a failing value is skipped, not sent. Desktop Electron main ignores AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN in a packaged build [code] (apps/cli/.env.example:14-19; apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:62-80).
- **CLI safety opt-outs remove protections** (AGIWORKFORCE_NO_SANDBOX, AGI_A2A_ALLOW_PRIVATE, AGI_POWERSHELL_ALLOW_UNSAFE, AGIWORKFORCE_VOICE_ALLOW_CLOUD); development only [code] (apps/cli/.env.example).
- **Execution boundary:** provider keys on web are managed-cloud keys (mode:cloud). CLI BYOK keys stay on the machine and go only to the issuing provider (mode:own-key). Local engines use no key (mode:local) [code] (apps/web/.env.example:307-321; apps/cli/.env.example BYOK block; packages/ai/providers/ollama/src/catalog.ts:6). Which app uses which mode at runtime is not established by this page.
- **Never hardcode a model ID** in config or code; use the generated catalog and family slots (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json) [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4).
- **Lock files** are never hand-edited, and new root files must be registered in scripts/check-repo-organization.mjs [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
