key_facts.fact: Each app owns one tracked example file; web has both .env.example (deployment contract) and .env.local.example (local dev). CLI, signaling and upload-scanner also have .env.example files.
The web app boots through a validator chain (validateEnvironment) that runs 15 checks including key registry, Stripe mode, OAuth callback isolation, optional features.
Production boot throws on validation errors unless AGI_ALLOW_INVALID_ENV=1; outside production it logs and continues.
AGI_ENFORCE_PRODUCTION_CONFIG=1 converts test-key, loopback and placeholder findings from warnings into a refused boot; findings are always logged and set a configuration gauge.
The web config-key registry classifies keys as secret or published, with owner, allowed environments and validators; a secret exposed to client code or an incomplete descriptor always refuses boot.
scripts/env-doctor.mjs defines contracts for 7 scopes: desktop, web, mobile, extension, cli, signaling, scanner; it reads process.env only and never prints values.
Database URL is DATABASE_URL with alias AGI_DATABASE_URL; production also requires Redis REST credentials (UPSTASH_* or KV_REST_API_*).
AGI_DATABASE_PROVIDER selects neon (default, WebSocket, edge) or postgres (TCP, not edge).
A development or test runtime cannot connect to a non-loopback database unless AGI_ALLOW_REMOTE_DATABASE carries the exact sentence the refusal prints.
Identity provider is Clerk only; AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER defaults to clerk and no second adapter exists.
CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES must list the Chrome extension origin or extension sign-in fails; unset it falls back to the origin of NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.
Web production requires five individual-plan Stripe Price IDs (BASIC USD, BASIC INR, PRO, MAX, MAX_20X); Team, enterprise and other INR prices only warn and keep that checkout closed.
Stripe server and client checkout gates (STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED, NEXT_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT_ENABLED) must match; production needs live-prefixed Clerk and Stripe keys.
Paid upgrades are open to an account only if AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1 or the billing.upgrades_open flag serves 'on' for that user; any read failure answers closed.
Native store purchases stay disabled (MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED=false) until real Apple and Google product ID maps and verification credentials are set.

Runtime feature flags are database rows with variants, rules, kill-switch bit, maturity and channel; key families include capability.*, model.*, provider.*, tenant.lockdown, routing.*, decision.*, billing.upgrades_open.
Flag tunables FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITION_CACHE_TTL_MS, FEATURE_FLAG_STALE_AFTER_DAYS, FEATURE_FLAG_STALE_CLEANUP_BATCH have defaults 30000, 60, 25 and bounded ranges; bad values keep defaults.
AGI_FREE_LANE_MODE accepts off, shadow, prefer, strict; default and invalid values resolve to off. It is read via a constant so the literal-read env contract scan does not see it.
Object storage is S3-compatible and provider-neutral (AGI_STORAGE_*), with Cloudflare R2 names kept as a fallback; a separate private bucket is required for generated media and attachments.
In production every upload is refused with no scanner configured unless UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false; the scanner token must match on both sides and be at least 32 characters.
OpenTelemetry export is off unless AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT is set; the same names serve web and signaling service.
Production environment drift is reconciled against env-doctor contracts every 6 hours by a CI workflow using Vercel API credentials.
CLI reads configuration from ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml (override dir AGIWORKFORCE_HOME), merges project config, and never loads .env; telemetry is read from global config only.
Mobile production builds use EAS environment variables (EXPO_NO_DOTENV=1); APP_ENV must equal EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV and preview/production need a live Clerk key.
The free-model promotion JSON window ended 2026-10-24, before today's date 2026-11-24, so the file is a past window.
VS Code settings live under agiWorkforce.* in package.json contributes.configuration (examples: apiEndpoint, model, cliPath, inlineCompletions.enabled, telemetryEnabled, memory.enabled).
Desktop Electron main ignores AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN when packaged and only accepts localhost or agiworkforce.com hosts.

Provider keys on the web server are managed-cloud keys; routing breakers, lockouts and canary/shadow stages are tuned by AGI_ROUTE_*, AGI_MODEL_LOCKOUT_*, AGI_CREDENTIAL_COOLDOWN_*, AGI_ROUTING_* names.

doc.summary: Commands to build, type-check, lint and test every AGI Workforce app, from root package.json and docs/agent-context/commands.json. It covers the two priority tiers (priority-level-1, security), the guard chain (check:llm-operability) and the traps: web and desktop use Vitest 5 while the root uses Vitest 4, the web type check needs an 8 GB heap, mobile Jest runs in shards, and loaded machines cause false failures.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page tells an engineer or an LLM how to check a change in the AGI Workforce monorepo (pnpm workspaces plus a Cargo workspace, run through Turborepo). It lists the command for each app, what the priority test tiers and the guard chain do, and the traps that cause false failures. Apps covered: surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:cli, surface:vscode, surface:chrome.

Status note: everything here is implementation status read from code [code]. No run was made for this page, so nothing is verified by execution.

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline is unrelated to checks, but the model catalog guard (`sync:models:check`) touches the model catalog. See the catalog file `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` (AGENTS.md section 4).

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
The verification ladder is in file:docs/development/agent-workflow.md (section 'Verification Ladder') [requirement]:

1. Run the smallest check for the owner path (the app or package you changed).
2. If you changed shared packages, schemas, crates or provider adapters, run the shared-contract checks.
3. If you changed docs, repo structure, agent context, generated files or import boundaries, run `pnpm check:llm-operability` (the guard chain).
4. Run full app suites only when the blast radius justifies it.

AGENTS.md section 12 adds: say what you ran, never report success without running it [requirement]. Stage files first, then run guards, because most guards read the working tree (`git ls-files -co`), not HEAD [requirement].

On the owner's 16 GB machine, wrap commands: heavy jobs (builds, full suites, `tsc`, cargo, dev servers, browsers, emulators, `git push`) go through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`; one test file, one package or lint on touched files goes through `scripts/dev/light-job.sh` [code] (scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh:1-4, scripts/dev/light-job.sh:1-4). The hook `.claude/hooks/heavy-job-gate.py` denies unwrapped heavy commands on machines with 24 GB or less [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, Delegation). This was seen live: a plain `grep` over package.json plus app names was blocked with 'This machine has 16 GB of RAM' [executed in this session only, not a project record].

Before a push, the pre-push hook runs the guard chain and then lint plus type-check for affected packages (see Commands).

### Hooks (husky)

- `.husky/pre-push`: runs `bash scripts/prepush-clean-worktree.sh` (a clean detached worktree at HEAD running `pnpm check:llm-operability`), or with `AGI_PREPUSH_ON_TREE=1` runs the chain on the live tree, then `turbo run lint typecheck --affected --concurrency=2` with `NODE_OPTIONS` defaulting to `--max-old-space-size=8192`, then `git diff --check`. `SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` skips it [code] (.husky/pre-push:1-20; scripts/prepush-clean-worktree.sh:1-25).
- `.husky/pre-commit` and `.husky/commit-msg` exist; their contents were not read [unknown].

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
**Priority tiers.** `scripts/run-priority-tier.mjs <token>` scans `apps/*/__tests__` for test files whose path contains the token, then runs `pnpm --filter <pkg> run test <token>` in each owning app [code] (scripts/run-priority-tier.mjs:11-65). If no app matches, it exits 1 on purpose, so a tier cannot pass while empty [code] (:34-45). AGENTS.md says only `priority-level-1` and `security` resolve [requirement]. Directories found: `apps/web/__tests__/priority-level-1`, `apps/mobile/__tests__/priority-level-1`, `apps/extension/__tests__/priority-level-1`, `apps/web/__tests__/security`, plus `security` folders inside each priority-level-1 folder [code, found by find].

**Guard chain.** `pnpm check:llm-operability` runs `scripts/run-guard-chain.mjs` with a long `&&` list of `pnpm <script>` steps (package.json:397) [code].
- Every step must match `^pnpm (--filter ...)? script$`; a repeated step or empty step throws (run-guard-chain.mjs:12-34).
- It runs four at a time by default; `AGI_GUARD_CONCURRENCY` sets 1 to 16 (run-guard-chain.mjs:23-27, 36-47).
- Four steps run alone first because they run cargo or rewrite tracked files: `check:protocol-types`, `check:cross-version-matrix`, `check:script-tests`, `check:rust-fmt` (run-guard-chain.mjs:15-20).
- A guard that fails beside others is re-run alone; it counts as green only if it then passes. The summary lists failures at the end (run-guard-chain.mjs:150-190).
- Most guards read the working tree, not HEAD. Stage first, run, then commit. `check:llm-failures:staged` reads index blobs [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- Guard names include `check:boundaries`, `check:trust-boundaries`, `check:model-id-literals`, `check:model-catalog`, `check:hardcoded-endpoints`, `check:css-tokens`, `check:secrets`, `check:db-isolation`, `check:neon-migrations`, `check:lane-ownership` (commands.json; package.json:144-295).

**Separate test-runner version in the web app.** `apps/web` and `apps/desktop` declare `vitest ^5.1.0` (apps/web/package.json:207; apps/desktop/package.json:182). The root package.json, `apps/extension` and `apps/extension-vscode` declare `^4.1.12` (package.json:469; apps/extension/package.json:72; apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1628) [code]. So the root binary is a different major. AGENTS.md says to run web tests through the package script or `pnpm exec vitest` inside apps/web, never the root binary, since mixed runs break `.rejects` [requirement]. `scripts/run-coverage.mjs` handles this by resolving each project's own vitest through `createRequire` at that project's folder (run-coverage.mjs:30-36) [code].

**Heap size for the web type check.** apps/web `typecheck` is plain `tsc --noEmit` with no heap flag (apps/web/package.json:12) [code]. AGENTS.md says it dies with SIGABRT unless `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` is set [requirement]. Where the flag is applied: CI sets it in several jobs (.github/workflows/ci.yml:283, 442, 550, 1256, 1417), `turbo.json` passes `NODE_OPTIONS` through (turbo.json:5), and pre-push defaults it (.husky/pre-push) [code]. So a bare `pnpm typecheck:all` on a laptop needs you to export it yourself [inferred].

**Loaded-machine failures.** AGENTS.md: a loaded machine fails tests that pass alone; long suites time out under browser or build work and look like assertion failures. Check `uptime` and re-run in isolation before chasing an intermittent red [requirement]. `pnpm test` limits Turbo to `--concurrency=2` (package.json:402) [code]. docs/development/troubleshooting.md also covers isolating a failing test [requirement, partly read].

**Mobile Jest.** One in-band Jest process keeps every module graph and runs out of heap, so `run-jest-shards.mjs` splits files into shards of at most 120 per process (apps/mobile/scripts/run-jest-shards.mjs:8-12, 26-30) [code]. `test:local` runs `--runInBand` and is not sharded.

**Other rules.**
- Commit subjects are lowercase conventional commits; capitalized tokens (filenames too) are rejected by commitlint [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 12).
- Never hand-edit lockfiles (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`); a hook blocks writes [requirement] (CLAUDE.md).
- New root files must be registered in `scripts/check-repo-organization.mjs` [requirement].
- `skills-lock.json` pins skill hashes; any edit fails CI until `node scripts/verify-skills-lock.mjs --regenerate` [requirement] (CLAUDE.md).
- Turbo dry runs prove task selection, not that tasks pass [requirement] (agent-workflow.md).
- Never weaken a test, lint rule or guard to make a change pass [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 9).

key_facts.fact: pnpm typecheck only checks desktop; pnpm typecheck:all runs turbo typecheck for every package.
pnpm test runs turbo test with concurrency 2; test:affected adds --affected.
Priority tiers are run by scripts/run-priority-tier.mjs, which matches a token against test file paths under apps/*/__tests__ and runs each owning app's test script with the token.
A tier that matches no tests exits 1, so an empty tier cannot pass.
Only priority-level-1 and security resolve as tiers (pnpm test:l1, pnpm test:security).
test:ci is test:l1 followed by test:coverage with a 75 percent line threshold.
The guard chain is pnpm check:llm-operability, which runs scripts/run-guard-chain.mjs over a list of pnpm scripts.
The guard chain runs 4 guards at a time by default; AGI_GUARD_CONCURRENCY accepts 1 to 16.
check:protocol-types, check:cross-version-matrix, check:script-tests and check:rust-fmt run alone before the concurrent pass.
A guard that fails beside others is re-run alone and counts as recovered only if it then passes.
Most guards read the working tree, so stage first, run guards, then commit; check:llm-failures:staged reads index blobs.
apps/web and apps/desktop use vitest ^5.1.0; the root, extension and extension-vscode use ^4.1.12.
Web tests must run through the package script or pnpm exec vitest inside apps/web, not the root binary, because mixed majors break .rejects.
apps/web typecheck is tsc --noEmit with no heap flag; it needs NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 or it aborts with SIGABRT.
CI sets NODE_OPTIONS to an 8192 MB heap in several jobs; turbo passes NODE_OPTIONS through; pre-push defaults it.
Pre-push runs the guard chain in a clean detached worktree at HEAD (or on the live tree with AGI_PREPUSH_ON_TREE=1), then turbo lint and typecheck on affected packages; SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 skips it.
Mobile tests run node tests plus Jest 29 in shards of up to 120 files per process to avoid heap exhaustion.
Loaded machines fail tests that pass alone; check uptime and re-run in isolation before chasing an intermittent failure.

Heavy local jobs go through scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh (one at a time, waits for 3 GB free by default); scoped tests and lint through light-job.sh (two slots); a hook denies unwrapped heavy commands on 24 GB or less.
CLI tests are Rust: cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib; build is cargo build --release -p agiworkforce-cli.
Desktop has Vitest unit tests, wdio and Playwright e2e, Rust lib tests, and many native GPUI test scripts.
Chrome extension is linted separately (pnpm lint:extension); pnpm lint excludes it.
Rust lint uses clippy with warnings and unsafe-code denied; dependency policy uses cargo deny.
pnpm docs:check chains doc-status, non-md-artifacts, reference-integrity, capability-preconditions and readme-facts.
Commit subjects must be lowercase conventional; lockfiles are never hand-edited.
Whether full suites pass today is not recorded in any document read.

doc.summary: The web app is a Next.js project on Vercel. Today the owner deploys it by hand with the pinned Vercel CLI; the automatic production and staging workflows exist but are disabled in GitHub. Migrations are applied by hand first, then code ships; the workflow only verifies the schema. Rollback moves code only, never the database. Signaling auto-deploys to Railway after green CI. Clients ship by tag.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page says how the AGI Workforce web app (surface:web) and its services reach production, who does it, which environments exist, in what order migrations and code go out, and what an agent must never do without the owner.

Key idea: there are two things to keep apart.

- **Implementation status** (is the code there): full workflows for staging, production, rollback and signaling exist in `.github/workflows/`.
- **Operating status** (what is switched on): `Deploy Production Surfaces` and `Deploy Staging Web` are disabled in GitHub, so production web is deployed by hand. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md:8-15), (docs/architecture/release-architecture.md:18-30). I could not read GitHub's live workflow state from the repo, so 'disabled' is a documented claim, not something I verified. [unknown]

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline is unrelated to deploys; no other deploy page id was provided.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
### A. What production does today (manual path)

1. Code is on `main` and CI is green for that exact commit. The required workflows are `CI`, `CodeQL analysis`, `Priority Level 1 tests`, `Security scanning`; the list is owned by `scripts/config/deploy-gates.json` (releaseReadiness.workflows). [code] (scripts/config/deploy-gates.json)
2. The owner (or an agent the owner told, in that message) takes a Neon backup branch of production, then applies pending migrations: `pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target production --confirm-production`. Then records the applied-through number in `scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json`. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:30-41)
3. Only then build, probe and promote the code, using the pinned Vercel CLI from a clean worktree. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md:8-11)
4. Check `api:GET /api/version`, which reports the commit and migration state served. [code] (apps/web/app/api/version/route.ts:1-14)

The recorded state in the repo: migrations applied through 425, recorded 2026-11-21, ledger commit 57bf292f5d. [code] (scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json)

### B. What the disabled workflow does when enabled

`deploy-staging.yml` and `deploy-production.yml` both trigger on a completed `CI` run (`workflow_run`). Production only accepts a run that succeeded, was a push, on `main`, from this repository. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:3-6,114-121)

Order:

1. Staging first: applies pending migrations to the persistent staging database (`pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target staging`), deploys a preview-environment build, verifies it, records a `staging-web` commit status. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:145,185)
2. Production `scope` job picks affected surfaces. `staging-gate` waits (up to 25 min per doc) for the staging verdict on the same commit. `release-gate` requires green scanning and a verified signaling relay. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:114,188,235)
3. `deploy-web` (environment `production-web`): check Vercel contract, reconcile env, run `pnpm db:migrate -- verify` (no mutation), pull settings, record the serving deployment, build, deploy prebuilt artifact, canary on its own URL, promote to the production domains, verify the serving path, run `pnpm db:migrate -- record --surface web`. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:258-514)
4. If a step fails after deploy, a step runs `vercel rollback` to the previously serving deployment. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:514-523)
5. `deploy-sandbox` deploys the separate artifact-sandbox origin and checks its isolation headers. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:600-737)
6. A daily `production-drift` job (07:00 UTC) fails if production does not serve `main` HEAD. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:11-12,46-86)

The workflow never applies a production migration. It only verifies the ledger and records state. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:32-35); [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:329 is `verify`, 511 is `record`; no `apply` for production)

### C. Signaling server (services/signaling-server)

`Deploy Signaling Server` is active. After a green push CI on `main` it tests, builds a container to GHCR and deploys to Railway (`deploy-railway`, environment `production-railway`). The Fly.io job (`deploy-fly`) runs only on manual `workflow_dispatch` with `deploy_target` fly or both. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-signaling-server.yml:14-17,224-243,292-309). The web release gate requires a verified relay (`production-relay` context from the Fly job). [code] (scripts/config/deploy-gates.json releaseReadiness.relay)

### D. Background workers

No separate worker deployable. Every scheduled job is a cron route in the one Next.js service, scheduled in `vercel.json` `crons` (about 47 entries). Each is registered in `apps/web/app/api/cron/deployable-components.json`, and a test in CI fails on an unregistered route. [code] (vercel.json), [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md:131-153)

### E. Client apps

Released by tag, independently of web, and cannot be rolled back (only a new version). Tags: CLI `v-cli-*`, public Desktop (Electron) `v-cloud-desktop-*`, retained Tauri `v-desktop-*` (workflow disabled), mobile `v-mobile-*`, VS Code `v-vscode-*`, Chrome `v-ext-*`. [requirement] (docs/architecture/release-architecture.md:34-46). Workflow files exist for each. [code] (.github/workflows/release-*.yml)

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
**Never without the owner saying so in that message** [requirement] (memory deploy-and-release, owner instruction; AGENTS.md §9 for irreversible actions):

- Deploy to production or staging (Vercel CLI, workflow dispatch, rollback).
- Apply a production migration. The runner needs `--confirm-production`.
- Deploy or change Fly or the relay. Owner instruction: no Fly or relay deploy until told. [requirement] (owner memory no-fly-until-told). Note the web release gate wants a verified relay, so this can block an enabled production workflow. [inferred] from deploy-gates.json.
- Push with `SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` without disclosing it. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md)
- Hand-edit lockfiles or edit an applied migration. [requirement] (AGENTS.md §5, §12)

**Traps**

1. The workflows being present does not mean they run. They are disabled; production is manual. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md:8-15)
2. Migrations first, then code. Code reading a column not yet applied breaks routes; rollback does not undo a migration. `check:migration-dependencies` and `scripts/config/migration-dependency-allowlist.json` guard this. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:43-48)
3. Database is never rolled back. Forward-fix with a new numbered migration; destructive changes are a two-release sequence. [requirement] (docs/architecture/release-architecture.md:106-118,230-235)
4. Rollback picks the newest READY deployment created before the serving one, not simply the newest READY. A rollback reason is required. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:61-65)
5. `scripts/config/rollback-floor.json` is `{"web": null}` now, so no floor is enforced. [code]
6. The daily drift alarm stays red after a rollback by design. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:111-114)
7. Production concurrency group is `production-surfaces` with no cancel, so a cancelled run cannot skip the rollback step. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:28-34)
8. Staging is a preview build in the same Vercel project with its own Neon database, never a branch of production, and its own Clerk dev keys, Stripe test keys and Redis. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is Production only. Do not mark `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values Sensitive. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md). Nothing in the migrate tool checks that the staging database is not production. [requirement] (same file)
9. A commit trailer `Deployment: hold` runs CI but blocks automatic deploys. Unknown directives fail closed. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md); implemented in `scripts/production-deploy-scope.mjs --automatic-deployment` [requirement]
10. There is no path that skips CI; a hotfix is a normal commit. Emergency levers are rollback, feature kill switches (`/api/admin/feature-flags/kill-switches`), or the laptop rollback script. [requirement] (docs/architecture/release-architecture.md:189-204)
11. Build must happen before migrating (owner memory), so the migration is not applied for code that does not build. [requirement] (owner memory deploy-and-release)
12. Vercel author-email block: a commit whose author email Vercel does not accept can be refused; the owner's memory records a fix. Details [unknown] from the repo.
13. `vercel-ignore-build.sh` skips builds for docs, `.github`, other apps, `crates`, `services` etc. and fails open. It only matters if Git deployments are on, and `git.deploymentEnabled` is false. [code] (vercel-ignore-build.sh, vercel.json)
14. Web-only coupling: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so a web deploy changes Desktop's renderer at once; mobile and extensions are older than the server for as long as users do not update. [requirement] (AGENTS.md §5; docs/architecture/release-architecture.md:130-139)
15. Mobile rollback levers: server rollback, kill switch, version disable, `expo-updates` OTA, new store binary, raising minimum contract version (mobile does not show the update message; recorded gap). [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:149-171)
16. Secrets live in GitHub environments (`production-web`, `staging-web`, `production-railway`) and Vercel; none in the repo. Names: `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`, `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET`, `AGI_DATABASE_URL`, `AGI_STAGING_DATABASE_URL`, `PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL`. Environment protection rules from `.github/rulesets/environments.json` may not be applied. [requirement] (docs/development/ci-and-deploys.md)

sections.markdown:

key_facts.fact: Production web is deployed manually with the pinned Vercel CLI from a clean worktree; the production and staging workflows exist but are disabled in GitHub.
vercel.json sets git.deploymentEnabled to false, so no push or merge deploys through the Vercel Git integration.
Hosting is Vercel (Next.js framework, output apps/web/.next, build via apps/web/scripts/build-with-chat.sh, pnpm pinned in install and build commands).
Scheduled background jobs are Vercel crons hitting /api/cron/* routes inside the one Next.js service; there is no separate worker deployable or broker.
Production deploy workflow triggers on a completed CI run and runs jobs only for a successful, push-triggered, main-branch, same-repository run, deploying the exact head_sha.
The production workflow never applies migrations to production; it runs 'db:migrate -- verify' before deploy and 'db:migrate -- record' after.
Manual production order is: Neon backup branch, apply migrations with --confirm-production, record applied-through number, then build, probe and promote code.
The migration runner refuses production mutation without --confirm-production and accepts targets local, ci, branch, staging, production.
Recorded production migration state: applied through 425 on 2026-11-21 at ledger commit 57bf292f5d; latest migration file is 0425_adult_eligibility.sql.
Staging workflow applies migrations to a persistent separate staging database, deploys a preview build, verifies it and publishes a staging-web commit status that production waits for.

Production deploy canaries the new deployment on its own URL before promoting to production domains, then verifies the serving path; a failure after deploy triggers vercel rollback to the previously serving deployment.
Rollback is a workflow_dispatch with rollback true and a required reason, or node scripts/release/rollback.mjs from a laptop; it reverts code only, never the database.
The rollback floor file is currently {"web": null}, so no oldest-allowed deployment is enforced.
Production concurrency group production-surfaces does not cancel in progress, so a cancelled run cannot skip the rollback step.
A daily production-drift job at 07:00 UTC fails if production does not serve main HEAD; it does not run while the workflow is disabled.
Signaling server auto-deploys to Railway after green CI on main; Fly.io deploy runs only on manual dispatch (deploy_target fly or both); the workflow is active.
The web release gate requires a verified relay (production-relay context from the Fly job) in addition to green scanning and zero open alerts.
A Deployment: hold git trailer lets CI run but blocks automatic staging, production and signaling deploys; unsupported directives fail closed.
Required status gates for a production mutation are CI, CodeQL analysis, Priority Level 1 tests and Security scanning on the exact commit.
Client apps (CLI, Desktop Electron, mobile, VS Code, Chrome) are released by their own tags and cannot be rolled back; the only remedy is a new version, a kill switch or a version disable.
The release audit trail is table public.release_events (migration 0263), append-only and hash-chained, readable at /admin/releases and GET /api/admin/releases.
api:GET /api/version reports the serving commit, deployment id, environment, region, migration state and a model registry digest.
Per owner instruction, nothing is deployed unless the owner says so in that message, and no Fly or relay deploy happens until told.
evidence: owner memory files deploy-and-release.md and no-fly-until-told.md (not in repo)

key_facts.fact: vercel-ignore-build.sh skips builds when only docs, .github, other apps, crates, services or similar change, and builds on any doubt.
Pre-push hook runs the guard chain and affected lint and typecheck in a detached clean worktree of HEAD; SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 is emergency only and must be disclosed.
A separate artifact-sandbox origin is deployed by the same production workflow (deploy-sandbox) and its isolation headers are checked after promotion.

doc.summary: placeholder

Web database changes are numbered SQL files in apps/web/db/neon, applied by scripts/neon-migrate.mjs. Each file is checksummed (SHA-256) into a ledger table; an edited applied file is drift and blocks deploys. Guards check naming, destructive statements, expand/contract, transactions, grants and down files. CI applies to empty databases and staging; production is applied by hand with --confirm-production, and the deploy workflow only verifies.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
The Web app (surface:web) keeps its Postgres schema on Neon. Every schema change is a numbered SQL file in `apps/web/db/neon/`. This page says how to write one, check it, apply it, and what is different in production. Desktop (Electron) loads the hosted web app, so it shares this database; the other apps reach it only through web APIs. [code] (AGENTS.md section 5; scripts/lib/neon-migrations.mjs:8)

Implementation status: the runner, guards, CI steps and workflows exist and are wired [code]. Verification status: no document in the repo records a run by me; I ran nothing. Recorded production state is `appliedThrough: 425` dated 2026-11-21 [code] (scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json:3). The newest file is `0425_adult_eligibility.sql` [code] (directory listing).

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
**Write a migration**
1. Take the next number. Files must be named `NNNN_lower_snake_case.sql` and numbers must be contiguous from 0001 with no gaps; the loader throws otherwise. [code] (scripts/lib/neon-migrations.mjs:13, 62-70)
2. Do not add `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` yourself unless one block wraps the whole file. The runner wraps each file in one transaction with `lock_timeout 10s` and `statement_timeout 120s`. [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:181-185; scripts/check-neon-migrations.mjs:537-575)
3. Make the change in two steps (expand, then contract). The guard refuses a column rename, a table rename, `ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL` with no default on an existing table, and adding and dropping columns on one table in one file. [code] (check-neon-migrations.mjs:~385-440)
4. If the file drops, truncates, deletes rows, retypes a column, sets NOT NULL on an existing table, or drops a policy/constraint/function/index it does not re-create, add a comment line `-- destructive: <why>`. A marker on a file that is not destructive is also an error. [code] (check-neon-migrations.mjs:~296-345)
5. Do not use `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public`; only 0037 may. Grant table by table. [code] (check-neon-migrations.mjs:~440-455)
6. New tables start with full rights for role `app_rls` (0037 default privileges). The privileges guard requires each new table above the applied watermark to name every privilege `app_rls` ends up with, and to have row-level security plus a policy, or a reason in `scripts/config/migration-table-privileges.json`. [code] (scripts/check-migration-table-privileges.mjs:1-45)
7. From 0097 on, add `down/<same name>.down.sql`: begin/commit, undo every object the up file touches, and end with `delete from public.schema_migrations where filename = '<up file>'`. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/down/README.md; check-neon-migrations.mjs:12, 140-215)
8. If web code reads the new table or column, the dependency guard fails until `scripts/config/migration-dependency-allowlist.json` names the file and migration number. [code] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:43-46; scripts/check-migration-dependencies.mjs)

**Check:** run `pnpm check:neon-migrations`, `pnpm check:migration-dependencies`, `pnpm check:migration-table-privileges`, then `pnpm db:migrate -- inventory`.

**Apply locally:** export `AGI_DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL` or `NEON_DATABASE_URL`) for a local database, then `pnpm db:migrate -- apply`. A localhost host infers target `local`. [code] (scripts/neon-migrate.mjs:86-120)

**Apply to production (by hand):** take a Neon backup branch, run `pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target production --confirm-production`, record the new number in `scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json`, only then build and promote code. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:30-48)

**Fix a mistake in an applied file:** never edit it. Add a new migration. Prose corrections go in `apps/web/db/neon/CORRECTIONS.md`. [requirement] (CORRECTIONS.md:1-12)

sections.heading: Commands
sections.markdown:
| Command | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm db:migrate -- inventory` | Counts files and prints first and latest. No database needed. | [code] (scripts/neon-migrate.mjs:196-207) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- status` (default) | Prints applied, pending, drift counts. Read only. `--json` available. | [code] (neon-migrate.mjs:241) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target T` | Takes a session advisory lock, creates the ledger if missing, refuses on drift, applies each pending file in its own transaction and inserts a ledger row in that transaction. | [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:172-218) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- verify` | Fails on drift or any pending migration. No writes to the ledger. | [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:314-324) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- record --surface web\|gateway --commit SHA --target T` | Runs verify, then upserts a row in `schema_migration_deployments` (head file, checksum, applied count, ledger digest). | [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:372-417) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- deployments` | Lists recent deployment records (default limit 20). | [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:18; neon-migrate.mjs:260) |
| `pnpm db:migrate -- baseline --through N --reason --evidence --target branch\|production --confirm-baseline` | Marks files 1..N as applied without running them, only if the ledger is empty and every table those files create exists. | [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:259-312) |

Targets in the code are `local, ci, branch, staging, production`. `apply` and `baseline` swap a Neon `-pooler` host for the direct host, because a pooled connection cannot hold the advisory lock. [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:16; neon-migrate.mjs:31, 86-100)

Guards (root package.json): `check:neon-migrations` (also runs the runner's unit tests), `check:migration-dependencies`, `check:migration-table-privileges`, `test:db-migrate`. `check:neon-migrations` and the other two are inside `check:llm-operability`. [code] (package.json:201, 206, 209, 359-360, 397)

CI: the database job runs `test:db-migrate`, then `apply --target ci` twice (second run proves a re-run does nothing), then `verify`, then RLS and lease probes. [code] (.github/workflows/ci.yml:205-211)

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
- **The checksum chain.** Each file's SHA-256 is stored in `public.schema_migrations` (sequence, filename, checksum, mode apply or baseline). Drift means a changed filename, a changed checksum, an unknown ledger row, or a gap before an applied one. Any drift makes `apply`, `verify` and `record` throw. [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:74-115, 160-164)
- **A comment edit changes the checksum.** On 2026-08-24 a comment-only edit to 0087 blocked a deploy with nine migrations queued; the file was restored. [requirement] (apps/web/db/neon/CORRECTIONS.md)
- **Second checksum list.** `scripts/config/applied-migration-checksums.json` records the checksum of every file up to the applied watermark, so the dependency guard reports `changed after it was applied` before any database is touched. [code] (check-migration-dependencies.mjs:95-110)
- **Frozen waivers.** `UNMARKED_DESTRUCTIVE_BASELINE` (34 old files) and `STAGED_COMMIT_BASELINE` (0182, 0243, 0281) may shrink, never grow. [code] (check-neon-migrations.mjs:~300, 522-535)
- **Production is never migrated by the deploy workflow.** It runs `verify` before building and `record --target production --confirm-production` after deploy. A pending migration therefore blocks the deploy. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:329, 511-512; docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:32-35)
- **Staging is migrated by workflow:** `apply --target staging` against the persistent staging database, so a migration meets real rows before production. [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:145)
- **Production needs `--confirm-production`;** `--target local` refuses a non-local host; baseline is only for branch or production. [code] (neon-migrate.mjs:107-120, 223-233)
- **Failure is rolled back.** A failing file rolls back its own transaction, so no partial schema and no ledger row. Files already applied in the same run stay applied. [code] (neon-migrations.mjs:179-212)
- **Down files restore the schema, never the rows.** Older than 0097 there is no reversal; undoing means a restore. The app does not run down files; the README describes the manual procedure. [code] (down/README.md; check-neon-migrations.mjs:12)
- **Non-transactional statements** (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `VACUUM`, `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`) cannot sit in the runner's transaction; only down files may declare `-- non-transactional:`. [inferred] from check-neon-migrations.mjs:~100 and the runner's single transaction (neon-migrations.mjs:181)
- **Test against real Postgres.** Unit tests mock the adapter; `apps/web/db/neon/verify/README.md` gives a Docker recipe that applies each file in its own transaction, as the runner does. [requirement]
- **Recovery:** Neon point-in-time branch is the restore mechanism, no scheduled `pg_dump`. After a restore, run `status` on the restored branch; a recovery point older than the newest migration shows a gap, and you decide whether to apply forward. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/database-backup-restore.md:7, 97-102)
- **Policy:** do not add `middleware.ts`-style shortcuts; `apps/web/db/neon` is append-only and checksummed; production apply needs `--confirm-production`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5)

key_facts.fact: Migrations are plain SQL files in apps/web/db/neon named NNNN_lower_snake_case.sql, contiguous from 0001; the newest is 0425_adult_eligibility.sql.
The runner is pnpm db:migrate, which runs scripts/neon-migrate.mjs; commands are inventory, status, apply, verify, baseline, record, deployments.
Each migration's SHA-256 checksum is stored in public.schema_migrations; any mismatch, renamed file, unknown row or gap is drift and stops apply, verify and record.
Each pending file runs in its own transaction with lock_timeout 10s and statement_timeout 120s, and its ledger row is inserted in that same transaction.
apply and baseline hold a session advisory lock and rewrite a Neon -pooler host to the direct host.
Mutating commands need --target (or AGI_MIGRATION_TARGET); production needs --confirm-production; local refuses a non-local host.
Connection string precedence is AGI_DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL, NEON_DATABASE_URL; the runner never prints it.
Valid targets are local, ci, branch, staging, production, but the help text omits staging.
The production deploy workflow only runs verify before the build and record after deploy; it never applies a migration to production.
Staging applies pending migrations automatically against a persistent staging database before deploy.
CI applies the chain to an empty database twice (idempotence), then verifies and runs RLS and lease probes.
Recorded production watermark is appliedThrough 425, recorded 2026-11-21 at commit 57bf292f5d.
A destructive statement needs a '-- destructive: <why>' comment; 34 older files are frozen in UNMARKED_DESTRUCTIVE_BASELINE.
Expand/contract is enforced: column or table rename, NOT NULL without default on an existing table, and add+drop column on one table in one file are errors.
Files from 0097 on require a down file that begins with BEGIN, ends with COMMIT, undoes every object, and deletes its ledger row; 329 down files exist.
Only 0182, 0243 and 0281 may commit in stages; all other files must be one atomic block or have no transaction control.
GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public is forbidden except in 0037; new tables must name every app_rls privilege and have RLS plus a policy.
A second checksum list, applied-migration-checksums.json, lets check:migration-dependencies fail an edited applied file without a database.
Web code that reads a table or column from an unapplied migration needs an entry in migration-dependency-allowlist.json (currently empty).
Editing 0087 by comment only in 2026-08 caused drift that blocked a deploy; corrections to applied files go in CORRECTIONS.md.
record writes public.schema_migration_deployments, unique per (surface, target, commit_sha), surfaces web and gateway.
baseline needs an empty ledger, --through N, --reason, --evidence, --confirm-baseline, and every table those files create must already exist.
Restore uses Neon point-in-time branches; there is no scheduled pg_dump; after restoring, run migrate status to see gaps.
Manual production deploy order: backup branch, apply with --confirm-production, update the watermark file, then build and promote code.
A rollback of code does not undo a migration.
Real execution of any migration command by this author: none; no run is recorded in the repo for this page.

evidence: AGENTS.md section 5: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app
no plan or entitlement logic appears in the runner or guards (scripts/neon-migrate.mjs)

Is production-migrations-applied.json updated by a script or by hand after each apply? The runbook only says to record it.
Which Neon history retention window does production use? The runbook says the repo does not record it.
Do non-web surfaces (gateway) have their own migrations? DEPLOYMENT_SURFACES lists gateway, but I found no separate chain.

doc.summary: Monitoring covers the web app only in depth. Production emits structured pino logs with trace and request ids, OpenTelemetry metrics and spans, and optional Sentry errors. Vercel crons probe health every 10 minutes and burn-rate alerts every 30. Alerts go through one dispatcher by email, pager and channel. Read a request by its x-request-id. Desktop, mobile, CLI and extension have only crash or error reporting.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page says what the AGI Workforce platform watches, where each signal lands, and how to follow one production request through logs and traces. Almost all of it lives in `surface:web` (the Next.js app in `apps/web`), which also serves the Desktop window and backs the phone, CLI and extensions.

**Implementation status vs verification status.** Everything below that is tagged [code] is present in the repository. None of it is recorded as executed against production in any document I read. The incident runbook describes an alert drill but records no result of one [unknown]. Capacity numbers are all marked unmeasured in `docs/runbooks/capacity-and-load-testing.md` [requirement].

### The signals at a glance

| Signal | What it is | Where it lands | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Structured logs | JSON lines from pino, with `trace_id`, `span_id`, `request_id`, `user_id`, `organization_id`, plus `service`, `version`, `region`, `deploy_env` | Process stdout, which the host (Vercel) collects | [code] (apps/web/lib/logger.ts:55-83; apps/web/lib/observability/trace-context.ts:93-102) |
| Span log lines | One `span` log line per HTTP request with duration, status, method, path | Same log stream | [code] (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:~320, the `logger.info({event:'span'...})` call) |
| Metrics | OpenTelemetry counters, histograms and gauges named `agi.*`, `http.server.*`, `db.client.*` | OTLP collector, only when `AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT` is set | [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/metrics.ts:17-62; otel-config.ts:15-17) |
| Traces | Spans bridged to OpenTelemetry, exported to the collector and to Sentry | Collector and Sentry, tail-kept (errors, slow spans, or a sampled ratio) | [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/trace-sampling.ts:25-31; instrumentation.ts) |
| Errors | Sentry events, with release, environment and organization tag | Sentry, only in a production build with a DSN | [code] (apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts:19-25) |
| Health | `/api/health` and `/status`, same checks | Public, on request | [code] (apps/web/app/api/health/route.ts) |
| Alerts | Probe, SLO burn, security anomaly, credit and quota crons | Email, pager webhook, incident channel webhook | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts) and [requirement] (docs/runbooks/incident-response.md) |
| Domain events | Durable, immutable business events (audit log, SIEM feed, read models) | Database audit trail and listed consumers | [requirement] (docs/standards/domain-events.md) |
| Client failures | Counted failure classes from the browser, no content | `api:POST /api/telemetry/client`, which records a metric | [code] (apps/web/app/api/telemetry/client/route.ts) |

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
### A. Read one production request (web)

1. **Get the request id.** Every API route wrapped in `withErrorHandler` sets response headers `x-request-id` and `traceparent` [code] (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:344-346). The header name is `x-request-id` [code] (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/header-names.ts:11). A caller may send its own id. It is kept only if `isWellFormedRequestId` accepts it. Otherwise the server uses the 32-hex trace id [code] (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:246-250).
2. **Search the logs for it.** Every log line written inside the request carries `request_id` and `trace_id` through the pino `mixin` [code] (apps/web/lib/logger.ts:50; trace-context.ts:93-102). Filter the host's function logs by `request_id`.
3. **Find the span line.** Look for the line with `event: "span"`, `span_name` of the HTTP server span, `duration_ms`, `status` and `http.response.status_code` [code] (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts, span log call). Its `parent_span_id` is the caller's span if a `traceparent` came in.
4. **Open the trace** in Sentry by `trace_id`, or in the OTLP backend, if either is configured. If neither is configured, the logs are the only record [inferred] from the opt-in config above.
5. **Check the release.** Log lines carry `version` (commit SHA), `region` and `deploy_env` [code] (apps/web/lib/logger.ts:36-46). Sentry events carry release and environment from the same variables [code] (apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts:42-63).

**Reading Vercel request logs from outside the dashboard.** The owner's working notes describe an HTTP call to the Vercel request-logs API with a CLI token, 50 rows per call, filtered by `requestPath` [unknown to the repo]. No document in the repository states this. Only the private memory note does, so treat it as unverified here.

### B. Follow a request across a queue

When work is handed to a background job, the trace carrier holds `traceparent` and the request id so the worker log line joins the original request [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/trace-propagation.ts:10-58).

### C. React to an alert

1. An alert mail, pager call or channel post arrives from `apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts` [code].
2. Match the subject to the triage section in `docs/runbooks/incident-response.md` (database, cache, search, vector, environment, stripe, probe_failed, credit settlement drift) [requirement].
3. For a cache fault, read the log line `Cache health check failed`. For Stripe, read `Stripe health check failed` and its `step` field [requirement] (incident-response.md triage sections).
4. If the cause is the release, roll back first (`docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md`).
5. Before calling a data incident resolved, run each reconciler cron that applies and require a non-500 answer [requirement] (incident-response.md, Data integrity section).

### D. Check live status without logs

- `/status` shows the same checks to a signed-out person [code] (apps/web/app/status/page.tsx).
- `/operator` has tabs `services`, `dashboards`, `routing`, `jobs` and `costs` for platform operators [requirement] (docs/runbooks/admin-surfaces.md, section on `/operator`). The dashboard panels come from `SERVICE_DASHBOARDS` [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/dashboards.ts:33).
- `api:GET /api/admin/observability` returns route and cache breakdowns by `route`, `model`, `user` or `tenant` for a platform admin [code] (apps/web/app/api/admin/observability/route.ts:10-45).

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
### Logging

- **Deployed log level has a floor of `info`.** `LOG_LEVEL=debug` or `trace` is ignored outside development, because those levels carry bodies and prompts that redaction only masks by key [code] (apps/web/lib/logger.ts:19-33). So you cannot turn on debug logs in production to chase a bug.
- **Logs are redacted twice.** String arguments pass through `redactSecrets`, and the record passes through `redactLogRecord` [code] (apps/web/lib/logger.ts:55-66). Field names such as `prompt`, `body`, `email`, `token`, `payload`, `text`, `query` are denied by final segment [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/log-field-policy.ts:6-35). Do not look for prompts or message text in logs. They are deliberately absent.
- **Health messages are scrubbed on purpose.** The public `/api/health` answers `unavailable` for a failed check and counts what it cannot name, so the payload shows no host, key or vendor text. The reason is only in the log line [code] (apps/web/app/api/health/route.ts:24-45) and [requirement] (incident-response.md, cache triage).
- **Only web routes wrapped in `withErrorHandler` get the request id header and the span line.** A route that does not use it has neither [inferred] from apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts.

### Tracing and metrics

- **No collector, no export.** With `AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT` unset, no SDK starts and no span leaves the process. The pino span lines are unchanged [code] (apps/web/.env.example:~730 comment; otel-config.ts:resolveOtelExportConfig returns null).
- **Sentry runs only in production builds with a DSN.** Preview builds also have `NODE_ENV=production`, so the environment tag comes from `VERCEL_ENV` first [code] (apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts:22-25,52-63).
- **Tail sampling.** Errored spans and spans at or above the slow threshold (default 1000 ms, `AGI_OTEL_SLOW_SPAN_MS`) are always kept. The rest are kept by trace-id ratio (`AGI_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO`) [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/trace-sampling.ts).
- **Metric labels are bounded.** `boundAttributes` caps cardinality, and request labels use closed sets (surface, client version, API version, else `unknown` or `unsupported`) [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/request-labels.ts; cardinality.ts).
- **Metric names are restated in two files** for media, and a test fails if they differ [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/metrics.ts comment; test:apps/web/lib/observability/metrics.media-names.test.ts).

### Alerting

- **Detection latency is up to 20 minutes.** The probe runs every 10 minutes and pages only on the second consecutive miss [requirement] (incident-response.md) and [code] (apps/web/app/api/cron/health-probe/route.ts:~20-25, `CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES_BEFORE_PAGE = 2`).
- **An undelivered alert is an HTTP 500.** When no channel reached anyone, the probe returns 500 so the Vercel cron log shows it [requirement] (incident-response.md). Check the cron log after any env var change.
- **Email needs both `RESEND_API_KEY` and a valid `AGI_SUPPORT_FROM_EMAIL`.** Pager needs `PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL`. Channel needs `INCIDENT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL` [requirement] (incident-response.md).
- **Escalation level lives in the key-value store** under `agi-incident:<key>` for six hours. With no store, every alert is level 1 [requirement].
- **Degraded is not unhealthy.** Stripe or retrieval outages are `WARNING`/`degraded`. Database, cache, `probe_failed` are `CRITICAL` [requirement] (incident-response.md, Severity table).
- **Low-power mode delays crons.** With `AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1`, crons that run more than once an hour do work only in the first 15 UTC minutes of each hour and otherwise answer `{"skipped":"db_low_power"}`. The health probe calls this skip, so in that mode probing is hourly, not every 10 minutes [code] (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:5-19; health-probe/route.ts:196-197) and [requirement] (capacity-and-load-testing.md). The `.env.example` default is `0` [code] (apps/web/.env.example:31). Whether production has it on is [unknown].
- **SLO alerts stay silent under 20 samples.** Fast burn: 1 hour window, rate 14.4, critical. Slow burn: 6 hour window, rate 6, warning [code] (apps/web/lib/server/slo/attainment.ts:211-215). Objectives exist only in `apps/web/lib/server/slo/catalogue.ts`. Some objectives have no source yet and say what instrument is missing [code] (catalogue.ts:SloDefinition.missingInstrument).
- **SLO analytics need consent.** Some indicators read `product_analytics_events`, so accounts that refused the analytics purpose are absent [code] (catalogue.ts:ANALYTICS_COVERAGE). Client failure ingest also needs telemetry consent [code] (apps/web/lib/observability/client-failure-transport.ts:29-31; telemetry/client/route.ts imports readServerTelemetryConsent).
- **No global backpressure and no database-pool alert.** Saturation first shows as latency [requirement] (capacity-and-load-testing.md).

### Other apps

| Surface | What is monitored | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface:cli | Opt-in crash reports with a release DSN baked at build time (`AGI_CLI_SENTRY_DSN`), disabled unless privacy mode is Managed, controlled by `AGI_CRASH_REPORTS` or config; reports hold version, OS, arch, panic location | [code] (apps/cli/src/crash_reports.rs:14-47) |
| surface:chrome | Error reporting client over a Sentry fetch adapter, gated on a consent snapshot, DSN from `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` | [code] (apps/extension/src/features/observability/errorReporting.ts:1-26) |
| surface:desktop | A telemetry service with a closed list of domains, `DESKTOP_TELEMETRY_DOMAINS`, emitted through `recordDesktopEvent` | [code] (scripts/check-desktop-telemetry-domains.mjs:14-18). The public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so web monitoring covers its server calls [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5) |
| surface:mobile | Not established. I found no Sentry or crash module under apps/mobile/lib or services | [unknown] |
| surface:vscode | Not examined; the web request labels treat `vscode` as a surface | [code] (request-labels.ts:VSCODE_SURFACE); monitoring itself [unknown] |

Local mode (`mode:local`) work stays on the device, so server logs do not see it. Server monitoring sees `mode:cloud` traffic, and `mode:own-key` traffic only where it goes through our servers [inferred].

sections.heading: Gaps in the documents
sections.markdown:
- **No document teaches reading production logs.** The incident runbook names log lines and the Vercel cron log but gives no command, no log-query recipe and no field list. This page rebuilds it from code. The Vercel request-logs API recipe exists only in private owner notes, not in the repository [unknown].
- **No document describes the request id contract.** `x-request-id`, how a caller's id is accepted and how it joins logs are only in code (`error-handler.ts`, `trace-context.ts`).
- **No document lists the `agi.*` metrics or says where they are viewed.** Which backend receives OTLP in production is not in the repository [unknown]. Whether Sentry or a collector is configured in production is [unknown].
- **The incident runbook table lists five detectors, but more crons exist.** Examples are `drain-background-jobs`, `reap-agent-runs`, `evaluate-model-rollout` and `recover-reservations` in `vercel.json`. They are mentioned in the reconciler table only in part.
- **Mobile and VS Code monitoring are undocumented** and I did not find code for mobile [unknown].
- **No recorded run of the alert drill, load tests or SLO alert** appears in `docs/research/` that I read [unknown].
- **Database pool saturation, CPU, memory, object storage and CDN have no alert in the repository** [requirement] (capacity-and-load-testing.md).
- **`docs/standards/domain-events.md` is about durable events, not operational monitoring.** It does not say how an event relates to logs or traces. Its table has 29 event rows [code] by my count of the table (39 matches for lines starting with a backtick include other tables, so I did not use that figure).

key_facts.fact: Web logs are pino JSON lines carrying trace_id, span_id, request_id, user_id, organization_id, plus service, version (commit SHA), region and deploy_env.
A deployed runtime refuses log levels below info, so LOG_LEVEL=debug or trace has no effect in production.
Log records and string args are redacted; field names such as prompt, body, email, token, payload, text and query are denied.
The request id header is x-request-id. A caller's id is honored only if well formed, else the server uses the trace id.
Routes wrapped in withErrorHandler return x-request-id and traceparent headers and write one span log line per request with duration, status, method and path.
OpenTelemetry export is off unless AGI_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT is set to a valid URL; related names are AGI_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, AGI_OTEL_HEADERS, AGI_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO, AGI_OTEL_SLOW_SPAN_MS.
Trace export keeps every errored span and every span at or above the slow threshold (default 1000 ms), and the rest by trace-id ratio.
Sentry is on only when NODE_ENV is production and a DSN is set; environment tag prefers VERCEL_ENV; release is the commit SHA.
Metric instruments are named under agi.*, http.server.request.*, db.client.operation.*; turn metrics include time to first token, duration, cost and retries.
vercel.json defines 47 cron jobs; health-probe runs every 10 minutes and evaluate-slo-burn at :05 and :35.
The health probe pages only after 2 consecutive failing runs, runs the same checks directly (no self-HTTP call), times out at 8 seconds, and returns HTTP 500 when no channel reached a human.
All alerts go through apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts to email (Resend), a pager webhook (PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL) and an incident channel webhook (INCIDENT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL).
On-call rotation is configuration: AGI_ONCALL_ROTATION, AGI_ONCALL_ROTATION_START, AGI_ONCALL_SHIFT_HOURS (default 168), AGI_ONCALL_ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES (default 15).
SLO burn alerts use a fast window (1 h, rate 14.4, critical) and a slow window (6 h, rate 6, warning) and stay silent under 20 samples.
Service level objectives are stated only in apps/web/lib/server/slo/catalogue.ts; some have no source and name the missing instrument.
Public /api/health reduces failed-check text to 'unavailable' and counts dependencies; detail is only in the server log line.
AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1 restricts multi-per-hour crons, including the health probe, to the first 15 UTC minutes of each hour; .env.example default is 0; production value unknown.
All capacity dimensions are marked unmeasured; no capacity figure is proven.
Client failure classes are ingested at POST /api/telemetry/client with a strict schema (no free text), CSRF, a rate limit and a consent check.
Platform admins can read route and cache breakdowns by route, model, user or tenant at GET /api/admin/observability.
The /operator page has tabs services, dashboards, routing, jobs, costs among eighteen.
CLI crash reports are opt-in, disabled unless privacy mode is Managed, and use a release DSN baked at build time.
The Chrome extension reports errors through a Sentry fetch adapter gated on a consent snapshot.

Domain events are durable immutable records with correlationId and causationId, retention and data class set by the catalogue, and a closed list of consumers (audit-log, siem-export, product-analytics, notifications, read-model).
Trace context and request id are carried into queued jobs so a worker log line joins the original request.
Cron routes authenticate with CRON_SECRET (minimum 32 characters) and answer 401 when absent.
Guards check logging hygiene: check:log-redaction, check:llm-log-hygiene and check:desktop-telemetry-domains are in the guard chain.

doc.summary: Troubleshooting map for AGI Workforce: how a failure becomes the words a user sees (error codes, provider failure classes, quota blocks), then symptom, likely cause, where to look and fix for sign-in, plan limits, provider errors, uploads, sync and local models. Built from code. No failure was reproduced, and several flows have open register rows.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
Use this page to go from a symptom to a cause, a file and a fix without exploring the repository again. It serves developers and support.

**Basis note.** Everything below is [code] unless tagged. Nothing here was run by me. Implementation status (the code exists and is wired) is kept apart from verification status (someone ran it). Many register rows say 'source-corrected, runtime acceptance open'. That means the code was changed but nobody has seen it work live.

**How a failure reaches a person (four layers).**

1. **API error envelope.** Web routes throw an `AppError`. `handleError` turns it into `{error:{code,message},requestId}`. The message is replaced by a generic one (for example 'Internal server error') unless the error is marked user-safe or its code is in the safe set. The safe set holds credit, subscription, rate-limit, validation, model, CSRF, MFA, IP, passkey, account-unavailable and all denial codes (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:41-75) [code]. So a vague message from the server is by design, and the real text is in the server log under the same `requestId`.
2. **Code vocabularies.** Three code families live in packages/contracts/types/src/errors.ts [code]: `ErrorCode` (transport and auth, with HTTP status map), `DenialErrorCode` (line 68: who refused, such as DISABLED_BY_ORGANIZATION, UPGRADE_REQUIRED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, OFFLINE), and `DomainErrorCode` (STORAGE_ERROR, SEARCH_ERROR, TOOL_ERROR, CONNECTOR_ERROR, SANDBOX_ERROR, SAFETY_BLOCKED, RESOURCE_DELETED).
3. **Provider failures.** An adapter reports a stream error chunk. `toUpstreamError` and the per-provider mappers in adapter-errors.ts keep the status, Retry-After and the adapter's own classification. `classifyError` (packages/ai/provider-runtime/src/errors.ts:817) sorts it into a category. `mapClassifiedUpstreamError` (upstream-error-copy.ts:260) writes the user sentence and a stable code [code].
4. **Client copy.** Clients that only have an HTTP status or an exception use `toUserMessage` (packages/ui/ui/src/lib/network-error.ts:117). It hides machine-shaped text (HTTP codes, stack frames, SQL, paths) and falls back to a status sentence [code]. Mobile has its own copy for auth (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/authErrorMessage.ts) and for usage limits (apps/mobile/services/failureCopy.ts).

**Product context for support.** Free usage, the five-hour and weekly windows, and credits apply to mode:cloud (Managed Cloud) only. The plan tiers `local-only` and `byok` carry zero managed allowance (managed-usage-limits.ts) [code]. So a limit message means the turn was going to the managed route. Mobile Free copy says 'Local mode keeps working' (failureCopy.ts:41) [code].

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
**Triage in five steps.**

1. Get the `requestId` (response header from `REQUEST_ID_HEADER`, JSON body field, or the id inside a stream error frame). It is the same string as in the server log line [code: upstream-error-copy.ts:20-37].
2. Note the **mode** (local, own-key, cloud) and the **app**. A limit or provider error can only come from cloud. A 'no local model' error can only come from local.
3. Note the **code**, not the sentence. Sentences differ per app. Codes are stable.
4. Look the code up in the tables below.
5. Before calling it new, search `audit/registers/known-flaws.md` for the area (AGENTS.md section 12 and bug-finding-guide.md step 2) [requirement].

### A. Sign-in problems

| Symptom | Likely cause | Where to look | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local web: every signed-in page loops through redirects | A Clerk development key (prefix `pk_test_`) forces a handshake redirect | docs/development/troubleshooting.md:58 [requirement]. I did not verify the handshake behaviour in code [unknown] | Use a live-format key for automated work |
| Local web: sign-in fails, session 'from an unrecognised party' | `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES` unset. It is listed in the 'important' env list in apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts [code]. The proxy and session-principal check read it, see test:apps/web/__tests__/proxy-clerk-authorized-parties.test.ts | validate-env.ts; apps/web/proxy.ts | Set the variable. Name only, never paste a value |
| API answers 403 `account_unavailable` | Account suspended or locked. Raised by `ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE` in apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:144, and by the chat gate (auth-gate.ts) and the device token route [code] | api-auth.ts; auth-gate.ts | Sign in on the web to see why. Mobile shows an appeal link (authErrorMessage.ts) |
| 403 `mfa_required`, `passkey_required`, `ip_not_allowed` | Account security policy refused the call | auth-gate.ts (checks for MFA, IP allow list, passkey) | Complete step-up or sign in from an allowed network. These are real policy answers, not bugs |
| 401 `invalid_api_key` or 403 `insufficient_scope` | API key unknown or missing a scope | auth-gate.ts; apps/web/lib/api-key-scope-error.ts | Use a key with the needed scope |
| 403 `terms_acceptance_required` | Current Terms version not accepted | auth-gate.ts (CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION, readTermsStanding) | Accept terms in the web app |
| 403 `subscription_inactive` or `billing_read_only` | Paid plan lapsed or in read-only billing state | auth-gate.ts. When a plan lapses the turn may be served as Free, with header `X-AGI-Billing-Notice` | Renew, or read the billing notice |
| Mobile: 'That code expired', 'The email and password do not match', 'sign-in provider is unavailable', 'Could not reach the server' | Clerk error classes mapped by `classifyAuthError` | authErrorMessage.ts | Follow the copy. 'provider_outage' means retry another method |
| CLI or VS Code device sign-in never completes | Device-code flow. Token route answers `authorization_pending` (403), `slow_down`, `expired_token`, `access_denied`, `invalid_grant` (400) and `account_unavailable` [code: apps/web/app/api/auth/device/token/route.ts:58-160] | token/route.ts; code/route.ts ('Code not found or expired', 404; already processed, 409) | Start sign-in again. A lost refresh reply burns the token and forces a full re-sign-in (register DESKTOP-REFRESH-LOST-REPLY-01) |
| CLI says to run `agi login` | Credential file unreadable or missing | apps/cli/src/auth.rs (`sign_in_command`, keyring with file fallback) | Run `agi login` |
| Session ends with a 401 'Your session has expired. Sign in again' | Client mapped HTTP 401 | network-error.ts:17 | Sign in. Clerk session lifetime is a Clerk setting, not in the repo [unknown] |

### B. Plan and limit problems

| Symptom (code) | Meaning | Where to look | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 429 `rolling_five_hour_limit_reached` | Rolling 5-hour managed capacity used | managed-usage-request-service.ts `reservationError`; copy in billing-catalog.ts `MANAGED_QUOTA_BLOCKS` | Wait for earlier usage to leave the window, upgrade, or switch to own-key or local |
| 429 `rolling_weekly_limit_reached` | Rolling weekly capacity used | same | same |
| 429 `flagship_weekly_limit_reached` | Weekly capacity for the most capable models used | same. The share is `FLAGSHIP_OF_WEEKLY_BUDGET_RATIO` in managed-usage-limits.ts | Pick a standard model |
| 429 `artifact_runtime_limit_reached` | One generated app used its share of the 5-hour budget (`ARTIFACT_RUNTIME_SHARE_OF_FIVE_HOUR_BUDGET`) | managed-usage-limits.ts | Other chats are unaffected |
| 402 `insufficient_credits` | Billing-period usage used up | `reservationError` case 'declined'; the reset time comes from the credit balance `period_end` | Upgrade, add credits, or wait |
| 402 `extra_usage_required` | Fast mode is billed to usage credits and they do not cover it | `reservationError` | Turn on credits or turn fast mode off |
| 409 `idempotency_in_progress`, `idempotency_replay`, `idempotency_conflict` | Same idempotency key reused | `reservationError`; managed-usage-idempotency.ts | A new turn needs a new key. Client retry bug if it repeats |
| 503 `billing_unavailable` | Usage accounting could not decide | `reservationError` default | Server side. Check logs by requestId |
| `free_trial_token_budget_reached`, `free_trial_model_only`, `free_trial_feature_unavailable`, `plan_upgrade_required`, `monthly_limit_exceeded`, `monthly_credit_limit_reached`, `rate_limit_exceeded` | Other managed quota codes the clients classify | `classifyManagedQuotaErrorCode` (billing-catalog.ts:991) gives each: show upgrade button, show reset time, suggest a standard model, cleared by credits | Per presentation fields |
| `free_allowance_exhausted` (429) | The shared free model pool, used by everyone on Free, is spent. It is not the user's limit | upstream-error-copy.ts (quota_exhausted with the free-pool hint); packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/free-quota.ts:17 | Wait. Do not tell the user to upgrade for this |
| Free account reads 'You have reached the free usage limit on your account' | Free-lane message `FREE_USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED_MESSAGE` (upstream-error-copy.ts:109). Mobile builds the matching text in `freeUsageLimitMessage` | failureCopy.ts | Per owner decision, Free screens show only Upgrade and no meters [requirement: owner memory note, not a repo document] |
| Free conversation too long for a promotional message | `FREE_MODEL_PROMOTION_LIMIT_MESSAGE` | upstream-error-copy.ts:115 | New chat or shorter message |
| 429 plain `Too many requests` | Route rate limit (`withRateLimit`), not a plan limit | apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts, rate-limit-headers.ts | Wait for Retry-After |
| 'Free allowances look larger than Basic' | Known: Free is above Basic in several windows | register PLAN-PAID-ALLOWANCES-BELOW-FREE-01; managed-usage-limits.ts | Owner decision pending |
| A plan name in docs differs from the code tier | Tier ids in code are `free`, `basic`, `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, and others | managed-usage-limits.ts | Read the catalog, not prose [inferred] |

### C. Provider failures

The table shows what `classifyError` categories become (upstream-error-copy.ts `upstreamCopy`) [code].

| Category | HTTP | Code the client sees | Meaning and routing | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rate_limit | 429 | `provider_rate_limited` | Provider is momentarily busy. Retry-After is shown only if the provider sent one (stated waits over 86,400 seconds are dropped) | Wait, or pick Auto or another model |
| server_overload, capacity_off_switch | 503 | `provider_overloaded` | Provider marked degraded via `markProviderDegraded` | Retry or change model |
| quota_exhausted | 429 | `provider_quota_exhausted` or `free_allowance_exhausted` | Provider quota window spent or spending cap hit. The pool leaves the ready set until reset | Pick another model |
| billing_exhausted | 503 | `provider_billing_exhausted` | Our provider account has no funds. Shown as our problem (503, not 402) on purpose | Operator tops up the account |
| auth | 401 | `provider_credentials_rejected` | Our provider key was rejected. Copy says a service configuration problem on our side | Operator checks the managed key |
| api_timeout | 504 | `provider_timeout` | Model too slow | Retry or faster model |
| connection | 502 | `provider_unreachable` | Could not reach the provider | Retry |
| server_error, unknown | 502 | `provider_error` | Generic failure | Retry or Auto |
| empty_response | 502 | `empty_response` | Provider reported success with no content. Auto may fail over. See register WEB-FREE-ROUTER-EMPTY-2026-09-22 | Retry |
| context_overflow | 400 | `context_length_exceeded` | Conversation too long for the model | New chat, drop attachments, larger-context model |
| max_output | 400 | `max_output_tokens_exceeded` | Output cap reached | Ask for less |
| safety, content_blocked | 400 | `content_filter`, `content_blocked` | Provider safety stop. Never rotated to another provider | Rephrase |
| media_too_large | 400 | `attachment_too_large` | Attachment over the model's media limit | Shrink or change model |
| unsupported_input | 400 | `unsupported_attachment` | This route cannot read the file type. Auto rotates this class, so reaching the user means every route refused | Pick a model that accepts the file, or attach text |
| invalid_model | 404 | `model_not_found` | Model retired or unavailable | Pick another or Auto |
| invalid_input, client_error | 400 | `provider_rejected_request` | Provider called the request malformed. Logged with `[upstream] provider rejected the request` (message text logged outside production only) | Remove odd attachments or parameters |
| tool_validation | 400 | `tool_call_invalid` | Model produced a bad tool call | Retry or turn tools off |
| pause_turn | 502 | `provider_paused_turn` | Provider paused mid-turn (register PROVIDER-ANTHROPIC-PAUSE-TURN-01) | Retry |
| aborted | 499 | `request_cancelled` | Client cancelled | None |
| any interrupting category after text began | | `stream_interrupted` | 'The response stopped part way through' (connection, timeout, server error, unknown only) | Retry for a complete answer |

Rules inside this table: the user sentence changes with context. A request already on Auto is told to 'pick a specific model', never 'choose Auto'. A Free-plan default model gets shorter copy [code].

Other provider points: the idle watchdog does not abort the upstream fetch (register PKG-STREAM-WATCHDOG-NO-UPSTREAM-ABORT-01). An Anthropic PDF page cap in the catalog differs from the provider page (PROVIDER-ANTHROPIC-PDF-PAGE-CAP-01). A quota 429 on the CLI is shown as a rate limit and retried (CLI-QUOTA-429-AS-RATE-LIMIT-01). A background call that fails after the provider started records no cost row (BILLING-BACKGROUND-FAILURE-COST-ROW-01).

### D. Upload failures

| Symptom | Likely cause | Where to look | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 'Chat attachments are limited to N each' (validation 400) | File over `MAX_CHAT_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`. The limits are in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-attachment-policy.json: 25 MiB per file, 25 MiB per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files. A lower set under `withoutHandshake`: 12 MiB, 12 MiB, 12 MiB, 10 files [code] | apps/web/app/api/uploads/chat-attachment/put/route.ts | Shrink the file. Read the JSON for the live numbers |
| 'The uploaded file was empty.' | Zero-byte body | same route | Re-select the file |
| 403 'This upload is not authorized' | Missing or bad upload token on the relay PUT | same route | Request a fresh presign (the URL lives 300 seconds, presign route) |
| 500 'Object storage is not configured' | Private object storage not configured in this deployment | `isPrivateObjectStorageConfigured` in apps/web/lib/server/object-storage | Operator configuration |
| 409 `UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` | Old client sent a project-source upload without the content-binding field | apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:227 | Update the app |
| Avatar 'limited to N MiB' | `MAX_AVATAR_BYTES` | presign route | Smaller image |
| Model says 'attachment unavailable: <name> ...' | Reasons: removed from Library, unreadable, unsupported, foreign, over_budget, empty, too_large, too_many, over_message_budget | apps/web/lib/chat-attachment-policy.ts (`CHAT_ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE_NOTES`) | The note names the cause |
| Large chat file stuck 'Verifying', second intake after reload | Known: no re-attach to the running intake (WEB-LARGE-FILE-REATTACH-INTAKE-01). Feature is behind `CHAT_LARGE_FILES_ENABLED` | apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/route.ts | Wait for the intake |
| Scanned PDF page unread | OCR not wired (WEB-LARGE-FILE-OCR-UNWIRED-01) | tool-loop.ts | Attach text |
| Large-file limits never run at stated maximum | WEB-LARGE-FILE-MAX-SIZE-PREP-UNRUN-01, WEB-LARGE-FILE-PLAYWRIGHT-UNRUN-01, WEB-LARGE-FILE-ADVISORY-LOCK-FAKE-ONLY-01 | register | Treat as unverified |

| Mobile toast 'Cloud changes haven't synced.' with Retry | Sync engine ended in error state while online, signed in and in cloud mode | apps/mobile/src/features/edge-cases/components/CloudSyncErrorNotice.tsx; apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts; store apps/mobile/stores/chat/cloudSyncStateStore.ts | Tap Retry (`syncNow`). The toast shows once per distinct error |

| Memory sync 'Invalid memory sync cursor' | Bad `since` cursor | route.ts | Reset the cursor |
| Memory pull seems incomplete | Pull returns at most 1000 rows and flags saturation (`MAX_MEMORIES_PULL`) | route.ts:29 | Pull again |
| Conflicts after offline edits | Conflict listing route exists | apps/web/app/api/memory/conflicts/route.ts | Resolve in the app |

The banner offers 'Use <name>' or 'Open Models' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/localModelRecovery.ts) | Download a model, or switch |

A failed system model is skipped for the session |

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |

| Frozen install fails after dependency merge | Manifest changed, lock not regenerated | Regenerate with the package manager. Never hand-edit lock files (AGENTS.md section 12; hook blocks it) |
| Version bump does nothing | Root `pnpm.overrides` wins | Check root package.json |
| Release will not install | Seven-day minimum release age | Wait, or list the exact version in the exclude list |

| Env value ignored | A value exported in the shell wins over `.env.local` | Check the shell first |

| CI job fails in 3 seconds, no steps | Platform refused the job (billing state) | Check Actions billing |
