sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
- **The server hides messages on purpose.** A generic 'Internal server error' or 'Upstream service error' is `GENERIC_MESSAGES` at work (error-handler.ts). The cause is in the log under the `requestId`. Do not widen the safe set to make a message visible [code].
- **Match on code, never on message.** The adapter's structured classification is read first so a file named `timeout.pdf` or `insufficient_quota.pdf` cannot choose the failure class (adapter-errors.ts:11-30; provider-adapter.ts:353) [code].
- **An out-of-funds provider is not an auth failure.** `billing_exhausted` is kept separate from `auth` so the turn does not rotate onto another paid provider. It is shown as a 503 on our side, not a 402 for the user [code].
- **The shared free pool is not the user's limit.** Use `free_allowance_exhausted` wording. Do not send that user to upgrade.
- **Safety stops are never rotated** to another provider.
- **Waits are stated only when a provider or server measured them.** A value over one day is dropped. Do not invent a wait time in support replies [code].
- **Limits apply to cloud mode only.** Local and own-key tiers have zero managed allowance. Nothing may silently move a Local chat to BYOK or cloud (AGENTS.md section 6) [requirement]. A support answer must not suggest it.
- **Sign-in is separate from payment.** Local inference is free of any subscription. Whether Local needs an account is a separate question; I did not establish it per app [unknown].
- **Upload limits live in one JSON file.** Never quote numbers from memory. The no-handshake set is half the size for bytes and count [code].
- **Do not hand-edit generated or applied things:** the model catalog JSON, applied migrations, lock files, generated iOS output (AGENTS.md) [requirement].
- **A green test is not proof the fix works.** Many rows say 'source-corrected, runtime acceptance open'. Treat those as unverified.
- **Docs older than code lose.** When a doc and the code disagree, the code wins (AGENTS.md section 2).
- **Taxonomy for reviewing failures in code.** docs/agent-context/llm-failure-taxonomy.json has 28 categories, such as error-handling-failures, state-management-failures, api-failures, llm-failures, mobile-failures, cli-failures. It is a keyword list for AI-written code, not a catalogue of runtime errors [code: file read].

- Chrome extension and VS Code sign-in failure copy: I found the VS Code device-auth module (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts, with fallbacks 'This AGI Cloud account cannot be used right now...' and 'AGI Cloud could not complete the device sign-in request. Start again.') but did not trace Chrome extension errors (apps/extension/src/features/auth/authInterop.ts) [unknown].
- Where mobile `chatSyncOffReason` text is produced is not traced [unknown].
- Local-model failure copy for the CLI beyond the Ollama context row, and for the Electron Desktop, is not documented. The desktop Ollama health code sits in retained Tauri code, not the public Desktop.
- Known-flaws.md rows are mostly 'source-corrected, runtime acceptance open'. There is no list of which user-visible symptoms have actually been reproduced live.
- The register lists billing-period reset times as read from the credit balance `period_end`. How each client displays them was not compared across the six apps.
- The taxonomy file's lastUpdated is 2026-06-02, older than the repo's current guards [inferred from header; file not compared with guards].

key_facts.fact: API errors are wrapped by handleError. The message is replaced by a generic one (for example 'Internal server error', 'Upstream service error') unless the error is user-safe or its code is in SAFE_TO_EXPOSE_CODES, which includes CREDIT_REQUIRED, SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, VALIDATION_ERROR, MFA_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE and all DenialErrorCode values.

Three code families exist: ErrorCode (with HTTP map), DenialErrorCode (who refused: user, organization, workspace, role, device policy, unsupported by model/provider/route/surface/OS/region, upgrade/seat/entitlement/quota, provider degraded/unavailable, offline, maintenance, feature lifecycle) and DomainErrorCode (storage, search, tool, connector, sandbox, safety, deleted).

Provider failures are classified by classifyError into categories (aborted, api_timeout, rate_limit, server_overload, capacity_off_switch, context_overflow, max_output, tool_validation, invalid_model, invalid_input, unsupported_input, media_too_large, auth, billing_exhausted, quota_exhausted, safety, content_blocked, empty_response, connection, pause_turn, server_error, client_error, unknown) and turned into user copy by mapClassifiedUpstreamError.

billing_exhausted (our provider account out of funds) is deliberately kept separate from auth and is shown as HTTP 503 code provider_billing_exhausted, so the user is not shown a payment error and the turn is not rotated onto another paid provider.
A spent shared free model pool yields code free_allowance_exhausted (429) with copy saying it is not a limit on the user's account; other quota exhaustion yields provider_quota_exhausted.

Managed usage refusals: 402 insufficient_credits, 402 extra_usage_required, 429 artifact_runtime_limit_reached, 429 rolling_five_hour_limit_reached, 429 rolling_weekly_limit_reached, 429 flagship_weekly_limit_reached, 503 billing_unavailable, and 409 idempotency_in_progress, idempotency_replay and idempotency_conflict.
Clients decide what a quota code looks like (upgrade button, reset time, suggest standard model, cleared by credits) through classifyManagedQuotaErrorCode and the MANAGED_QUOTA_BLOCKS table.
Managed allowances come from MANAGED_USAGE_LIMITS per plan tier. The local-only and byok tiers have zero managed credits, so usage-limit errors apply only to managed cloud turns.
Free allowance sits above Basic in several windows. This is an open owner decision.
Stated waits in user copy are only used when a provider or server supplied Retry-After; values under 1 second or over 86,400 seconds are dropped.
A failure after answer text has started (connection, timeout, server error, unknown) is shown as stream_interrupted with the text 'The response stopped part way through...'.
The adapter's structured classification is read before any message text, so a user-chosen file name cannot decide whether a turn is retried or rotated.
Chat attachment limits live in chat-attachment-policy.json: 25 MiB per file, 25 MiB per message, 20 MiB per image, 20 files, with a lower withoutHandshake set (12 MiB, 12 MiB, 12 MiB, 10 files).

The relay upload PUT refuses empty bodies and bodies over the limit with validation errors, refuses a missing token with 403, and fails with an internal error if private object storage is not configured. Presign URLs live 300 seconds.
Presign answers 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED to an old client that sends a project-source upload without the content-binding field.
Memory sync refuses a client whose sync protocol is below the minimum with a client-update-required error, and a client newer than the server with a validation error. Pull is capped at 1000 memories.
Mobile shows the toast 'Cloud changes haven't synced.' with a Retry action when sync is in the error state while online, signed in and in cloud mode.

Device sign-in token route answers authorization_pending (403), slow_down, expired_token, access_denied, invalid_grant and account_unavailable. The code route answers 404 for unknown or expired codes and 409 for already-processed codes.

The chat auth gate returns terms_acceptance_required, invalid_api_key, insufficient_scope, mfa_required, passkey_required, ip_not_allowed, account_unavailable, subscription_inactive and billing_read_only as distinct codes.
Mobile maps Clerk auth errors to fixed sentences (code expired, incorrect, link expired, suspended with appeal link, locked, wrong credentials, provider outage, network unreachable).

On mobile a missing local model raises 'No local model is configured for this device.' and the banner offers 'Use <name>' or 'Open Models'. System model states are turned_off, preparing, failed, not_eligible with fixed notes.
Local runtimes known to the shared package are foundation_models, aicore, executorch and llama_rn, in tiers 1 to 3.
The retained desktop Ollama health check polls every 30 seconds and tells the user to run 'ollama serve'. This is Tauri code, not the public Electron Desktop.

Client message fallback hides machine-shaped text (HTTP status strings, stack frames, paths, SQL, ZodError) and falls back to a status sentence, for example 401 'Your session has expired. Sign in again to continue.'
The CLI local Ollama path sends no num_ctx and budgets against a 128,000-token window, which can silently drop the system prompt and tools. Open defect.
Several large-file upload behaviours have never been run at stated maximum, in the browser spec, or against a real database lock.
AGI_KV_PROVIDER accepts upstash, redis, memory or none.
The known-flaws register is the first stop before calling a bug new, and a fixed row is deleted rather than annotated.

doc.summary: Recovery in AGI Workforce is a set of runbooks plus code. Web rollback re-points Vercel to an older deployment (scripts/release/rollback.mjs); it never reverts the database. The database is restored with Neon point-in-time branches, then the erasure ledger is replayed before promotion. Incidents page through one dispatcher. Breach notice clocks are in a draft runbook. Users can restore soft-deleted chats, media and memories within 30 days.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.markdown:
This page tells an engineer or an LLM how AGI Workforce recovers from six kinds of trouble, and which code and documents back each one. Every claim has a basis tag. [code] means a file line was opened. [requirement] means a project document states it. [inferred] means reasoned from code. [unknown] means not established.

Important scope fact: almost all recovery is a **web server and cloud database** matter. The six apps (surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:cli, surface:vscode, surface:chrome) talk to one hosted backend, so the web rollback and database restore reach every app on the next request [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:164). Data held only on a device (mode:local) is outside every server mechanism [requirement] (docs/runbooks/business-continuity.md, section 'Backup behaviour by synced object'). Local mode data never reaches the servers, which narrows breach scope [requirement] (docs/runbooks/personal-data-breach.md, section 3).

Implementation status and verification status are kept apart. Code exists for most paths. Real runs recorded in documents are few: one Neon drill (2026-09-19), one local logical drill (2026-09-05), and weekly CI drills that touch no production data [requirement] (docs/runbooks/database-backup-restore.md:513-521). No production restore has ever been performed [requirement] (docs/runbooks/business-continuity.md, 'Recovery time').

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.markdown:
### 1. Roll back a release (web)
1. Look at `/admin/releases` (platform operators only) or `GET /api/admin/releases`. It shows the serving commit, the migration ledger match, `public.release_events` and the audit hash chain [requirement] (docs/runbooks/release-rollback.md:22-35). Route files exist: apps/web/app/admin/releases/page.tsx and apps/web/app/api/admin/releases/route.ts [code].
2. Dispatch the workflow **Deploy Production Surfaces** with `rollback` true and a `rollback_reason`. `rollback_to` is optional; empty picks the newest READY production deployment created before the one now serving [code] (.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml:15-25; scripts/release/rollback.mjs:162-207). Approve the `production-web` environment [requirement] (release-rollback.md:73-74).
3. The job builds nothing. It calls Vercel `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/rollback/{deploymentId}` [code] (scripts/release/rollback.mjs:219), appends a `rolled_back` row via `public.append_release_event` [code] (rollback.mjs:231), then re-runs `scripts/verify-deployment.mjs` against the apex [requirement] (release-rollback.md:76-81).
4. If GitHub Actions is down, or the workflow is disabled, run `node scripts/release/rollback.mjs --reason "..."` from a laptop with the Vercel and database variables set. Without `AGI_DATABASE_URL` the act is not audited [requirement] (release-rollback.md:102-111). `--reason` is required [code] (rollback.mjs:44).
5. The runbook says the workflow has been disabled in GitHub Actions since 2026-11-11 and production is deployed by hand with the Vercel CLI, so it must be enabled first [requirement] (release-rollback.md:61-63). Whether it is enabled now is [unknown].
6. The rollback does not revert the database, and the daily `production-drift` alarm stays red until a fix lands on main [requirement] (release-rollback.md:113-121).

**Deploying by hand:** apply migrations first (Neon backup branch, then `pnpm db:migrate -- apply --target production --confirm-production`, record the number in `scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json`), and only then promote code [requirement] (release-rollback.md:37-55).

**Mobile and extensions:** a shipped mobile binary cannot be rolled back. Use, fastest first: web rollback; a kill switch (`apps/web/lib/feature-flags/kill-switches.ts`); a version disable (`apps/web/lib/feature-flags/version-disable.ts`); an over-the-air JavaScript update via `expo-updates`; a new store binary; or a raised minimum contract version. That last lever shows a generic error on mobile, not an update prompt, so prefer a version disable [requirement] (release-rollback.md:156-178). Both flag files exist [code].

### 2. Restore the database
The mechanism is a Neon point-in-time branch. There is no `pg_dump` schedule and no backup under Neon's history window [requirement] (docs/runbooks/database-backup-restore.md:185-212).
1. Check `history_retention_seconds` in the Neon console or API. The repository does not record it. One drill saw 21,600 seconds; Neon's default is 86,400 [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:199-208, 519-521).
2. Pick the last known-good time in RFC 3339 form.
3. Make a disposable branch with `scripts/db-restore-drill.mjs --at=<time> --keep`. It only creates branches and never prints a connection string [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:231-244).
4. Point ONE preview deployment at the branch via `AGI_DATABASE_URL`. Remove `RESEND_API_KEY` from that preview so no real email is sent. Run `node scripts/verify-deployment.mjs <preview url>` [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:246-270).
5. Run `node scripts/neon-migrate.mjs status` against the branch to find a migration gap.
6. Replay the erasure ledger: call `/api/cron/purge-deleted-accounts` then `/api/cron/drain-background-jobs` on the preview with the object backup variables set. Do not promote until a purge run re-arms nothing and reports `resurrected` 0. This is `isSafeToPromote` [code] (apps/web/lib/server/erasure-tombstones.ts:328) and the step gates promotion [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:283-335).
7. Promote with the in-place restore `POST /projects/{id}/branches/{id}/restore` and `preserve_under_name` set. Connection strings do not change. Never run the in-place restore as a first attempt [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:337-355).
8. On production, run `/api/cron/reconcile-billed-plans` and `/api/cron/reconcile-credits`. They report divergence from the payment provider and do not heal it [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:357-379).
9. Encrypted rows need the old key: put it in `<NAME>_RETIRED` and run the `scripts/reencrypt.mjs` sweep. Otherwise `connector_oauth_grants`, `user_custom_connectors`, `github_installations` and `user_two_factor` rows stay unreadable [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:381-391).

**Host swap:** `AGI_DATABASE_PROVIDER` chooses `neon` (default) or `postgres`; the logical drill `scripts/db-restore-drill-logical.mjs` proves the dump and restore path [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:393-505).

### 3. Respond to an incident
1. Detection: `/api/cron/health-probe` every 10 minutes (pages after two consecutive misses, so up to 20 minutes), `evaluate-slo-burn` at :05 and :35, `page-security-anomalies` every 30 minutes, `reconcile-credits` daily, `remind-free-quota-renewal` hourly [requirement] (incident-response.md:14-41). Schedules for health-probe, evaluate-slo-burn and others match vercel.json [code] (vercel.json:110,114).
2. Alert path: `apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts` sends email (Resend), then the `PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL` webhook, then the `INCIDENT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL` webhook. With none delivered, the probe returns HTTP 500 [requirement] (incident-response.md:44-70). Files in apps/web/lib/server/incident/ exist: dispatch.ts, on-call.ts, pager.ts, out-of-band.ts [code].
3. Escalation: level 1 on-call, level 2 after `AGI_ONCALL_ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES` (15), level 3 everyone after twice that [requirement] (incident-response.md:72-90).
4. Triage by failing check: database, cache, search/vector, environment, stripe, probe_failed, credit settlement drift [requirement] (incident-response.md:155-285). Database and cache outages page as CRITICAL; Stripe and retrieval are WARNING only.
5. If the release caused it, revert first (procedure 1).
6. Update `/status` (apps/web/app/status/page.tsx [code]) and send the availability notice from the template in incident-response.md:104-125.
7. Do not call it resolved until the reconcilers that apply have run clean (see Commands).
8. Blameless postmortem within five working days from `docs/runbooks/incident-postmortem-template.md`. Each follow-up becomes a row in `audit/prior-audits/active-issues-register.md` or `audit/registers/known-flaws.md`. A repeat cause needs a decision record under `docs/decisions/` [requirement] (incident-response.md:330-355).

### 4. Handle a personal data breach
The runbook is a draft, not reviewed by counsel (`Legal review: pending-counsel`) [requirement] (personal-data-breach.md header).
1. Start the clock at first awareness, not at confirmation. Declare in writing with a timestamp and name one owner (the founder by default) [requirement] (personal-data-breach.md section 1-2).
2. Preserve evidence BEFORE remediating: Vercel logs, a `security_audit_logs` snapshot (purged at 90 days), a Neon dump or branch, the deployment SHA and migration head. Then contain.
3. Scope the breach with the questions in section 3.
4. Notify the Data Protection Board 'without delay' and each affected person 'without delay'; the detailed Board report is due within 72 hours. Neither notice waits for legal review. GDPR has its own 72-hour clock where it applies.
5. Mail reality: single-account mail exists. `sendBulkTransactionalEmail` exists as a tested primitive with no production caller and no operator entry point, so a bulk notice is a script an engineer writes on the day. No in-product notice to a set of users exists. Do not promise users an email [requirement] (personal-data-breach.md section 5).
6. Review within five working days; record durable defects in `audit/registers/known-flaws.md`.

### 5. Continue the business through an outage
The continuity page lists, for each production dependency, what is lost, what the code does and who recovers it. Order: restore environment and credentials first, confirm every core dependency is ready, and promote a restored database last [requirement] (business-continuity.md, 'Recovery by dependency' and 'Vendor recovery is not product recovery'). Key degraded behaviours: model provider outage fails over to another provider for the same family; billing outage keeps serving entitlements from the ledger; cache outage fails closed so turns refuse; object storage outage refuses uploads and downloads only; local inference on a device is unaffected by our servers [requirement] (same table). This is a one-person operation with no 24/7 rotation, no declared RPO or RTO and no second region [requirement] (business-continuity.md, 'Known gaps').

### 6. Restore a user's deleted data (where the product allows it)
| Thing | How it comes back | Window | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chat conversation | `POST /api/chat/conversations/{id}/restore` sets `deleted_at` to null for the caller's own row | 30-day recovery window is the policy value | [code] (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/restore/route.ts; apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:12) |
| Media asset | `restoreMediaAsset`, via the `/api/media` route | Only if deleted within 30 days | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:711-723; apps/web/app/api/media/route.ts:82) |
| Memory | `/api/memory/{id}/restore` | not read | [code] route exists (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/restore/route.ts); window [unknown] |
| Custom agent | `/api/custom-agents/{id}/restore` | not read | [code] route exists; window [unknown] |
| Account scheduled for deletion | Cancel via `/api/user/delete-account/cancel` or `/cancel-schedule` before the deadline. Deletion is scheduled 24 hours ahead | 24 hours | [code] (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:481; cancel routes listed) |
| Workspace scheduled for deletion | `/api/settings/organization/deletion/cancel` | before the deadline | [code] route exists |
| Erased account | Not recoverable. The erasure ledger exists to keep it erased, even after a database restore | none | [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:286-336) |

The web UI for deleted chats is apps/web/features/settings/sections/DeletedChatsSection.tsx [code]. Whether desktop, mobile and the extensions show a restore control: only a string match in apps/desktop/src/stores/chat/chatStore.ts and apps/extension/src/features/privacy/dataHandling.ts was seen; [unknown].

An operator cannot restore a single user's rows from Neon in place: a database restore returns every user's tombstoned deletions to live [requirement] (business-continuity.md, synced-object table). A per-user restore from a branch is [proposed], not documented.

### 7. Operator access during recovery (break-glass)
Holding credentials is not access. Reading one workspace needs a grant requested through `POST /api/admin/support-access` (`action: request`, at least a 20 character reason, scopes, ticket) and approved by a DIFFERENT platform operator. A grant lasts at most eight hours and defaults to one hour, enforced by a check constraint. Every transition and every refused read lands in the append-only, hash-chained `support_access_events` [requirement] (break-glass-production-access.md). The route exists [code] (apps/web/app/api/admin/support-access/route.ts).

sections.heading: Rules and traps
sections.markdown:
- A web rollback never undoes a migration. Code written against a new column breaks until the migration is applied, so migrations go first [requirement] (release-rollback.md:50-55).
- The rollback floor file `scripts/config/rollback-floor.json` currently holds `{"web": null}` [code], so no floor is enforced yet. Once set, rollback refuses older targets, and a floor file it cannot read stops the rollback [code] (rollback.mjs:111-207).
- 'Newest READY deployment' is the wrong target after an earlier rollback; the script picks the newest one created BEFORE the one serving [code] (rollback.mjs:162).
- `public.release_events` is append-only and hash chained; UPDATE is refused, DELETE only after 400 days [requirement] (release-rollback.md:137-147).
- Never first-attempt the in-place Neon restore. Branch, verify, then promote with `preserve_under_name`.
- Erasure ledger replay gates promotion. The ledger copy lives in the object backup bucket at `erasure-ledger/tombstones.ndjson`; an unreadable ledger fails closed, because an empty and an unreadable ledger look the same and promoting would resurrect erased accounts [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:293-335).
- A restore undoes user deletions made after the recovery point for every tombstone type; only account erasures are replayed [requirement] (business-continuity.md).
- The preview that serves a restored branch holds real emails: drop `RESEND_API_KEY`, never use a live payment credential, scope the variable to one preview.
- Backups: object replication is off until four `AGI_STORAGE_BACKUP_*` variables are set. A second bucket on the same endpoint is a copy, not a disaster-recovery copy (`crossRegion` flag) [requirement] (database-backup-restore.md:534-550; business-continuity.md).
- Soft-delete purge is OFF unless `SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED` is true [code] (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-soft-deleted-resources/route.ts:14-16). Media purge runs daily at 04:00 with a 30-day window [code] (vercel.json:82; apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-deleted-media/route.ts:35). Whether the flag is on in production is [unknown].
- Legal holds can preserve rows past their window [code] (purge-soft-deleted.ts imports legal-hold-gate; docs/runbooks/legal-hold.md exists, not read).
- Health pages: `degraded` (Stripe, retrieval) must not page as a platform outage; cache loss does page because limits fail closed [requirement] (incident-response.md:93-118).
- Never claim a cause, availability number or date that is unconfirmed in customer notices [requirement].
- Breach: do not rotate credentials or redeploy before logs are captured; there is no materiality threshold; loss of availability counts; legal review does not pause sending [requirement].
- Trust boundaries: recovery tools must never move Local data to BYOK or cloud. Nothing here does; no recovery path reads device-only data [inferred].
- Mobile forced-update refusal is not understood by `apps/mobile/services/api.ts` today [requirement] (release-rollback.md:172-178); not re-verified in code.

sections.heading: Gaps in the documents
sections.markdown:
- No declared RPO or RTO. Database RPO depends on a Neon setting the repository does not record. No production restore has been done, and recovery time is unmeasured [requirement] (business-continuity.md).
- The Neon point-in-time drill against the real project is in no workflow, leaves no stored attestation, and ran once by hand (2026-09-19). Key rotation drill is likewise unscheduled.
- Most dependency rows say 'no recorded drill'.
- The breach runbook is unreviewed by counsel; no bulk-notice operator tool, no in-product notice, no public notice route; the breach notice drill has never run. The subprocessors page is described as incomplete.
- The DPA customer notice has no approved template.
- Release rollback: no recorded real production rollback; whether the workflow is enabled is unclear since the runbook says it is disabled.
- No documented per-user restore of deleted data from a database branch; user restore is only the product restore routes.
- Windows for memory and custom agent restore are not documented in the runbooks.
- Which apps expose restore controls is not documented in these runbooks.
- No second region or provider; no 24/7 rotation.
- Mobile app does not display a forced-update refusal (recorded gap).

key_facts.fact: Web rollback is a workflow dispatch or a laptop script that re-points Vercel to an earlier READY deployment; it builds nothing and does not revert the database.
Rollback requires a reason (--reason) and records a rolled_back row in public.release_events via append_release_event; without AGI_DATABASE_URL the act is not audited.
The rollback floor file currently holds {"web": null}, so no floor is enforced; once written, older targets are refused.
The runbook says Deploy Production Surfaces has been disabled in GitHub Actions since 2026-11-11 and production is deployed by hand with the Vercel CLI; current state of the workflow is unknown.
A weekly Recovery Drills workflow runs a logical restore drill (Mondays 05:13 UTC) and a rollback drill that only resolves the target; the drill flags stale after 35 days in /admin/releases.
Database recovery is Neon point-in-time branching; no pg_dump schedule and no backup beneath Neon's history window; the repository does not record the window.
Production restore uses the in-place Neon branch restore with preserve_under_name only after a disposable branch has been verified; connection strings do not change.
Promotion of a restored database is gated on the erasure ledger replay: no subject re-armed and resurrected = 0 (isSafeToPromote).
The erasure ledger is mirrored to the object backup bucket at erasure-ledger/tombstones.ndjson and replayed by /api/cron/purge-deleted-accounts (daily 04:07 UTC).

Only one real Neon restore drill (2026-09-19, PASS) and one local logical drill (2026-09-05) are recorded; no production restore has ever been performed; RTO is unmeasured and no RPO or RTO is declared.
Object storage replication to an independent backup bucket runs hourly at minute 6, 200 objects per run, and does nothing until four AGI_STORAGE_BACKUP_* variables are set.
Incidents reach people only through apps/web/lib/server/incident/dispatch.ts: email via Resend, then pager webhook, then incident channel webhook; if none delivers, the probe returns HTTP 500.
Health probe runs every 10 minutes and pages after two consecutive misses; SLO burn evaluates at :05 and :35.
Escalation has three levels (on-call, plus next, everyone), with a 15-minute default step, held in the key-value store for six hours.
Stripe and retrieval outages are WARNING/degraded; database, cache and probe failures are CRITICAL; a cache outage makes turns refuse because limits fail closed.
Before closing a data incident, seven reconcilers must be run against the serving deployment; an HTTP 500 means it did not finish.
Severity 1 and 2 incidents need a blameless postmortem within five working days; a repeat cause needs a decision record under docs/decisions/.

The personal data breach runbook is a draft pending counsel review; the clock starts at first awareness; Board and individual notice are both 'without delay'; detailed report within 72 hours; legal review does not hold sending.

Bulk breach mail has a tested primitive (sendBulkTransactionalEmail) but no production caller or operator entry point; no in-product notice to a set of users exists; the breach drill has never been run.
Local mode data never reaches our servers, so a server breach cannot expose it; BYOK keys are encrypted on-device.
Operator access to a workspace needs a grant approved by a different operator, max eight hours, logged in append-only hash-chained support_access_events.
A user can restore a deleted chat via POST /api/chat/conversations/{id}/restore, which clears deleted_at on the caller's own row.
Deleted media can be restored only if deleted within 30 days; the policy recovery window for soft-deletable resources is 30 days.
Hard purge of soft-deleted resources is off unless SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED is true; it runs daily at 04:10 UTC and respects legal holds.
Account deletion is scheduled 24 hours ahead and can be cancelled before the deadline; erased accounts are not recoverable.
A database restore returns post-recovery-point user deletions to live for tombstone types; only account erasures are replayed; device-only bytes are outside every mechanism.
A shipped mobile binary cannot be rolled back; levers are kill switch, version disable, expo-updates OTA, store release, or minimum contract version, and the last gives mobile users a generic error.

Restored encrypted rows need the key active at the recovery point supplied as <NAME>_RETIRED and a reencrypt sweep, or connector grants, custom connectors, GitHub installations and 2FA rows stay unreadable.
AGI_DATABASE_PROVIDER selects neon (default) or postgres, making a host swap a configuration change; the logical drill proves dump and restore portability.

doc.summary: Glossary of about 150 terms that reconciles the user-facing name, the interface label and the code name for AGI Workforce: apps, plans (tier ids versus labels such as pro = Premium), the three modes (local, byok, managed shown as Local, BYOK, Cloud), features such as Scheduled, agents and tools, billing terms and repository jargon. sections.heading: How to read this glossary
sections.markdown:
This page lines up three vocabularies for the same thing:

1. **User-facing name**: what marketing and the product call it.
2. **Interface label**: the exact string a person sees on a button, tab or menu. These strings live in the English locale files.
3. **Internal name**: the identifier in code (a type, a tier id, a route, a table, a panel id).

The three often differ. Example: the plan whose internal tier id is `pro` is labelled "Premium" (T/billing-catalog.ts:191, I/pricing.json:5).

**Path shortcuts used in every table.**

| Shortcut | Full path |
| --- | --- |
| `T/` | `packages/contracts/types/src/` |
| `I/` | `packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/` |
| `W/` | `apps/web/` |
| `D/` | `apps/desktop/src/` |
| `M/` | `apps/mobile/` |

**Evidence basis.** Every row is `[code]` (I opened the file at the cited line) unless the row says otherwise. `[inferred]` means reasoning from code with no explicit statement. `[unknown]` means I could not establish it. `[requirement]` means a project document states it.

**Implementation status versus verification status.** Implementation status says whether code exists and is wired. Verification status says whether anyone ran it. I ran nothing and read no project document that records a run of these screens, so the verification status of every row is `[unknown]`. Where a row says "defined", it means only that the code is present.

**Plan spelling.** Plans are written as the tier id in backticks, for example `max_15x`, followed by the label in quotes when it differs. Relationship names use `plan:<tier id>`.

**Modes.** Three trust modes exist. Their internal ids are `local`, `byok`, `managed`. Their labels are "Local", "BYOK", "Cloud". In relationship names they are `mode:local`, `mode:own-key`, `mode:cloud`. The word "mode" is overloaded; see the Modes section for every separate meaning.

**Overloaded words with their own rows.** mode, tier, Code, Work, Scheduled, Agent, Managed, Cloud. Search the sections for these.

**Model names.** This page never names a model. The model list is generated from `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` into `T/models.json`; routing is in `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json`.

| Brand | AGIWORKFORCE | "AGIWORKFORCE home" (header link) | `PRODUCT_BRAND` | Brand string; the plain app names hang off it | T/product-names.ts:1; I/common.json:84 |

key_facts.fact: Three trust modes exist with internal ids local, byok, managed and user labels Local, BYOK, Cloud.

The chat execution mode ids are local_only, byok and cloud_managed, labelled 'Local Mode + Local LLMs', 'Local Mode + BYOK' and 'Cloud'. Provider modes are Local, DirectByok, ManagedGateway and ManagedNative.
Local mode never reaches Cloud and never syncs; own-key mode bills the user's key and fails over only inside its trust boundary; Cloud uses the platform key and syncs across devices.
Plan tier ids differ from labels: pro is Premium, max_15x is Ultra, team_premium is Team Premium. Legacy hobby maps to basic and pro_plus maps to max.
Ten tiers exist: local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. Unknown values normalise to free.
Team premium is a seat type; on the wire it is the team plan with seat_type premium.
Plain product names (Chat, Mobile, Desktop, CLI, Extension, Code, Work) come from PRODUCT_NAMES; brand string is AGIWORKFORCE and company name is AGI Workforce.
Only Web is marked 'Available now' in the web site status map; Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome are 'Coming soon'. Desktop platform list is macOS only.

The Scheduled screen has different names per app: web label 'Scheduled' (nav id schedules, /chat/schedules); desktop label 'Schedules' (nav id scheduled, view work-scheduled, component AgiWorkScheduled, Cloud variant cloud-schedules); mobile label 'Schedules'; tables scheduled_tasks and scheduled_task_runs.

Work has many internal names: interaction mode id agiwork, capability agi_work, feature work, request field work_mode, desktop nav id tasks, i18n namespace agiWork. The app label is 'Work' but billing labels still say 'AGI Work'.
One credit is 5000 microUSD, so 200 credits per USD; the top-up constant is 50 units per USD. Both constants exist and were not reconciled here.
Managed usage has windows: current session (5-hour), this week, most capable models (30 percent of weekly) and this billing period.
The public Electron Desktop cannot enter Local app mode: supportsLocalAppMode is true only for Tauri or a dev flag, and the app mode is forced to cloud otherwise.
Desktop and mobile app mode have two values (local, cloud) while trust modes have three; BYOK is a separate trust mode, not an app mode toggle.

Ten interaction modes are registered: chat, agiwork, search, research, code, office, image, video, voice, study. Only chat and code list local among their trust modes; agiwork, research, office, image, video, voice and study are managed only.

Per-app display names are inconsistent with the registry: Electron productName is Desktop, Tauri productName is AGI, iOS display name is AGI Mobile, VS Code displayName is AGI Code, Chrome manifest name is AGI Extension.
Auto routing has three profiles shown as Economy, Balanced and Best; the selectable alias is auto labelled 'Auto' and the picker shows 'Auto (Recommended)'.
Plan 'tier' has at least three meanings: BillingPlanTier (what is paid), SubscriptionAccessTier (what a model requires; merge due 2026-12-01) and PickerModelTier (economy, balanced, premium).
Mobile sells nothing in the current build: nativePurchases is false, which hides purchase controls and drops the Play Billing permission.
Paid upgrades can be closed per account; the pricing page then offers a waitlist or access code. An environment variable acts as a Cloud kill switch.
The CLI primary command is agi with alias agiworkforce; the Cargo package is agiworkforce-cli.

Code means three things: the VS Code app (product key Code), the /code run-in-sandbox interaction mode, and AGI Code the plan test (sandboxes plus a daily coding budget) which differs from the developer_surfaces capability.
Free managed monthly credits (2000) exceed Basic's (400) in the allowance table.
The repository keeps a checked glossary (terminology.json) that retires abbreviations org, ws, msg, convo, usr, acct, perm, ent.
Four ways to say 'a thing that holds your stuff' differ: account (person), tenant (row scope), organization (billed company), workspace (switchable container).
Verification status: none of the glossary rows were run or exercised in an app; all statuses are unknown.

open_questions: Local inference on Desktop: the requirement says local inference on desktop needs no paid subscription, but supportsLocalAppMode is true only for the Tauri shell or a dev flag, and the Electron build coerces app mode to cloud. Whether the public Desktop is meant to gain Local mode is a product choice the code leaves undecided.

Local mode and sign-in: the pricing copy says Local needs no account (pricing.json localFeature3), but I did not trace whether the mobile or desktop apps still require sign-in to open. Account requirements for Local are unknown.

Credits: credits.ts gives 200 credits per USD while billing-topups.ts gives 50 credits per USD for top-ups. I did not establish whether this is a deliberate markup or a defect; both constants are in code.
Free versus Basic: managed-usage-limits.ts gives Free 2000 monthly credits and Basic 400. I did not establish whether the Free allowance is meant to be spent on cheaper models only.

Sales dates: a project memory note mentions a date before which no subscriptions are sold on any app. I found no such date in code; the code only shows a waitlist/access-code note and a mobile nativePurchases=false flag.

Which name wins: PRODUCT_NAMES says Code and Extension, but the VS Code manifest says AGI Code and the Chrome manifest says AGI Extension; Desktop is Desktop in Electron and AGI in Tauri. No document resolves this.
Work label: app labels say Work while billing labels (BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_LABELS, USAGE_WORKLOAD_LABELS) still say AGI Work. Whether the billing copy should drop the prefix is undecided.
Scheduled label: web says Scheduled, desktop and mobile say Schedules, and the desktop agent task panel hard-codes Scheduled outside i18n.
Routines and Operator: the Routines nav label and the /operator page exist; I did not trace what they do or whether they are wired.
Mobile store top-up amounts (10, 20, 50, 100) differ from web presets (20, 50, 100, 250, 1000); I did not check whether that is intended.

Two AGI Code tests: planIncludesAgiCode (sandboxes plus coding budget, basic and up) and the developer_surfaces capability (pro and up) can disagree for a plan; not traced which one each screen uses.

sections.heading: How to read this page
sections.markdown:
This page collects what the repository records as product requirements and founder decisions. It is an index for citing, not a spec.

**Basis tags.** [code] means I opened the file at that line. [requirement] means a project document states it. [inferred] is my reasoning from code. [proposed] is my suggestion. [unknown] means not established. Nothing here is [executed]: no document I read records a real run of these requirements, and I ran nothing.

**Two statuses.** Implementation status is whether code exists and is connected. Verification status is whether anyone ran it. This page gives only implementation status, and only where quick to check. The surface matrix says a Present cell has been located, not exercised (file:docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md, header).

**Precedence.** AGENTS.md section 2 ranks code above prose. Where a document disagrees with code, code wins and the document is listed under Contradictions.

**Handles.** REQ-* names are my stable short names for requirements. D-yyyy-mm-dd-nn are the founder's own decision IDs.

sections.heading: Contradictions between documents
sections.markdown:
| Item | Document A says | Document B or code says | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop public count | file:docs/product/competitive-guidance.md (2026-11-19) and experience-contract.md 12.2: Electron is the one public Desktop; Tauri is not a public product | D-2026-09-15-04 amendment of 2026-10-24: Tauri ships as a second public app | Unresolved; the later dated decision outranks the guidance, but the guidance was updated 2026-11-19, after it. Ask the owner. |
| Desktop modes | requirements.md 12: Desktop exposes Local, BYOK and Cloud | definition.md and experience-contract.md 12.2: Electron is Cloud chat plus host; inference is Managed Cloud | definition.md and the decision; requirements.md section 12 is stale |
| Website scope | requirements.md 11: pricing is a placeholder, no full Cloud chat before controls proven | definition.md: Managed Free chat open to signed-in users since 2026-06-27 | definition.md |
| Mobile status | suite.md: unpublished, Desktop steering planned | requirements.md section 10 treats store release as the bar; store state [unknown] | Not a conflict; status unknown |
| Serial order | definition.md: one surface active at a time | Founder decisions of 2026-11-10 to 11-13 push mobile, desktop and web work in parallel | The decisions; the serial rule is no longer how work runs [inferred] |
| Paid gate wording | commercial.md, suite.md: waitlist or access code gated | Code: a runtime operator flag plus env override plus beta_redemptions row (billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-52) | Code; the documents omit the flag mechanism |
| Plan names | D-2026-09-27-01 and commercial.md use Pro, Max 5x, Max 20x, max_15x | Code labels: pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra (billing-catalog.ts:192-207); the Max 15x ID no longer matches a '20x' label | Code |
| Decision index | docs/decisions/README.md lists dated records but omits 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13, and lists wire-or-cut.md | Both files exist | Directory; README is incomplete |
| Matrix counts | open-questions.md: 184 present, 95 absent, 63 unverified, 1 partial | JSON today: 190, 106, 60, 1 | JSON |
| Model picker routing | D-2026-11-12-07: Auto only on mobile | Web and desktop still offer Instant, Best, Economy | Recorded as a deliberate deviation |
| Local to Cloud on mobile model picker layout | D-2026-11-10-02 says side panel only | Amended twice (2026-11-12-02, 2026-11-13-05) | Latest |
| Design rule 6 forbids decorative glow | D-2026-11-13-01 allows voice glow that carries state | Decision records the deviation | Decision |
| Tauri-related guidance | competitive-guidance.md date 2026-11-19 but research baseline 2026-09-21 | Its own text says prefer the later comparisons | Later comparisons |

key_facts.fact: Plan IDs are local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; public labels differ (pro is Premium, max_15x is Ultra).
Local plan and BYOK plan cost zero; isFreeOfChargePlanTier covers local-only, byok and free.
Entitlement resolves to free unless subscription status is active or trialing.
One AGI account has one effective subscription across all six surfaces; surfaces never create a second entitlement.
Mobile v1 sells nothing in the app: nativePurchases is false.
Paid upgrades are gated by a runtime operator flag, an env override AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1, or a beta_redemptions row; unreadable flag means closed.
Managed Free is public alpha after sign-in since 2026-06-27; AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA is only a kill-switch.
Local mode never silently reaches BYOK or Cloud; the typed Local contract has cloudEgressAllowed false and failover refuse.
Mobile has no BYOK mode in v1.
Individual plans are monthly only; Team keeps yearly. Decided 2026-09-27.
Electron is the public Desktop; a 2026-10-24 amendment says Tauri also ships as a second public app, name undecided.
Serial surface order is Website, Mobile, Desktop, Chrome, CLI, VS Code (founder 2026-09-21).
Surface feature matrix today: 190 present, 106 absent, 60 unverified, 1 partial over 51 features; Present means located, not exercised.
Two continuity domains: Account Cloud (Web, Mobile Cloud, Desktop Cloud, eligible Chrome) and Host Developer (Desktop Code, CLI, VS Code).
On mobile in Local mode only device-scoped destinations are shown; unclassified screens count as cloud.
Model-improvement training switches (chats, voice) are decided opt-in and off by default on 2026-11-13, pending lawyer review; nothing uses customer content for training today.
Model picker on mobile: Auto only, with Instant, Economy, Images, Files filters from the catalog; web and desktop keep Instant, Best, Economy.
Managed turns that cross a usage window finish on the plan; monthly allowance is a hard edge (2026-10-25).
Per-seat credits, two-seat minimum for Team (decision 29, 2026-10-22).
US-only managed data and inference, on a region-neutral design.
Model IDs may be literals only in the generated catalog; defaults reference family slots.
Competitive guidance: ChatGPT and Claude primary references; parity measured by outcomes and continuity, not label matching.
No release has been shown to have run as of 2026-11-11: surface workflows have no runs, one draft release, store availability unverified.
A no-sales-before-2027-01-01 decision and an 18-and-over rule appear only in owner memory, not in any repository document I read.

open_questions: Whether Local mode on mobile and Electron desktop works fully signed out is documented as yes (requirements.md 7.1) but not verified in code; mobile age assurance may interact.
Whether the owner's recorded 2027-01-01 sales deferral and the 18-and-over rule exist in any repository record; none found.
Which of the 2026-10-24 Tauri-as-second-public-app decision and the 2026-11-19 competitive guidance (Tauri not public) stands.
Whether every surface calls effectivePlanTier and the shared entitlement path; only the contract file was read.
The Free chat daily share per account versus the 2026-10-07 no-cap decision (no record of that decision found).
Whether surface-by-mode support matrix (item 25) is published anywhere; no default exists.
The full contents of founder-actions.md (106 KB) and wire-or-cut.md (976 KB) were not read; requirements and decisions inside them may be missing.
Whether mobile has been submitted to any store; the repository does not settle it.
Model-improvement switch wording and minimum age thresholds await legal review.
